Debutant director Aladdin Mostafa, producer Hamdy…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
The Black Sea Explores Universal Human Emotions Through a Distinctive Cinematic Approach at IFFI 2026
The film examines the extremes of human desire and their consequences: Director Aladdin Mostafa
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 1:12PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

The makers of the Arabic-language feature film The Black Sea addressed the media today at the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Media Centre during the 57th International Film Festival of India in Goa. Debutant director Aladdin Mostafa, producer Hamdy Sameh, and film editor and executive producer Motaz Nashy interacted with journalists, sharing insights into the film’s genesis, universal relevance, and deliberate editorial craft.

Speaking about the inspiration behind The Black Sea and choosing the subject for his maiden feature, director Aladdin Mostafa expressed his delight at presenting the film at IFFI and bringing a story from Arab culture to an international platform. Elaborating on the central theme, he stated that the film examines how unchecked human desires can spiral when individuals pursue their goals at any cost, questioning the lengths to which people go when they resort to extreme actions to fulfil their ambitions.

Responding to a question on bringing an Egyptian film to Indian and global audiences at the festival, producer Hamdy Sameh highlighted the story's cross-cultural resonance. He noted that although The Black Sea is an Egyptian production in the Arabic language, it is not restricted to any specific culture or geography. “It speaks to something shared by people across nations. Human beings everywhere experience the same fundamental desires, which allows the film to connect with audiences in India and across the world,” he said.

Sharing perspectives on the technical and narrative approach of the film which revolves around characters confined indoors and drawn into a dark psychological app, film editor and executive producer Motaz Nashy spoke about using rhythm and pacing to convey tension and confinement. He noted that the primary challenge lay in ensuring the film’s deeper concepts were effectively communicated to all viewers. Rather than opting for rapid cuts, the team consciously adopted a slower, deliberate pace so that audiences could immerse themselves in the characters' experience and feel the core message the filmmakers set out to deliver.

The press conference concluded with the filmmakers expressing gratitude to festival organizers and Indian audiences for their warm reception. With its atmospheric pacing and thought-provoking premise, The Black Sea offers viewers at IFFI 57 an immersive cinematic experience that bridges regional storytelling with global human truths. The Press Conference was moderated by Ms. Shrushti Suresh Kulye.

Rooted in Egyptian culture yet exploring themes that resonate across societies, The Black Sea reflects the spirit of IFFI 2026’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’. Through its universal exploration of human desires and its distinctive approach to storytelling, the film illustrates how cinema transcends linguistic and cultural boundaries, bringing audiences together through shared human experiences.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
List of Outcomes: State visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 9:35PM by PIB Delhi

Inaugurations / Groundbreakings / Project Dedications:

Launch of Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur.

Laying of the Foundation Stone of a new ICP at Banbasa and progress in the construction of the ICPs at Bhairahawa, Sunauli and Dodhara Chandani.

Inauguration of a new cross-border motorable bridge between Dharchula (India) and Darchula (Nepal).

Laying of Foundation Stone for Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project (669 MW).

Dedication of Phase II of the Motihari–Amlekhgunj Oil Pipeline (MAPL).

Laying of the Foundation Stone of Jhapa petroleum terminal of the planned Siliguri-Jhapa petroleum pipeline.

Announcements:

Development Cooperation Package of Rs. 15,000 crores (NPR 24,000 crores) to support Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development.

Acees to additional Indian ports for Nepal’s transit cargo — Deendayal port (Kandla, Gujarat) and Paradip port (Odisha).

Setting up of an Agro-Industrial Park in Chitwan, Nepal.

Setting up of an off-shore IIT campus in Nepal.

Finalisation of Final Location Survey for the proposed Raxaul–Kathmandu electrified broad-gauge railway line.

Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs):

Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for Academic and Research Collaboration between National Forensic Sciences University, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, and Crime Investigation Department, Nepal Police.

MoU between Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), India, and National Police Academy (NPA), Nepal.

MoU between National Centre for Good Governance, Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances, Government of India, and Nepal Administrative Staff College, Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, Government of Nepal, on Capacity Building Training Programme for Civil Servants of Nepal.

MoU between Government of India and Government of Nepal on Cooperation in the field of Ayurveda and other Traditional Systems of Medicine.

MoU between Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Government of India, and Ministry of Information and Communication (MOIC), Government of Nepal, on Establishment of Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the Utilization of South Asia Satellite.

MoU between Government of India and Government of Nepal on Technical Cooperation in the field of Sustainable Urban Development.

MoU between Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, and Ministry of Health and Food Safety, Government of Nepal, on Cooperation in the field of Health and Medicine.

MoU between Government of India and Government of Nepal on Cooperation in the field of Livestock and Fisheries Development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Joint workshop of the Ministries of Agriculture and Rural Development, on their role in eradication of poverty, concludes in Delhi under the chairmanship of Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Encouraging officers and employees, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan says: “You have not merely framed schemes; you have built the nation. You are the true drivers of this development journey”
“Extreme poverty has declined from 27.1% to 2.6%; our resolve is to lift those still left behind out of poverty”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
“Agriculture growth rate reaches a historic 4.45%, taking India’s farm sector beyond even the Green Revolution era”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
“Lakhpati Didis, permanent houses, rural roads, Viksit Bharat - G RAM G and watershed development have transformed the lives of the rural poor”: Shri Shivraj Singh
ICAR innovations have increased farmers’ incomes, delivering an economic return of ₹13.85 for every rupee invested
“Celebrate this achievement with joy and a sense of occasion”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan appreciates the efforts of everyone, from Section Officers to Secretaries
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan sits among employees for direct interaction and seeks their suggestions; the next goal is to make a mark in global markets through FTAs
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 9:15PM by PIB Delhi

Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has achieved unprecedented, extraordinary and historic milestones in the field of poverty eradication. According to the World Bank’s recent report, nearly 500 million people in the country have moved out of poverty, while the rate of extreme poverty has declined from 27.1 per cent to just 2.6 per cent. This remarkable progress reflects the contribution of several sectors and government initiatives, particularly agriculture and allied activities, agricultural research, land resources and rural development. To assess the role played by these areas in the achievement and discuss the strategy for the road ahead, a special one-day workshop was organised today at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi. The joint workshop was chaired by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Bhagirath Choudhary and Union Minister of State for Rural Development Shri Kamlesh Paswan also participated. Describing the country’s progress, Shri Chouhan called it an “extraordinary, unimaginable and unprecedented miracle”.

The workshop brought together the senior-most officials of all four departments whose work and initiatives were being reviewed. Those present included Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra; Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal; Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Shri Dilip Kumar; and Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Dr M. L. Jat. Senior officials and scientists from the four departments also attended, along with Section Officers, Assistant Section Officers and a large number of other officers and employees. The participation of staff across different levels reflected the workshop’s focus not only on reviewing departmental achievements, but also on recognising the contribution of those involved in taking policies and schemes from the planning stage to implementation.

Lifting 500 million people out of poverty, more than the population of the United States, is a miracle

Addressing officers and employees of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, ICAR, Department of Rural Development and Department of Land Resources, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the achievement India had secured under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi was truly extraordinary, remarkable and unimaginable. The World Bank itself had acknowledged that no other country in the world had reduced poverty at such a rapid pace. The fact that nearly 500 million people had moved above the poverty line represented a historic development, particularly given the scale of the population involved. Shri Chouhan said that this progress was the result of the Prime Minister’s leadership, vision and hard work, but it was also important to recognise the contribution made by every officer and employee in the two ministries. The achievement, he stressed, was not the work of any one individual or department; it reflected the collective effort of people working across the government machinery to deliver development and improve lives.

“You have not merely framed schemes; you have built the nation”: Celebrate this achievement

Encouraging officers and employees, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that this success had not come about on its own. Behind it lay the hard work, dedication and sustained efforts of everyone who had contributed to the implementation of government programmes. He urged those attending the workshop to participate with a sense of joy and celebration, observing that when the country had achieved something so significant, the happiness and pride it inspired should also be visible on their faces. Shri Chouhan recalled that the Prime Minister had emphasised that “you have not merely framed schemes; you have built the nation”. He explained that review meetings are generally attended by senior officials, but he had consciously decided to make this workshop different. He wanted colleagues at every level, from Section Officers and Assistant Section Officers to Secretaries, to be present because they were the foundation stones of the administrative system and the work on files began at these levels. He told the employees that they were not merely witnesses to the country’s development journey, but its true drivers and participants. Demonstrating his intention to engage directly with them, Shri Chouhan left the stage and sat among the audience, speaking with employees and seeking to understand their experiences on the ground and their suggestions.

Resolve to bring those still left behind out of poverty

Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that people work not merely to earn a livelihood, but also to find purpose in their lives and serve the people of the country. He observed that every stage in the journey of a government scheme involves the contribution of employees. Whether a scheme is developed from the grassroots, considered and approved by the Cabinet, or eventually implemented on the ground, the efforts of people working at different levels are essential to its success. He said that two major commitments made by the Prime Minister now lay before the nation. The first was to ensure that those who had already risen above the poverty line did not fall back below it under any circumstances. The second was to rapidly bring the remaining 2.6 to 2.7 per cent of the population out of poverty and improve their standard of living. Shri Chouhan emphasised that the progress achieved so far must be protected, while the government continued working to reach those who had yet to benefit sufficiently from the country’s development. The task ahead, therefore, was both to sustain the gains made and to ensure that the remaining people were also able to lead better lives.

Agriculture growth rate reaches a historic 4.45%; ICAR research delivers returns of 13.85 times the investment

Highlighting the achievements of the agriculture sector, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that the past 12 years had witnessed remarkable progress, with work being undertaken in agriculture that the country could take pride in. He pointed out that even during the Green Revolution, the agriculture growth rate generally remained in the range of 3 to 3.5 per cent. India’s decadal agriculture growth rate had now reached the historic level of 4.45 per cent, surpassing the levels recorded during that period. Among the key initiatives contributing to the sector’s progress, he highlighted the direct assistance of more than ₹4.66 lakh crore provided through the PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The sector had also recorded foodgrain production of 376.56 million tonnes and horticulture production of 386.91 million tonnes. Affordable agricultural credit, crop insurance, natural farming, the establishment of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and digital initiatives such as AgriStack had further supported farmers and contributed to increasing their incomes. Together, these measures reflected the progress made in strengthening agricultural production and improving the support available to farmers.

A presentation by the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE/ICAR) highlighted the economic returns generated by scientific research and innovation. It stated that every rupee invested in agricultural research and education had yielded an economic benefit of ₹13.85, while investment in animal husbandry research had generated a return of ₹20.81. Since 2014, a total of 3,436 new crop varieties had been released, of which 93 per cent were climate-resilient. The presentation also highlighted the contribution of biofortified crop varieties, fish production of 19.78 million tonnes and the availability of more than 500 agricultural machines. In addition, digital outreach through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) was reaching five crore farmers every year. These research-led developments, technological interventions and knowledge-sharing efforts had helped strengthen the rural economy and extend the benefits of agricultural science to farmers across the country.

Rural development and DoLR schemes have transformed the lives of villages and the rural poor

The workshop also examined in detail the impact of schemes implemented by the Department of Rural Development and the Department of Land Resources. Shri Chouhan said that these departments had played a highly significant role in the country's progress towards poverty eradication. Presentations highlighted the reach of several rural development initiatives. Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission, more than 10 crore women had been connected with self-help groups, and 3.76 crore women had so far become ‘Lakhpati Didis’. The Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) had enabled the construction of 3.99 crore permanent houses, while the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) had created a network of 7.99 lakh kilometres of all-weather rural roads. Under Viksit Bharat - G RAM G (VB-G RAM G), rural households are now assured of 125 days of employment. Social assistance programmes and 99.9 per cent transparency in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) have also helped empower the last person in the queue. These initiatives have contributed to changing the lives of rural families by supporting livelihoods, providing housing, improving connectivity and strengthening the delivery of assistance to beneficiaries.

Under the Department of Land Resources (DoLR), the watershed development component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY) has supported water conservation and land improvement works across 3.40 crore hectares. These interventions have directly benefited 61.15 lakh farmers. The work has contributed to an increase in irrigated areas and milk production, while farmers’ average annual incomes have recorded growth of up to 70 per cent. The figures presented at the workshop highlighted the contribution of watershed development to improving land and water resources, strengthening agricultural activity and supporting the livelihoods of farming communities. The programme's impact was also reflected in the number of farmers who had directly benefited from these interventions and the reported improvement in their annual incomes.

Suggestions sought to improve budgets and schemes; call to take achievements to the public

During the concluding session of the workshop, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan extended an open invitation to officers and employees to share their ideas and suggestions. He emphasised that the achievements made so far did not mean there was no scope for further improvement. Several useful suggestions had already been received on schemes such as PM-KISAN and e-NAM. He encouraged everyone to write to him without hesitation if they had any ideas concerning the budget, changes to existing schemes or the introduction of new initiatives that could help increase farmers’ incomes. Shri Chouhan said that he would also hold informal, department-wise meetings with employees working at lower levels in the future. As the head of the department, he assured colleagues that he would remain accessible and approachable to everyone, regardless of their position or level of responsibility. He invited them to contribute their practical experience and ideas to the process of improving government programmes and making them more effective.

Shri Chouhan also placed particular emphasis on the need to ensure that the departments’ achievements and public welfare initiatives did not remain confined to files and formal communications, but were effectively taken to the people and farmers. He said that communicating the work being done by the departments and its impact on people's lives was an important responsibility. Giving an example, he observed that when officials go directly to the ground and engage with people, the positive message reaches the entire country. He stressed that the development journey was far from over and that the targets set for 2029, 2030–31 and ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’ had to be achieved on time. Referring to the Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), he said that the next objective was to enable Indian agricultural products to make their mark in markets across the world. The country now had to build on the progress achieved in agriculture and ensure that its products reached and competed successfully in global markets.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi joins the Shabad Kirtan on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
The entire Sikh tradition is synonymous with the spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture: PM
Today, conflicts are underway in numerous parts of the world, with countless innocent people and families facing violence and unrest; In such times, to ensure peace in every corner of the globe, safety for every family, and the opportunity for every individual to live with dignity, the spirit of 'Sarbat Da Bhala' becomes all the more vital: PM
Every youth of the nation should be free from addiction, fulfill their dreams, study well, and bring pride to their family and nation; Families play a major role in this effort, and together, our Sangat, Gurudwaras, and social organisations can guide the youth and give them the courage to choose the right path: PM
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today joined the Shabad Kirtan on the sacred occasion of the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister opened his remarks with the greeting Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh! Bowing with reverence to Guru Nanak Dev Ji in the sacred atmosphere and expressing heartfelt gratitude for the opportunity to participate in the Shabad Kirtan, he extended festive greetings to the nation.“I extend countless greetings to all countrymen on the occasion of Parkash Purab,” remarked Shri Modi.

Describing every Shabad of Gurbani and every melody of Kirtan as far more than mere music, the Prime Minister characterized it as a spiritual practice in itself and like diving into an ocean of knowledge. “Therefore, whenever I receive an invitation for such an event, whenever I get the opportunity, I definitely attend the Sangat and Kirtan,” remarked PM Modi.

Recalling Guru Nanak Dev Ji's teaching of Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo as a natural part of his life from childhood, the Prime Minister spoke fondly of bowing in Gurdwaras, immersing in Gurbani, experiencing the joy of Seva, partaking in Langar, and paying obeisance at Sri Harmandir Sahib on numerous occasions. “Old colleagues would know that I have also spent a lot of time in Punjab, and that period has been one of the most special memories of my life,” remarked Shri Modi.

Expressing gratitude for continually receiving the company of Sikh saints by the Guru's grace, including the privilege of hosting numerous saints and scholars at the Prime Minister's residence, Shri Modi noted the distinct spiritual energy felt through their presence at the event and felicitated all Sikh brothers. “On this occasion, I bow to all saints and scholars,” remarked PM Modi.

Highlighting that this year's Parkash Purab coincides with the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who laid down his life on the very soil of Delhi to protect the nation's identity, faith, belief, and values, the Prime Minister noted that even after 350 years, the inspiration of that sacrifice remains deeply ingrained in the soil and every corner of the nation. “Every citizen of the country will always remain grateful to him for it,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Observing that the entire Sikh tradition has been synonymous with sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture, exemplified by the martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji as well as the unabated spirit during the freedom struggle, the Prime Minister paid tribute to Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji for his vital role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement and lifelong dedication to service. “This year also marks the completion of one hundred years of his martyrdom; on this occasion, I bow to him as well,” noted PM Modi.

Recalling that India endured centuries of slavery and that even during its most difficult historical periods the Gurus kept alive the flame of protecting the nation, the Prime Minister emphasized that today's great national resolves and the goal of Viksit Bharat can only be achieved through their inspiration and ideals. “Therefore, it is the responsibility of all of us to keep Sikh traditions and the heritage of Sikhi ahead as a beacon of light,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing how the government has fulfilled this responsibility with complete faith over the past 12 years, the Prime Minister cited the celebrations of the 350th Parkash Purab of Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the 550th Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji across India and abroad. He noted that commemorative coins and postage stamps were released, special trains were run, Gurbani programs were organized nationwide, and a national event was held at the Red Fort to mark the 400th Parkash Purab of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. “With this same spirit, we are currently also observing the 350th Martyrdom Day of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji,” noted PM Modi.

Noting that the nation will observe the next Veer Bal Diwas on December 26, the Prime Minister explained that the national observance was initiated to pass on the immortal saga of the brave Sahibzadas' martyrdom and Mata Gujri's resolve to the younger generation. “When our children learn about the circumstances of that era, how the Sahibzadas and Gurus attained martyrdom, and how our faith remained protected, this knowledge and inspiration will build youth dedicated to the nation,” asserted Shri Modi.

Pointing out that efforts to celebrate the glory of the Gurus extend beyond India's borders, the Prime Minister recalled his recent visit to Khalsa Diwan, the oldest Gurdwara in the Philippines, where the Government of India is supporting its redevelopment. “It is our effort that the light of our Gurus reaches every person, and with their blessings, India touches new heights,” affirmed PM Modi.

Quoting the Ardas prayer ‘Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhane Sarbat Da Bhala’, the Prime Minister noted that Gurbani imparts the universal teaching of working for the welfare of all. “The thought of wishing well for everyone awakens in the mind only when we begin to consider everyone as our own,” observed Shri Modi.

Referring to ongoing conflicts around the world where innocent people and families face violence and unrest, the Prime Minister emphasized the universal need for peace, safety for every family, and a life of dignity for every individual. “In such times, the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala becomes even more important,” asserted PM Modi.

Observing that the greatest test of the life values imparted by Guru Sahib takes place in everyday life, the Prime Minister drew attention to the pressing societal challenge of drugs. “When a young person falls into the grip of addiction, the dreams of the entire family shatter along with them,” observed Shri Modi.

Calling for every youth in India to be free from addiction so they can study well, fulfill their dreams, and bring pride to their families and the nation, the Prime Minister underscored the vital role of families, the Sangat, Gurdwaras, and social institutions in guiding youth toward the right path, before concluding with Parkash Purab greetings and the traditional Sikh salutations. “I am confident that with Guru Sahib's grace and the collective efforts of society, we will be able to give our new generation a safe and bright future,” affirmed PM Modi.

 

Happy to join the Shabad Kirtan marking the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. https://t.co/YMDdLpFvot

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DELIVERY OF ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT, ‘ASHANK’ (YARD 3036)
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

‘Ashank’, one of the Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW SWC), indigenously designed and built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE), Kolkata, was delivered to Indian Navy on 23 Nov 2026 at Visakhapatnam.

The ASW SWCs (ex-GRSE) have been designed and constructed in accordance with the Classification Rules of Indian Register of Shipping (IRS).

Equipped with state-of-the-art lightweight torpedoes, indigenous rocket launchers and advanced sonar systems, Yard 3036 ‘Ashank’ is a potent platform designed to strengthen the Navy’s underwater surveillance and Anti-Submarine Warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal water. These ships are among the largest Indian Naval warships propelled by waterjets. The ship will further strengthen the Navy’s Anti- submarine, coastal surveillance and mine-laying capabilities. 

The delivery of ‘Ashank’ is yet another milestone in the Indian Navy’s pursuit of indigenous shipbuilding, in line with the Government’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. With over 80 percent indigenous content, the ship stands as a testament to the growing strength of the domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem and reducing dependency on imports.

***

VM/SPS                                                                                                          253/26

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's address at the Shabad Kirtan on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 8:22PM by PIB Delhi

Guru Pyari Saadh Sangat Ji, Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!

Revered saints of the Sikh community, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji, Chief Minister of Delhi Sister Rekha Gupta ji, my colleagues in Parliament, other ministers of the Delhi Government, all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,

In this sacred atmosphere, I respectfully bow to Guru Nanak Dev Ji. I extend lakh-lakh greetings to all the people of the country on the occasion of Prakash Parv. On this holy occasion of Guru Purab, I sincerely thank Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji for giving me the opportunity to participate in this Shabad Kirtan.

Friends,

Every word of Gurbani and every note of Kirtan is not merely music. It is a form of spiritual practice in itself. It is like diving into an ocean of knowledge. Therefore, whenever I receive an invitation to such an event, whenever I get an opportunity, I make it a point to be present in the Sangat and Kirtan.

Friends,

Guru Nanak Dev Ji used to say: Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo. These teachings have been a natural part of my life. Bowing my head at Gurdwaras, immersing myself in Gurbani and experiencing spiritual bliss, finding joy in service, and then partaking in Langar, this has been a continuous part of my journey from childhood to my days as an organisational worker. Many times, I have had the good fortune of bowing my head at Sri Harmandir Sahib. Old colleagues know that I spent a considerable amount of time in Punjab as well, and that period remains one of the most special memories of my life.

Brothers and sisters,

By Guru’s grace, I have continued to receive the company of Sikh saints. At the Prime Minister’s residence too, I have had the privilege of hosting many Sikh saints and Gyanis. Even today, the presence of our saints at this gathering is creating a unique spiritual energy. On this occasion, I bow to all the saints and Gyanis. I extend my greetings to all Sikh brothers and sisters.

Friends,

This year’s Prakash Parv is accompanied by another sacred remembrance. This year marks 350 years since the martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. It was here on the soil of Delhi that Guru Sahib sacrificed his life for the protection of the identity of this nation, for faith, belief, and values. Three hundred and fifty years have passed since that event, yet the inspiration of that sacrifice remains deeply embedded in the soil of India and in every particle of this nation. The people of this country will always remain grateful to him.

Friends,

The spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture has always been synonymous with the Sikh tradition. The martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji reminds us of this. This spirit continued uninterrupted even during the struggle for Independence. As our Lieutenant Governor explained in detail, Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji himself is a shining example of this tradition. He played an important role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement. He dedicated his entire life to service. This year also marks one hundred years since his martyrdom. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.

Friends,

India endured centuries of slavery. During the most difficult periods in our history, our Gurus kept the flame of protecting the nation burning. Today, when great national resolutions stand before us, when the goal of a Developed India lies ahead of us, this journey can be completed only through the inspiration of our Gurus and the strength of their ideals. Therefore, it is our responsibility to keep Sikh traditions and the heritage of Sikhi shining before society like a beacon of light.

Friends,

Over the past twelve years, we have sincerely tried to fulfil this responsibility. We celebrated the 350th Prakash Parv of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. We celebrated the 550th Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Numerous ceremonies were organised across India and abroad. Commemorative coins and postage stamps were issued. Special trains were operated. Programmes dedicated to Gurbani were organised throughout the country. Similarly, on the 400th Prakash Parv of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, a national event was held at the Red Fort. With the same spirit, we are currently commemorating the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

Friends,

One month from now, on 26 December, the country will observe another Veer Baal Diwas. We began observing this day nationally because it is our responsibility to take to the younger generation the immortal saga of the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas, the resolve of Mata Gujri, and that unparalleled courage and valour. When our children learn about the circumstances of those times, when they understand how the Sahibzadas and the Gurus made the supreme sacrifice and how our faith was protected through their sacrifices, that knowledge and inspiration will create youth dedicated to the nation.

Our efforts to honour the Gurus are not limited to India. Just a few days ago, I was in the Philippines. There too, I visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara, the oldest Gurdwara in the Philippines. The Government of India is also supporting the redevelopment of the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara. Our effort is that the light of our Gurus should reach every person. With their blessings, India should continue to reach new heights.

Friends,

In our Ardas, we say: Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhaane Sarbat Da Bhala. This teaching of wishing well for all comes to us from Gurbani. And the thought of working for everyone's welfare arises only when we begin to regard everyone as our own.

Friends,

Today, conflicts are taking place in many parts of the world. Many innocent people and families are facing violence and unrest. In such times, the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala, Sarbat Da Bhala, becomes even more important, so that there may be peace everywhere, every family may remain safe, and every individual may have the opportunity to live with dignity.

Friends,

The greatest test of the values given to us by Guru Sahib comes in our everyday lives. Today, one such challenge before our society is the problem of drugs. Because when a young person falls into the grip of addiction, the dreams of an entire family are shattered along with him.

Friends,

Every young person in the country should be free from addiction. They should fulfil their dreams, study well, progress in life, and bring honour to their family and the nation. In this effort, the role of families is extremely important. Our Sangat, our Gurdwaras, and our social institutions can together guide young people and give them the courage to choose the right path. I am confident that with Guru Sahib’s blessings and the collective efforts of society, we will be able to provide a safe and bright future for our younger generation. With this sentiment, I once again extend lakh-lakh greetings to all of you on the sacred Prakash Parv of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj.

Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!

Come, join me in raising the Jaikara - Bole So Nihal! Sat Sri Akal!

Thank you very much!

DISCLAIMER: This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister’s address. Original address was delivered in Hindi. 

****

MJPS/SS/VJ/ST

item.title: ‘Pagla Ghora’ and ‘Ohh My Dog’ Explore the Profound Dimensions of Human Conscience and Unconditional Love at 57th IFFI

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘Pagla Ghora’ and ‘Ohh My Dog’ Explore the Profound Dimensions of Human Conscience and Unconditional Love at 57th IFFI
Art Has No Borders, Only Roots: Sekhar Das on the Universal Appeal of ‘Pagla Ghora’
Animals Do Not Carry the Burden of Prejudice; Their Loyalty Is Absolute: Amit Rai, Director of ‘Ohh My Dog’
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 8:10PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 23 November 2026

 

While one story brings the ghosts of the past face to face with a restless conscience, the other celebrates a love so pure that no distance or adversity can diminish it. Exploring two contrasting yet deeply moving dimensions of the human experience, ‘Pagla Ghora’ and ‘Ohh My Dog’, the Bengali and Hindi selections in the Indian Panorama, took centre stage at a press conference today at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Filmmakers Sekhar Das and Amit Rai, accompanied by acclaimed Bengali actress Gargee RoyChowdhury and producer Dr. Prabir Bhaumik, interacted with the media, sharing insights into their respective films and their exploration of guilt, betrayal, empathy and unconditional devotion. Together, these narratives celebrate cinema's power to transcend linguistic and cultural boundaries through the universal language of human emotion.

Pagla Ghora: A Haunting Journey into Guilt, Remorse and the Human Conscience

National Film Award-winning filmmaker Sekhar Das, along with lead actress Gargee RoyChowdhury and producer Dr. Prabir Bhaumik, shared insights into the cinematic adaptation of legendary playwright Badal Sircar’s post-realist theatrical masterpiece, ‘Pagla Ghora’. Set against the eerie backdrop of a forest crematorium at night, the film follows four men who gather for the cremation of a woman who died by suicide. As her spirit confronts them, their buried secrets surface, revealing a shared history of betrayal and infidelity. What unfolds is a haunting exploration of guilt, emotional abandonment and the human conscience, underscoring the painful truth that remorse often comes too late.

Speaking about the enduring relevance of Badal Sircar's work and the universal appeal of regional cinema, Director Sekhar Das underscored the power of authentic storytelling to transcend linguistic and geographical boundaries. "Art does not have any borders; it only has roots. When a story is deeply rooted in human conscience and emotional truth, it speaks to audiences everywhere, regardless of language," he remarked.

Gargee RoyChowdhury reflected on the emotional intricacies of portraying a character whose presence becomes both a mirror to human frailty and a catalyst for moral awakening. Her role, she highlighted, demanded a delicate engagement with the film's layered emotional landscape.

Producer Dr. Prabir Bhaumik emphasized the significance of supporting literary and theatrical adaptations, noting their vital contribution to preserving India's rich artistic and dramatic heritage while introducing timeless works to contemporary cinematic audiences.

 

Ohh My Dog: Celebrating the Extraordinary Bond of Unconditional Love and Loyalty

Moving from the complexities of human relationships to the extraordinary purity of the human-animal bond, acclaimed filmmaker Amit Rai presented his Hindi feature ‘Ohh My Dog’, a heartwarming yet emotionally charged narrative celebrating empathy, courage, resilience and unconditional affection.

Amit Rai, known for acclaimed films such as Road to Sangam, I-pad and OMG 2, brings together two parallel journeys across India. In Assam, 14-year-old Apu embarks on a desperate quest to rescue his kidnapped dog, Momo, while in Bihar, Oscar, a fiercely loyal dog, sets out to find his kidnapped 15-year-old owner, Prince. Separated by distance but united by an unbreakable bond, their journeys unfold into a heartwarming tale of courage, resilience and unconditional love, celebrating the extraordinary power of devotion to transcend all boundaries.

Sharing the inspiration behind the film's dual narrative, Director Amit Rai spoke about the remarkable emotional honesty of animals and their ability to transcend the prejudices and conditions that often complicate human relationships. "Animals do not carry the burden of prejudice or conditional affection; their loyalty is absolute. Through these parallel journeys, I wanted audiences to experience how empathy and devotion can bridge any distance and overcome every fear," he said.

The Press Conference was moderated by Shri Mahesh Kumar.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat - NSS Records Over 73,500 Participations Across the Nation During Week 10 of ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ Campaign
More than 28,300 individuals take Nasha Mukt pledge; 17,699 youth participate in 366 sporting tournaments
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 8:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through the Directorate of MY Bharat - National Service Scheme, organised Cluster of Block Level Sports Meets and awareness activities during Week 10 of the 100-Week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’, recording 73,529 total participations across 162 participating institutions. The activities included 366 sporting tournaments involving 17,699 participants, 200 pledge ceremonies in which 28,360 individuals took the Nasha Mukt Sankalp and 1,006 grassroots activities. Female participants accounted for nearly 49 per cent of the gender-disaggregated entries.

Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on August 2, 2026, the campaign is built around four core pillars: Prevent, Protect, Recover and Lead. Week 10 activities were organised under the Month 3 theme, ‘Strong Communities, Healthy Youth (Gram Seva & Sangathan)’, with a focus on promoting fitness, teamwork, community participation and awareness about substance abuse. The programme covered block-level sports grounds, district stadiums, university and college campuses and Gram Panchayat venues, with participation from 162 institutions across the Nation.

Of the 73,529 total participations recorded, 73,436 were gender-disaggregated entries, comprising 37,471 male and 35,965 female participants. A total of 28,360 individuals, including 14,275 male and 14,085 female participants, took the Nasha Mukt Sankalp during 200 oath ceremonies. Meanwhile, 17,699 athletes, including 9,188 male and 8,511 female participants, competed in sporting tournaments. Female participation accounted for 48.1 per cent of sports competitors and 49.7 per cent of oath participants. Dedicated races for Children With Special Needs (CWSN) were also organised by participating units, including GMSSS-46 in Chandigarh.

In terms of regional participation, Bhopal recorded the highest turnout with 10,403 participations, followed by Chennai with 9,175, Bangalore with 8,478, Chandigarh with 7,992 and Delhi with 7,384. Other regions reporting substantial participation included Hyderabad (5,660), Guwahati (5,490), Jaipur (4,681), Pune (4,027), Kolkata (3,752), Lucknow (2,885), Trivandrum (2,251) and Bhubaneswar (1,351).

The Cluster of Block Level Sports Meets brought together university campuses, affiliated colleges, NSS units and local youth clubs. Competitions were organised in Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Volleyball, Athletics, Football, Badminton, Basketball, Cricket, Tug-of-War, Chess, Carrom and traditional indigenous games such as Pittu, Gilli Danda and Satoliya. Dedicated competitive categories for female athletes were organised across participating centres.

The sporting events were complemented by awareness activities, including street plays, rallies, walkathons, quizzes, declamation contests and poster and essay competitions. A total of 181 awareness kiosks and stalls were set up across 49 kiosk events, engaging 4,441 individuals. These stalls, organised in coordination with local medical authorities and youth organisations, disseminated Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials on substance abuse risks, counselling services and the National De-Addiction Helpline (14446).

NSS volunteers also staged 142 street plays (Nukkad Nataks), musical performances and slogan-writing sessions, engaging 9,194 youth and spectators. Another 249 activities, including anti-drug rallies, drug-free youth walkathons, declamation contests, quizzes and poster and essay competitions, mobilised 13,835 participants.

To strengthen community engagement, 108 institutions invited Guests of Honour and subject experts from district administrations, police departments, narcotics and civil excise departments, medical institutions, universities, Panchayati Raj institutions and non-governmental organisations. These included District Administrators, Police Superintendents, medical professionals, University Vice-Chancellors, College Principals, Panchayat Sarpanches and recovery advocates associated with Alcoholics Anonymous and partner NGOs.

Youth volunteers also used digital platforms to amplify the campaign's message, uploading 1,137 Instagram reels and more than 1,278 social media posts using the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva.

*****

Gaurav Saini

(Release ID: 2340577)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat Mobilises Over 95,000 Participants Across 36 States/UTs During Week 10 of ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ Campaign
440 programmes organised, including 322 Cluster of Blocks Level Sports Meets and 118 Neighbourhood Youth Parliament sessions
Campaign combines grassroots sports, traditional games and youth-led discussions to promote awareness against substance abuse
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The tenth week of the 100-week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan’ witnessed participation of 95,147 youth and citizens across 36 States and Union Territories through 440 programmes organised by MY Bharat. The activities included 322 Cluster of Blocks Level Sports Meets and 118 ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Par Paricharcha’ (Neighbourhood Youth Parliament) sessions, as per the provisional report dated 22 November 2026.

 

The Cluster of Blocks Level Sports Meets, organised on 21 and 22 November 2026, brought together youth from multiple blocks and villages for sporting competitions, traditional games and other sports activities. The initiative aimed to promote physical fitness, teamwork, discipline and sportsmanship while connecting grassroots communities with district-level sporting opportunities and providing talented young participants a platform for recognition.

A total of 322 sports programmes were organised, witnessing participation of 81,489 youth and citizens across 1,053 activities. Prominent participation was reported from Uttarakhand, Ernakulam in Kerala, Tirap and Kra Daadi in Arunachal Pradesh, Shopian and Samba in Jammu and Kashmir and Gopalganj in Bihar.

Alongside the sporting activities, ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Par Paricharcha’ (Neighbourhood Youth Parliament) sessions were organised at the block level on 21 November 2026. With a minimum participation target of 80 youth per block, each NYP featured four structured sessions covering an introduction to the MY Bharat Portal; Understanding Substance Abuse: Challenges before India’s Youth; From Awareness to Action: Tools for a Nasha Mukt Yuva; and an audio-visual presentation on Stories of Change: The Journey Towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The 118 Neighbourhood Youth Parliament programmes recorded participation of 13,658 youth across 360 activities. The sessions provided a platform for young people to discuss the challenges posed by substance abuse, preventive measures and their role in promoting a drug-free society.

Partner organisations, including Brahma Kumaris and Heartfulness, supported the campaign activities. Heartfulness also extended support to sporting events, including badminton competitions organised at Pune.

The campaign also witnessed collaborations at the local level. MY Bharat Meerut organised a Neighbourhood Youth Parliament at Shobhit University, Meerut, in the presence of Dr. Laxmikant Bajpayee, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha. In Kupwara, MY Bharat, in coordination with the Indian Army, Keran Bowl and Khatana Action Club, jointly organised a session at Kundian in Keran Block. Other notable initiatives included programmes at Chaibasa Engineering College in Jhinkpani Block, Jharkhand, and Garudeshwar in Narmada district, Gujarat.

By bringing together grassroots sporting competitions and structured youth-led discussions, MY Bharat is combining community participation with awareness-building efforts to promote healthy lifestyles and strengthen the campaign against substance abuse.

*****

Gaurav Saini

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of 60,693 Citizens
Quiz Remains Open for Participation Until November 25, 2026
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Reaches Over 35.96 Crore People, Including 14.39 Crore Youth and 11.37 Crore Women
Over 34.36 Lakh Activities Conducted in Educational Institutions; 39.91 Lakh Persons Treated and Rehabilitated Through More Than 755 DoSJE-Supported De-addiction Centres
Over 50.19 Lakh Nasha Mukt Pledges Taken; More Than 2 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras Registered
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi

The online ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’, organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), has witnessed encouraging participation from citizens across the country.

The quiz recorded participation of 60,693 citizens as per the latest officially reported figures available as of November 23, 2026. The initiative seeks to strengthen public awareness about the harmful effects of substance use and encourage citizens, particularly young people, to actively contribute towards building a drug-free India.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the quiz launched on October 26, 2026,  is being conducted through the MY Bharat portal and will remain open for participation until November 25, 2026.

He said the citizens, especially youth, are encouraged to participate in this nationwide awareness initiative and become active contributors to the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

MY Bharat Quiz QR

The Official said the interested participants can access the quiz through the Participation Link: https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/detail/Url9dlIwCinQVSf8lwPB9w/

The quiz comprises 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), which participants are required to answer within 10 minutes.

The Official said a participation certificate is generated for every participant who successfully submits the quiz while participants can also view the correct answers upon completion, enabling them to enhance their understanding of substance use prevention.

Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan aims to strengthen drug demand reduction efforts through preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and community participation, he said.

He said initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has subsequently expanded its coverage to all districts across the country, emerging as a nationwide people's movement against substance use.

The Official said the Abhiyaan has reached over 35.96 crore people, including 14.39 crore youth and 11.37 crore women, reflecting the extensive outreach and growing public engagement in the campaign.

Under the Abhiyaan, more than 34.36 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions to promote awareness and encourage informed choices among students and young people, he said.

Furthermore, 39.91 lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated through a network of more than 755 Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE)-supported De-Addiction Centres operating across the country, the Official said.

NMBA Mobile App

The Official remarked that community participation continues to be a key pillar of the Abhiyaan.

More than 50.19 lakh Nasha Mukt pledges have been taken by citizens, while over 2 lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras have registered to support awareness generation, community mobilisation and preventive initiatives at the grassroots level, he said.

The Official noted that as the Abhiyaan progresses through its seventh year, the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ seeks to deepen public understanding of the harmful consequences of substance use, promote informed decision-making and encourage young people to become ambassadors of awareness and prevention.

The initiative reinforces the vision of a healthy, empowered and drug-free society as an essential foundation for achieving Viksit Bharat, he said.

 

 

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration QR Code

Through this digital initiative, the Ministry aims to strengthen community participation, encourage responsible choices and mobilise citizens, particularly youth, to contribute meaningfully to the nationwide movement against substance use, the Official remarked.

NMBA e-pledge QR Code

The Official appealed all citizens, especially young people, to participate in the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ before November 25, 2026, and join the collective endeavour of building a healthier, stronger and drug-free India.

***

PR-244-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Feeling” Before Story: Aquí and The Huntress Carry Human Emotions Across Borders at IFFI 2026
Directors Tiago Guedes and Suzanne Andrews Correa discuss films that explore human relationships, emotions and the pursuit of justice
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 7:32PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 23 November 2026

 

Two very different films at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa have one thing in common: both aim to make the audience feel before they understand, placing human emotions at the centre of storytelling. Filmmakers Tiago Guedes and Suzanne Andrews Correa addressed the press during the festival today, sharing insights into their respective films, Aquí and The Huntress (La Cazadora).

Aquí, directed by Tiago Guedes, is a dystopian drama adapted from J. M. Coetzee’s Jesus trilogy, screening in the International Competition section. The Huntress (La Cazadora), the debut feature of Mexican-American filmmaker Suzanne Andrews Correa, is a Spanish-language drama thriller inspired by real-life violence against women in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.

Aquí: A Family Built on Choice

Aquí, a 2026 film that premiered at the Cannes Film Festival on 18th May 2026, is being screened in the International Competition at IFFI 2026, being held from November 20th to 28th in Goa. Adapted into a single film from Coetzee’s Jesus trilogy, it is set in a society where people begin their lives with no memory of the past, memories are erased and conformity is enforced.

The story follows Simón, who takes in a young boy named David, whom he meets on the journey to this new world. Believing the boy needs a mother, Simón seeks out Inés, who agrees, and the three slowly form an unconventional family. But a society that expects everyone to follow its rules cannot easily accept David, who refuses to fit in. Through his imagination and his desire for freedom, he challenges the world around him. Simón and Inés realise that raising a child is an uncertain journey, full of questions and without easy answers.

Director Tiago Guedes said the film seeks to explore what it means to be human, raising philosophical questions that he believes everyone should reflect upon. On adapting Coetzee’s books, he explained that while reading them, he focussed more on the feelings the story evoked than on the plot itself. This, he said, helps the intensity of the book’s essence reach the screen as a visual experience.

Guedes also explores the idea that family is not always defined by blood relations, but by choices made through a deeply human experience, without turning to religion or gods. The title, which means ‘Here’ in Spanish and Portuguese, reflects this too. As the characters make their choices, the camera subtly shifts from wider to tighter shots, drawing the audience closer to understanding them. Guedes also leaves silences and some ambiguity in the film, so that viewers can form their own interpretations of the story. Aquí is scheduled to be screened in Portugal, Spain and France in January.

The Huntress: A Cry for Justice

The Huntress (La Cazadora) is a 2026 Spanish-language drama thriller written and directed by Suzanne Andrews Correa. Adriana Paz stars as a factory worker and assault survivor in Ciudad Juárez, who turns to vigilante justice. The film draws upon the real-life incidents of violence against women and the 2013 case of “Diana, Hunter of the Bus Drivers”, an unidentified vigilante who fatally shot bus drivers amid widespread impunity.

Set in the border region between Mexico and Texas, the film portrays the experiences of women working in factories who faced sexual violence and exploitation. The story unfolds over 24 hours, focusing on the protagonist's experiences and her pursuit of justice.

Correa said her objective was to give viewers a sensory experience of the protagonist’s powerlessness and desperation, so that they can empathise with why she took justice and revenge into her own hands when calls for help went unanswered. The film is also a call for change towards justice and against the crimes against women that continue to prevail.

Correa said the film took her ten years to make, alongside other projects. The journey showed her that filmmaking combines persistence and dedication with the vision to “stay with the story”, and with finding ways to communicate well with the crew, the actors and the audience. Like Guedes, she said her intention was to communicate “feeling” to the audience, rather than focus solely on the story. Although she had initially worried that the story might not appeal to international audiences without the real-life context, but she was both saddened and humbled to see the protagonist’s fear and emotions resonate with audiences across cultures and borders.

The session was moderated by Ms. Sriyanka Chatterjee.

Stories Without Borders

Though one is set in an imagined world without memory and the other in a very real border city, Aquí and The Huntress meet at the same place: they speak to the heart before the mind. Both directors chose to place feeling ahead of plot, and both use that feeling to ask difficult questions, about human relationships, the meaning of family, personal freedom and the pursuit of justice. Their films illustrate how stories rooted in specific cultural and social contexts can connect with audiences across languages and borders, reflecting the spirit of this year's IFFI theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoSJE Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Cumulative Sales of Approximately ₹1.16 Crore As on Nov 22, 2026
Strong Consumer Response Highlights Growing Demand for Indigenous Products and Traditional Craftsmanship
Aligned with guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’, of Hon'ble PM Shri Narendra Modi
Trade Fair To Conclude On November 27, 2026
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The pavilion of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in the National Capital here, has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹1.16 Crore as of November 22, 2026, reflecting an encouraging response from visitors and growing appreciation for indigenous products and traditional craftsmanship.

 

The visitors are exploring its pavilion thereby supporting the artisans by purchasing their indigenous and handcrafted products.

Located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, the Ministry's pavilion showcases India's diverse cultural heritage, traditional skills and indigenous craftsmanship. It offers visitors an opportunity to explore a wide range of authentic handcrafted products while contributing to the economic empowerment of artisans through direct purchases.

 

The impressive sales performance highlights the increasing consumer interest in India's rich artistic traditions, handcrafted products and the entrepreneurial capabilities of artisans from diverse communities.

The pavilion continues to provide a significant platform for artisans to showcase their products, connect directly with consumers and expand their market reach. The Trade Fair will conclude on November 27, 2026.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said that more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the fair through the Ministry's three Apex Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).


He said the participation of these Apex Corporations reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

The Official said these efforts are aligned with the vision of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi under his guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas , Sabka Prayas’.

He said the pavilion features an extensive collection of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products. These products represent the distinctive artistic identities, traditional skills and cultural diversity of different regions across the country, he added.

Expressing satisfaction, the Official said the participation in a prestigious national-level platform such as IITF enables artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand changing consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities. He said it also provides an opportunity to strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities and build sustainable business prospects.

 

A significant highlight of the Ministry's participation is the promotion of TULIP (Traditional Artisans' Upliftment Livelihood Programme), which aims to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among consumers, he added.

Through the TULIP initiative, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation, strengthen entrepreneurial capabilities and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, the Official said.

The Official said the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, brings together producers, entrepreneurs, traders and consumers from across the country and abroad, providing a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Reimagining the Superhero: Ayan Mukerji and Basil Joseph Converse on Crafting Culturally Rooted Worlds
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 7:00PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 23 November 2026

 

The extraordinary possibilities of mythology, superheroes and fantastical worlds, rooted in India's rich cultural heritage, took centre stage at an engaging In-conversation session titled ‘The Epic Genres – Mythologies, Superheroes & New Worlds’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Filmmakers Ayan Mukerji and Basil Joseph, in a conversation moderated by Puja Talwar, explored the creative challenges of bringing superheroes and mythological narratives to the screen, the influence of Indian folklore and spirituality, and the evolving role of technology in cinematic storytelling.

Speaking about the challenges of making superhero films in India, Basil Joseph observed that Indian cinema has traditionally portrayed its leading men as larger-than-life figures, often possessing qualities associated with superheroes. This makes creating a distinct superhero cinematic universe particularly challenging. Reflecting on his film Minnal Murali, he explained how creative challenges, and budgetary constraints too, can inspire inventive storytelling. Scenes featuring a superhero running with a lungi covering his face and wearing chappals in the movie Minnal Murali emerged from such considerations.

Ayan Mukerji shared that the idea of extraordinary powers residing within ordinary people was what initially attracted him to the superhero genre. Discussing the challenge of creating an Indian identity for films that draw inspiration from Western fantasy, he acknowledged that Brahmastra initially carried certain Western influences, partly because of his admiration for stories such as Harry Potter. However, incorporating elements of spirituality into the writing helped give the film its distinct Indian identity.

Emphasising the importance of authenticity in filmmaking, Basil Joseph said that filmmakers must remain true to their characters and themselves rather than attempting to make their films appear artificial. He stressed that simplicity and creative honesty are essential, adding that one should never compromise one's own identity in the pursuit of making a film look ‘cool’.

Recalling the making of Brahmastra, Ayan Mukerji described the film as a logistically challenging undertaking. He noted that working within restrictions often pushes filmmakers to think beyond conventional approaches and discover more imaginative solutions. Creative challenges, he observed, can become catalysts for innovation rather than obstacles.

The conversation also explored India's deep-rooted relationship with mythology and folklore. Basil Joseph observed that Indian audiences have grown up listening to stories of divine beings and extraordinary powers. Unlike the West, where mythological superheroes are relatively less pervasive in popular storytelling, India has a vast tradition of divine figures who appear to protect and rescue people in times of distress. With an immense reservoir of mythological and folkloric references, filmmakers naturally draw upon stories and experiences absorbed during childhood while creating cinematic worlds.

Ayan Mukerji highlighted how technological advancements have expanded the possibilities of visual storytelling, enabling filmmakers to bring ambitious narratives and fantastical worlds to life. He noted that mythology has always been a constant presence in Indian storytelling, with technology now providing new avenues to present these age-old narratives to contemporary audiences.

Sharing his perspective on the future of filmmaking in the age of Artificial Intelligence, Basil Joseph observed that AI primarily reproduces existing content rather than creating something truly original. He underlined that originality would become increasingly valuable in an era where technology can replicate creative material with ease.

The speakers also discussed how the growth of OTT platforms has transformed the reach of Indian cinema. Basil Joseph pointed out that films made in one language are now finding appreciation across different regions of the country, with audiences able to experience them in their own languages. This growing accessibility, he noted, has opened new avenues for regional cinema to connect with audiences beyond linguistic boundaries.

The conversation offered valuable insights into the evolving landscape of Indian films in the genre, highlighting how technological possibilities, creative ingenuity and an enduring connection with indigenous mythology can come together to create cinematic worlds that are both imaginative and distinctly Indian.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRIME MINISTER OF NEPAL CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT OF INDIA
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister of Nepal, Rt. Hon’ble Mr. Balendra Shah, called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 23, 2026).

Welcoming Prime Minister Shah to Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President congratulated him on the strong mandate for his government in the March 2026 elections, and wished him success in his efforts to fulfill the aspirations of the people.

The President expressed her condolences for the loss of life caused by the Bhotekoshi floods. She said that as always, in this difficult time, India has stood by Nepal, providing prompt humanitarian assistance and technical support, and will continue to do so as a close partner in the recovery and reconstruction efforts.

The President underlined that climate change is a shared challenge for both our nations, and we must work together to strengthen early warning systems and disaster management.

The President said that the unique and multi-faceted India-Nepal relations are based on our shared civilizational heritage and the deep cherished bonds between the people of the two countries.

She said that the Joint Vision document announced during this visit reflects the aspirations of the people of both our nations, especially the youth. She expressed confidence that it will provide a clear direction for our future cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, development partnership, connectivity, cultural and people to people exchanges, as well as in new and emerging sectors such as start-ups, digital services, space and innovation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal amends Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 and extends accreditation period of Accredited Prospecting Agencies and Mining Plan Preparing Agencies from three to five years
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal has notified the Mineral Concession (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026 vide G.S.R. 999(E) dated 17 November 2026. Subsequently, the accreditation cycle has been extended from three to five years for Accredited Prospecting Agencies (APA) and Mining Plan Preparing Agencies (MPPA).

The reform will reduce the number of periodic assessments and re-accreditations, thereby saving the time of accredited agencies on repetitive assessment and accreditation. The longer validity of accreditation will ensure continuity in the preparation of geological reports and mining plans, which are prerequisites for operationalization of coal and lignite blocks.

This reform is a significant step towards Ease of Doing Business and trust-based governance in the coal sector.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal issues Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Coal has issued the “Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026” on 20 November 2026. The Guidelines shall come into force 30 days from the date of its issue. The Guidelines provide an outcome-oriented framework for systematic and scientific mine planning and mine closure. It complements the existing statutory framework and avoids redundancy in compliance requirements covered under other statutory provisions.

Under the Guidelines, defined timelines have been laid down at different stages of scrutiny and approval, ensuring a time-bound decision-making process. The timeline for reimbursement from the escrow account for mine closure works has been reduced to one month from the receipt of claim, with provision for test-check of claims. In addition, the ambit of agencies for verification of five-yearly claims for withdrawal from the escrow account has been widened.

Keeping pace with emerging technologies, the Guidelines recognize Underground Coal Gasification as a mining method, and the “Guidelines for preparation and approval of Mining Plan for Coal and Lignite Blocks/Mines for Underground Gasification 2026” have been made an integral part of these Guidelines. Project proponents have also been given greater flexibility in line with prevailing conditions, enabling faster operationalization of mines.

The Guidelines are expected to improve Ease of Doing Business through simpler, practical and time-bound processes, and to accelerate the operationalization of mines, supporting the country’s energy security. It provides a clear and focused regulatory framework, while promoting scientific mine closure and repurposing for the benefit of local communities.

***

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF PRAKASH PARV OF GURU NANAK DEV JI
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu sends greetings to her fellow citizens on the eve of Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

In a message, the President has said, “On the occasion of Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, I extend my warm greetings and best wishes to all Indians living in India and abroad.

The message of ‘Ik Onkar’ given by Guru Nanak Dev Ji is, in essence, a message of the unity of all humanity. He emphasised the need to build a society free from caste distinctions, social hierarchies and discrimination. He taught that love, compassion and service to humanity should form the foundation of our lives.

The principles of ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhako’ hold a special place in his teachings. He encouraged people to remember the Almighty, earn their livelihood through honest and diligent work and share their earnings with others. Through the tradition of Langar, he demonstrated the values of social equality, fraternity and selfless service in practice.

On this sacred occasion, let us resolve to follow the teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and contribute to the welfare of society and the nation by upholding the values of service, equality and harmony”.

 

***

MJPS/SS/PRK
