item.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Lauds India’s Achievement of Administering Over 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months
item.category: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Lauds India’s Achievement of Administering Over 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months Prime Minister Describes the Achievement as a Significant Milestone in India’s Journey Towards Strengthening Preventive Healthcare and Protecting Adolescent Girls Against Cervical Cancer Hon’ble Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Appreciates the Collective Efforts of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, State Governments and Healthcare Professionals Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Lauds India’s Achievement of Administering Over 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months
Prime Minister Describes the Achievement as a Significant Milestone in India’s Journey Towards Strengthening Preventive Healthcare and Protecting Adolescent Girls Against Cervical Cancer
Hon’ble Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Appreciates the Collective Efforts of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, State Governments and Healthcare Professionals
Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda Highlights Prime Minister’s Vision and Leadership in Advancing HPV Vaccination and Building a Healthier, Viksit Bharat
WHO South-East Asia Region Congratulates India on Administering 10 Million HPV Vaccine Doses, Recognises Collective Efforts to Protect Girls Against Cervical Cancer
Campaign Achieves Nearly 87% Coverage of Annual Target Cohort of Approximately 1.2 Crore 14-Year-Old Girls
Six States Achieve 100% Coverage of Identified Target Populations; 12 States Cross 80% Coverage
Uttar Pradesh Leads with Over 29.33 Lakh Girls Vaccinated, Followed by Bihar with Over 13.70 Lakh and Gujarat with Over 7.75 Lakh
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:44PM by PIB Delhi

India’s sustained efforts to strengthen preventive healthcare and protect the health of its daughters have reached an important milestone, with Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi lauding the achievement of administering over 1 crore doses of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign. The achievement marks a significant step towards protecting adolescent girls against HPV infections that can cause cervical cancer and reflects the growing reach of preventive healthcare services across the country.

In his message, the Prime Minister described the achievement as a significant milestone in India’s journey towards preventive healthcare. He noted that every dose is a step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer and ensuring a healthier future for them and commended all stakeholders whose efforts contributed to this achievement.

A significant milestone in our journey towards preventive healthcare. Every dose is a step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer and ensuring a healthier future for them. I commend all the stakeholders whose efforts have ensured this remarkable feat.

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 23, 2026

Hon’ble Vice-President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan has also appreciated the achievement of administering over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in less than nine months, describing it as a significant milestone in the fight against cervical cancer. He appreciated the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, State Governments and healthcare professionals involved in the successful implementation of the nationwide campaign. The Vice-President also acknowledged the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the Government’s continued commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare, protecting adolescent girls and building a healthier future for generations of women.

India’s achievement of administering over 1 crore doses of the HPV vaccine in less than 9 months is a significant milestone in the fight against cervical cancer. I appreciate the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the State Governments and all healthcare professionals involved in the successful implementation of this nationwide campaign. Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, this remarkable progress reflects the Government’s continued commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare, protecting adolescent girls and building a healthier future for generations of women. A significant step towards a healthier India! @MoHFW_INDIA

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 22, 2026

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda expressed gratitude to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for his visionary leadership and unwavering commitment to preventive healthcare. He remarked that the Prime Minister’s vision and leadership continue to inspire the achievement of meaningful milestones, step by step, towards building a healthier and Viksit Bharat. Highlighting the achievement of administering over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses, Shri Nadda said that it marks a significant step towards safeguarding India’s daughters against cervical cancer. He reaffirmed the commitment to ensuring that this vital protection reaches every eligible girl across the country, advancing the collective resolve to build a healthier and stronger India.

Grateful to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji for his visionary leadership and unwavering commitment to preventive healthcare. His vision and leadership continue to inspire us to achieve meaningful milestones, step by step, towards building a healthier and Viksit Bharat. The achievement of 1 crore HPV vaccine doses marks a significant step towards safeguarding India’s daughters against cervical cancer. We remain firmly committed to ensuring that this vital protection reaches every eligible girl across the country, advancing our collective resolve for a healthier and stronger India.

— Jagat Prakash Nadda (@JPNadda) November 23, 2026

The World Health Organization (WHO) South-East Asia Region has also acknowledged India’s achievement of administering over 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls, describing it as a significant milestone in efforts to prevent cervical cancer. WHO-SEARO recognised the collective commitment of the Government, healthcare workers, communities, parents and partners in achieving this progress. It highlighted the importance of ensuring that every girl has access to the protection offered by HPV vaccination, as part of efforts to protect girls against cervical cancer.

.@WHO congratulates #India 🇮🇳 on administering over 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls – a significant milestone in efforts to prevent cervical cancer. This achievement reflects the collective commitment of the Government, health workers, communities, parents and partners to protect girls from #cervicalcancer and ensure that every girl has access to the protection offered by #HPV vaccination. #VaccinesSaveLives

— World Health Organization South-East Asia (@WHOSEARO) November 23, 2026

 

National HPV Vaccination Campaign: Progress and Coverage

Launched by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in February 2026, the National HPV Vaccination Campaign provides free, safe and voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination, with parental consent, to 14-year-old girls at designated Government health facilities. In less than nine months, over 1 crore doses have been administered, achieving nearly 87% coverage of the annual target cohort of approximately 1.2 crore girls.

State-wise Progress in HPV Vaccination

Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations. Twelve States have crossed 80% coverage.

Assam has recorded 95.63% coverage, Telangana 95.28%, Karnataka 93.16%, Uttarakhand 90.17%, Chhattisgarh 86.21% and Rajasthan 85.23%. Kerala has recorded 77.02%, Tamil Nadu 76.12% and Odisha 74.90%. The Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu has recorded 72.99%.

In terms of the number of girls vaccinated, Uttar Pradesh leads with over 29.33 lakh, followed by Bihar with over 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with over 7.75 lakh. States have adopted locally tailored approaches to extend vaccination services across rural, urban, remote and geographically challenging areas. State-led initiatives in Bihar, Tamil Nadu and Sikkim have also been integrated with the national campaign.

Centre-State Coordination and Community Engagement

The campaign is being implemented through coordination between the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, State and Union Territory Governments, district administrations and healthcare teams. Paediatricians, gynaecologists and specialists from premier medical institutions such as AIIMS have supported awareness efforts through credible, science-based information. Teachers, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs) and other frontline workers have engaged with parents and communities to address concerns and encourage informed participation.

U-WIN Supports Digital Monitoring and Access to Vaccination

The U-WIN platform enables real-time monitoring, beneficiary tracking and digital vaccination records. It helps programme managers monitor district-level progress, identify coverage gaps and eligible girls yet to be vaccinated, and support planning and resource allocation. Parents can also use the platform to book HPV vaccination slots for their daughters and download digital vaccination certificates.

HPV Vaccination: An Important Preventive Intervention Against Cervical Cancer

Persistent infection with certain high-risk types of Human Papillomavirus is responsible for the vast majority of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination is among the most effective preventive interventions against such infections. More than 800 million HPV vaccine doses have been administered worldwide, while nearly two decades of research and real-world experience demonstrate strong protection against vaccine-targeted HPV infections and associated precancerous conditions. Vaccination at the age of 14 years aims to provide protection well before potential exposure to HPV.

Beneficiary Safety Remains a Central Priority

Vaccination sessions are conducted at designated Government health facilities under the direct supervision of trained Medical Officers. Sites are linked to 24×7 healthcare centres for prompt assessment, monitoring and management of any rare Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI). Established safety protocols, trained personnel and appropriate medical arrangements support the safe conduct of vaccination sessions. The Ministry continues to emphasise transparent communication, scientific evidence and informed parental consent.

Sustaining Momentum Towards Reaching Every Eligible Girl

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will continue working with State Governments, district administrations, medical professionals, frontline healthcare workers, educational institutions and communities to address coverage gaps and reach all eligible girls. Parents and guardians can visit their nearest designated Government health facility or access the U-WIN platform for information and vaccination slot booking.

The achievement of administering over 1 crore HPV vaccine doses in less than nine months marks important progress in India's efforts to protect adolescent girls against cervical cancer. The National HPV Vaccination Campaign reflects the Government's continued commitment to strengthening preventive healthcare and ensuring that every eligible girl has access to this vital protection.

President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S MESSAGE ON THE EVE OF ‘MARTYRDOM DAY’ OF GURU TEGH BAHADUR JI
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu in her message on the eve of ‘Martyrdom Day’ of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji says:- 

 “On the occasion of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji’s Martyrdom Day, I pay my humble tribute to him. 

The life of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji is a unique example of spiritual devotion, sacrifice, compassion and indomitable courage. He always upheld the values of truth, justice and humanity. When the religious freedom of people came under threat, he laid down his life in defence of their rights. His supreme sacrifice stands as a symbol of human dignity and respect for the rights of others. 

His life will continue to inspire us to stand fearlessly against injustice, respect all religions and promote love, fraternity and harmony in society. 

Let us resolve to imbibe his ideals and work towards building a society founded on the principles of freedom, equality and mutual respect”.

 

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Tamil movie ‘Koodu’ Explores Environmental Conservation and Community Responsibility at 57th IFFI
Director Joyal Vijay Highlights the Importance of Coexistence, Saying Earth Belongs to all Living Beings, not Humans Alone
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:42PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 23 November 2026

 

Director Joyal Vijay, along with producers Rajesh Menon and Ganesh M, and actor V. Jayaprakash, interacted with the media at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today. The team shared insights into their film Koodu (Nest), its inspiration and its underlying environmental message.

Set in Vachathi, Tamil Nadu, the film unfolds when a power outage leads to the discovery of a sparrow's nest containing eggs inside a village transformer. Guided by village head Agathiyan, agriculture graduate Kathir and the villagers decide to go without electricity for 35 days to protect the birds. However, their decision faces strong opposition. Despite these challenges, Kathir and the villagers make considerable sacrifices to ensure the nest remains safe.

Through the film, director Joyal Vijay sought to convey that the earth does not belong to human beings alone but is also home to countless other living creatures. Emphasising the importance of coexistence, he said that humans must recognise their responsibility to respect, protect and live in harmony with other forms of life.

Actor V. Jayaprakash shared how being part of the film influenced his personal habits. He said he agreed to the project within minutes of hearing its synopsis, particularly drawn by the fact that it was based on a real-life incident. Reflecting on the film's environmental message, he said his biggest personal takeaway was becoming more conscious of his use of tissue paper, recognising the connection between everyday consumption and the cutting down of trees. He added that the film had encouraged him to minimise its use in his daily life, highlighting how its message had influenced his personal habits.

Producer Rajesh Menon highlighted the emotional appeal of the story and the screenplay's engaging approach to communicating its environmental message. He noted that the film addresses the practical questions and challenges that arise from the villagers' decision to remain without electricity for 35 days, using meaningful dialogues and relatable situations rather than presenting the subject in an overly serious manner. He also said that the film's underlying message and relevance to audiences motivated them to support the project.

The press conference was moderated by Praveen Kumar S.

Watch the full press conference here

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Manual Sewer Cleaning to Robotic Sanitation Operations
NAMASTE Training Supports a Safer and More Dignified Occupational Transition
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

Transitioning sanitation workers from hazardous manual cleaning to mechanised sanitation operations is an important step towards improving occupational safety, health and dignity. Training and access to technology can help workers build technical skills and undertake sanitation work in safer conditions.

Raja (Name Changed), a 41-year-old Scheduled Caste sanitation worker from Mysuru, Karnataka, spent nearly 15 years engaged in manual sewer and septic tank cleaning, with prolonged direct exposure to hazardous waste. Inadequate access to machinery and training, along with the health challenges associated with toxic exposure, affected his physical well-being. With limited education and his family dependent on his income, opportunities to move to safer work remained constrained.

With an interest in mechanised sanitation operations, he received Occupational Safety and Mechanised Sanitation Training under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme in 2026, as part of a batch of 45 sanitation workers. The training covered occupational health hazards, safe work practices and operation of the Bandicoot robotic sanitation system.

Following the training, Rajagopala is now working as a Bandicoot robotic sanitation system operator, marking a significant shift from manual sewer cleaning to machine-based sanitation operations. His new role enables him to undertake sanitation work with reduced direct exposure to hazardous waste and in a safer, more dignified environment.

His journey highlights how occupational safety training and mechanised equipment under the NAMASTE Scheme can support sanitation workers in acquiring technical skills, improving work conditions and moving towards safer and dignified livelihoods.

***

SS-194-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Press statement by Prime Minister during Joint Press Statement with Prime Minister of Nepal
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, प्रधानमंत्री बालेन्द्र शाह जी,
दोनों देशों के delegates,
मीडिया के साथियों,
नमस्कार!

नेपाल के प्रधानमंत्री बनने के बाद, अपनी पहली bilateral विज़िट पर बालेन्द्र शाह जी का भारत में स्वागत करते हुए मुझे बहुत खुशी हो रही है।

कुछ महीने पहले, जब उन्होंने विश्व के सबसे युवा प्रधानमंत्री के रूप में UN को संबोधित किया था, तब हमें उनकी दूरदर्शिता की स्पष्ट झलक दिखाई दी थी। और आज, पिछले कुछ घंटों की बातचीत में, मैंने नेपाल के भविष्य और भारत-नेपाल संबंधों के लिए उनके clear vision और commitment को महसूस किया है। इस वर्ष नेपाल की जनता ने उन्हें जो ऐतिहासिक जनादेश दिया है, वह नेपाल की नई पीढ़ी की आकांक्षाओं और उम्मीदों को दर्शाता है।

भारत एक सशक्त और समृद्ध नेपाल की विकास यात्रा में हमेशा से सहभागी रहा है। इसी भावना से आज हमने अपने संबंधों को नई ऊँचाइयों पर ले जाने के लिए कई महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिए हैं।

Friends,

भारत और नेपाल का रिश्ता केवल पड़ोस का नहीं, बल्कि अपनेपन और अटूट विश्वास का रिश्ता है। हमारी खुशियाँ साझी हैं, और हमारी चुनौतियाँ भी। हम एक-दूसरे की प्रगति में साथी हैं, और मुश्किल समय में एक-दूसरे का सहारा भी।

अगस्त में नेपाल में आई भीषण बाढ़ से हुई जनहानि के लिए हम गहरी संवेदना व्यक्त करते हैं। और आज, नेपाल के पुनर्निर्माण और दीर्घकालिक विकास को नई मजबूती देने के लिए हम चौबीस हजार करोड़ नेपाली रुपये के Development Cooperation Package की घोषणा करते हैं।

हमारा संकल्प होगा कि प्रभावित परिवारों का जीवन फिर पटरी पर लौटे, नए अवसर पैदा हों, और भविष्य की आपदाओं से निपटने के लिए नेपाल की क्षमता भी और मजबूत हो।

Friends,

भारत और नेपाल के संबंध साझा इतिहास, आस्था, संस्कृति और गहरे people-to-people ties के धागों से बुने हैं। भगवान राम और माता सीता हमारी साझा सभ्यता और आस्था की पहचान हैं। 2018 में जनकपुर की पावन धरती पर मैंने कहा था, "नेपाल के बिना हमारे धाम अधूरे हैं, नेपाल के बिना हमारे राम भी अधूरे हैं।"

2024 में अयोध्या में रामलला की प्राण प्रतिष्ठा हुई। इस ऐतिहासिक अवसर ने हमारी साझा आस्था को नई ऊर्जा दी। इसके बाद से करोड़ों श्रद्धालु रामलला के दर्शन के लिए अयोध्या पहुँच रहे हैं। 2025 में ही, देश और दुनिया से लगभग 30 करोड़ श्रद्धालुओं ने अयोध्या की यात्रा की।

आज शुरू की गई Train सेवा ‘सरयू-कमला एक्सप्रेस’ से हम इस पवित्र रिश्ते को एक नया आयाम दे रहे हैं। इससे अयोध्या आने वाले श्रद्धालुओं के लिए अब जनकपुर जाकर माता सीता के दर्शन करना भी सुगम हो जाएगा।

हम लुम्बिनी और बोधगया सहित दोनों देशों के बौद्ध और शिव-शक्ति से जुड़े पवित्र स्थलों के बीच कनेक्टिविटी बढ़ाने के लिए भी मिलकर काम करेंगे।

Friends,

आज हमने उत्तराखंड और नेपाल के बीच, धारचूला road bridge का उद्घाटन और बनबसा में integrated check post का शिलान्यास किया है। इसके साथ-साथ हम नेपाल की ओर दोधारा-चाँदनी Integrated Check Post का काम भी तेजी से आगे बढ़ाएँगे। इन पहलों से उत्तराखंड और नेपाल के बीच व्यापार और लोगों की आवाजाही और सुविधाजनक होगी।

साथ ही, हम बिहार, उत्तर प्रदेश और भारत के अन्य राज्यों और नेपाल के बीच road, rail और border connectivity के projects को भी नई गति देंगे। नेपाल के transit trade को और सुगम बनाने के लिए हम कांडला और पारादीप पोर्ट का access उपलब्ध कराएँगे। मुझे विश्वास है कि बेहतर Trade, Connectivity और Investment के इन सभी प्रयासों से नेपाल के आर्थिक विकास को नई गति मिलेगी।

Friends,

नेपाल की नदियों में स्वच्छ ऊर्जा की अपार संभावनाएँ हैं। भारत का विशाल energy market इन संभावनाओं को नेपाल की आर्थिक समृद्धि का एक मजबूत आधार बना सकता है।

आज Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project का शिलान्यास और Arun-3 को समय पर पूरा करने की हमारी प्रतिबद्धता इसी विज़न का हिस्सा है।

Friends,

भारत कई वर्षों से नेपाल के लिए पेट्रोलियम पदार्थों और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं का विश्वसनीय supplier रहा है। हमारी Neighbourhood First Policy की भावना के अनुरूप, इस वर्ष oil supply से जुड़ी गंभीर चुनौतियों के बावजूद, हमने नेपाल को fuel, fertilizers और अन्य आवश्यक वस्तुओं की सप्लाई बनाए रखी।

आज मोतिहारी-अमलेखगंज Pipeline के ‘Phase Two’ का लोकार्पण और झापा Petroleum Terminal का शिलान्यास इस साझेदारी को और मजबूत करेगा।

Friends,

नेपाल की युवा पीढ़ी प्रतिभा, ऊर्जा और बड़े सपनों से भरी है। उनके सपनों को साकार करने में भारत पूरी प्रतिबद्धता से सहभागी बनना चाहता है।

इस संकल्प को साकार करने के लिए, हम नेपाल में Start-up Incubator, Innovation Hub, और Indian Institute of Technology का एक offshore campus स्थापित करेंगे।

हम नेपाली students के लिए भारत में Law और Technology में scholarships के अवसर बढ़ाएँगे। और Food processing और value-addition को बढ़ावा देने के लिए हम नेपाल में Agro-Industrial Park विकसित करने में भी सहयोग करेंगे।

Friends,

रामायण की कथा आज फिल्मों और आधुनिक टेक्नॉलजी के माध्यम से नई पीढ़ी और पूरी दुनिया तक पहुँच रही है। हम चाहते हैं कि भारत और नेपाल के युवा creators मिलकर अपनी साझा विरासत को नए माध्यमों से दुनिया तक पहुँचाएँ। इसी दिशा में, अगली WAVES Summit में हम नेपाल के एक बड़े delegation का स्वागत करेंगे।

sports, खासकर क्रिकेट में भी हम नेपाल में infrastructure के विकास और खिलाड़ियों की training में सहयोग बढ़ाएँगे।

Your Excellency,

आज हम अपने साझा भविष्य को नई दिशा देने के लिए एक Joint Vision Document जारी कर रहे हैं। यह “विकसित भारत और समुन्नत नेपाल” के अपने-अपने संकल्पों को मिलकर साकार करने का blue-print है।

हमारे पास स्पष्ट लक्ष्य हैं, आपसी विश्वास है, उन्हें साकार करने का सामर्थ्य भी है। और सबसे बढ़कर हमारे साथ माता सीता, भगवान राम और भगवान बुद्ध के आशीर्वाद है।

मुझे विश्वास है कि इसी भावना के साथ हम अपने साझा विज़न को ठोस उपलब्धियों में बदलेंगे। और साथ मिलकर भारत-नेपाल संबंधों का एक नया सुनहरा अध्याय लिखेंगे।

भारत–नेपाल मैत्री अमर रहोस्!
बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

 

****

MJPS/SS/VJ

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
Blooming Beyond Borders
“The Rise of India’s Floriculture Economy”
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 1:43PM by PIB Delhi

Roots of a Blooming Industry

India is a land of remarkable natural diversity, stretching from snow-bound mountains and fertile plains to arid deserts and long coastlines. These varied agro-climatic conditions support the cultivation of an extraordinary variety of flowers that bloom across regions and seasons. Coupled with the deep cultural, spiritual, and emotional significance of flowers in India, these natural advantages have fostered a thriving floriculture sector.

Recognising its economic and aesthetic potential, the government has identified floriculture as a “sunrise industry”. What was once a relatively niche segment within Indian agriculture has evolved into a dynamic component of the horticulture sector. The sector contributes to farmer incomes, agricultural exports, and rural enterprise development while increasingly adopting modern cultivation practices and technologies. Today, floriculture encompasses a diverse range of products, production systems, and value-added applications. Rising consumer demand, widening market opportunities, policy support, and technological advancements are driving its continued growth.

Inside India’s Floral Economy

Floriculture is the art and science of growing flowers to achieve high standards of flower quality and aesthetic appeal. As an integral branch of horticulture, it includes the cultivation of flowers and ornamental crops from planting to harvesting. The sector also involves the production of planting material through seeds, cuttings, budding, and grafting. It further includes the marketing of flowers and flower-based products.

Floriculture Product Categories

Loose flowers are harvested and marketed without long stems. These are generally sold by weight and are commonly used for garlands and gajras. Examples include marigolds and jasmine.

Retail Shop selling loose flowers as Garlands  

Cut Flowers are harvested and marketed with stems. These are commonly used in bouquets and vase arrangements. Examples include roses, gerberas, carnations, orchids, and lilies.

Cut flowers sold in bunches as bouquets

In addition to flowers, floriculture includes cut foliage, potted and bedding plants, and ornamental planting materials like seeds for propagation and landscaping.

Flowers that Shape the Market

India cultivates a variety of flowers tailored to domestic and international demand. Key varieties include:

  • Roses: Widely grown in Karnataka and Maharashtra; high in export value.
  • Marigolds: Popular in religious ceremonies; extensively grown in Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh.
  • Carnations, Chrysanthemums, Gerberas: Grown in controlled environments for export.
  • Lilies and Orchids: High-end flowers grown in select regions like Sikkim and Mizoram.

The demand for exotic flowers has increased, with orchids and anthuriums becoming commercially viable in the north-eastern region. These flowers are also gaining traction in urban landscaping, event decor, and the wellness industry.

From Open Fields to Protected Farms

Cultivation of flowers in India takes place through both open-field and protected systems like greenhouses, depending on crop requirements. Open-field cultivation is commonly used for crops such as Chrysanthemum, Rose, Gaillardia, Lily, Marigold, Aster, and Tuberose.

Rising demand for quality flowers and year-round availability have encouraged greater adoption of protected cultivation such as greenhouses. Greenhouses are particularly important for export-oriented crops such as Gerberas and Carnations. This ensures better control over temperature, humidity, and other growing conditions. This helps ensure uniform quality, improved productivity, and compliance with international market standards.

Beyond Bouquets: The Many Uses of Floriculture

Flowers play an important role in everyday life in India and are closely linked with cultural, social, and religious practices. Beyond these traditional uses, floriculture has evolved into a diversified sector with expanding applications in perfumery, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals.

Key domestic uses:

  • Religious and social practices- Flowers such as Jasmine, Marigold, and Crossandra are commonly used in worship, social ceremonies, and personal decoration.
  • Lifestyle and decorative uses- Increasing urbanisation and rising disposable incomes have driven demand for bouquet gifting, venue decoration and beautification of residential and commercial spaces.
  • Perfumery and cosmetics- Flowers, including Jasmine, Lavender, and Rose petals, are used as raw material in fragrance and cosmetic products.
  • Pharmaceutical applications- Floricultural crops such as Calendula, Hibiscus, and Chamomile are utilised in pharmaceutical preparations.
  • Dye and colour extraction- Marigold and Hibiscus are used for natural dyeing and colour extraction.

Mapping India's Flower Belt

Supported by favourable climatic conditions and expanding market demand, floriculture cultivation has expanded across several regions of the country. According to the Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26, the total area under floriculture cultivation stood at 410 thousand hectares. During the same period, production included 3,653 thousand metric tonnes of loose flowers and 1,229 thousand metric tonnes of cut flowers. Total floriculture output amounted to 4,882 thousand metric tonnes, reflecting the scale and commercial significance of floriculture cultivation in India.

The States Driving Floral Production

Floriculture production in India is concentrated in a few leading states.  According to the Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh accounted for about 31 percent of the country’s total flower production. It is followed by Tamil Nadu (14 percent), Madhya Pradesh (11 percent), Karnataka (10 percent), and West Bengal (8 percent). Other major producers included Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Telangana.

 The Northeastern states together accounted for about 4 percent of India’s total flower production, with Assam contributing substantially through both loose and cut flowers. This was followed by Nagaland, particularly in cut flowers. This distribution reflects the diverse geographical spread of floriculture across the country.

A strong production base and diversified cultivation systems have also supported India's growing presence in the international flower trade.

India's Growing Footprint in Global Flower Markets

Floriculture forms part of value-added agricultural exports and provides additional income opportunities beyond traditional crop cultivation. India’s floriculture exports have followed a clear upward trend over the past few years, signalling increasing international demand for Indian floral products. Exports of floriculture, including fruits and vegetable seeds, rose from USD 216.74 million in FY 2021-22 to USD 258.26 million in FY 2025-26. This growth reflects rising international demand for Indian floral products and strengthening export competitiveness.

India’s Top Global Destinations

In FY 2025-26, India’s floriculture and seeds recorded strong demand across key international markets. The United States emerged as the top destination, with exports worth USD 45.94 million. It was followed by the Netherlands, a significant base of the international flower trade, with USD 42.18 million. Bangladesh accounted for floriculture imports worth USD 16.51 million. The United Arab Emirates and Italy imported products valued at USD 16.35 million and USD 9.69 million, respectively. This highlights India’s expanding footprint in traditional and emerging markets for floriculture exports.

A Diverse Floral Export Portfolio

This export performance is supported by a diverse range of floricultural crops that are commercially relevant in the global cut flower trade. Prominent export crops from India include Rose, Carnation, Chrysanthemum, Gerbera, Gladiolus, Gypsophila, Liatris, Nerine, Orchids, Achillea, Anthurium, Tulip, and Lilies, enabling the country to cater to varied market preferences and quality requirements worldwide.

Further, floriculture exports from India comprise multiple product categories, each catering to specific international markets:

  • Fresh cut flowers are exported mainly to Europe, Japan, Australia, the Middle East, and the United States of America
  • Loose flowers are supplied largely to markets serving expatriate Indian communities in the Gulf region
  • Cut foliage is exported primarily to European countries
  • Dry flowers are exported to a wide range of destinations, including the United States of America, Europe, Japan, Australia, the Far East, and Russia
  • Potted plants are exported to a limited number of countries.

Among these export segments, dry flowers constitute a major share of India’s total floriculture exports, owing to their longer shelf life and wider market reach.

Export Breakthrough from the North East

In February 2025, the first-ever export consignment of Anthurium flowers from Mizoram to Singapore was flagged off. This marked a significant milestone for floriculture exports from India’s North Eastern Region. The consignment contained 1,024 Anthurium cut flowers (weighing 70 kg) packed in 50 corrugated boxes. The initiative was led by APEDA in collaboration with the Department of Horticulture, Government of Mizoram. It highlights new overseas market linkages and emerging trade opportunities for floriculture growers in the region.

Enabling Growth Through Policy Support

The government has initiated a range of developmental programmes to promote floriculture across the country. These efforts focus on production, infrastructure, research, capacity building, and export facilitation.

Key areas of government support include:

  • Policy and Institutional Support- Developmental initiatives are implemented primarily through the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), including the National Horticulture Mission (NHM), the Horticulture Mission for North East and Himalayan States, and the National Horticulture Board.
  • Financial assistance and credit support - The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) provides financial assistance to farmers to adopt protected cultivation and precision farming practices, thereby improving productivity and quality.
  • Seed production and planting material - To meet growing demand for flower seeds, several seed companies have established production units in major flower-growing states. Thus, supporting the availability of quality planting material.
  • Incentives and concessions - Concessions are provided on seeds, planting materials, equipment, and air freight to support floriculture exports and improve competitiveness in international markets.
  • Export Promotion - Export-related support is provided through the Ministry of Commerce, mainly via the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA).
  • Training and capacity building- The Government has introduced various training programmes for farmers and entrepreneurs. These programmes are strengthening farmers’ technical skills, promoting the adoption of modern practices, and enterprise development in floriculture.
  • Research and development - Floriculture research is carried out at multiple institutions under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR). The research is also conducted in the horticulture departments of State Agricultural Universities, and under the All India Coordinated Floriculture Improvement Project.

The sector continues to benefit from policy support, financial assistance, and institutional backing. Improved frameworks and targeted interventions will further enhance India's competitiveness in the floriculture trade.

Cultivating Innovation: From Scientific Research to High-Value Floriculture

As floriculture becomes increasingly market-oriented, advances in research and technology are improving productivity, quality, and product diversification.

CSIR Floriculture Mission

The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has developed two flagship programmes to strengthen India’s flower and aroma sectors through science-driven interventions.

  • The CSIR Floriculture Mission, launched in 2021, seeks to enhance farmers’ incomes, support entrepreneurship, and promote technology-led development in the floriculture industry.
    • As of December 2025, under this mission, more than 2,208 hectares have been brought under floricultural cultivation.
    • This has benefitted16,220 individuals across 399 clusters in 26 states and union territories of the country.

The programme has also developed and transferred multiple technologies to entrepreneurs and conducted numerous training and capacity-building initiatives.

  • The CSIR Aroma Mission, launched in 2017, focuses on improving rural livelihoods through the cultivation and processing of aromatic crops. Thesecrops provide quality raw materials for the aroma and essential oil industry.
    • As of December 2025, aromatic crop cultivation had expanded to more than 51,000 hectares.
    • The mission had also established over 4,500 aroma clusters across 28 States, including 20 clusters in tribal areas.
    • The mission prioritised skill development, with 2,096 training and awareness programmes training 1.22 lakh persons. These included10,000 women and supported more than 110 entrepreneurs in developing value-added products.
    • In total, these interventions have generated around 1 crore rural employment opportunities and enabled the production of over 6,000 tonnes of essential oils. The output valued at aboutRs.600 crore supplied key inputs to the aroma and allied industries.

These research initiatives highlight the importance of scientific support in strengthening India's floriculture sector.

From Laboratory to Field: The Story of India’s Exotic Flowers

Tulips in the Himalayas: A Garden of Possibilities

In the Himalayan region (Palampur), scientific research under the CSIR - Institute of Himalayan Bioresource Technology (IHBT)-Floriculture Mission, has helped convert natural climatic advantage into structured floriculture opportunity. Leveraging cool temperatures and suitable agro-ecological conditions, tulip cultivation has been supported through research-driven interventions. The work has focussed on planting material selection, flowering cycles and crop management practices. These efforts have enabled the successful growth of tulips meeting international quality parameters. They have also strengthened the region’s position in premium ornamental flower segments. As of May 2026, the Tulip Garden at Palampur attracted more than 1.5 lakh visitors, highlighting its potential to support floriculture-based tourism.

The Himalayan tulip initiative demonstrates how targeted technological interventions can support crop diversification. It also highlights the potential for strengthening regional specialisation in high-value floriculture.

Tulip Garden at CSIR-IHBT Palampur, Himachal Pradesh

 

Eustoma in Odisha: A New Bloom of Hope

In contrast to the cool Himalayan landscape, another CSIR laboratory has created floral history. The successful cultivation of Eustoma in parts of Odisha (Sambalpur) represents a breakthrough in adapting exotic flowers to non-traditional environments. Once considered unsuitable for warmer regions, the crop was grown with scientific guidance on temperature management, disease control and cultivation practices. The outcome demonstrated that innovation can overcome climatic constraints, opening new income avenues for farmers. The Odisha experience highlight show science-led cultivation can connect farmers with high-value markets.

First Bloom of Eustoma in Odisha

 

For visitors walking through the tulip fields of Palampur or admiring the pastel blooms of Eustoma in Sambalpur, the experience extends beyond visual appeal. It represents the quiet yet impactful transformation of laboratory knowledge into practical field-level success. Here, innovation takes root and strengthens India's evolving floriculture landscape.

A Sector Poised for Sustainable Growth

India’s floriculture sector has moved beyond a niche segment of horticulture to become a diversified and commercially significant agricultural activity. Its growth is anchored in the country’s rich agro-climatic diversity, expanding domestic demand, stronger market linkages, and growing export opportunities. The sector’s future lies in moving from cultivation to value creation. Greater adoption of protected cultivation, precision technologies, improved planting material, post-harvest management, and quality standards can strengthen productivity and market competitiveness. With continued policy support, stronger institutions, and better market linkages, floriculture can boost farm incomes, rural enterprises, and agricultural exports.

The sector’s expanding footprint, from traditional flowers to exotic varieties and value-added applications, also opens avenues for regional specialization and new entrepreneurial opportunities. As India looks towards a more diversified and technology-enabled agricultural economy, the future of floriculture holds the promise of growing both value and livelihoods- “one bloom at a time”.

item.title: Gyan Bharatam Session at the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum Reconnects the Manuscript Heritage; Language, Script and Manuscript Traditions
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Culture
item.description: Ministry of Culture Gyan Bharatam Session at the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum Reconnects the Manuscript Heritage; Language, Script and Manuscript Traditions Scholars and delegates from SCO Member States and Dialogue Partners discuss manuscript preservation, translation, digitisation and international cooperation Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi India’s manuscript heritage, encompassing knowledge of polity, economy, medicine, mathematics, astronomy, agriculture and sustainable living, reflects a rich civilizational journey in which…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Gyan Bharatam Session at the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum Reconnects the Manuscript Heritage; Language, Script and Manuscript Traditions
Scholars and delegates from SCO Member States and Dialogue Partners discuss manuscript preservation, translation, digitisation and international cooperation
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

India’s manuscript heritage, encompassing knowledge of polity, economy, medicine, mathematics, astronomy, agriculture and sustainable living, reflects a rich civilizational journey in which knowledge travelled across regions through lipi (script), bhāṣā (language) and jñāna (knowledge). Rooted in the spirit of the Ṛgvedic prayer “ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvataḥ” (let noble thoughts come to us from all sides), this shared legacy was the focus of Session IV on “Language, Literature, Script and Manuscript Traditions”, convened by the Ministry of Culture under the Gyan Bharatam Mission on 22 November 2026 at Purana Qila (Old Fort), New Delhi. The session brought together eminent scholars, experts and delegates from SCO Member States and Dialogue Partners to deliberate on the shared manuscript heritage and avenues for collaboration.

The session was part of the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum, held from 20 to 22 November 2026 and inaugurated by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi.

Shri Inderjeet Singh, CEO (Gyan Bharatam) & Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, briefed participants from SCO countries on the Gyan Bharatam Mission and its operational activities to the participation SCO Countries: Survey and Cataloguing; Conservation and Capacity Building; Technology and Digitization; Linguistics and Translation; and Research, Publication and Outreach. He highlighted the key features of AI and its integrated features, Gyan-MitramAI, Pandulipi Darpana and BharatiyaGPT, and the milestone achieved that over 1.26 crore manuscripts have been reported through the National Manuscript Survey.

Emphasising the collaborative vision of the Mission, he stated, “For the Gyan Bharatam Mission, this is both a responsibility and an invitation to work together.” He also highlighted the significance of Indic scripts across the SCO region and the role of manuscripts in fostering global dialogue and building a global digital repository of knowledge.

Prof. Anirban Dash, Project Director, Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture, moderated the session and welcomed the participants. He observed that language gives voice to our thoughts, Language and literature preserve them, and these manuscripts carry wisdoms across time and places. He highlighted how knowledge travelled across mountains and seas, underwent translation and adaptation, and became part of the intellectual life of diverse societies.

Thereafter, the session begin with discussion over 4 key themes, “Many tongues, Many scripts: India’s Linguistic and Script Heritage and its imprint on Asian Languages; Literature in Motion: transmission, translation, and Localization of Indian texts across Asia; Manuscripts Beyond Borders: The Global Presence and Dispersal of India’s Manuscript Heritage; Reconnecting Dispersed Knowledge: Gyan Bharatam and the Digital Future of Manuscript Heritage”.

Prof. Rajnish Kumar Mishra, Professor, SSIS, Jawaharlal Nehru University, emphasized India's vivid linguistic and script heritage and its imprint on Asian languages. He spoke on the varied nature, concepts and modes of expression that spread across the world through the communication and writings of our great seers, and noted that Indian culture also spread across the oceans via the Silk Route. He talked about scholars such as Shankaracarya, Ramashekhar, Acarya Abhinavagupta and others, and also threw light on the different regional manuscript traditions and recessions.

Prof. K.K. Mishra, Head and Associate Professor, Department of Sanskrit, University of Calcutta, focused on enhancing the pathway for digitisation, translation into more languages, multiple uses of AI, and global accessibility via the establishment of NDR. He referred to the BnF, Thailand and Vietnam, Mongolia and Russia, Google Arts & Culture, and bilateral and archival ties, and also touched upon translators, pilgrims and Nalanda.

Dr. Viswajanani J. Sattigeri, Head, TKDL Unit, spoke on Gyan Bharatam and the digital future of manuscript heritage. She stressed the need to protect our knowledge from piracy and spoke on the published nature of our traditional knowledge, IPR, patent codes, codified metadata on the database, and controlled access to avoid duplication and misappropriation, like TKDL.

Prof. K. Rama Subramaniyam, IIT Bombay, spoke on manuscripts and their importance in interpreting things rightly, as it shapes thought, expression and mind. Citing the example of the Pañcatantra, which has been translated into over 50 foreign languages, such as Arabic, Persian and others, he stressed the need to keep translations of the content free from biased interpretation. He observed that knowledge is bound to decay and has to be preserved. A manuscript preserved for hundreds of years is treasured not only for its content but also for the journey of time and traditions it carries.

Delegates from several SCO countries, including Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Cambodia, Uzbekistan, Laos and Nepal, actively participated in the discussions. They shared their respective efforts and initiatives for manuscript preservation and expressed interest in collaborating with Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in various manuscript related activities.

The session concluded with a shared commitment to strengthen cooperation in manuscript preservation, script training, comparative literary studies, research and translation, cataloguing, academic exchanges, authorised digital access and joint research, reaffirming the role of shared heritage and knowledge traditions in fostering cultural understanding and cooperation across the SCO region.

***

M Annadurai

(Release ID: 2340254)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat to organise Yuva Samvad on Constitution Day; Programme to cover over 600 districts across 30+ States/UTs under the theme ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’
Nationwide Student Engagement to Highlight India’s Achievements, Constitutional Values and the Role of Youth in Nation-Building; Participants to collectively read the Preamble to the Constitution
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 1:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), will organise the ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad’ on the occasion of Constitution Day, between 24th and 26th November 2026, across more than 500 colleges in over 600 districts spanning 30+ States and Union Territories. The nationwide initiative aims to connect young people in the age group of 15–29 years with India's developmental journey, its achievements and aspirations for the future, while inspiring them to become active participants in the nation's transformation into a developed country by 2047.

In keeping with the spirit of Constitution Day, participants across institutions will collectively undertake a reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, reaffirming their commitment to constitutional values and the ideals enshrined in the Constitution. The programme will also provide a nationwide platform for engaging young people through interactive dialogues and awareness sessions, encouraging them to reflect on India's progress, emerging opportunities and their role in shaping the country's future.

To translate this vision into meaningful engagement at the grassroots level, distinguished Youth Icons will lead sessions at participating universities and colleges. As a key component of these engagements, each Youth Icon will deliver a specially curated presentation on the theme ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’, taking students through India's developmental journey, its achievements in recent years and its aspirations for becoming a developed nation by 2047. The presentation will highlight the country's progress in poverty reduction and socio-economic transformation, including efforts to improve the lives and livelihood opportunities of millions of people through inclusive development and welfare initiatives. It will also showcase India's significant progress in addressing Naxalism, restoring peace and creating an enabling environment for development in previously affected regions. Further, it will emphasise the importance of building a healthy, empowered and addiction-free society, highlighting how substance abuse undermines individual potential, family well-being, societal progress and national productivity. The presentation will underline that a Nasha Mukt Bharat is fundamental to realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, with the youth playing a decisive role in driving this transformation.

Adding further depth to these interactions, Padma Awardees will engage with students and share their life journeys, personal experiences and insights, highlighting the challenges they have overcome, the milestones they have achieved and the values that have guided their journeys. These interactions will provide young participants with an opportunity to draw inspiration from their experiences and understand the importance of dedication, perseverance and commitment in contributing to nation-building.

The initiative draws inspiration from the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, articulated in his address on 15th August 2023 from the ramparts of the Red Fort, wherein he called upon the Yuva Shakti to play a pivotal role in realising Viksit Bharat@2047. Recognising the Amrit Peedhi as a key driver of nation-building, the programme seeks to channelise youth energy and leadership towards achieving this national vision.

To translate the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 into action,  the MY Bharat Portal (mybharat.gov.in) will serve as the digital platform for registrations and programme-related activities, enabling wider youth participation and facilitating the onboarding of young people into the MY Bharat ecosystem. By combining institutional outreach with digital engagement, the initiative seeks to extend opportunities for participation to youth across the country and encourage them to take up meaningful volunteer-led activities.

The programme will also establish a sustained institutional connection with participating colleges and universities. MY Bharat Chapters may subsequently be established in these institutions to facilitate continued youth engagement, promote volunteerism and support the implementation of future MY Bharat initiatives. This will help nurture a network of socially responsible and motivated young citizens who can take forward the spirit of participation, leadership and service beyond the programme.

Through the ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad’, MY Bharat seeks to channelise the energy, ideas and potential of the Amrit Peedhi towards the national vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. India's journey towards becoming a developed nation is rooted in inclusive growth, social transformation, peace and security, and the empowerment of its citizens. A drug-free India is not merely a social aspiration; it is a national imperative that calls for the active participation of every young citizen. With the message ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’, the programme aims to transform awareness into action, dialogue into determination and youth participation into a nationwide movement for change.

This Constitution Day, MY Bharat invites the youth of India to come together for a collective reading of the Preamble, reaffirm their commitment to the ideals enshrined in the Constitution, and raise their voices for a healthier, stronger and drug-free Bharat. The journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047 will be shaped not only by the aspirations of our youth, but also by the choices they make and the actions they take today.

For registrations, programme updates and opportunities to engage with MY Bharat initiatives, visit www.mybharat.gov.in.

*****

Gaurav Saini

(Release ID: 2340251)

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
Ayush Pavilion Emerges as a Major Attraction at India International Trade Fair 2026
Draws Large Crowds with Free Healthcare Consultations, Yoga Sessions and Interactive Wellness Activities
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 12:12PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Ayush is showcasing India’s diverse traditional healthcare systems at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, being held from 13 to 27 November at Hall No. 2, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Ayush Pavilion is offering visitors an engaging experience through healthcare consultations, interactive activities, traditional dietary preparations, medicinal plant displays and educational presentations highlighting the relevance of Ayush systems in promoting preventive healthcare and healthy living.

The pavilion brings together institutions and research councils under the Ministry of Ayush, presenting a wide range of activities that connect traditional knowledge with everyday health practices. The CCRAS–CARI is providing Ayurveda OPD services and Prakriti Pariksha, along with information on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and Ayurvedic wellness. The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, is presenting commonly used herbs and spices, including Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Arjuna, Amla, Haridra and Guduchi, with information on their classical applications and relevance to health promotion. Visitors are also being sensitised to the importance of appropriate dosage, individual health conditions and professional guidance before using medicinal herbs.

The National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Jaipur, is showcasing Ayush Aahar products such as Ragi Cookies, Triphala Jam, Aloe Vera Gel and herbal Lip Balm. Interactive attractions include Ayurvedic Snakes and Ladders based on Ahara (diet) and Vihara (lifestyle), along with virtual reality experiences offering visualisation of human body systems. IEC materials are also being displayed to create awareness about Prakruti, Panchakarma, Ayurvedic cooking and the role of Ayurveda in daily life.

Rashtriya Ayurveda Vidyapeeth (RAV) is promoting Ayurveda-based food innovations through the display of POSHAK cookies, Ayurvedic bread and the traditional drink Pankam. Activities such as “Dadi Se Puchho” and “Millets on the Wheel” are engaging visitors while spreading awareness about traditional dietary practices, the nutritional benefits of millets and healthy living.

The Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY) is conducting regular yoga demonstrations and sessions on a dedicated platform at the pavilion. Visitors are also receiving personalised yoga consultations based on their age, health concerns and lifestyle. Yoga quizzes and asana competitions are further encouraging participation, with visitors showing interest in incorporating yoga into their daily routines.

The Unani stall, managed by the Regional Research Institute of Unani Medicine (RRIUM), New Delhi, under the Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), is highlighting traditional Unani dietary preparations and healthcare practices. Visitors are being offered tastings of Unani Qahwa, Hareera, Halwa Gheekawar, Gulkand and Murabba Amla. A modified digital Mizaj Assessment Kiosk is enabling visitors to assess their temperament and receive personalised dietary advice. The stall also features digital presentations and documentaries on Unani medicine. On 18 and 19 November, the Unani OPD provided free consultations and medicines to 151 patients.

The Siddha stall, managed by the Central Council for Research in Siddha (CCRS) and the National Institute of Siddha (NIS), Chennai, raises awareness of Siddha principles, preventive healthcare practices, and therapeutic applications. The display covers Siddha Ahar, nutrition, lifestyle modification, diagnostic methods, traditional formulations and therapies, including Varma therapy. Digital presentations, documentaries and IEC materials are being used to engage visitors. The stall also highlights NIS's academic and research activities, including its BSMS, MD (Siddha), and PhD programmes, encouraging students to explore education and careers in Siddha.

The Central Council for Research in Yoga & Naturopathy (CCRYN) is presenting Yoga and Naturopathy through digital audio-visual content, IEC material and an Ayush Aahar display. Visitors are being introduced to healthy snack options such as Makhana Ladoo, Peanut Ladoo, Til Ladoo and Namkeen. Free consultations on Yoga, Naturopathy, dietary practices and lifestyle modifications were also provided on 17 and 18 November.

The National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa is offering visitors insights into the ancient healing traditions of the Himalayan region. The stall features detailed information on Sowa-Rigpa diet, therapeutic regimens and herbal formulations, with practitioners offering personalised guidance based on classical Sowa-Rigpa texts.

The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB) is highlighting the importance of medicinal plants through live displays, information material and the distribution of Satavari medicinal plants. Plants featuring QR codes are helping visitors access information, while brochures, pamphlets and the comic book “Professor Ayushman” are being distributed to promote awareness about medicinal plants and their uses.

Through its diverse displays and interactive activities, the Ayush Pavilion at IITF 2026 is providing a platform for visitors to experience India’s traditional healthcare systems and learn about their role in preventive healthcare, nutrition and wellness. The pavilion reflects the Ministry of Ayush’s continued efforts to promote public awareness and bring Ayush practices closer to people through accessible, engaging and educational initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Nayi Chetna 5.0 to be Launched on 25 November
Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments and Signed Quadripartite MoU on Violence-Free Village Initiative to be Unveiled
Posted On: 23 NOV 2026 10:28AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development will launch the fifth edition of its national gender campaign, Nayi Chetna – Pahal Badlav Ki, on 25 November 2026, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. The month-long campaign will be implemented nationwide from 25 November to 23 December 2026 under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Hon’ble Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, will inaugurate the national launch in the presence of Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon’ble Union Minister of Women and Child Development. The event will also witness the presence of Shri Kamlesh Paswan, Hon’ble Minister of State, Rural Development along with senior officials of participating Ministries, representatives of State Governments, development partners and women leaders from community institutions across the country.

The launch will take place at 2:00 PM at Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, NASC Complex, Dev Prakash Shastri Marg, Pusa, New Delhi – 110012.

The theme of Nayi Chetna 5.0, “From Access to Agency: Empowering Women through Livelihoods and Equal Opportunities for a Viksit Bharat,” highlights the importance of women’s access and mobility as critical enablers of economic empowerment, livelihood participation and independent decision-making.

Four interconnected areas of focus

Nayi Chetna 5.0 will place women’s economic empowerment at the centre of its approach, with a focus on four interconnected areas: recognising women as economic contributors, strengthening women’s access to and control over assets, promoting safe mobility, and redistributing unpaid care work. Particular emphasis will be placed on addressing barriers that restrict women’s access to livelihood opportunities, markets, financial services, public spaces and essential services, and their ability to move freely, safely and independently. The campaign aims to move beyond awareness generation towards coordinated action and measurable improvements in women’s economic participation, agency and decision-making.

The highlights of the event

Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments

A key highlight of the national launch will be the release of a Joint Inter-Ministerial Advisory involving 15 Ministries/Departments. The Advisory will reflect a shared commitment to advance the objectives of Nayi Chetna 5.0 through coordinated action and convergence. It will provide a framework for Ministries and Departments to align their schemes, programmes, institutional mechanisms and frontline networks with the campaign’s objectives. It will seek to strengthen coordinated interventions at the national, State, district and community levels, particularly to improve women’s access to livelihoods, assets, financial services, safe mobility, essential services and institutional support.

Signed Quadripartite MoU on Violence-Free Village Initiative

The event will also feature the release of the signed Quadripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the Violence-Free Village Initiative, among the Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Justice and National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU will provide a framework for coordinated institutional action to prevent and respond to gender-based violence at the community level. It is intended to strengthen convergence between community institutions, legal services authorities and relevant government mechanisms, including awareness of legal rights, access to justice, institutional support and collective action towards building violence-free villages.

Strengthening community institutions and women’s leadership

DAY-NRLM’s extensive network of Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Village Organisations (VOs), Cluster Level Federations (CLFs), Gender Resource Centres (GRCs) and other community institutions will play a central role in the implementation of Nayi Chetna 5.0. During the launch, new Gender Resource Centres will be inaugurated as community-level platforms to facilitate access to services, entitlements, support systems and grievance redressal mechanisms. SHG women leaders from different States will share their experiences, innovations and perspectives on strengthening women’s collective action and leadership.

The programme will also feature two panel discussions during the day. The first panel, “Advancing Ministerial Convergence through Gender Resource Centres (GRCs), One Stop Centres (OSCs), Legal Services Authority (LSA), and Health System,” will bring together representatives from relevant Ministries and institutions to deliberate on strengthening convergence and coordinated responses to women’s concerns. The second panel, “Women Leaders from the Field: Experiences, Innovations and the Way Forward,” will provide a platform for grassroots women leaders to share their experiences and recommendations.

Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report

The Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report will be released during the national launch. The report will present the assessment of the previous edition and its key learnings to inform and strengthen future campaign interventions.

The programme will also include the screening of State-level videos and presentations of good practices, highlighting community-led initiatives and approaches towards gender equality. Video resources developed for the campaign will also be launched.

Spearheaded by DAY-NRLM, Ministry of Rural Development, Nayi Chetna has evolved since its inception in 2022 into a nationwide collective movement to address gender-based violence (GBV), challenge discriminatory social norms and advance gender equality. Through Nayi Chetna 5.0, the Ministry seeks to strengthen collective action among Ministries, State Governments, community institutions and other stakeholders to create an enabling environment for women’s economic participation, safety and agency. The campaign will also encourage the active engagement of men, boys and youth in challenging discriminatory social norms and promoting equality and shared responsibility.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR A PEOPLE’S MOVEMENT TO MAKE YAMUNA CLEAN AND ENSURE ITS UNINTERRUPTED FLOW
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT MUST NOT COME AT THE COST OF ENVIRONMENT; SCIENTIFIC TREATMENT OF SEWAGE AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE ESSENTIAL: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER SAYS RIVER CONSERVATION IS A COLLECTIVE MORAL RESPONSIBILITY AND VITAL TO SAFEGUARDING FUTURE GENERATIONS
ENVIRONMENT-FRIENDLY LIFESTYLES AND PUBLIC PARTICIPATION KEY TO PROTECTING RIVERS AND WATER RESOURCES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER PARTICIPATES IN NATIONAL CAMPAIGN FOR YAMUNA CONSERVATION; ADMINISTERS SANKALP TO PARTICIPANTS TO MAKE THE RIVER CLEAN
Posted On: 22 NOV 2026 10:37PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today called for a sustained people’s movement to make the river Yamuna clean and ensure its uninterrupted flow. Emphasising that government efforts must be supported by active public participation, he urged citizens, institutions, industry and social organisations to make river conservation a shared responsibility.

Shri Birla made these observations while addressing the National Campaign of Conservation and Public Resolution for River Maa Yamuna Ji at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. On the occasion, the Speaker also administered a Sankalp to the invitees to make  Yamuna clean and called upon everyone to contribute to fulfilling this collective resolve.

Highlighting the importance of rivers in India’s civilisational journey, Shri Birla observed that rivers have sustained human settlements, agriculture, industry and livelihoods for generations. The Ganga and the Yamuna, he said, are integral to India’s spiritual and cultural heritage, and their conservation is essential to protecting both this legacy and the well-being of society. He emphasised that preserving India’s traditions and values must also involve safeguarding its rivers and natural environment.

Shri Birla stressed that every member of society must act responsibly to preserve the cleanliness and sanctity of the Yamuna. Keeping riverbanks clean and ensuring that everyday conduct does not contribute to pollution, he said, must become a collective moral responsibility. He observed that conservation efforts gain strength and achieve lasting results when they become a Jan Andolan supported by all sections of society.

Calling upon industry to contribute actively to river conservation, Shri Birla said that industries are an important foundation of development, but their growth must not come at the cost of the environment. He emphasised the need for scientific treatment and effective systems to prevent sewage and industrial waste from entering rivers. Development, environmental protection and water conservation, he noted, must advance together.

Lok Sabha Speaker Speaker underlined the importance of adopting environment-friendly lifestyles, recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s appeal for responsible individual and collective action to protect the environment. He referred to initiatives such as ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ and encouraged citizens to participate in efforts that promote greenery, conserve water and reduce environmental degradation. Lasting improvements, he said, require changes in habits and behaviour alongside institutional measures.

Appreciating the efforts of Swami Chidanand Saraswati Ji, Shri Birla said that his work brings together spiritual consciousness and social responsibility to promote environmental protection. He commended his initiatives to mobilise society for river conservation, water conservation and tree plantation, and urged participants to carry forward the resolve to rejuvenate the Yamuna. He also acknowledged the dedication of young volunteers working for the conservation of the Ganga and the Yamuna.

Shri Birla observed that the Yamuna supports the lives and livelihoods of people across several States and called for comprehensive measures for river conservation, prevention of erosion and protection of water resources. He emphasised that sustained community cooperation is indispensable to keeping rivers clean and maintaining their flow. Recalling the relative improvement in river cleanliness during the COVID period, he urged society to reflect on the impact of human activities and accept responsibility for preventing pollution.

Referring to the Yamuna’s special association with Mathura, Vrindavan and the traditions of Lord Shri Krishna, Shri Birla said that the river occupies a deeply cherished place in India’s spiritual consciousness. This sense of reverence, he observed, must translate into practical and sustained action to protect the river wherever it flows.

Emphasising the need to secure a safe future for the coming generations, Shri Birla said that clean rivers and a healthy environment are essential to their well-being. He described climate change as a shared global challenge and observed that India, guided by the philosophy of _Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam,_ has a responsibility to contribute to collective solutions and provide leadership in environmental protection.

 

नदियाँ हमारी सभ्यता, संस्कृति और जीवन का आधार हैं। इनका संरक्षण हमारी साझा जिम्मेदारी है। नई दिल्ली के भारत मंडपम में यमुना परिवार काउंसिल द्वारा आयोजित माँ यमुना के संरक्षण एवं पुनर्जीवन के राष्ट्रीय अभियान में सहभागिता की। इस अवसर पर माँ यमुना को स्वच्छ एवं अविरल बनाए रखने, आध्यात्मिक चेतना के माध्यम से जनजागरूकता बढ़ाने और इस दिशा में समाज की सामूहिक भागीदारी के महत्व पर विचार साझा किए। मेरा विश्वास है कि सामूहिक संकल्प और निरंतर प्रयासों से माँ यमुना को स्वच्छ, निर्मल और अविरल बनाए रखने का लक्ष्य प्राप्त किया जा सकता है।

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 22, 2026

भारत की सनातन संस्कृति, संस्कार और विरासत को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए हमारी नदियों और पर्यावरण का संरक्षण भी आवश्यक है। गंगा और यमुना जैसी नदियाँ हमारी सभ्यता, विकास और जीवन का आधार रही हैं। https://t.co/RaA0qXfchH

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 22, 2026

मुरारिकायकालिमाललामवारिधारिणी तृणीकृतत्रिविष्टपा त्रिलोकशोकहारिण। नई दिल्ली के भारत मंडपम में यमुना परिवार काउंसिल द्वारा आयोजित माँ यमुना के संरक्षण एवं पुनर्जीवन के राष्ट्रीय अभियान को संबोधित किया। माँ यमुना भारतीय सभ्यता, संस्कृति और आध्यात्मिक चेतना की अविच्छिन्न धारा हैं। भगवान श्रीकृष्ण की लीलाओं से लेकर ब्रज की लोकपरंपराओं तक, यमुना का उल्लेख हमारे धार्मिक एवं सांस्कृतिक वाङ्मय में विशेष श्रद्धा के साथ मिलता है। यमुनोत्री से प्रयागराज तक प्रवाहित माँ यमुना केवल आस्था का केंद्र नहीं, बल्कि उत्तर भारत के विशाल भूभाग की कृषि, आजीविका और जल सुरक्षा का भी महत्वपूर्ण आधार हैं। यमुना का पुनर्जीवन केवल जल की स्वच्छता तक सीमित नहीं, बल्कि उसके प्राकृतिक प्रवाह, सहायक नदियों, जलग्रहण क्षेत्रों और जैव विविधता के संरक्षण से जुड़ा व्यापक प्रयास है। सीवेज एवं औद्योगिक अपशिष्ट का वैज्ञानिक उपचार, वर्षा जल संचयन, भूजल पुनर्भरण और नदी के पूरे बेसिन का समन्वित प्रबंधन इस दिशा में आवश्यक हैं। इसके लिए केंद्र एवं राज्य सरकारों के साथ संत समाज, सामाजिक संगठनों, उद्योग जगत और नागरिकों की सक्रिय भागीदारी भी जरूरी है। मेरा विश्वास है कि श्रद्धा जब कर्तव्य में और संकल्प जब सामूहिक प्रयासों में परिणत होता है, तभी परिवर्तन की वास्तविक राह बनती है। माँ यमुना को स्वच्छ, निर्मल और अविरल बनाए रखना हमारी सांस्कृतिक विरासत के संरक्षण के साथ-साथ आने वाली पीढ़ियों के प्रति हमारी जिम्मेदारी भी है।

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Interaction with Tea Industry Stakeholders at Kurseong, Darjeeling
Deliberations Focus on Revitalising Darjeeling Tea, Strengthening Tea Auctions and Enhancing Exports
India Remains the World’s Largest Producer of Black Tea and Third-Largest Exporter, Recording USD 988.13 Million in Tea Exports in FY 2025–26
Posted On: 22 NOV 2026 10:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, chaired an interaction with tea industry stakeholders at Kurseong, West Bengal, organised by Tea Board India. The meeting was also attended by Member of Parliament, Darjeeling, Shri Raju Bista, and MLA, Kurseong, Shri Sonam Lama.

Senior officials of the State Government, representatives of various tea associations and stakeholders from different segments of the Indian tea industry participated in the interaction. The meeting provided an important platform for constructive dialogue on key challenges, emerging opportunities and measures required to strengthen the long-term growth, sustainability and global competitiveness of the Indian tea sector.

India continues to be the world's largest producer of black tea and the third-largest exporter of tea globally. During the financial year 2025–26, India exported 282.11 million kg of tea, valued at USD 988.13 million, underscoring the sector's significant contribution to the country's agricultural economy and export earnings.

Detailed deliberations were held on a wide range of issues, including the revitalisation of the Darjeeling tea industry, making the tea auction system more responsive, faster and robust, strengthening tea research, quality enhancement, export promotion, welfare of tea workers and initiatives under the Export Promotion Mission (EPM).

An extensive brainstorming session was also held on making the existing tea auction system more robust, efficient, faster and responsive to the evolving requirements of the industry. The importance of technology-driven reforms, greater transparency, improved operational efficiency and reduction of transaction-related difficulties was highlighted.

Ease of Doing Business emerged as a key priority, with emphasis on simplifying processes, improving efficiency and creating a more enabling environment for stakeholders across the tea value chain.

Considerable emphasis was placed on strengthening Indian tea exports through focused promotional measures and effective utilisation of opportunities under the Government of India's Export Promotion Mission. Stakeholders shared suggestions for expanding India's presence in international markets, strengthening the global positioning of Indian tea, improving market access and enhancing export competitiveness. Discussions also highlighted the need for coordinated efforts between the Government, Tea Board India and industry stakeholders to promote Indian tea in both traditional and emerging markets.

The critical role of research and development in improving the quality, productivity and competitiveness of Indian tea was emphasised during the interaction. Discussions focused on strengthening tea research, encouraging innovation and adopting improved scientific practices to address emerging challenges and meet the evolving quality requirements of domestic and international markets. The services of the Tea Research will be extended to small tea growers.

The welfare of tea plantation workers and their families remained an important area of discussion. In this context, reference was made to the proposed implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Cha Shramik Protsahan Yojana (PMCSPY), aimed at improving the welfare of tea workers, particularly women and their children, in West Bengal. The significance of effective implementation of the scheme and its intended benefits in the areas of education, healthcare and improved living conditions was highlighted.

The interaction provided an opportunity for stakeholders to present their concerns, share suggestions and deliberate on practical measures for the overall development of the tea sector. The discussions underscored the importance of a coordinated approach towards revitalising the Darjeeling tea industry, modernising tea trading infrastructure, promoting Ease of Doing Business, strengthening research and quality assurance, enhancing exports, improving the welfare of tea workers and strengthening the tea auction system.
