item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's address during participation in Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 9:49PM by PIB Delhi

उत्तर प्रदेश के ऊर्जावान मुख्यमंत्री योगी आदित्यनाथ जी, केन्द्रीय मंत्रिमंडल में मेरे वरिष्ठ साथी और इसी संसदीय क्षेत्र से प्रतिनिधित्व कर रहे श्रीमान राजनाथ सिंह जी, श्रीमान जयंत चौधरी जी, संसद में मेरे पंकज चौधरी जी, उपमुख्यमंत्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य जी, ब्रजेश पाठक जी, अन्य जनप्रतिनिधि और मेरे युवा साथियों,

मुझे खुशी है कि हमारे मित्र जयंत चौधरी जी ने कौशल विकास के इतने बड़े कार्यक्रम के लिए लखनऊ को चुना। आपने ताली तो बजा दी, लेकिन मैं अभी बात तो बताना मेरी बाकी है। मुझे खुशी इसलिए है कि उत्तर प्रदेश के सांसद होने के नाते मेरे लिए गर्व की बात है और मेरे सौभाग्य है, उत्तर प्रदेश के सांसद के नाते देशभर से आए हुए, मेरे युवा दोस्तों का स्वागत करने का मुझे आज अवसर मिल रहा है।

साथियों,

आज अपने जीवन का एक अहम पड़ाव पार किया है। अब आप राष्ट्र निर्माण की प्रक्रिया से सीधे जुड़ने वाले हैं और आज का दिवस मेरे लिए बड़ा महत्वपूर्ण है। मैं आज सुबह दिल्ली से निकला, बंगाल गया और आज के दिन का मेरा पहला कार्यक्रम आईआईटी में था। 75 साल हुए आईआईटी को, देश का पहला आईआईटी खड़गपुर बना था, उसके 75 साल का समारोह था और जिस ऊर्जा के साथ, जिस सपनों को लेकर, जिस आशा और अरमान को लेकर के मैं आईआईटी के बच्चों के पास गया था, उतने ही उमंग और उत्साह के साथ मैं आईटीआई के बच्चों के पास आया हूं। चाहे आईआईटी हो या आईटीआई हो, मेरे लिए तो यही मेरे देश की अमानत है, यही मेरे देश का सामर्थ्य है और यही मेरे देश का भविष्य है। आईटीआई में पढ़ते हुए जो स्‍किल आपने सीखी है, जो हुनर आपने सीखा है, वो अब विकसित भारत की बड़ी ऊर्जा है, ये विकसित भारत आप ही के हाथों से, आप ही के हुनर ने बनने वाला है। कोई भी राष्‍ट्र अपने युवाओं के कौशल से इसी तरह कुशलता से आगे बढ़ता है और हमारा देश तो हमेशा से ही कौशल का सम्मान करने वाला देश है। आप यहां लखनऊ में ही देखिए, चिकनकारी का काम कितना काम होता है, लंबे समय तक दुनिया में भारत की पहचान ऐसे ही कौशल से रही है। बहुत बारीक मलमल, बनारस और कांजीवरम का रेशम, कश्मीर की पश्मिना, हमारे सूती कपड़े, कलमकारी, दुनिया की, दुनिया की श्रेष्ठ तलवारों को बनाने वाली स्टील, कांस्य और पंचधातु की मूर्तियों का निर्माण, ऐसे सैकड़ों अनगिनत काम, शायद कोई एक व्यक्ति एक साथ गिना भी नहीं सकता है और जो हमारे समाज का आधार स्तम्भ हुआ करते थे।

साथियों,

हमारे यहां पहले की समाज व्यवस्था ही कौशल के इर्द गिर्द ही रची हुई थी। मेरे जन्म गुजरात में हुआ, मैं गुजरात का एक अनुभव बताता हूं। गुजरात में एक शब्द प्रयोग है- वसवाया। ये वसवाया परंपरा रही है यानी जहां कोई गांव बसेगा, वहां अपने कौशल से गांव का जीवन चलाने वाले हुनरमंद लोग भी बसेंगे और वो होंगे तभी तो गांव बसेगा यानी ऐसे हुनरमंद लोग जिनके बिना गांव के जीवन की कल्पना भी मुश्किल होती थी।

साथियों,

हमारे यहां प्राचीन काल से देश के हर क्षेत्र में ऐसी व्यवस्था रही है। लेकिन दुर्भाग्य से धीरे-धीरे यह व्यवस्था महत्व खोती चली गई। मैं जब गुजरात में मुख्यमंत्री था, तब मेरे सामने एक बार ये प्रश्‍न उठा था कि किस तरह के कितने कौशल होते हैं, जिनके बिना हमारा जीवन बहुत मुश्किल हो जाएगा? मैंने अपने अफसरों को ये काम दिया, वो लेकर आए कोई 30-35 चीजों को करने के लिए, मैंने कहा- ये ऐसा मत करो, थोड़ा मैं एक रास्ता दिखाता हूं, आप सोचिए! और मैंने उनको कहा कि - सुबह जागने से लेकर के रात सोने तक और जन्म से लेकर मृत्‍यु तक व्यक्ति को, परिवार को, समाज को किन-किन चीजों की आवश्यकता पड़ती है, कितनी प्रकार की सेवाओं की जरूरत होती है, हर व्यक्ति को अनिवार्य रूप से चाहिए ही, मैंने कहा अरे याद करके जरा लिस्ट बनाइए अपने अनुभव से। - जब पहले डिपार्टमेंट के लोग मेरे पास 30-35 चीज लेकर के आए थे। उन्होंने जब बैठ करके, सोच करके सूची बनाई, एक सप्ताह के बाद मुझे मिले, एक हजार काम ढूंढकर लाए थे वो, यानी हमें गुलदस्ता बनाने वाला भी चाहिए, हमें खिलौना बनाने वाला भी चाहिए, हमें मेहंदी लगाने वाले भी चाहिए, कितने प्रकार की सेवाओं की जरूरत पड़ती है और यही तो वो स्किल्स थीं, वो कौशल था, जो हमारे समाज को गतिमान बनाए हुए थे। मैंने अफसरों से इसी पर फोकस करने को कहा और फिर वहां गुजरात में कौशल विकास का एक आधुनिक इकोसिस्टम तैयार हुआ।

साथियों,

भारत में कौशल व्यवस्था की तबाही में एक और बात का दोष रहा। जब हमारे देश में आक्रांता आए, हमारा देश स्‍वर्णिम युग लेकर के दुनिया के लिए आकर्षण का भी केंद्र था, ईर्ष्या का भी केंद्र था और भारत में जब आए, उन्होंने क्या किया? सबसे पहली चोट उन्होंने हुनर पर की, आप में भी बहुत बच्‍चों ने इतिहास में पढ़ा होगा, हमारे ऐसे जो कारीगर हुआ करते थे, कोई चीज बना लें और वो चीज सबसे ज्‍यादा अच्‍छी बने, तो उस बनाने वाले के अंगूठे काट दिए जाते थे, क्यों? उन आतताइयों को पता था कि ये हुनर ही है, ये इसके हाथों में जो कौशल है, वो ही भारत को महान और समृद्ध बना रहा है और इसलिए उसकी शक्ति नष्ट करनी है, तो उसके अंगूठे काट दो, बाद में अंग्रेज आए, वो जरा बड़े sophisticated थे, उन्होंने तरीका बदला, उन्होंने देश के लोगों को, मैकाले ने एक ऐसी शिक्षा व्यवस्था थोपनी शुरू की जिसमें स्किल आधारित हमारी व्यवस्था सिर्फ कागजी क्लर्क बनाने तक सीमित हो गई। काले क्लर्क बनाने का काम कारोबार शुरू हो गया। अंग्रेजों ने भारत में कौशल को तबाह करके अपने यहां इंडस्ट्री को आगे बढ़ाया, यहां से सारी चीजे ले गए, अपने यहां मैन्युफैक्चरिंग को आगे बढ़ाया और समय के साथ अंग्रेजों का कागजी क्लर्क होने को सम्मान के साथ देखा जाने लगा। हमारे समाज की स्थिति कैसी है, अगर कोई बच्चा आईटीआई में दाखिल होता है, तो उसके मां-बाप, यार-दोस्तों को, रिश्तेदारों को बताते नहीं है कि आईटीआई में जाता है, छुपाते हैं। उन्हें शर्म आती है, क्यों? वो यूनिवर्सिटी में नहीं जा रहा है, कॉलेज में नहीं जा रहा है, ये तो ब्लू कलर के कपड़े पहनकर के ये हाथ से काम कर रहा है, ये परिस्थिति पैदा हो गई और मैंने ठान लिया है, मुझे इस परिस्थिति को बदलना है। जितना सम्मान आईआईटी के लोगों का होगा, उतना ही सम्मान मेरे आईटीआई के बच्चों का भी होगा। अरे बड़ी से बड़ी कम्पनी हो, ये कागजी सर्टिफिकेट लेकर के घूमने वाले दो-तीन लोग होते हैं, लेकिन उस कम्‍पनी को ताकत देने के लिए 200-300 आईटीआई वालों की जरूरत पड़ती है, तब जाकर के कम्‍पनी चलती है।

और इसलिए साथियों,

सामाजिक जीवन में एक मनोवैज्ञानिक परिवर्तन की बहुत बड़ी आवश्यकता है और मैं जयंत चौधरी जी को और उनके सभी अधिकारियों को भी मैं बधाई दूंगा। अभी मैं देख रहा था, जो बेटे-बेटी यहां सर्टिफिकेट लेने आए थे, उनका ठाठ देखा था, उनके कपड़े देखे थे, किसी यूनिवर्सिटी के convocation में ऐसे कपड़े नहीं होते, जैसे मेरे ITI के बच्चों के होते हैं। ये ठाठ, ये रुबाब, देश का प्रधानमंत्री ITI के बच्चों को सर्टिफिकेट देने के लिए बंगाल की यात्रा से दौड़ करके लखनऊ आकर के उनके पास खड़ा होकर के गर्व अनुभव कर रहा है।

साथियों,

वो गुलामी की मानसिकता थी, जिससे देश आजादी के बाद भी बाहर नहीं निकल पाया। आजादी के बाद भी क्लेरिकल जॉब पर जोर रहा और कौशल पीछे छूटता गया। एक बार मैंने दादा धर्माधिकारी जी की किताब पढ़ी थी, कोई Postgraduate किया हुआ सज्‍जन उन्हें मिलने आया, वो कहता था कि कोई कि परिचय हो तो नौकरी लगा दो, तो दादा धर्माधिकारी जी ने पूछा भई तुम्हें आता क्‍या है? बोले- मैं Postgraduate हूं, अरे बोले Postgraduate हो भई तुझे आता क्‍या है ये तो बताओ, अरे बोले मेरे पास गोल्‍ड मेडल है, मेरे पास certificate है, मैं Postgraduate हूं। अरे तुझे कुछ आता है क्‍या? तो वो समझा नहीं, बार-बार कह रहा था- मैं Postgraduate हूं। तो दादा धर्माधिकारी जी ने पूछा- अच्‍छा भाई तुम ये बताओ, तुझे गाड़ी चलाना आता है क्‍या? बोले- नहीं। बोले- खाना पकाना आता है क्‍या? बोले-नहीं! तो तुझे आता क्‍या है? मेरे पास certificate है। देश में एक वक्‍त था जो कागज़ी certificate वाला कार्यकाल रहा होगा, वक्त बदल रहा है और मैं आज आपको बात कहने जा रहा हूं। आज आपने देखा होगा, मीडिया में, सोशल मीडिया में एक चर्चा चल रही है और उस चर्चा में कह रहे हैं आज सब लोग कि मोदी जी ने Parliament में 2023 में कहा था कि आप ये भारत सरकार के जो PSUs हैं, उसमें पैसा लगाइए मालामाल हो जाएंगे और उस समय लोगों ने मेरी मजाक उड़ाई थी और आज इतिहास गवाह है कि जिन्‍होंने पैसे लगाए, वो मालामाल हो गए। मैंने दूसरी एक बात कही थी दोस्‍तों एक साल पहले, मैंने कहा था- मैं देशवासियों से आग्रह करता हूं, एक साल के लिए अगर जरूरत न हो तो कृपा करके सोना मत खरीदिए, गोल्‍ड मत खरीदिए और मुझे खुशी है, अगर लाल बहादुर शास्‍त्री ने कहा था देशवासियों को कि एक टाइम खाना छोड़ दो, इस देश ने उनकी बात को माना था। मेरे देश का चरित्र वही है, मेरे जैसे एक सामान्‍य व्‍यक्‍ति ने कहा कि गोल्‍ड कम खरीदिए, देशवासियों ने गोल्‍ड कम खरीदा, गोल्‍ड के दाम टूट गए। आज लोग मुझे कह रहे हैं- मोदी जी आपने कहा, आपकी बात मानी, हमारे पैसे बच गए। मैं आज एक और बात कहने जा रहा हूं, आप लिखकर रखिए, वक्त बदल रहा है, ये कागजी certificate लेकर के कोट पैन्ट टाई पहनकर के घूमने वाले लोग, उससे ज्यादा ये हुनर वालों की कदर होने वाली है। जिसके पास कौशल है, जिसके पास हुनर है, उसकी मांग बढ़ने वाली है। मैं जब सऊदी अरेबिया जाता हूं, दुबई जाता हूं, अबू धाबी जाता हूं, कतर जाता हूं, कुवैत जाता हूं, तो वहां के रॉयल फैमिली के लोग एक बात हमेशा कहते हैं कि ये जो हमारे शानदार आधुनिक शहर दिख रहे हैं न आपको, ये हमारे पैसों से नहीं, हिन्‍दुस्‍तान के कारीगरों के परिश्रम से बने हैं। ये दुबई की रौनक, ये अबु धाबी की चमचमाता हुआ अबु धाबी, ये सऊदी अरेबिया, ये भारत के कारीगरों के हुनर और परिश्रम का परिणाम है, हर रॉयल फैमिली भारत की शक्ति का गौरवगान करती है दोस्तों। आज दुनिया में जितनी भी सरकारें हमारे साथ समझौता कर रही हैं, उसमें एक बात उनकी होती है, हमें हर साल 90 हजार लोग चाहिए, हमें हर साल डेढ़ लाख लोग चाहिए, हमें हर साल एक लाख लोग चाहिए। आज पूरी दुनिया भारत के लोगों को मांग रही है। और कौन चाहिए यूनिवर्सिटी से निकले हुए नहीं, आईटीआई से निकले हुए लोग चाहिए। जिसके पास कौशल है, जिसके पास हुनर है, दुनिया में उसकी मांग बढ़ रही है। और इसलिए मैं कह रहा हूं दोस्तों, आने वाले बीस साल, बीस साल के बाद, वो मूवी की बात नहीं कर रहा हूं मैं, बीस साल के बाद विकसित भारत!

साथियों,

21वीं सदी का भारत कौशल को, स्किल को सम्मान देकर ही आगे बढ़ सकता है। इसलिए, बीते वर्षों में हमारी सरकार ने श्रमेव जयते की भावना से एक के बाद एक कई कदम उठाए हैं। हमने अलग स्‍किल मिनिस्‍ट्री बनाई, वहीं से शुरू किया। हमारे यहां पहले केवल कॉलेज-यूनिवर्सिटी में डिग्री पाने वालों के लिए दीक्षांत समारोह होते थे। बड़ा-बड़ा टोपा पहन करके आते थे, बड़े-बड़े कोट-वोट पहन करके आते थे। मैंने कहा- नहीं। अगर आन बान शान के साथ दीक्षांत समारोह होगा, तो मेरे आईटीआई के बच्चों का होगा। मुझे उनकी उंगलियों में भारत का भविष्य दिखता है। मुझे उनके हुनर में हिन्‍दुस्‍तान का सामर्थ्य नजर आता है। हमने जब नई नेशनल एजुकेशन पॉलिसी बनाई, तो उसमें भी कौशल विकास पर बहुत ज्यादा जोर दिया।

साथियों,

आज के इस आधुनिक जमाने में AI को लेकर क्या कुछ कहा जा रहा है, AI से ये हो जाएगा, AI वो हो जाएगा, AI से इसका रोजगार छिन जाएगा, उसका रोजगार छिन जाएगा। लेकिन मेरी ये बात अच्छे से समझ लीजिए, जिसके पास स्किल है, उसका रोजगार कोई नहीं छीन सकता। हमने कोविड के दौरान देखा है, हर एक को पता है कैसे हाल हो गए थे हर परिवार के, लोग असहाय हो गए थे, जिनकी सेवाओं से उनका जीवन चलता था, वो मौत के डर से गांव छोड़-छोड़ करके अपने यहां चले गए थे और तब लोगों को पता चला कि हम कितने ही पैसे वाले क्‍यों न हो, ये स्किल्ड मैनपॉवर के बिना हम गुजारा नहीं कर सकते जी और तब वो स्‍किल वर्कर ही था, जिसने देश की कई बातों को संभाला था, काम किया था।

साथियों,

जब आप कोई हुनर सीखते हैं, तो आप केवल मशीनों पर काम नहीं करते। आप लोगों की जिंदगी को आसान बनाते हैं। आप देश का सामर्थ्य बढ़ाते हैं, वो भी एक वक्‍त था, हिन्‍दुस्‍तान मोबाइल फोन इंपोर्ट करता था और आज मेरे देश की बेटे-बेटियां वो मोबाइल फोन बनाती हैं, दुनिया भी में भारत का बना मोबाइल फोन जा रहा है दोस्तों। देश की मैन्युफैक्चरिंग कैपेसिटी आप के कारण बढ़ती है। इसलिए, आज ITI को इतना महत्व दिया जा रहा है। 2014 के बाद हमारी सरकार ने सिर्फ एक दशक में लगभग 5 हज़ार नई ITI बनाई हैं। ITI में पढ़ने वालों की संख्या भी 5 लाख से अधिक बढ़ी है और इसमें भी लड़कियों की संख्या ढाई गुणा से अधिक हो चुकी है।

साथियों,

ITI में ट्रेनिंग, क्वालिटी, फैकल्टी और इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर, ये भी हमारे लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण रहा है। पहले इसमें भी ITI नेटवर्क पिछड़ता जा रहा था। Skill और vocational courses के नाम पर वो पुराने trade पढ़ाए जा रहे थे। आज ITIs में 30 से अधिक New age trades की पढ़ाई होने लगी है। Gen Z ने जिसका उल्लेख भी किया। एयरोनॉटिकल स्ट्रक्चर, आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस के असिस्टेंट की बात हो, साइबर सिक्योरिटी असिस्टेंट की बात हो, ड्रोन टेक्नीशियन की बात हो, ग्रीन हाइड्रोजन टेक्नीशियन की बात हो, इंडस्ट्रियल रोबोटिक्स की बात हो, इलेक्ट्रिक व्हीकल्स हो, एनिमेशन एंड स्पेशल इफेक्ट्स, सेमीकंडक्टर टेक्नीशियन, ITI में ऐसे हर कोर्स वर्तमान और भविष्य की जरूरतों को देखते हुए इंट्रोड्यूस किए गए हैं। आप के शहर में कितना ही बड़ा hospital क्यों न हो, दुनिया भर में बड़ी-बड़ी पढ़ाई करके आया वो कितना ही बड़ा डॉक्टर क्यों न हो, लेकिन वहां पर hospital में जो मशीन होते हैं न, उसको चलाने वाले ITI के बच्चे न हों, तो एक भी मरीज ठीक नहीं हो सकता है, कितना ही बड़ा डॉक्टर क्यों न हो, ये ताकत आपके पास है। मैं आपको उस ताकत का एहसास कराने के लिए निकाला हूं दोस्तों, मैं आपको उस सामर्थ्‍य की पूजा करने निकला हूं, मैं आपके उस सामर्थ्य को सम्मान देने के लिए निकला हूं। क्योंकि मुझे पता है कि आईटीआई आने वाले भविष्य के लिए एक गौरवपूर्ण गाथा लिखने वाला है।

और साथियों,

ये जो काम हो रहे हैं, वो केवल भारत की जरूरतों के हिसाब से नहीं है, ये पूरी दुनिया की जरूरतों को देखते हुए डिजाइन किए जा रहे हैं। आप आए दिन सुनते हैं कि भारत इस देश के साथ ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट कर रहा है, उस देश के साथ FTA की चर्चा चल रही है, ये सब आप युवाओं के लिए ही हो रहा है, ये आपके लिए नया अवसर बना रहा है।

साथियों,

हमारा प्रयास है कि ITI का Curriculum को भी बदले, उसकी मशीनें भी बदलें, Trainer भी नई Technology सीखें और Training का Industry से सीधा संबंध भी बनना चाहिए। तभी पीएम सेतु स्कीम के तहत 60 हज़ार करोड़ रुपए खर्च किए जा रहे हैं। इसका बहुत बड़ा लाभ आप सभी युवाओं को होने जा रहा है।

साथियों,

आज भारत जिस तेजी से विकास कर रहा है, उसमें भी आप युवाओं के लिए स्किल्ड वर्कर्स के लिए रोजगार के नए अवसर बन रहे हैं। अभी आपने सुना होगा, बीते 12-13 वर्षों में ही भारत में 50 करोड़ लोग गरीबी से बाहर आए हैं, ये बहुत बड़ी घटना है। आजादी के बाद का हिन्‍दुस्‍तान का अगर सबसे बड़ा कोई अचीवमेंट है, तो मेरी दृष्‍टि से ये 50 करोड़ लोगों का गरीबी से बाहर आने का है। और विकसित भारत का रास्‍ता भी इसी से गुजरने वाला है। सरकार ने इन लोगों को सुविधाएं दीं, गरीब को empower किया, इन्हें भरोसा मिला कि वो गरीबी से बाहर निकल सकते हैं। और इस महाअभियान में देश में स्किल्ड वर्कर्स के लिए भी लाखों-लाख नए मौके बने। जैसे 4 करोड़ गरीबों के घर बने, तो वहां इलेक्ट्रिशियन को, कारपेंटर को काम मिला। कहीं पानी की पाइप लाइन बिछी, कहीं पहली बार बिजली लाइन पहुंची, तो काम आप जैसे युवाओं के द्वारा ही सफल हुआ।

साथियों,

आज देश में नए-नए सेक्टर्स में अलग-अलग स्किल्स की डिमांड बढ़ रही है। मैं आपको एक और उदाहरण देता हूं। कुछ महीने पहले जब पश्चिम एशिया में युद्ध शुरू हुआ, गैस की सप्लाई बाधित हो गई, LPG मिलेगा, नहीं मिलेगा, संकट के बादल छा गए और हमारे जो खास प्रेमी लोग हैं, वो तो उछल गए। अब गैस मिलने वाला नहीं है, चूल्हा जलने वाला नहीं है, लोग भूखे मरने वाले हैं, पेट्रोल पंप पर लाइनें लगने वाली हैं, देखा होगा आप जरा अखबार निकाल के देख लीजिए, क्‍या-क्‍या कहा जाता था, लेकिन ऐसा कुछ नहीं हुआ। लेकिन दूसरी तरफ जब होर्मुज का संकट आ गया, LPG आएगी या कि नहीं आएगी, तो हम भी तो कोई सो करके सोते हुए रहने नहीं चाहते थे, हम भी कदम उठाना चाहते थे और तब सरकार ने तय किया कि एक दिन में कम से कम शहरों के अंदर जो लोग रहते हैं, उनके घरों में डेली एक लाख PNG कनेक्शन जरूर दे, पाइप गैस देने के लिए हर घर में पाइप लाइन लगाकर के गैस देने की व्यवस्था करें, ताकि संकट आ जाए, तो हम टिक पाएं और मैं खुद उसका रिव्यू मीटिंग लेता था, क्योंकि मेरा इरादा था हर दिन एक लाख होने चाहिए, ताकि मैं कोई बड़ा संकट आने से पहले व्यवस्था कर पाऊं। और जब मैं रिव्यू मीटिंग बुलाता था, तो एक ही बात सामने आती थी, मैं कहता था- भई 15-20 हजार से आपका आंकड़ा क्यों बढ़ता नहीं है, कभी 22 हजार, कभी 23 हजार, कभी 20 हजार, एक दिन में एक लाख नहीं पहुंच पा रहे थे, सरकार पैसे देने को तैयार थी। आपको पता है, क्या जवाब मिला, बोले- साहब हमारे पास सब हमने ताकत लगा दी, हमें प्‍लंबर्स नहीं मिल रहे, प्‍लंबर्स की कमी पड़ रही है। देखिए, क्या ताकत है आपकी, देश तरस रहा था कि हमें प्‍लंबर्स चाहिए। यानी अगर आप स्किल्ड हैं, तो आपके पास रोजगार पाने के लिए मौके उतने ही ज्यादा हैं। आज हमें सोलर पावर से जुड़े सेक्टर में बहुत बड़ी संख्या में स्किल्ड मैनपावर चाहिए। आज देश में पूरी एक नई स्पोर्ट्स इकॉनमी बन रही है। हमें स्पोर्ट्स इक्विपमेंट बनाने वाले, खेल से जुड़ा जो और सामान है उसकी इंडस्ट्री के लिए, फिटनेस के लिए यानी स्पोर्ट्स इकोसिस्टम में भी आपके लिए नए अवसरों के यानी एक प्रकार से आसमान तक के लिए आपके रास्‍ते खुले पड़े हैं जी। हमारे युवाओं को इन अवसरों का पूरा लाभ उठाना है।

साथियों,

आज भारत, विश्व की स्किल कैपिटल बनने की तरफ आगे बढ़ रहा है, स्किल कैपिटल मतलब आप लोग हैं उसके केंद्र में। और मैं हिन्‍दुस्‍तान की बात नहीं, दुनिया की बात कर रहा हूं, आपके भरोसे कर रहा हूं दोस्तों। और एक खुशखबरी सभी युवाओं के लिए है, उत्तर प्रदेश के लिए है। अगले साल यानी 2027 में, अगले साल 2027 में भारत World Skills Asia प्रतियोगिता की मेजबानी करेगा वाला है, दुनिया के एशिया के नौजवान यहां आने वाले हैं और यह आयोजन, यह आयोजन 2027 में उत्तर प्रदेश के ग्रेटर नोएडा में होगा। दुनिया के अनेक देशों के युवाओं को यूपी होस्ट करने वाला है। मैं यूपी को इसके लिए भी अग्रिम शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

साथियों,

उत्तर प्रदेश आज देश के विकास को गति दे रहा है। एक समय था, जब यहां के नौजवानों के सामने अवसरों की बहुत कमी थी। हमारे योगी जी, मौर्य जी, ब्रजेश जी, पंकज चौधरी जी, इन सबने मिलकर के, इन सबके नेतृत्व में, डबल इंजन सरकार ने इस स्थिति को बदल दिया है। आज यूपी वाले गर्व से कहते हैं कि यूपी एक्सप्रेस वे प्रदेश है, यूपी में इतने सारे इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट है, यहां बड़ी-बड़ी यूनिवर्सिटीज़ बन रही हैं, टूरिज्म फल-फूल रहा है, यहां मोबाइल बनाने वाली बड़ी फैक्ट्रियां हैं, यूपी में चिप बनाने वाली फैक्ट्री बन रही है और जिसकी सबसे ज्यादा चर्चा है ऑपरेशन सिंदूर, ऑपरेशन सिंदूर में दुश्मन की नींद उड़ाने वाली ब्रह्मोस भी अब यूपी में बन रही है। यूपी में हो रहे इन सारे विकास कार्यों की वजह से आज आप सब युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर बन रहे हैं।

साथियों,

यूपी में पहले क्या होता था? वो भी हमें भूलना नहीं है। कुछ दिन पहले मैं अपने Parliamentary Constituency काशी में मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में था। वहां एक फैक्ट्री का उद्घाटन हुआ, वहां एक बिटिया ने मुझे बताया कि वो अब रात 11 बजे भी यहां काम करके आराम से घर लौटती है, ये सामान्‍य बात नहीं है, वो उत्तर प्रदेश वालों को पता है कि सूरज ढलने के बाद बेटी का घर से बाहर निकलने का मतलब क्या होता है। वो बेटी कह रही थी, बोली- रात 11 बजे मैं फैक्ट्री में काम करने के बाद अकेली घर जाती हूं। योगी जी के नेतृत्व में यहां भाजपा सरकार ने सुरक्षा का ये वातावरण बनाया है। सुरक्षा का एहसास और समृद्धि का विश्वास ही विकसित भारत बनाएगा। इसलिए मैं देश के हर युवा से कहता हूं कि आपके सामने इस समय पूरा आसमान है, बड़े सपने देखिए, अपने कौशल का विकास करिए और अपने सपनों को पूरा करने के लिए पूरी ताकत लगा दीजिए। और कभी भी यह महसूस करना मत कि आप अकेले हैं, जब भी आपको लगेगा, आप अकेले है, आप सोच लेना मैं आपके साथ खड़ा हूं। इसी विश्वास के साथ एक बार फिर आप सब जन जब नए जीवन की तरफ आगे बढ़ रहे हैं, आपके माता-पिता के सारे सपने आप पूरे कीजिए, आपने जो कुछ पाया है, उसे समाज की शक्ति बनाने में समर्पित कर दीजिए, आप भी बढ़ेंगे, देश भी बढ़ेगा, आपका परिवार भी गौरव से भर जाएगा। इसी भावना के साथ आप सबको इस विशेष अवसर पर आज मैं अभी देख रहा था टीवी पर, अनेक ITIs में सब नौजवान बैठे हुए हैं, मैं आपको, उनको, सबको बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं, बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

मेरे साथ बोलिए-

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

भारत माता की जय!

बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद!

***

MJPS/SS/SS/AV

(Release ID: 2339781)

item.title: Renowned Actor Rakesh Bedi Unpacks the Art of Characterisation at IFFI 2026’s ‘Dhurandhar’ Press Conference
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Renowned Actor Rakesh Bedi Unpacks the Art of Characterisation at IFFI 2026’s ‘Dhurandhar’ Press Conference Theatre roots and in-depth character study shaped Jamil Jamali in ‘Dhurandhar’, reveals Rakesh Bedi at IFFI 57 Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 9:29PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 21 November 2026 Aditya Dhar’s Hindi feature film Dhurandhar, which opened the Mainstream Cinema Feature Film category of the Indian Panorama section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), was the focus of an engaging press…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Renowned Actor Rakesh Bedi Unpacks the Art of Characterisation at IFFI 2026’s ‘Dhurandhar’ Press Conference
Theatre roots and in-depth character study shaped Jamil Jamali in ‘Dhurandhar’, reveals Rakesh Bedi at IFFI 57
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 9:29PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Aditya Dhar’s Hindi feature film Dhurandhar, which opened the Mainstream Cinema Feature Film category of the Indian Panorama section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), was the focus of an engaging press conference held on the second day of the festival at the festival’s Media Centre in Panaji, Goa.

The interactive session featured veteran actor Rakesh Bedi and acclaimed production designer Saini S. Johray, who shared insights into the film’s creative journey, nuanced characterisation and visual world-building. The session was moderated by Shri Mahesh Kumar, Additional Director General, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting.

Speaking about his portrayal of Jamil Jamali, Rakesh Bedi highlighted the importance of layered character writing in contemporary cinema. Drawing on his extensive theatre experience, which he described as an enduring foundation of his craft, Bedi spoke about the meticulous research that went into developing his character. He emphasised that a character’s actions must be driven by the demands of the scene, making the performance a complete character portrayal rather than an exercise in mere mimicry.

Reflecting on his five-decade-long career, marked by diverse and challenging roles, Bedi spoke about the changing reach and visibility of cinema. Recalling the immense popularity of earlier films such as ‘Ek Duuje Ke Liye’, ‘Tirangaa’ and ‘Chashme Buddoor’, he observed that while cinema enjoyed tremendous public appeal even then, its reach was limited by the absence of digital connectivity.

In contrast, social media has transformed how audiences discover and engage with performances, allowing an actor's work to reach audiences across the world with a single click.

Responding to a question from a film enthusiast about his comic and dramatic timing, Bedi explained that such nuances are never accidental. Every gesture and expression, he said, is carefully planned as part of the script and character arc, serving as a deliberate means of expression to bring authenticity to the portrayal.

On being asked how he switches between emotions so effortlessly and whether he rehearses in front of a mirror, Bedi offered insights into his approach to acting. He advised against practising in front of a mirror, explaining that watching oneself while performing can stunt an actor’s growth, as it is difficult to objectively assess one’s performance while executing it. Instead, he emphasised the importance of deeply understanding and internalising a character. Once an actor understands the character’s psyche - speech, reactions and emotional transitions flow naturally.

Production designer Saini S. Johray detailed the architectural authenticity of the film, revealing that the team constructed over 40 practical sets. Without physical access to locations in Pakistan, Johray relied on exhaustive research, studying news archives, local gang-war reports, urban textures, and Google Maps, to faithfully reconstruct the film’s environment from scratch.

The press conference underscored the 57th IFFI’s role as a vibrant platform for meaningful conversations on cinema, bringing filmmakers, artists and audiences together to explore the creative processes behind filmmaking.

Through such interactions, the festival celebrates not only compelling stories on screen but also the craft, research and collaborative efforts that bring them to life, fostering a deeper appreciation of the diverse dimensions of cinematic expression.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
India and Spain Explore New Avenues for Cooperation in the Media and Entertainment Sector at IFFI 2026
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 9:22PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

India and Spain are exploring new avenues to strengthen cooperation in the media and entertainment sector, with discussions focusing on updating the bilateral audiovisual co-production agreement and expanding collaboration through the World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit (WAVES). The engagement comes in the context of Spain’s participation as the Country of Honour at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).

In this regard, Shri Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary (Broadcasting), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, along with officials of the Ministry and India Cine Hub (ICH), held a meeting with the Spanish delegation led by Ms. Marta Serrano, Director General, Spanish Institute of Cinematography and Audiovisual Arts (ICAA), Ministry of Culture, Spain, in Goa.

The discussions centred on opportunities to deepen bilateral engagement in film and audiovisual production, including through an updated co-production framework that can facilitate greater collaboration between the creative industries of the two countries.

The existing India–Spain audiovisual co-production agreement was signed in 2012. Discussions on updating the agreement are aimed at strengthening the framework for bilateral cooperation in film and audiovisual production. The proposed framework, as outlined by the Spanish side, envisages cooperation across fiction, animation and documentary projects, as well as television series and films.

Spain’s participation as the Country of Honour at IFFI 2026 provides an opportunity to showcase contemporary Spanish cinema and foster professional engagement between the Indian and Spanish film industries. The festival is being held in Goa from November 20 to 28, 2026.

The 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar, being held in Panaji from November 20 to 24, 2026, offers another platform for interaction between the two audiovisual industries. The Spanish programme includes a dedicated Spanish Day on November 22, featuring an industry panel and opportunities for interaction between professionals from both countries.

The discussions underline the shared interest of India and Spain in strengthening audiovisual cooperation and creating greater opportunities for co-production, creative collaboration and professional exchange.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Secretary, Ministry of I&B, Shri Chanchal Kumar Inaugurates Publications Division Stall at 57th IFFI in Goa
Publications Division Showcases Books on India's Rich Cultural Heritage, History, Art, Cinema and Literature at Stall No. 24
Stall Offers Film Enthusiasts, Delegates and Visitors an Opportunity to Explore India's Diverse Literary and Cultural Legacy
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 9:03PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Shri Chanchal Kumar, inaugurated the Publications Division stall (Stall No. 24) at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI 2026) in Goa today, in the presence of Smt. Kanchan Prasad, Director General, Publications Division.

The 57th edition of IFFI is being held in Goa from 20 to 28 November 2026, bringing together filmmakers, cinema enthusiasts, industry professionals and delegates from across India and around the world.

Located at Stall No. 24, the Publications Division stall features a diverse collection of books and publications covering India's rich cultural heritage, history, art, cinema, literature and other subjects of national importance. The stall provides visitors with an opportunity to explore informative and enriching publications that reflect the country's cultural diversity, creative traditions and intellectual heritage.

A special focus has been placed on publications related to Indian cinema, offering film enthusiasts, students, researchers and delegates an opportunity to gain deeper insights into the evolution of cinema, the creative journeys of filmmakers and the contributions of prominent personalities to India's cinematic heritage.

Publications Division, a premier publishing institution under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, has been engaged in publishing books and journals on a wide range of subjects since 1941. Through its publications, the Division continues to preserve and disseminate India's literary, historical, cultural and intellectual heritage.

The participation of Publications Division at IFFI 2026 is part of its continued efforts to promote reading, encourage engagement with books and make valuable knowledge accessible to a wider audience.

The stall serves as a platform connecting cinema with literature, enabling festival delegates and visitors to explore India's rich storytelling traditions beyond the screen.

Through its presence at the festival, Publications Division reaffirms its commitment to promoting a culture of reading, celebrating India's creative achievements and preserving the nation's cultural and literary legacy for present and future generations.

item.title: Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat: “Shared Cultural Heritage a Strong Bridge Connecting SCO Nations”
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Culture
item.description: Ministry of Culture Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat: “Shared Cultural Heritage a Strong Bridge Connecting SCO Nations” Day 2 of SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum Witnesses Deliberations on Cultural Expressions of Civilisations, Art and Architecture, and Historical Trade Relations Purana Qila is a Living Story of India's Shared Cultural Heritage and Diversity: Dr. Musaddiq Masood Malik Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:44PM by PIB Delhi The second day of the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue Forum , being hosted…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat: “Shared Cultural Heritage a Strong Bridge Connecting SCO Nations”
Day 2 of SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum Witnesses Deliberations on Cultural Expressions of Civilisations, Art and Architecture, and Historical Trade Relations
Purana Qila is a Living Story of India's Shared Cultural Heritage and Diversity: Dr. Musaddiq Masood Malik
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:44PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue Forum, being hosted by India in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, featured a series of sessions focusing on the cultural expressions of civilisations, shared heritage in art and architecture, and historical trade relations. The sessions brought together ministers, senior representatives, academicians, historians, and experts in art and culture from SCO member states and dialogue partner countries. The day-long deliberations explored various dimensions of cultural exchange, shared artistic traditions, and historical connections among different civilisations.

It may be recalled that Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the Forum on November 20. The objective of the event is to strengthen cultural ties among SCO member states, promote mutual understanding and cooperation through shared civilizational heritage, and create new opportunities for cultural dialogue. The Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) is the Knowledge Partner for the event.

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, while chairing the first and second joint sessions on the theme ‘Civilizational and Cultural Expressions’ on the second day, said that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing countries closer to one another. They have also effectively highlighted the immense potential of cultural cooperation in fostering mutual understanding, trust, and friendship.

He said that today's deliberations are deeply rooted in the spirit of the eternal Vedic prayer referred to by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi yesterday (November 20): “Om Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manamsi Janatam.” This means, “Let us move together, deliberate together, and let our minds be in harmony with one another.”

He further observed that our civilisations are not merely legacies of the past but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate our present and inspire future generations.

He emphasized that the shared civilizational knowledge and heritage should be harnessed to advance collective efforts through dialogue, institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges, and meaningful cooperation. He expressed confidence that the Forum would emerge as a lasting platform for fostering civilizational understanding, strengthening cultural ties, and deepening connections among the member states of the SCO.

Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Vivek Agrawal, in his welcome address and introduction to the themes of the Forum, said that the SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum provides member states with an important opportunity to understand their rich cultural heritage, historical connections, and shared civilizational values, while facilitating the exchange of ideas.

Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musaddiq Masood Malik, referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions. This, he said, was the very diversity that the delegates had been invited to celebrate. He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’.

He further stated that dialogue takes place amid diversity. Referring to his conversation with Shri Shekhawat the previous day, he said that the layers of history and culture had been an integral part of the region's way of life for thousands of years. It was therefore important to recognise that distinct identities have their own significance, while dialogue among diverse identities is equally essential. He said that the participants had gathered precisely for this purpose—to bring together multiple voices and identities and facilitate the free flow of ideas among them. He emphasised that wisdom and courage lie in acknowledging, respecting, embracing, and moving forward together with these diverse identities.

Shri Alok Dimri, Additional Secretary, Ministry of External Affairs, and National Coordinator for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), presented a summary of the discussions during the first session. Expressing his views from the perspective of the SCO, he said that it had clearly emerged that the organisation now needed to move beyond its security-centric approach. He observed that several common themes had emerged during the discussions, including cultural networks, climate, youth, digitalisation, and joint projects.

He further noted that the discussions had highlighted the need to take culture beyond the confines of the state and government institutions and bring it closer to the people. Undoubtedly, he said, the Forum was a powerful medium for connecting hearts and minds.

During the joint session, several dignitaries and representatives shared their perspectives, including Azerbaijan’s Minister of Culture, Mr. Adil Karimli; Nepal’s Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Mr. Khadga Raj Poudel (Ganesh); Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musaddiq Masood Malik; and Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture, Ms. Matlubakhon Amonzoda Sattoriyon. Representatives from Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Cambodia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan, and other countries also participated.

In the subsequent session, scholars and experts from India and other countries shared their perspectives on the historical and cultural connections among civilisations. The speakers included Prof. Chandrashekhar from the Department of Persian, University of Delhi; Prof. Srikanth Kondapalli from Jawaharlal Nehru University; Indologist Shri Megh Kalyanasundaram; Dr. Sanjeev Kumar, Senior Research Fellow at the Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA); and Prof. Puneet Gaur from Jawaharlal Nehru University.

The third session, held in the afternoon, focused on ‘Art and Architecture Across Civilisations: Shared Aesthetics’. Titled ‘A Shared Cultural Canvas: Artistic and Architectural Exchanges Among SCO Nations’, the session explored the interconnections between the artistic traditions, architectural styles, and cultural influences of different countries.

The session was chaired by Shri Yadubir Singh Rawat, Director General, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), and moderated by Dr. Sanjay Kumar Manjul, Additional Director General, ASI. Her Excellency Ms. Sadat Yusifova, Deputy Minister of Culture of Azerbaijan, attended as the Special Speaker.

The fourth session of the day also focused on ‘Art and Architecture Across Civilisations: Shared Aesthetics’. Its special sub-theme was ‘Trade: Merchants, Monks and Monarchs – Diverging Networks to Converging Cultures’. The session was chaired by Shri Yadubir Singh Rawat, Director General, ASI, and moderated by Shri Jhanvi Sharma, Additional Director General, ASI.

The session deliberated on historical connections that developed between different regions through trade routes, travellers, Buddhist monks, and rulers, as well as their cultural impact. Representatives from various countries also shared their perspectives.

Thereafter, participants visited the exhibition ‘The Light and the Lotus: Relics of the Awakened One’ at the Rai Pithora Cultural Complex in New Delhi. The day's programme concluded with a cultural performance, followed by an official dinner hosted by the Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

The second day of the First SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum proved significant in exploring the shared cultural heritage, art, architecture, historical connections, and common civilizational values of different countries, while identifying new avenues for cooperation.

*****

M. Annadurai

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment NISD Exchanges 23 MoUs with Universities and Institutions Across India to Strengthen Social Defence Initiatives Institutional Partnerships Expand to 30, Promoting Prevention Education, Research, Training and Capacity Building Across Social Defence Areas MoUs to Strengthen Collaborative Efforts for Drug Abuse Prevention, Welfare of Senior Citizens, Transgender Welfare and Prevention of Beggary Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under Ministry of Social…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NISD Exchanges 23 MoUs with Universities and Institutions Across India to Strengthen Social Defence Initiatives
Institutional Partnerships Expand to 30, Promoting Prevention Education, Research, Training and Capacity Building Across Social Defence Areas
MoUs to Strengthen Collaborative Efforts for Drug Abuse Prevention, Welfare of Senior Citizens, Transgender Welfare and Prevention of Beggary
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, organised an MoU Exchange Ceremony at its campus in the National Capital, here today.

The ceremony was graced by Dr Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Dr Sandeep Rewaji Rathod, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment and Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director, NISD, New Delhi, and other senior officers of the Ministry.

On the occasion, 23 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) were exchanged between NISD and universities and institutions from across the country.

  

Out of these, 15 institutions participated in person and 8 institutions joined virtually. With this, NISD’s institutional partnerships have increased to 30, building upon the 7 MoUs signed earlier with universities and organisations.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar said the exchange of MoUs with 23 institutions across the country marks a significant and historic initiative towards strengthening the work of NISD through institutional collaboration.

He emphasised that partnerships with universities, rural development institutes and other reputed institutions can help advance training, capacity building, rehabilitation, livelihood opportunities and social inclusion for individuals affected by substance use, transgender persons, senior citizens and persons vulnerable to beggary.

The Minister said the initiative would strengthen efforts towards enabling vulnerable individuals to lead dignified, self-reliant lives and contribute meaningfully to society.

Dr Kumar underscored the need to have regular dialogue and consultations, review of initiatives and sharing of best practices among institutions would help extend effective interventions across different States and regions.

Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, highlighted the important role of educational institutions in preventing drug abuse among young people. He enjoined upon institutions to organise regular anti-drug awareness activities and pledges, enabling students to carry the message of drug prevention from their campuses to families, peers and communities. Shri Pant also stressed the need for regular coordination, monitoring and mutually beneficial training programmes between NISD and partner institutions.

The Secretary said that sustained awareness activities, including periodic anti-drug pledges in educational institutions, could help create a wider chain of awareness and collective action towards a drug-free India. He urged NISD and its partner institutions to explore regular coordination, monitoring and short-term training programmes within campuses to strengthen collaborative efforts in drug abuse prevention.

The 23 institutions include State Institute of Rural Development, Ranchi, Jharkhand; State Institute of Rural Development, Meghalaya; State Institute of Rural Development (SIRD), Manipur; Telangana Institute of Rural Development (TGIRD), Telangana; Central University of Andhra Pradesh; Central University of Karnataka; Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Lucknow; National Law University, Jodhpur; Shri Vishwakarma Skill University, Haryana; and Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University,

Karnataka.

In addition, CHRIST University, Bengaluru; Yenepoya (Deemed to be University), Karnataka; Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi; Aligarh Muslim University, Uttar Pradesh; Indian Adult Education Association, New Delhi; Andhra Pradesh State Institute of Panchayat Raj & Rural Development; AIIMS Jodhpur, Rajasthan; Administrative Training Centre, Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA), Puducherry; Kerala Institute of Local Administration (KILA), Kerala; Maharashtra National Law University, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar; Chanakya National Law University, Patna; Mahatma Gandhi Central University, Bihar; and Maharashtra National Law University, Nagpur, are among other institutions who signed MoUs with NISD.

The scope of these MoUs covers Prevention Education, Research, Training and Capacity Building, Curriculum Development, and Outreach and Advocacy in the field of Social Defence, including Drug Abuse Prevention, Welfare of Senior Citizens, Transgender Welfare and Prevention of Beggary.

The partnerships are expected to facilitate institutional collaboration, knowledge exchange, training opportunities and the development of effective interventions across these areas.

The Union Minister administered ‘Senior Citizen’ and ‘Anti Drug’ Pledges to the participants, refreshing the sense of responsibility towards working for creating awareness among common masses, to uphold respect,  dignity and and to ensure healthcare and welfare of the senior citizens besides Drug Abuse Prevention and treatment and rehabilitation of the persons affected by the substance abuse. 

The expanded network of institutional partnerships is expected to create a sustained framework for training, awareness generation, research and evidence-based interventions in the field of Social Defence.

Through collaboration with universities, public training institutions and specialised organisations across the country, NISD will further strengthen its efforts towards the welfare, rehabilitation, empowerment and social inclusion of vulnerable sections of society.

The initiative reinforces the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to strengthening institutional collaboration and advancing a socially secure, inclusive and empowered India.

Ms Anushka Bhardwaj, Junior Consultant at NISD, conducted the proceedings

Conceived by Prasar Bharati Chairman Padma…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Prasar Bharati Launches ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’ to Discover New Voices in Indian Storytelling, at IFFI 57
Ten participants pitch their original scripts before an eminent jury on the inaugural day; winners to be announced on November 24
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:34PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Prasar Bharati today inaugurated its first Script Pitching Lab, ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’, at Kala Academy, Panaji, as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Conceived by Prasar Bharati Chairman Padma Shri Prasoon Joshi, the initiative is envisioned as an annual national platform for emerging writers from across India to pitch original scripts in ten Indian languages across the categories of feature films, documentaries and short films.

Addressing the occasion, Prasoon Joshi emphasised the importance of authentic storytelling rooted in personal experiences and cultural perspectives. He said that Prasar Bharati is committed to nurturing distinct voices and providing a platform for stories emerging from different parts of the country. Every region and folk tradition in India, he observed, carries its own distinctive narratives, which can be truly told and understood through an appreciation of its native culture.

Doordarshan Director General Ms. Rina Sonowal Kouli delivered the welcome address and highlighted the role of the initiative in showcasing India's linguistic and creative diversity.

The pitching sessions feature ten participants presenting their original scripts before an eminent jury comprising Padma Shri Manoj Joshi, actor and National Film Award winner for Best Supporting Actor; Sandeep Balakrishna, author, editor and independent researcher in Indian history, culture and literature; Shree Narayan Singh, filmmaker and editor known for Toilet: Ek Prem Katha and Batti Gul Meter Chalu; and Anant Vijay, National Film Award-winning journalist, author and film critic, and Vice-Chairman of the Governing Council of FTII, Pune.

The inaugural event was attended by Shri Dhirendra Ojha, Principal Director General, Press Information Bureau; Shri Yogesh Kumar Baweja, Principal Director General and Press Registrar General of India (PRGI); and Shri Prithul Kumar, Joint Secretary (Broadcasting & Administration), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

The Script Pitching Lab is being held from November 21 to 23, 2026. Through this annual initiative, Prasar Bharati seeks to connect emerging writers with industry professionals and provide opportunities for their original ideas to be developed into screen productions across feature films, documentaries and short films.

The winners of ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’ will be announced on November 24, 2026.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Sixth Round of India–Canada CEPA Negotiations Concludes in New Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Canadian Minister Maninder Sidhu Reaffirm Commitment to a Balanced and Mutually Beneficial CEPA Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal and Canadian Vice Minister Mr. Glenn Purves review status of talks Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi The sixth round of negotiations for the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) was held in New Delhi from 11 to 20…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Sixth Round of India–Canada CEPA Negotiations Concludes in New Delhi
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Canadian Minister Maninder Sidhu Reaffirm Commitment to a Balanced and Mutually Beneficial CEPA
Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal and Canadian Vice Minister Mr. Glenn Purves review status of talks
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

The sixth round of negotiations for the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) was held in New Delhi from 11 to 20 November 2026. The Indian delegation was led by Dr. Brij Mohan Mishra, Chief Negotiator, while the Canadian delegation was led by Ms. Mary-Catherine Speirs, Chief Negotiator. The negotiations covered key areas, including Trade in goods, Trade in services, Rules of origin, Trade Remedies, Intellectual Property and Investment promotion.

The negotiating round opened with a warm and constructive meeting in New Delhi on 11 November between Shri Piyush Goyal, Minister of Commerce and Industry and Mr. Maninder Sidhu, Canada’s Minister of International Trade. Both Ministers underscored the importance of a balanced and mutually beneficial CEPA that delivers meaningful market access, builds on the complementarities of both economies and creates new opportunities for trade and investment. They reviewed progress in the negotiations and guided their teams to advance discussions productively.

The round witnessed constructive and substantive discussions across the negotiating tracks, with both sides making progress towards advancing the negotiations. The discussions were guided by the shared objective of concluding the negotiations within the ambitious timelines envisaged by the leaders of the two nations.

Towards the conclusion of the round, the Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal held a productive meeting with Mr. Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation in New Delhi. The meeting provided an opportunity to review the progress achieved during the sixth round of negotiations and take stock of the overall status of the India-Canada CEPA discussions. Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries.

It was underscored that the proposed CEPA would unlock new opportunities in trade and investment, strengthen resilient and diversified supply chains, and further deepen the economic partnership between India and Canada. The successful conclusion of the sixth round reflects the continued engagement and commitment of both sides towards advancing the negotiations and strengthening bilateral economic and commercial ties.

***

Abhishek Dayal/Abhijith Narayanan

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  participates in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
21st-century India can progress only by honouring skills; Therefore, over the past years, our government has taken a series of steps guided by the spirit of 'Shrameva Jayate': PM
When you learn a skill, you do not merely work on machines; you make people's lives easier and strengthen the nation's capabilities: PM
Today, India is advancing towards becoming the skill capital of the world: PM
I urge every young person in the country; the entire sky lies open before you today, dream big, hone your skills, and dedicate all your energy to fulfilling your dreams: PM
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi


Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister expressed happiness that Lucknow was chosen to host such a major skill development event, noting that as a Member of Parliament from Uttar Pradesh, it is a matter of pride for him as well.

Observing that the graduating youth have crossed an important milestone in their lives and are now set to join the process of nation-building directly, the Prime Minister emphasized that the skills and craftsmanship they acquired at ITIs serve as a major driving force for a Viksit Bharat. He added that any nation progresses capably in this very manner through the skills of its youth. Highlighting India's long-standing respect for craftsmanship, he cited Lucknow's Chikankari, fine muslin, Banaras and Kanjeevaram silk, Kashmir Pashmina, cotton textiles, Kalamkari, steel for the world's finest swords, and bronze and Panchdhatu idols as hundreds of traditional crafts that once formed society's foundational pillars. “For a long time, India's identity in the world has been through such skills,” observed PM Modi.

Explaining that India's earlier social system was structured around skills, the Prime Minister shared the example of Gujarat's Vasavaya tradition, under which skilled artisans who sustained village life settled wherever a new village was established. “These were such skilled people without whom it was difficult even to imagine village life,” remarked Shri Modi.

Pointing out that while such a system existed across every region of India since ancient times, it gradually lost importance, the Prime Minister recalled an exercise he assigned to officers as Chief Minister of Gujarat to list every task and service a person needs from waking up to sleeping and from birth to death, which yielded around one thousand essential skills that kept society moving. “I asked the officers to focus on this very thing, and then a modern ecosystem of skill development was created there in Gujarat,” noted PM Modi.

Attributing the decline of India's skill ecosystem to the colonial education system which reduced a skill-based society to producing paper clerks while the British advanced their own industry and manufacturing, the Prime Minister observed that clerical jobs came to be revered even after independence while skilled craftspeople were subjected to an inferiority complex and began shying away from their trades. “Our country has had to suffer a huge loss due to this mentality of slavery,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the government's successive initiatives driven by the spirit of Shrameva Jayate, including extending the tradition of convocations beyond college and university degree holders to ITI skill certificate recipients and placing strong emphasis on skill development in the new National Education Policy, the Prime Minister underscored the importance of honoring craftsmanship. “The India of the 21st century can move forward only by giving respect to skill,” asserted PM Modi.

Addressing widespread discussions and anxieties about Artificial Intelligence taking away jobs in the modern era, the Prime Minister recalled how during the COVID pandemic, when everyone felt helpless, it was skilled workers who managed critical operations and kept things running. “Understand this point of mine very well: whoever has skill, no one can take away their employment,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing that learning a craft goes beyond operating machines to making people's lives easier while strengthening national capability and manufacturing capacity, the Prime Minister highlighted the unprecedented focus on ITIs since 2014, noting that nearly 5,000 new ITIs have been built in a single decade. “The number of those studying in ITIs has also increased by more than 5 lakh, and in this too, the number of girls has become more than two and a half times,” noted PM Modi.

Highlighting the focus on training, quality, faculty, and infrastructure in ITIs, which had previously lagged behind with outdated trades, the Prime Minister noted that over 30 new-age trades have now been introduced, including Aeronautical Structure, Artificial Intelligence Assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician, Green Hydrogen Technician, Industrial Robotics, Electric Vehicles, Animation and Special Effects, and Semiconductor Technician, designed for both Indian and global needs alongside India's ongoing trade agreements and FTA discussions. “All of this is being done for you, the youth; new opportunities are being created for your future,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing efforts to modernize ITI curricula and machinery, train instructors in new technologies, and build direct links between training and industry, the Prime Minister highlighted the investment of 60,000 crore rupees under the PM-SETU scheme.“Our youth are going to benefit immensely from this,” affirmed PM Modi.

Noting that India's rapid development is generating vast employment opportunities for skilled workers, the Prime Minister pointed to the 50 crore people lifted out of poverty over the past 12 to 13 years through government facilities that instilled confidence. Citing mega campaigns such as building 4 crore houses for the poor, laying water pipelines, and delivering first-time electricity lines where electricians, carpenters, and other skilled youth found work, he underlined the scale of job creation. “In this mega campaign, lakhs and lakhs of new opportunities were also created for skilled workers in the country,” observed Shri Modi.

Highlighting rising skill demand across emerging sectors, the Prime Minister cited the disruption in gas supplies during the West Asia conflict a few months ago, when the government targeted at least one lakh PNG connections per day and review meetings repeatedly flagged a shortage of plumbers delaying targets, while pointing to huge skilled manpower needs in solar power and the burgeoning sports economy spanning sports equipment manufacturing and fitness. “If you are skilled, you have that many more opportunities to get employment,” asserted PM Modi.

Announcing that India is advancing toward becoming the skill capital of the world, the Prime Minister shared good news for youth and Uttar Pradesh that India will host the WorldSkills Asia competition in 2027 in Greater Noida, welcoming youth from numerous countries. “I extend advance best wishes to UP for this as well,” remarked Shri Modi.

Praising Uttar Pradesh for accelerating national development, the Prime Minister credited the present government under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for transforming the state into an expressway state with multiple international airports, major universities, flourishing tourism, large mobile manufacturing plants, an upcoming chip factory, and manufacturing of BrahMos, which shook the enemy in Operation Sindoor. “Because of all these development works happening in UP, new opportunities are being created for you youth,” observed PM Modi.

Recalling a recent interaction during a factory inauguration in his parliamentary constituency of Banaras where a young woman told him she now returns home comfortably even at 11 PM, the Prime Minister credited the current government under Yogi Adityanath for creating an environment of security, asserting that the sense of security and confidence of prosperity will build a Viksit Bharat, and extended his heartiest best wishes to all youth. “The entire sky is before you at this time; dream big, develop your skills, and put your full strength into fulfilling your dreams,” asserted Shri Modi.

item.title: “Becoming Is a Spiritual Journey That Continues at Every Moment”: Director Leena Yadav at IFFI 57

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Becoming Is a Spiritual Journey That Continues at Every Moment”: Director Leena Yadav at IFFI 57
Language is only one tool of communication; emotions transcend words, says filmmaker of Indian Panorama's opening non-feature film
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 8:13PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Language is only one of the many tools of communication, while human emotions can transcend linguistic barriers, said filmmaker Ms. Leena Yadav, director of the Ladakhi non-feature film Becoming, at a press conference on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Selected as the opening non-feature film of Indian Panorama 2026, Becoming explores a spiritual journey through the cultural landscape and traditions of Ladakh.

Reflecting on her experience of directing local, non-professional actors, Ms. Yadav said she communicated largely in Hindi, while many of the performers spoke Ladakhi and had limited familiarity with Hindi. Despite the language barrier, the actors were able to understand and express the emotions of their characters. The experience, she observed, reinforced the importance of listening, sensitivity and communication beyond words.

Written and directed by Ms. Yadav, Becoming follows Agyal, a young boy in Ladakh whose unusual bond with nature and memories seemingly drawn from another life lead him towards the ancient Likir Monastery. When he identifies belongings associated with a revered Rimpoche, the monks begin to believe that he may be the spiritual teacher's reincarnation. The film explores themes of rebirth, identity, destiny and the relationship between the past and the present.

Describing the film as a spiritual experience, Ms. Yadav explained that the idea of Becoming extends beyond the journey of its central character. It represents the continuous process of transformation in human life, which does not arrive at a definitive end. She also spoke about the influence of Buddhist philosophy and the distinctive landscapes of Ladakh on the film's narrative and visual language.

Recalling the origins of the project, producer and cinematographer Shri Aseem Bajaj said the film emerged from an opportunity to test camera equipment in demanding conditions. Rather than simply endorsing the equipment, he proposed making a short film in Ladakh. He offered Ms. Yadav three starting points: the title Becoming, the world of Buddhism and Ladakh as the setting. These elements gradually developed into a story as the filmmakers responded to the location and the people they encountered.

Speaking about the production process, the filmmakers said that a compact crew of 19 members from outside Ladakh worked with local collaborators to develop the script, cast non-professional actors and complete the shoot within 15 days, including the period required for acclimatisation to the high-altitude environment. Ms. Yadav noted that the process demanded flexibility, with the location and its people contributing to the unfolding of the film.

Shri Bajaj explained that the film used no visual effects, relying instead on the natural landscape and on-location cinematography. With temperatures reportedly falling to around minus 20 degrees Celsius, the team faced considerable physical challenges, although the equipment performed reliably. Both filmmakers spoke of being humbled by the scale of nature and by the warmth and hospitality of the people of Ladakh.

The filmmakers also reflected on local accounts and Buddhist traditions associated with reincarnation, which offered insights into the beliefs and cultural context within which the film is situated.

Sharing an interesting detail about the film's poster, Ms. Yadav recalled that its striking image of a young boy seen from behind and draped in red emerged from an unscripted moment during filming. The interplay of cloth, shadows and surrounding light created an image that, in the filmmakers' view, captured the spirit of Becoming.

Both Ms. Yadav and Shri Bajaj expressed gratitude for the film's selection as the opening non-feature film of Indian Panorama at IFFI 2026. The film's journey, shaped by human connections, cultural traditions and the natural landscape of Ladakh, offers audiences an opportunity to experience a story that reaches beyond linguistic and geographical boundaries.

The press conference was moderated by Shri Kiran Murali.

item.title: “Documentary Filmmaking Is an Intimate Process”: Julie Bertuccelli on Trust, Ethics and Social Responsibility, at IFFI 57
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting “Documentary Filmmaking Is an Intimate Process”: Julie Bertuccelli on Trust, Ethics and Social Responsibility, at IFFI 57 French filmmaker emphasises ethical engagement with communities, cinema's power to influence perceptions and the importance of human creativity Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 21 November 2026 Documentary filmmaking is not merely about capturing reality; it is also about earning trust, understanding lived experiences and accepting responsibility for how people's lives are…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Documentary Filmmaking Is an Intimate Process”: Julie Bertuccelli on Trust, Ethics and Social Responsibility, at IFFI 57
French filmmaker emphasises ethical engagement with communities, cinema's power to influence perceptions and the importance of human creativity
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 7:41PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Documentary filmmaking is not merely about capturing reality; it is also about earning trust, understanding lived experiences and accepting responsibility for how people's lives are represented. While documentary cinema brings audiences closer to realities and voices often unheard, portraying real lives also raises important questions about artistic freedom, privacy and ethical responsibility.

These questions formed the focus of an In-Conversation session titled ‘From Witness to Change: The Social Responsibility of Documentary Cinema’, held at Kala Academy, Panaji, on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Acclaimed French filmmaker and screenwriter Julie Bertuccelli was in conversation with National Award-winning Indian filmmaker Haobam Paban Kumar.

Describing documentary filmmaking as an intimate process, Bertuccelli observed that films can have a profound impact on the lives of their subjects and, in some cases, even put them at risk. She emphasised the importance of building trust, spending time with communities and allowing people to become comfortable with the presence of the camera. Observing people in their everyday environments, she noted, helps filmmakers understand how they see themselves and how they wish to be seen by society.

Reflecting on cinema's potential to influence social change, Bertuccelli said that films may not transform society overnight but can shape individual perceptions and encourage change. “If I just put a little bit of a seed in the brain of some people, this is a lot,” she observed. She added that she preferred films that offered hope and showcased positive examples, inspiring people to believe that change was possible.

Discussing her creative process, Bertuccelli explained that documentary ideas often emerge from unexpected encounters, places or subjects that spark curiosity. Referring to School of Babel and Since Otar Left, she observed that real-life experiences frequently provide the starting point for her films. While scripts and proposals are often necessary to secure funding, the actual filmmaking process remains open to the unpredictability of real life.

Recalling her professional journey, she spoke about spending nearly 15 years as an assistant to renowned directors, including Krzysztof Kieślowski, Rithy Panh and Bertrand Tavernier. Her work also took her across countries such as Russia, Georgia and Cambodia, providing her with experiences across different cultural and filmmaking environments.

Responding to a young filmmaker seeking advice on documenting sensitive social issues such as untouchability and patriarchy in his village, Bertuccelli underscored the importance of trust and sustained engagement. Filmmakers must demonstrate genuine interest in the communities they document and clearly communicate the purpose of their work, she said.

Offering an international perspective on documentary filmmaking, Bertuccelli discussed France's institutional support for the genre, including the contribution of cinema ticket revenues towards film financing and the role of protected theatrical windows. She also shared that preparations were underway for a retrospective of Indian documentaries in Paris in the coming years, acknowledging India's rich documentary filmmaking tradition.

Expressing reservations about the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Bertuccelli highlighted concerns relating to creativity, copyright and environmental costs, particularly the consumption of water and electricity. She cautioned that excessive dependence on AI could undermine human memory, independent thinking and creative authenticity.

Emphasising the distinctive value of documentary cinema, she observed that it captures something AI cannot replicate: the spontaneous emotions, silences, gestures and imperfections of real human interactions.

The session offered valuable insights into documentary filmmaking as an exercise in trust, ethical responsibility and human understanding, while highlighting cinema's enduring ability to bring overlooked realities into public consciousness and inspire meaningful change.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Our Endeavour Was to Represent India in Its Truest Sense Through Cinema”: Non-Feature Jury Chairperson Himansu Sekhar Khatua
Indian Panorama Jury shares insights into the rigorous selection process, diversity of Indian storytelling and evolving role of technology in filmmaking at IFFI 57
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 7:24PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

The Indian Panorama Non-Feature Film Jury at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) shared insights into the rigorous selection process, highlighting the diversity of Indian cinema, the power of storytelling and the evolving role of technology in filmmaking during a press conference held today. The interaction offered a glimpse into the deliberations behind selecting 20 films from an impressive pool of 358 entries.

The session featured Shri Himansu Sekhar Khatua, Chairperson of the Jury, along with jury members Smt. Aarti Patel, Shri Abhijeet Arvind Dalvi, Smt. Ragini Sona, Shri Shiv Sunny, Shri Shankhajeet De and Shri Dhanesh Yadhav T. R. The interaction was moderated by Shri Mahesh Kumar, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau.

Speaking about the philosophy underpinning the selection process, Shri Himansu Sekhar Khatua emphasised that the jury's foremost endeavour was to represent India in its truest sense through cinema. Referring to IFFI's theme, Stories Without Borders, he observed that the selected films sought to capture the country's multifaceted identities, lived experiences and cultural richness while reflecting the universal spirit of storytelling.

Elaborating on the selection procedure, Shri Khatua highlighted that the jury undertook a rigorous evaluation across multiple rounds, looking beyond conventional cinematic frameworks and mainstream sensibilities. The exercise involved identifying films that offered distinctive perspectives and compelling narratives from different parts of the country. He noted that the selected works collectively reflect India's diverse customs, traditions and cultural landscapes. Emphasising the jury's holistic approach, he explained that films were assessed in their entirety rather than judged on isolated elements such as style or storytelling.

Addressing the growing influence of Artificial Intelligence in filmmaking, Shri Khatua underscored that human imagination, sensibility and perspective remain distinctive and irreplaceable. While acknowledging AI's potential as a valuable creative tool, he maintained that technology should complement and enrich artistic expression rather than substitute the human mind behind it.

Sharing her experience, jury member Smt. Aarti Patel described the selection exercise as both overwhelming and immensely rewarding, particularly in view of the extraordinary range of subjects, themes and perspectives represented in the submissions. She observed that cinema transcends linguistic, geographical and cultural boundaries, serving as a universal language that brings people and communities closer.

Shri Abhijeet Arvind Dalvi remarked that the films offered the jury a panoramic glimpse of India, capturing its diverse social realities and cultural ethos through an array of distinctive cinematic voices. He highlighted how the submissions reflected the richness of the country's filmmaking traditions and the varied ways in which filmmakers interpret their surroundings.

Describing her association with the jury as a valuable learning experience, Smt. Ragini Sona appreciated the festival's theme, Stories Without Borders, calling it beautiful and meaningful. She emphasised the significance of stories that transcend boundaries and connect audiences through shared human experiences.

Shri Shiv Sunny drew attention to cinema's transformative power, emphasising that meaningful storytelling can extend beyond entertainment to provoke thought, shape perspectives and inspire positive social change.

The press conference provided an opportunity to understand the jury's approach to film selection and the considerations involved in identifying works for Indian Panorama. By bringing together stories rooted in different regions, cultures and lived experiences, the selection reaffirms Indian Panorama's role in showcasing the richness of Indian cinema and its ability to connect audiences across geographical and cultural boundaries.
