item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
BHASHINI Concludes Participation at Global Digital Health Summit 2026, Highlights Role of Multilingual AI in Building Inclusive and Empathetic Healthcare
DIBD, CEO - Amitabh Nag Delivers Keynote Address On Breaking Language Barriers In Healthcare Through AI, Highlighting The Importance Of Empathy And Patient-Centric Care
BHASHINI Showcases Healthcare Applications, Data Daan For Health And Interactive AI Demonstrations
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, concluded its participation at the Global Digital Health Summit (GDHS) 2026, held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 20–21 November 2026. Across the two-day summit, BHASHINI showcased its multilingual Artificial Intelligence (AI) ecosystem and demonstrated how language technologies can strengthen healthcare delivery, facilitate clinical workflows and enable more accessible, inclusive and patient-centric healthcare experiences.

On the concluding day of the summit, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, Digital India BHASHINI Division, delivered a keynote address titled "Breaking Language Barriers in Healthcare Through AI: Sharing BHASHINI's Model of Removing Linguistic Barriers Using AI." The address highlighted the need to integrate language intelligence into digital healthcare infrastructure, ensuring that patients can understand, communicate and access healthcare services in their preferred languages.

Emphasising that language is a critical yet often overlooked layer of digital healthcare, the keynote explored how multilingual AI can support communication between doctors and patients, simplify clinical documentation and improve access to medical information. It also highlighted the importance of empathy in healthcare, recognising that healing extends beyond diagnosis and medication to the human connection between doctors, caregivers and patients.

When care is communicated in a patient's own language, whether Bodo, Marathi, Punjabi or Maithili, it can feel more familiar, reassuring and accessible. The ability to express care, reassurance and understanding in a language that patients relate to can foster comfort, trust and a stronger connection with healthcare professionals. Through BHASHINI's language technologies, such interactions can become more inclusive and compassionate, helping ensure that patients feel heard and understood.

The keynote also highlighted BhashaDaan for Health, reflecting the importance of community-driven contributions in developing language resources for healthcare and strengthening multilingual AI capabilities for medical and public health applications.

Data Daan for Health was highlighted as an initiative to build multilingual healthcare datasets by capturing colloquial expressions used by people to describe symptoms and health conditions, alongside their corresponding medical terminology. The focus is on documenting how people naturally communicate health concerns in their everyday language, including regional phrases and commonly used expressions that may not directly correspond to formal medical vocabulary. For instance, a phrase such as "पैर में पानी भर गया है" can be mapped to the medical term Oedema. By capturing such expressions across Indian languages and mapping them to standard medical terminology, the initiative aims to help AI systems better understand how people describe their symptoms, recognise health-related concerns and facilitate more effective communication between patients and healthcare professionals.

At the BHASHINI exhibition stall, demonstrations continued across healthcare-focused applications and multilingual AI capabilities. The exhibition featured use cases from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), and the Directorate General of Medical Services, Indian Army, showcasing the application of speech and language technologies in clinical settings.

At JIPMER, the integration of e-BHASHINI with the e-Sushrut Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) enables voice-based documentation of clinical histories, IPD notes and discharge instructions. At AIIMS, demonstrations highlighted speech technologies supporting doctor-patient conversations across languages, alongside the integration of BHASHINI's speech-to-text facility with NIC's eHospital prescription module. The Directorate General of Medical Services (Army) showcased the use of BHASHINI's capabilities in i- Dhanwantri, where doctors' spoken clinical notes are converted into typed text to support medical documentation.

The stall also featured demonstrations highlighting multilingual conversations between doctors and patients, showcasing how BHASHINI's speech and language technologies can facilitate communication across languages, support patient understanding and make healthcare interactions more accessible and inclusive.

An interactive AI-powered healthcare persona was also demonstrated at the BHASHINI stall, illustrating how conversational and voice-enabled AI can facilitate more accessible interactions and make technology-based healthcare experiences more engaging and intuitive.

Other demonstrations included the BHASHINI mobile application, showcasing its translation and voice-based capabilities; Shrutlekh, supporting real-time multilingual transcription and translation; Data Daan for Health, a community-driven initiative to build medical language datasets by capturing colloquial expressions used to describe symptoms and health conditions, alongside their corresponding medical terminology; and Granthika, BHASHINI's guided platform for collecting and digitising written and oral language resources.

Through its participation at GDHS 2026, BHASHINI highlighted how multilingual AI can extend beyond language translation to become an enabling layer across healthcare systems. By bringing together institutional use cases, speech technologies, medical language resources and community-led contributions, the exhibition and keynote reinforced the importance of making healthcare more accessible, efficient, empathetic and responsive to India's linguistic diversity.

About Digital India BHASHINI Division

The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is building a national ecosystem for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and enables the integration of Language AI capabilities across government and public-facing digital services. The BHASHINI ecosystem has recorded over 11 billion inferences, with approximately 24 million inferences being processed daily, reflecting the growing adoption of its multilingual AI technologies. Its ecosystem includes technologies for translation, speech recognition, speech synthesis, transliteration and other language services, helping make digital information and services more accessible across India's linguistic diversity.

About GDHS 2026

The Global Digital Health Summit (GDHS) 2026 was held on 20–21 November 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme "Implementing Artificial Intelligence – AI in Action". The summit brought together stakeholders from government, healthcare, industry and academia to explore the practical implementation of AI in healthcare through technology exhibitions, demonstrations, scientific discussions and interactions focused on advancing digital health solutions and their adoption across healthcare systems.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President graces 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai
Preserving Tamil language,culture and identity goes hand in hand with strengthening the nation: Vice-President
Research and innovation will shape the future; students must prepare themselves for it: Vice-President
Education must go beyond academic excellence to build responsible and compassionate citizens: Vice-President
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School at Kottivakkam, Chennai, the Vice-President paid rich tributes to K.Kamaraj, recalling his selfless leadership, simplicity and commitment to public welfare.

He said that as long as the legacy of the great leader K. Kamaraj lives in Tamil soil, no force in the world can erase the spirit of nationalism from Tamil Nadu.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, graced the 42nd Annual Day celebrations of Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School at Kottivakkam, Chennai, today. Highlighting the importance of scientific temper, research and responsible use of AI, he appreciated the school’s Atal Tinkering Labs for nurturing young innovators. He called upon students to dream big, work hard and combine academic excellence with strong values, discipline and a spirit of service to the nation.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 21, 2026

He said that Kamaraj’s achievements in infrastructure and education remain unparalleled. Recalling the construction of several major dams during his tenure, he observed that the foundation laid by Kamaraj had been instrumental in making Tamil Nadu a state admired for its educational achievements and human resources. He described Kamaraj as a leader who never considered electoral gains or personal interests, but always placed public welfare above everything else.

Recalling Kamaraj’s contribution to the expansion of the school midday meal programme, the Vice-President said it reflected his commitment to ensuring that children from disadvantaged backgrounds had access to both education and nutrition.

Appreciating the Nellai Thoothukudi Nadar Mahamai Paripalana Sangam for its contribution to education, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan said that the school, established in 1985 with just 85 students and seven teachers, had grown into an institution serving around 3,500 students with nearly 200 teachers and staff. He said this growth represented the fulfilment of the aspirations of thousands of families, particularly those from economically and socially disadvantaged backgrounds.

Emphasising that education must go beyond academic performance, he said schools must nurture students with strong values, compassion and a sense of social responsibility.

Referring to the Atal Tinkering Lab at the school, the Vice-President encouraged students to develop scientific temper, research aptitude and innovative thinking. He said India was making significant strides in research and development, and called upon students to prepare themselves to excel in research, innovation and new discoveries.

Highlighting the National Education Policy 2020, introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said it emphasised holistic development, mother-tongue education, experiential learning, vocational skills, research and innovation. He stressed the need to move beyond rote learning towards conceptual understanding and creative thinking.

The Vice-President also emphasised that scientific and technological progress must remain rooted in India’s cultural heritage and human values. He said that the preservation of Tamil language, culture and heritage was intrinsically linked to the strength of the nation. “If Tamil culture, the Tamil people and the Tamil language are to be protected, Bharat must remain strong,” he said.

Referring to India’s vision of becoming a developed nation by 2047, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan called upon students to contribute to the nation’s progress through knowledge, innovation and dedication. He urged them to dream big, uphold integrity and achieve their goals through hard work and perseverance, without resorting to shortcuts.

During the occasion, the Vice-President inaugurated the Sports Auditorium and the Men’s Hostel of Nellai Nadar Engineering College.

The Vice-President also paid floral tributes to the statues of Thiruvalluvar and Thiru K. Kamaraj at Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, paid floral tributes to the statues of Thiruvalluvar and Thiru K. Kamaraj at Nellai Nadar Matriculation Higher Secondary School, Kottivakkam, Chennai, during the school’s 42nd Annual Day celebrations today. https://t.co/eskoYmJGVl

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 21, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Humour Is an Intelligent Way to Approach Life”: Spain’s Looking for Michael Makes World Premiere at IFFI 57
A musical road film inspired by a real-life woman's journey explores resilience, friendship and the power of laughter in confronting life's challenges
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 6:54PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

What happens when life's hardships are met with laughter? Spain's Looking for Michael (Persiguiendo a Michael), a 2026 comedy-drama directed by Juana Macías, explores this through a heartwarming story of courage, friendship and resilience. The film had its world premiere today at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), being held in Panaji, Goa.

The film follows Sonia, a young woman diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, who chooses to face her circumstances with courage and a renewed outlook on life. Supported by members of her music therapy group, who are also living with the condition, she embarks on a journey to meet renowned actor Michael J. Fox, who has publicly spoken about living with Parkinson's disease. Blending music and humour, the road film explores the determination to live life on one's own terms, even in the face of adversity.

Inspired by the journey and dream of a real-life woman, Yess Andréz, who was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in her mid-thirties, the film draws warmth and authenticity from her experiences. Its close observation of everyday life lends an emotional honesty to the narrative, bringing the challenges and aspirations of its characters to the screen.

Speaking at the session, director Juana Macías observed, “Humour is an intelligent way to approach life.” She noted that everyone encounters difficulties at some point, whether through illness, profound loss or other unexpected challenges. According to her, this universality gives the film its wider appeal, allowing its central message to resonate with audiences across borders and generations, in keeping with the theme of the 57th IFFI.

Actor Lorena López, who plays Doris, spoke about what drew her to the character's resilience, spirited personality and friendship with Sonia, played by Nuria Herrero. Doris, who uses a wheelchair, becomes both a friend and a guide to Sonia during her journey, highlighting the importance of companionship and mutual support in confronting life's challenges.

Macías also shared her approach to directing the actors, explaining that she encouraged improvisation during rehearsals and filming. She noted that improvisation is particularly valuable in comedy, helping actors develop natural relationships and interactions between their characters.

Speaking about the role of music in the film, Macías explained that the songs reflect Sonia's evolving relationship with her condition and are closely woven into the characters' emotions and experiences. Referring to the film's opening song, she described how it touches upon Sonia's daily routine of taking eight pills to manage her condition, using music to bring an everyday reality into the film's emotional narrative.

On the research behind the film, Macías spoke about her extensive interviews with Yess Andréz and other people living with Parkinson's disease. She emphasised that an authentic and honest understanding of people's experiences is essential when bringing their stories to the screen.

Responding to a question on how Spanish films can connect with Indian and international audiences, Macías observed that music and stories of overcoming adversity have universal appeal. She also spoke about plans to collaborate with Spanish and international OTT platforms to reach a wider audience.

The film's world premiere at IFFI brought to the festival a story that transcends geographical and cultural boundaries, reminding audiences of the enduring power of humour, music and human connection in navigating life's uncertainties.

The session was moderated by Shri Kuldeep Meena.

 

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
ITRA, Jamnagar Organises Three National CME Programmes, Bringing Together 90 Ayurveda Faculty Members from 13 States
Six-Day Programmes Focus on Strengthening Diagnostic Competencies, Clinical Skills and Teaching Capabilities
Around 45 Experts from Reputed Institutions Participate as Resource Persons
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, organised three simultaneous six-day National Continuing Medical Education (CME) programmes from 16 to 21 November 2026. Conducted by the Departments of Kriya Sharir, Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan, and Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga, the programmes brought together 90 Ayurveda faculty members from 13 states. Around 45 eminent academicians, clinicians and healthcare experts from reputed institutions participated as resource persons.=

The programmes were conducted under the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, with the objective of strengthening subject-specific knowledge, diagnostic competencies, clinical skills and teaching capabilities of Ayurveda faculty members. They also focused on integrating classical Ayurvedic principles with contemporary medical knowledge and diagnostic methodologies.

At the inaugural session, Prof. (Dr.) Tanuja Nesari emphasised the importance of continuous professional development, scientific understanding of diagnostic methodologies and the integration of contemporary medical knowledge with the classical foundations of Ayurveda. Resource persons contributed through expert lectures, interactive discussions and practical sessions, facilitating interdisciplinary learning and exchange of academic and clinical experiences.

The CME chairpersons, including Prof. Shilpa Donga, Prof. Darshana Pandya and Dr. Swati Khandale, highlighted the importance of patient-centred healthcare, accurate diagnosis, clinical reasoning, evidence-based research and contemporary teaching methodologies in improving Ayurveda education and clinical services.

CME by the Department of Kriya Sharir

The CME organised by the Department of Kriya Sharir focused on strengthening the understanding of human physiology through classical Ayurvedic perspectives and contemporary scientific developments. The sessions explored the integration of traditional Ayurvedic concepts with modern physiological knowledge to enhance teaching and clinical understanding.

CME by the Department of Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan: ‘MADHAV MIMAMSA-2026’

The Department of Roganidan and Vikriti Vigyan organised its CME under the title ‘MADHAV MIMAMSA-2026’, focusing on strengthening diagnostic competencies through the integration of classical Ayurvedic diagnostic principles with contemporary medical techniques.

The six-day programme covered subjects such as Nadi Pariksha, modern teaching methodologies, clinical diagnosis, advanced laboratory investigations, electrocardiography (ECG), computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The sessions highlighted systematic clinical assessment and the appropriate use of diagnostic investigations in disease evaluation.

CME by the Department of Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga

The Department of Prasuti Tantra and Streeroga conducted a six-day CME for teachers, covering key developments in obstetrics and gynaecology and their integration with classical Ayurvedic principles.

The academic sessions addressed Garbhini Paricharya, high-risk pregnancy, infertility and assisted reproductive techniques (ART), recurrent pregnancy loss, obstetric emergencies, puerperal care, contraception, breast diseases, congenital anomalies and gynaecological disorders.

Practical training and demonstrations included episiotomy and suturing techniques, colposcopy, Pap smear, vaginal smear, culture techniques and antenatal ultrasonography. The role of Panchakarma procedures in Stree Roga and Vandhyatva was also discussed in the context of integrative women's healthcare.

The three CME programmes provided a national platform for professional development, interdisciplinary knowledge exchange and capacity building among Ayurveda faculty members. The initiative reinforced the importance of diagnostic accuracy, clinical competence, research orientation and contemporary teaching methodologies in strengthening Ayurveda education and healthcare delivery.

The programmes reflect ITRA, Jamnagar's continued commitment to advancing Ayurveda education, research and clinical practice through faculty development and the integration of classical knowledge with contemporary scientific approaches.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Beyond the Screen: IFFI 2026 Brings India's Cinematic Legacy to the Printed Page
Two publications released by Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, spotlight cinematic thought, creative journeys and the unfinished legacy of filmmaker Awtar Kaul
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 6:02PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Cinema captures the imagination of generations, reflecting society, preserving memories and shaping cultural identities. Beyond the moving images on screen, books play an equally important role in documenting the ideas, creative processes and journeys that shape the cinematic landscape. Recognising this significance, the Publications Division released two books at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, celebrating different dimensions of India's cinematic heritage.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, emphasised the importance of documenting the creative journeys behind films and preserving India's rich cinematic heritage for posterity. He observed that cinema is not merely a medium of entertainment but also a reflection of society, the spirit of different generations and evolving ideas. “Films tell us a story. Books on cinema help us understand how these stories came to life,” he said, highlighting how publications offer valuable insights into the experiences of filmmakers, the evolution of cinematic techniques and the ideas that have shaped Indian cinema.

The two books released on the occasion were Cinema: Vividh Aayam, compiled by Shri Rajendra Bhatt, and Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story, authored by Shri Vinod Kaul. While the former brings together important writings and perspectives on cinema, making them accessible to Hindi readers, the latter documents the life and unfinished creative legacy of filmmaker Awtar Kaul.

Referring to Cinema: Vividh Aayam, Shri Chanchal Kumar appreciated the collection of writings by filmmakers and scholars, offering insights into celebrated films, filmmaking and world cinema. He particularly appreciated the effort to make these works accessible to Hindi readers. Speaking about Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story, he recalled the legacy of filmmaker Awtar Kaul, whose only film, 27 Down (1974), became a landmark of Indian New Wave cinema.

Congratulating the Publications Division, Shri Rajendra Bhatt, Shri Vinod Kaul and all those associated with the publications, the Secretary expressed hope that the books would inspire students, filmmakers and cinema enthusiasts to explore India's cinematic heritage more deeply.

Ms. Kanchan Prasad, Director General, Publications Division, highlighted the Division's longstanding association with cinema and its role in documenting India's cultural and creative heritage. Observing that while cinema captures moments in time, books ensure that these moments are preserved, she spoke about the Division's efforts to document creative journeys, preserve stories and celebrate the contributions of those who have shaped India's cultural identity.

Shri Rajendra Bhatt elaborated on the editorial journey behind Cinema: Vividh Aayam, explaining how the Publications Division took forward the initiative of bringing important writings on cinema to Hindi readers.

The session was moderated by Ms. Smita Vats Sharma, Director General, Press Information Bureau, in the presence of Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, and Dr. K. K. Nirala, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

About the Books

Awtar Kaul: The (In)Complete Story

Authored in English by Shri Vinod Kaul, the book chronicles the life and unfinished legacy of filmmaker Awtar Kaul through letters, photographs, memories and conversations. His only film, 27 Down (1974), became a milestone of Indian New Wave cinema and won the National Film Award. The award was announced on the very day he tragically drowned in Mumbai at the age of 34 while attempting to save a friend.

Cinema: Vividh Aayam

Compiled in Hindi by Shri Rajendra Bhatt, this anthology brings together adapted articles and dialogues from FTII's magazine Lensight. It offers insights into film history, cinematography, world cinema and the creative processes behind filmmaking, bringing diverse perspectives on cinema to a wider Hindi readership.

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah congratulates NCB and US DEA on the exemplary success of Operation Monsoon Thunder, jointly launched to scuttle cross-border drug trafficking
The arrests made and seizures effected in India and the US under this campaign stand as a testament to the power of the India-US partnership in curbing the menace of drugs
Under the leadership of PM Modi Ji, we are firmly committed to ensuring that neither a gram of narcotics enters India nor leaves for other countries
US Ambassador to India also commended the Operation Monsoon Thunder, highlighting the joint success of NCB and US DEA
US Ambassador thanks Home Minister Shri Amit Shah for his leadership
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 5:55PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has congratulated the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) on the exemplary success of Operation Monsoon Thunder, jointly launched to scuttle cross-border drug trafficking.

The Home Minister posted on X, “Heartiest congratulations to the NCB and the US DEA on the exemplary success of Operation Monsoon Thunder, jointly launched to scuttle cross-border drug trafficking. The arrests made and seizures effected in India and the US under this campaign stand as a testament to the power of the India-US partnership in curbing the menace of drugs. Under the leadership of PM Modi Ji, we are firmly committed to ensuring that neither a gram of narcotics enters India nor leaves for other countries.”

Heartiest congratulations to the NCB and the US DEA on the exemplary success of Operation Monsoon Thunder, jointly launched to scuttle cross-border drug trafficking. The arrests made and seizures effected in India and the US under this campaign stand as a testament to the power of the India-US partnership in curbing the menace of drugs. Under the leadership of PM Modi Ji, we are firmly committed to ensuring that neither a gram of narcotics enters India nor leaves for other countries.

— Amit Shah (@AmitShah) November 21, 2026

Shri Sergio Gor, US Ambassador to India, also commended the Operation Monsoon Thunder, highlighting the joint success of NCB and US DEA.

US Ambassador posted on X, “A great example of the U.S.-India partnership in action! Under Operation Monsoon Thunder, India’s Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in close coordination with the U.S. DEA disrupted a transnational drug trafficking network supplying illegal drugs to consumers across the United States - and apprehended six individuals. Thank you, Home Minister @AmitShah, for your leadership.

A great example of the U.S.-India partnership in action! Under Operation Monsoon Thunder, India’s @narcoticsbureau, in close coordination with the U.S. @DEAHQ, disrupted a transnational drug trafficking network supplying illegal drugs to consumers across the United States - and apprehended six individuals. Thank you, Home Minister @AmitShah, for your leadership.

— Ambassador Sergio Gor (@USAmbIndia) November 21, 2026

Key Operational Outcomes: 

  • 6 persons arrested across 4 Indian cities 
  • Approximately 3,000 parcels involving nearly 500 thousand tablets identified which were shipped within USA
  • Data relating to over 59,000 US subjects shared with US DEA 
  • 2 live consignments intercepted by US DEA 

The operation underscores the strength of India–US law enforcement cooperation and the commitment of both agencies to dismantling transnational drug trafficking networks. Further investigation is underway to identify the masterminds, dropshipers, trace financial proceeds and establish wider international linkages.

****

item.title: “Why Should I Be Perfect by Someone Else’s Standards?”: Girish Kasaravalli Champions Cultural Authenticity at IFFI 57
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting “Why Should I Be Perfect by Someone Else’s Standards?”: Girish Kasaravalli Champions Cultural Authenticity at IFFI 57 Society’s Cruel Process of ‘Othering’ Has Always Been at the Heart of My Stories: Girish Kasaravalli Reflects on 50 Years of Parallel Cinema at 57th IFFI Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 21 November 2026 Cinema, for Girish Kasaravalli, is not merely the art of telling stories; it is the courage to confront the stories society refuses to see. From caste and social hierarchies to…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Why Should I Be Perfect by Someone Else’s Standards?”: Girish Kasaravalli Champions Cultural Authenticity at IFFI 57
Society’s Cruel Process of ‘Othering’ Has Always Been at the Heart of My Stories: Girish Kasaravalli Reflects on 50 Years of Parallel Cinema at 57th IFFI
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 21 November 2026

 

Cinema, for Girish Kasaravalli, is not merely the art of telling stories; it is the courage to confront the stories society refuses to see. From caste and social hierarchies to religious hegemony and the marginalisation of vulnerable communities, the process of ‘othering’ has remained a recurring concern throughout his five-decade-long cinematic journey. This philosophy took centre stage at the ‘In Conversation’ session, ‘The Moral Universe of Parallel Cinema: 50 Years of Girish Kasaravalli’, held today at Kala Academy, Goa, during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).

Tracing his remarkable cinematic journey from his 1977 debut Ghatashraddha to acclaimed films such as Tabarana Kathe, Thaayi Saheba and Dweepa, the celebrated Kannada filmmaker and 14-time National Film Award laureate challenged the conventional divide between commercial and art-house cinema, emphasising that every cinematic expression carries an ideological position. “There is nothing called ‘only entertainment’. Even entertainment is a political form,” he remarked, underscoring that filmmakers inevitably either endorse or challenge dominant social ideologies.

Reflecting on the evolution of New Kannada Cinema, he spoke about the need to develop an indigenous cinematic language rooted in India's social and cultural realities rather than borrowed frameworks. “Style is not imposed on a film; it comes from within the content itself,” he observed. Articulating his storytelling philosophy, he added, “The plot of the story is not important, but the vision of the story is important.” He identified ‘othering’—the marginalisation and exclusion of vulnerable communities—as a recurring concern at the heart of his films.

Rejecting simplistic moral conclusions, Kasaravalli explained that cinema should provoke thought rather than prescribe judgments. Invoking writer U.R. Ananthamurthy's philosophy of ending every answer with a ‘but’, he said, “To say through a film that ‘this is right, this is wrong’ itself is wrong. I don't make easy judgments, because that forces the audience to think.”

The conversation also explored the portrayal of women and their remarkable resilience in his films. Referring to Dweepa, he highlighted protagonist Nagi's pragmatic approach to adversity, recalling her words: “Let me make the present pleasant.” He observed that women often demonstrate an extraordinary ability to negotiate changing circumstances and confront life's uncertainties.

Sharing insights into his creative process, Kasaravalli explained his preference for meticulously detailed scripts over storyboards, enabling his collaborators to translate his visual imagination onto the screen. “Cinema is germinated in my mind, but it is executed by others,” he said, underscoring the collaborative nature of filmmaking. He added that cinema is ultimately about imparting an experience, not merely making statements.

Concluding with a passionate appeal for cultural authenticity, he invoked Julio García Espinosa's philosophy of ‘imperfect cinema’, urging Indian filmmakers to remain rooted in their own cultural and visual identities rather than measure themselves against externally imposed standards. “Why should I be ‘perfect’ by someone else's standards? I should be loyal to my own milieu,” he affirmed.

The session offered an illuminating retrospective of a filmmaker whose five-decade-long contribution to Indian cinema continues to challenge conventions, interrogate social hierarchies and explore the complexities of human dignity and conscience. His reflections also served as a reminder that the strength of Indian cinema lies in its ability to find its own voice, rooted in the country's diverse cultural experiences.

The session was moderated by acclaimed film journalist, critic and author Naman Ramachandran.

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh Hosts Lunch for  Delhi University and JNU students hailing from J&K, mostly Jammu region
Dr. Jitendra Singh Assures Jammu Students in Delhi of Support; Says They Can Reach Out to Him as Their “Local Guardian”
Students Discuss Hostel Concerns, Career Opportunities, Employment Prospects and Issues Related to J&K
Students Appreciate Dr Jitendra Singh's Development Initiatives and Government Schemes in Jammu; Dr. Jitendra Singh Shares Experiences from His Student Days
Minister Encourages Students to Become Good Learners and Strengthen Jammu’s Representation on National and International Platforms
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh today  hosted a lunch at his residence in New Delhi for Delhi University (DU) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) students hailing from Jammu & Kashmir, mostly from Jammu, who are pursuing higher education in various institutions of Delhi.

During the interaction, the Minister assured the students that they could reach out to him directly for any problem, assistance or facilitation required during their stay in Delhi, saying he was like their “local guardian”.

Dr. Jitendra Singh encouraged them to pursue their academic and professional aspirations with confidence and appreciated the growing number of students from Jammu and Kashmir moving to Delhi for higher education in diverse disciplines, including specialised subjects such as European Studies and International Studies.

The interaction brought together students from Delhi University, JNU, Delhi School of Economics, and other academic streams. Many of the students including Sachiv Sharma, Atavika Chandan, Karmang Raina, Saksham Khajuria, Palak Jasrotia, Monalika Sharma, Aditya Jamwal, Migrank Magotra, Abhishek Khajuria, Vanshika Sumbria, Dheeraj Kumar, Shivam Rajput and Aditya Baru participated in the interaction, sharing their experiences, aspirations and concerns.

The students discussed issues concerning hostel accommodation, career opportunities, employment prospects and other matters affecting the youth from J&K. They also raised issues related to Jammu and exchanged views on the region's development and future prospects. Students expressed appreciation for the Government’s efforts, development initiatives and schemes in Jammu, reflecting their positive perspective on the progress being undertaken in the region.

Dr. Jitendra Singh encouraged the students to cultivate the habit of being good learners, remain curious and continuously expand their knowledge beyond formal academic pursuits. Sharing experiences from his own student days, he spoke about the importance of learning, perseverance and staying connected with one's roots while pursuing opportunities in wider academic and professional arenas.

The interaction also included discussion on strengthening the representation of Jammu’s youth on national and international platforms, enabling them to contribute to wider discourse, opportunities and emerging fields.

Accommodation and dining-related concerns raised by the students, including issues concerning hostel facilities and the mess, were immediately taken up by the Minister with the concerned authorities of Delhi University for necessary attention. The students also suggested introducing a few additional dishes in the dining menu of the University mess and canteen, adding a lighter and personal dimension to the interaction.

Reiterating his assurance of support, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the students should not hesitate to contact him whenever they face any difficulty or require any assistance in Delhi. The interaction brought together student welfare, mentorship and an exchange of views on J&K’s development, with the Minister encouraging young people to make the most of their educational opportunities and emerge as confident contributors to the nation.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to participate in Cooperative Function and launch various development projects of Arunachal Pradesh at Itanagar on November 22, 2026
Important initiative to strengthen the cooperative movement and give fresh impetus to the rural economy of Arunachal Pradesh, in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’
Shri Amit Shah to unveil ‘Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047’ and felicitate outstanding-performing cooperative societies
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation to distribute loan and registration certificates to cooperative institutions and interact with members of women Self-Help Groups and cooperative societies
Shri Amit Shah to launch four major development initiatives worth ₹5,610.95 crore, including Mission Shikshit Arunachal – Phase II, power development, rural road development and 199 projects under the Vibrant Villages Programme
Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate a foodgrain storage warehouse at Raga LAMPS and launch an e-commerce webpage for products of the Arunachal State Rural Livelihoods Mission
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation to flag off a Mobile Medical Van and inaugurate the SARAS Mela
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will participate in a Cooperative Function at the Dorjee Khandu State Convention Centre in Itanagar, the capital of Arunachal Pradesh, on Sunday, November 22, 2026, and launch various development schemes of the State. In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the event will mark an important step towards strengthening the cooperative sector and making it more empowered, self-reliant and inclusive. Several significant initiatives related to strengthening cooperative institutions, expanding rural livelihoods, women’s empowerment, financial inclusion and the overall development of the State will be undertaken during the programme. The event will also be attended by Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju, Deputy Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Chowna Mein, Agriculture Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Gabriel Denwang Wangsu and other dignitaries.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will launch several important development schemes of Arunachal Pradesh. These include ‘Mission Shikshit Arunachal – Phase II’, with an outlay of ₹1,500 crore; the ‘Chief Minister’s Comprehensive State Power Development Programme’, with an outlay of ₹2,000 crore; and the ‘Chief Minister’s Comprehensive State Rural Road Development Programme’, with an outlay of ₹2,000 crore. In addition, 199 projects worth ₹110.95 crore under the Vibrant Villages Programme will be launched across 11 border districts of the State. Shri Amit Shah will also launch ‘Mission SURAKSHA’. These initiatives aim to strengthen education, power and road infrastructure, promote the development of border areas and improve public welfare facilities across the State.

Several important initiatives will also be undertaken to strengthen infrastructure and market access in the cooperative sector. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will remotely inaugurate a foodgrain storage warehouse constructed at Raga LAMPS under the Foodgrain Storage Scheme. This will help strengthen storage facilities at the local level and expand the role of cooperative institutions. Shri Amit Shah will also launch an e-commerce webpage for products of the Arunachal Pradesh State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ArSRLM). This initiative is expected to provide wider market access to rural products through digital platforms and promote the economic activities of women Self-Help Groups.

During the programme, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will unveil the ‘Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047’. The vision document will mark an important initiative towards the long-term development of the cooperative movement in the State. Shri Amit Shah will also felicitate cooperative societies that have demonstrated outstanding performance in various sectors. Namsai Dairy Cooperative Society will receive the ‘Cooperation Award’; Lower Subansiri Fish Farmers Cooperative Society will be recognised as the Best Fisheries Cooperative Society; Kemli LAMPS will be recognised as the Best Handloom, Textile and Weavers Cooperative Society; and Jang LAMPS will be recognised as the Best PACS/LAMPS.

With the objective of expanding the financial capacity and activities of cooperative institutions, financial assistance and other facilities will be extended to various cooperative societies during the event. The National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) will provide a loan sanction certificate to Lagun Multipurpose Cooperative Society Limited. The Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) will distribute vegetable seed mini-kits. In addition, NABARD will provide a Micro-ATM to Poma Jute Dairy and Livestock Cooperative Society, while the Arunachal Pradesh State Cooperative Apex Bank Limited will provide a loan sanction certificate to Wakro LAMPS. A registration certificate will also be handed over to Khamyer Ane Multipurpose Cooperative Society Limited, formed by a Cluster Level Federation (CLF) of women Self-Help Groups. These initiatives are expected to enhance the financial access, institutional capacity and economic activities of cooperative institutions.

At the beginning of the programme, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will flag off a Mobile Medical Van and inaugurate the SARAS Mela. He will visit various stalls set up at the Mela and interact with members of women Self-Help Groups and cooperative societies. The Mela will provide an important platform to showcase local products, traditional crafts, women-led entrepreneurship and the activities of cooperative institutions.

The Cooperative Function in Arunachal Pradesh will provide an important opportunity to strengthen the rural economy through cooperation, promote the better utilisation of local resources, encourage women-led enterprises and connect cooperative institutions with modern financial and digital facilities. The launch of development projects related to education, power, roads and border areas will further contribute to accelerating the inclusive and balanced development of the State.

***


AK/AP

(Release ID: 2339565)

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's address at the Platinum Jubilee celebration of IIT Kharagpur
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi

पश्चिम बंगाल के राज्यपाल आर. एन. रवि जी, यहां के लोकप्रिय मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी जी, केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल में मेरे साथी सुकांता मजूमदार जी, राज्य सरकार के मंत्री भाई जगन्नाथ चट्टोपाध्याय जी, IIT खड़गपुर के माननीय टी.वी. नरेंद्रन जी, सुमन चक्रवर्ती जी, कार्यक्रम में उपस्थित स्टूडेंट्स, एल्युमनाई मेंबर्स, अन्य महानुभाव, देवियों और सज्जनों।

सबसे पहले तो मैं आप सबकी क्षमा चाहता हूँ, क्योंकि मुझे आने में देरी हुई, क्योंकि weather के कारण मैं पहुंच नहीं पाया समय पर, फिर बाय रोड भाग आए वहां से लेकिन फिर भी आने में देर हो गई। आपको विलंब से और मेरा इंतजार भी करना पड़ा, इसके लिए मैं आप सबको जो असुविधा हुई, मैं क्षमा चाहता हूँ।

साथियों,

IIT खड़गपुर के इस प्लैटिनम जुबली समारोह में आज मेरे सामने भारत के अतीत, भारत का वर्तमान और भारत का भविष्य, सबकुछ जुड़ा है। एक बहुत ही, बहुत ही टेलेंटेड एस्पेरेशनल पीढ़ी यहां मौजूद है। आज हम सब इस संस्थान के 75 सालों की यात्रा को सेलिब्रेट करने के लिए, इनकी लीगेसी को ऑनर करने के लिए यहां सब इकट्ठे हुए हैं। अपनी स्थापना के 75 सालों में, IIT खड़गपुर ने बहुत सारे माइल-स्टोन्स बनाए हैं। और इन 75 वर्षों में भारत ने बैलगाड़ी से लेकर के बुलेट ट्रेन तक, डाक पत्रों से लेकर के सोशल मीडिया मैसेज तक, बहुत कुछ बदलते हुए देखा है। और इन बदलावों के हर दौर में देश के पहले IIT के तौर पर, IIT खड़गपुर ने अपनी एक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई है। मैं यहां सभी स्टूडेंट्स को, फैकल्टी मेंबर्स को, यहां के पूरे स्टाफ को और IIT खड़गपुर के सभी alumni को इस अवसर पर बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूँ ।

साथियों,

IIT खड़गपुर की जिंदगी की कुछ यादें तो ऐसी होती हैं, जो जीवनभर साथ रहती हैं। मुझे विश्वास है कि यहां के कई Alumni को दशकों बाद भी छेदीस पर चाय पर चर्चा खूब याद आती होगी। दूसरे संस्थानों में Hostels होते हैं, लेकिन आपके यहां Halls होते हैं। और मैं जानता हूँ कि हर स्टूडेंट को अपने Hall पर कितना गर्व होता है। अभी मुझे यहां आने से पहले दिवाली के चित्र दिए गए और अभी-अभी आप लोगों ने दिवाली मनाई है। और मुझे बताया गया है कि IIT खड़गपुर में दीपावली का उत्साह कुछ अलग ही होता है। यहां की इलुमिनेशन की अपनी ही रौनक होती है, और अलग-अलग हॉल्स के बीच इसको लेकर कंपटीशन और इसको और भी विशेष बना देती है। इस बार कौन-सा हॉल जीता है? अच्छा, देखिए कितने गर्व से बता रहे हैं। चलिए, विजेताओं को मेरी बधाई। विजेता ही ताली नहीं बजाते, तो और कौन बजाएगा आपके लिए।

साथियों,

बंगाल की ये धरती, वो धरती है, जहां आईडियाज को बल मिला है, जहां से नेशनल मूवमेंट बने हैं। और यह संस्थान तो उसी जगह पर बना है, जहां कभी स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों के लिए Detention Camp हुआ करता था। आप कल्पना कीजिए, जो स्वतंत्रता सेनानी यहां डिटेंशन कैंप में रहे होंगे, दिनभर क्या बातें करते होंगे? क्या सोचते होंगे? इस पूरे वायुमंडल में उनकी उस समय की जिंदगी, उस समय की सोच, उस समय की गतिविधि, वो आज भी एक मंत्र की तरह गूंजती होगी, जो आप लोगों के लिए प्रेरणा देती होगी। दशकों पहले, इन्हीं Detention Camp ने उन भारतीयों का अदम्य उत्साह देखा था और साहस देखा था, जो अपना शासन चाहते थे, जो भारत को बुलंदियों पर देखना चाहते थे और आज, इसी भूमि पर नये रंग-रूप से सजी हुई हमारी IIT, इसी स्थान पर ऐसे युवा तैयार हो रहे हैं, जिनका Innovation और जिनके Ideas भारत को आत्मनिर्भर बनाने की ताकत बन रहे हैं। ये भूमि जहां Self-Rule की आकांक्षा थी, आज Self-Reliance का संकल्प यहां दिखाई दे रहा है। तब Freedom का सपना था, आज Future बनाने का अवसर है। आकांक्षा से आत्मनिर्भरता तक का ये सफर ही विकसित भारत के निर्माण की असली ऊर्जा है।

साथियों,

जब IIT खड़गपुर ने अपनी यात्रा शुरू की, तब भारत की आज़ादी नई-नई थी। देश में पहला General Election भी नहीं हुआ था। उस समय भारत को अपनी इंडस्ट्री और इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर के लिए Engineers की जरूरत थी। जैसे-जैसे देश की Scientific Capabilities बढ़ीं, यहां के Graduates ने, हमारे Space और Atomic Energy Programmes को आगे बढ़ाने में योगदान दिया। फिर Information Technology का युग आया, Global Economy के नए अवसर आए, तो यहां से निकले युवाओं ने देश की Software Industry को सशक्त किया। दुनिया की बड़ी-बड़ी कंपनियों का नेतृत्व करने में भूमिका निभाई। यानि हर दौर में, आपके इस संस्थान ने Nation Building में आगे बढ़कर अपना दायित्व निभाया है। और अब आज जब हम विकसित भारत के लक्ष्य के साथ आगे बढ़ रहे हैं, तो IIT खड़गपुर का 75 वर्षों का अनुभव देश के विकास में, देश के इनोवेशन प्रोफाइल में बहुत बड़ी भूमिका निभाने वाला है। मुझे विश्वास है कि आप आज के Aspirational India के सपनों को पूरा करने में कोई कसर बाकी नहीं रखेंगे।

साथियों,

हमारा सामर्थ्य क्या है, ये इससे तय होता है कि हम कितनी चुनौतियों को चुनौती देने का साहस करते हैं, मुझे कई बार लोग पूछते हैं, चुनौतियों के संबंध में, मैंने कहा मेरे स्वभाव में ही बना है कि मैं चुनौती को चुनौती दिए बिना रह नहीं सकता हूं।

साथियों,

हम चुनौती को चुनौती देते है या हम कितनी जल्दी संतुष्ट होकर के बैठ जाते हैं। अक्सर कुछ लोग खुद ही अपनी सोच पर सीमाएं लगा लेते हैं, उसकी लीमिट तय कर देते हैं। और इसी को कहा जाता है- Limiting beliefs और Limiting beliefs है क्या? Limiting beliefs है, अपने सपनों को लिमिट करना, Limiting beliefs है, अपने टैलेंट को लिमिट करना, Limiting beliefs है, अपने देश के सामर्थ्य को लिमिट कर देना और हम खुद ही तय कर लेते हैं कि क्या संभव है और क्या नहीं है। और ज्यादातर लोग, नहीं यार, ये हो नहीं सकता, यहीं से शुरू करते हैं, मरी पड़ी सोच को लेकर के जीने वाले लोग, जिंदगी भी नहीं जी सकते दोस्तों। हम अपनी सोच की सीमा को ही, हमारी जितनी सोच की सीमा है ना, अपने दुनिया की सीमा उसी को मान के बैठ गए हैं।

साथियों,

राष्ट्र भी अपनी क्षमताओं को तभी पहचानते हैं, जब वे अपनी सोच की सीमाओं को तोड़ते हैं। और पिछले कुछ वर्षों में भारत ने यही करके दिखाया है। भारत ने डंके की चोट पर कहा- Break the Limits. Unlock the Possibilities. मैं आपको इसके कुछ उदाहरण भी आज बताता हूं। आप सोचिए, 20 साल पहले तक हमारे देश में गरीबी को एक परमानेंट प्रॉब्लम समझा जाता था। पांच दशक पहले लाल किले से गरीबी हटाने के नारे लगते थे। लेकिन, इसके बाद जब भी पॉलिसी लेवल पर कुछ होना होता था, तो पूरा का पूरा सिस्टम बस फाइल बनाकर बैठ जाता था।

साथियों,

ऐसा इसलिए, क्योंकि सबकी सोच यही थी कि भाई गरीबी दूर नहीं हो सकती और इतनी पॉपुलेशन है, अरे अब तो ऐसे ही चलेगा, यानी कोई हिम्मत भी नहीं दिखाता कि गरीबी दूर करने के लिए सही नीतियों के साथ काम हो।

साथियों,

जब हम सरकार में आए, तब भी स्थितियां तो यही थी और मैंने लाल किले से कहा कि मैं गरीबों के लिए शौचालय बनाऊंगा। तो पार्लियामेंट में लोग मजे लेकर बोलते थे, बताओ, ये कैसा प्रधानमंत्री है, ये लाल किले से टॉयलेट बनाने की बात कर रहा है। ऐसे लोगों की सोच ही नहीं थी कि टॉयलेट एक गरीब के लिए, एक गरीब माता-बहन के लिए कितनी बड़ी जरूरत है। ऐसी ही सोच के कारण पूरा देश ऐसी अनेक सारी फैसिलिटीज से वंचित रहा। 12 साल में हमने यही सोच बदली। हमने गरीबों को सशक्त किया, Power to Empower, इस मूल मंत्र को लेकर के मैं जी रहा हूं, उन्हें empower किया। उनकी Ease of Living के लिए योजनाएं शुरू कीं और इसका नतीजा देश आज देख रहा है। अभी आपने वर्ल्ड बैंक की ताजा रिपोर्ट पर खबरे जरूर पढ़ी होंगी या सुनी होगी। वर्ल्ड बैंक ने कहा है, सिर्फ 12-13 साल में भारत में 50 करोड़ लोग गरीबी से बाहर निकले हैं।

साथियों,

ये कोई छोटा चेंज नहीं है, ये उस सोच का परिणाम है, जो कहती है- Break the Limits.

साथियों,

मैं आपको एक और उदाहरण देता हूं। जब मैंने सेमीकंडक्टर मिशन शुरू किया, तो बहुत सारे सवाल हुए। अरे इस मिशन की अब क्या जरूरत है? ये देश भी बना रहो है, वो देश भी बना रहा है, और 50 साल से सेमीकंडक्टर बन रहा है। अब हम सेमीकंडक्टर बनाकर क्या ही हासिल कर लेंगे? यही सब बोला जाता था। सोचने की सीमा।

साथियों,

आप जानकर हैरान होंगे कि भारत में 50 साल पहले एक कंपनी आई थी, वो हमारे यहां सेमीकंडक्टर बनाने आई थी, लेकिन उसे लाल झंडा दिखाकर वापस भेज दिया गया। मैं जानता हूं, कोई ताली नहीं बजाएगा, ये लाल झंडे का काम रहा था। और इसलिए जब मैंने सेमीकंडक्टर मिशन की बात की, तो फिर कहा गया कि अब तो देर हो गई।

साथियों,

मैं भी ठानकर बैठा था। मैंने कहा- पहले देर हुई तो क्या, भारत अब भी हाथ पर हाथ धरकर ही बैठा रहेगा क्या? हमने शुरुआत की। मैंने खुद अफसरों को लेकर प्लान बनवाना शुरू किया और आज आप देखिए, 4 साल के अंदर देश में ढेर सारी सेमीकंडक्टर फैसिलिटीज शुरू हुईं हैं। भारत आज चिप्स का एक्सपोर्ट करने लगा है। आज आपके पुराने स्टूडेंट्स ऐसी कई फैसिलिटीज को चला रहे हैं, उनकी लीडरशिप, उनका एक्जीक्यूशन, वे लोग कर रहे हैं। और आप पक्का मानिए दोस्तों, आपके लिए तो अवसर ही अवसर है। चिप से लेकर के शिप तक, सबकुछ यहीं होगा, आप जैसे नौजवानों के हाथों से होगा। पर सोचिए, अगर हम यही मानते कि वहां हो गया है, अब हम क्यों सेमीकंडक्टर बनाएं, तब तो कुछ होता ही नहीं।

साथियों,

मैं एक और Strong example दूंगा स्पेस सेक्टर का। हमारे देश में एक लिमिटेड प्लेटफॉर्म इसरो का था, जिसमें एंट्री ही काफी हद तक रेस्ट्रिक्टेड होती थी। वहां कोई भी लॉन्च करना हो, कोई भी मिशन शुरू करना हो, तो सबका अलग सिस्टम था। इसरो के बाहर जो नौजवान थे, उन्हें तो उनको एंट्री ही नहीं, मौके का तो सवाल ही नहीं था। मैंने मंत्रालय को कहा कि इस सेक्टर में हमारे यंग इनोवेटर्स को मौका मिलना ही चाहिए। हमने भारत के स्पेस सेक्टर को भारत के नौजवानों के लिए Open कर दिया और आज आप देखिए, IIT खड़गपुर से निकले एक स्टूडेंट पवन ने स्काईरूट एरोस्पेस बनाकर भारत को पहला प्राइवेट रॉकेट लॉन्च करने का गौरव दिया है। आज ऐसे बहुत सारे स्पेस स्टार्टअप्स भारत के स्पेस प्रोग्राम को नई स्पीड से आगे बढ़ा रहे हैं। कभी ये चीजें असंभव लगती थीं, लेकिन आज ये सब Possible है, ये सब रियलिटी है। और मैं गर्व से कह सकता हूं कि आपकी एल्युमनाई ने इस Impossible को Possible करने में बहुत बड़ा योगदान दिया है।

साथियों,

आप सभी से देश को बहुत उम्मीदें हैं। आने वाले दो दशक आपके जीवन के मोस्ट प्रोडक्टिव ईयर्स में से एक होंगे। 2047 तक, आप में से बहुत सारे लोग लीडरशिप पोज़ीशन्स में होंगे। ये वर्ष भारत के विकास के भी सबसे निर्णायक वर्ष होंगे। और इसलिए, आपकी हर सफलता देश के लिए अहम होगी। ऐसे में आपको हमेशा खुद से ये सवाल पूछना है कि देश के सामने ऐसी कौन-सी चुनौती है, जिसे हल करने में आप योगदान देना चाहेंगे? मेरा मंत्र याद रखिएगा दोस्तों - Nation First. जब आप इस माइंडसेट से आगे बढ़ेंगे, तो निश्चित ही, ये आपके लिए भी नए अवसर लेकर आएगा, और देश को भी बहुत लाभ होने वाला है।

साथियों,

आपने बीते 75 वर्षों में शानदार काम किया है, अब आपको ये दृढ़ निश्चय लेकर आगे बढ़ना है कि 100 वर्ष के समारोह, जब IIT खड़गपुर 100 ईयर मनाए ना, वो विकसित भारत में ही मनना चाहिए। 25-27 में इसी धरती पर जो लोग स्वतंत्र सेनानी बंद पड़े थे, उन्होंने संकल्प लिया था, आजादी लेके रहेंगे, 20 साल में लेके रहे, आज यहीं से संकल्प लें, 20 साल में विकसित भारत बना करके रहेंगे, हम करके रहेंगे। और इसके लिए जी जान से जुटेंगे, बहुत मेहनत करेंगे। और आज जब बंगाल की धरती पर आया हूं तब, मैं स्वामी विवेकानंद जी के शब्दों के साथ अपनी बात समाप्त करूंगा। उठो, जागो और तब तक मत रुको, जब तक लक्ष्य प्राप्त ना हो जाए। एक बार फिर आज के इस विशेष अवसर पर आप सभी को मेरी ढेर सारी शुभकामनाएं।

बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

नमस्कार।

*****

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
GeM Signs MoU with TICCI to Expand Public Procurement Opportunities for Tribal Entrepreneurs
Partnership to Strengthen Onboarding, Capacity Building and Market Access for Tribal Businesses Through GeM
Posted On: 21 NOV 2026 11:48AM by PIB Delhi

Government e Marketplace (GeM), the national public procurement portal, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tribal Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (TICCI) on 20 November 2026 to strengthen the participation of tribal entrepreneurs and enterprises in government procurement. The collaboration aims to connect tribal businesses with public procurement opportunities through targeted outreach, capacity building, onboarding assistance and sustained handholding support.

The MoU was signed by Additional CEO, GeM, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, and Founder and Chairman, TICCI, Shri Sudhakar Dharavath, formalising the partnership to promote awareness, capacity building and greater participation of tribal entrepreneurs in public procurement through GeM.

Speaking about the collaboration, CEO, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar said, “This partnership with TICCI is an important step towards expanding public procurement opportunities for tribal entrepreneurs. We aim to strengthen their awareness, build capabilities and enable greater inclusion on GeM and further improve their participation in GeM’s transparent and inclusive procurement ecosystem.”

Under the MoU, TICCI will identify and mobilise tribal entrepreneurs, facilitate regional and national outreach programmes, provide field-level support and develop a network of trainers and mentors. GeM will support these efforts through training resources, onboarding facilitation, capacity-building initiatives and appropriate issue-resolution mechanisms. Both organisations will also work together to develop action plans, monitor progress and incorporate feedback from entrepreneurs to improve participation.

At the MoU signing, Shri Ajit B. Chavan said, “This partnership will help take GeM closer to tribal entrepreneurs through focused outreach, training and handholding, enabling greater access to government procurement opportunities.”

The collaboration reinforces GeM’s commitment to making public procurement more inclusive by enabling enterprises from diverse backgrounds to participate in the national procurement ecosystem and access opportunities for business growth.

*****

Abhishek Dayal/ Shabbir Azad/ Abhimanyu Panwar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs foils smuggling attempt of cocaine worth Rs. 5 crore (approx.) at Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 10:46PM by PIB Delhi

Based on data analysis and intelligence-led surveillance, officers of Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs, foiled an attempt to smuggle cocaine through the Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi.

The consignment, declared as “Beans Cloths” and originating from Entebbe, Uganda, had remained unclaimed for a considerable period after its arrival. No Bill of Entry had been filed for its clearance.

Accordingly, officers of Air Cargo Import, Delhi Customs, conducted a detailed examination of the consignment and recovered approximately 1.975 Kg (gross weight) of fabric suspected to be laced with a narcotic substance, along with raw pulses and beans. A separate packet of 350 grams (gross weight) containing white powder suspected to be cocaine was also recovered.

Preliminary testing of the white powder indicated the presence of cocaine. The 1.975 kg impregnated / laced fabric material and 350 grams. packet containing white powdery substance suspected to be cocaine / NDPS substance has been seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

The estimated street value of the seized cocaine is approximately ₹5 crore. It is estimated at ₹10–15 crore per kilogram in the international market. Further investigation is underway.

****

KT/KMN

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 8 kg methamphetamine (Yaba) tablets in Agartala; one drug trafficker arrested
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 10:03PM by PIB Delhi

Another successful interdiction by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has resulted in the seizure of 8 kg methamphetamine tablets (Yaba) in Agartala, Tripura, and the arrest of one drug trafficker. The operation, conducted by DRI on 17 November 2026, marks another significant addition to DRI's sustained efforts to curb the cross-border trafficking of synthetic drugs in the North-Eastern region.

Acting on specific intelligence regarding the movement of a consignment of narcotic drugs, officers of the DRI intercepted the suspected vehicle. When suspected white Maruti Suzuki Swift Dzire was spotted and signalled to stop, its driver attempted to evade interception by speeding away. DRI officers swiftly pursued and intercepted the vehicle near the railway crossing at Iccha Bazar. The occupants abandoned the vehicle and attempted to escape on foot. However, officers managed to apprehend one of them, while the others escaped.

A detailed search of the vehicle led to the recovery of a plastic bag concealed in the footwell of the front passenger seat. The bag contained eight black packets, each holding five white packets, which in turn contained ten pouches of orange-coloured tablets suspected to be methamphetamine.  

The recovered 8 kg (net) of methamphetamine tablets, along with the vehicle, was seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. One person was arrested under the provisions of the Act.

This seizure adds to DRI's sustained efforts to interdict substantial consignments of synthetic drugs in the North-Eastern region. Recent operations by DRI in the region have resulted in significant seizures of methamphetamine tablets and crystal methamphetamine, including the seizure of 20 kg Yaba tablets in Silchar last week; 20 kg crystal methamphetamine and 30 kg methamphetamine tablets in two operations during last month in Silchar and Aizawl respectively.

These successive interdictions underscore DRI's intelligence-gathering capabilities and operational vigilance in identifying and disrupting narcotics trafficking networks operating in the region.

****

item.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum
item.dc:creator: Prime Minister's Office
item.description: Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum Empires may have redrawn the maps of the world, but civilisational dialogues have transformed and enriched global thought; Therefore, the SCO Civilisational Summit is not merely a ceremonial platform;it can become a platform to give direction to the world: PM 21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity in the world; Along the routes where our ancestors once had to travel for months, today people of those very countries can connect with one another…
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum
Empires may have redrawn the maps of the world, but civilisational dialogues have transformed and enriched global thought; Therefore, the SCO Civilisational Summit is not merely a ceremonial platform;it can become a platform to give direction to the world: PM
21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity in the world;  Along the routes where our ancestors once had to travel for months, today people of those very countries can connect with one another in just a few seconds: PM
Digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange, and international collaboration easier than ever before; SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities: PM
A priceless heritage of thousands of years is preserved across the museums, libraries, and archives of our nations;  Ancient manuscripts, rare texts, historical documents, and artefacts illuminate the many facets of our deep-rooted ties; Today, technology offers tremendous opportunities to pass this heritage on to the younger generation: PM
We can collaborate on the digitisation and translation of ancient texts, and through joint research projects, uncover new dimensions of our shared history; This will enable youth in any part of the world to gain a far deeper understanding of another nation's cultural heritage: PM
Our culture has taught us 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', meaning this entire world is our family; Therefore, here, the aspiration for our own welfare is deeply intertwined in the spirit of global welfare; We consider mutual harmony to be the basis of global wellbeing: PM
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 9:34PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the First Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, he welcomed dignitaries, SCO ministers, ambassadors, high commissioners, scholars, artists, and guests from across SCO member states, highlighting the significance of holding a dialogue on civilizational connections at a time when global discussions are dominated by war and unrest, and noting that cultural connect serves as the strongest guarantee for world peace and builds upon the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's 25th anniversary and growing cooperation in security, economy, and connectivity. “Our shared civilizational experiences will play an important role in uniting the world,” asserted Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the historic setting of Purana Qila,a cultural heritage site whose history scholars trace back thousands of years to the Mahabharata era, the Prime Minister noted how grand cultural performances, energetic Vedic recitations, Buddhist philosophy presentations, and depictions of Hanuman ji's journey at the ancient venue showcased Indian culture alongside universal messages of love, unity, and human welfare that transcend geopolitical borders. “You all will also enjoy this event, and by making it historic, will also lay the foundation of a new tradition for which the future will remember all of you,” remarked PM Modi.

Tracing centuries-old international collaboration and people-to-people ties from trade links between the Indus Valley Civilization and Mesopotamia around five thousand years ago to Silk and trade networks connecting India, China, Central Asia, and Eurasia,where merchants, scholars, travelers, and Buddhist monks such as Faxian, Xuanzang, Yijing, and Kucha-born Kumarajiva, alongside institutions like Nalanda and centers like Kucha and Dunhuang, enriched civilizations through exchanges of ideas, languages, and Buddhist texts,the Prime Minister underscored the enduring power of cultural dialogue. “Empires have certainly changed the maps of the world, but civilizational dialogues have changed the ideas of the world and enriched them,” asserted Shri Modi.

Observing that as knowledge travels across regions, its expression may evolve while its illuminating impact remains constant, the Prime Minister cited how India's Panchatantra traveled to Persian and Arabic as Kalila wa Dimna to become immortal across generations and how the Ramayana enriched local culture, performing arts, and literature in Southeast Asia as Reamker in Cambodia. “Knowledge, in whichever form it exists, spreads light alone,” remarked PM Modi.

Highlighting the importance of cross-cultural exchange in science and mathematics, the Prime Minister noted how the mathematical ideas of Indian scholar Brahmagupta reached Baghdad. “There, scholars like Al-Khwarizmi made an important contribution in taking the knowledge of mathematics forward,” observed Shri Modi.

Pointing to shared legacies in architecture and music,including links between Central Asian Maqam and Indian Raga traditions, Sufi influences enriching Qawwali in India, and Central Asian garden traditions from Samarkand and Herat shaping the Charbagh style,the Prime Minister stressed the value of sustaining open cultural exchanges. “That this exchange continues in a free flow even today, for that, the role of this summit and of such initiatives becomes important,” asserted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that 21st-century technology has unlocked unprecedented opportunities for cultural connectivity,enabling people across regions that once required months of travel to connect within seconds while digital platforms streamline knowledge sharing, cultural exchange, and international collaboration,the Prime Minister called for leveraging these advancements. “SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities,” asserted Shri Modi.

Sharing suggestions with the gathered guests on preserving and sharing thousands of years of heritage housed in museums, libraries, and archives,such as ancient manuscripts, rare texts, historical documents, and artifacts,the Prime Minister proposed cooperation in digitizing and translating ancient texts as well as joint research projects on shared history. “Because of this, a youth sitting in any part of the world will be able to understand the cultural heritage of another country in a much better way,” observed PM Modi.

Noting that many great literary and intellectual works remain available in limited languages despite expanded resources today, the Prime Minister pointed to technological tools for broadening access. “With the help of AI, new momentum can be given to their translation,” asserted Shri Modi.

Highlighting additional avenues for cultural exchange,including joint exhibitions by museums and cultural institutions, scholar and researcher exchanges between universities, heritage circuits and cultural routes linking Silk Route and Buddhist heritage sites, cultural tourism, joint cultural festivals, and artist exchanges,the Prime Minister expressed confidence in the human impact of such initiatives. “Through such efforts, our citizens will get opportunities to know and understand each other's culture even more closely,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Stressing that the responsibility of carrying today's civilizational dialogue to new heights in coming decades rests with younger generations who are tech-savvy and eager to understand the world, the Prime Minister called for greater opportunities for youth to engage with diverse languages, literature, and cultural traditions while involving local artists and artisans. “Our young artists, writers, and filmmakers, through digital media and other creative platforms, can convey our shared heritage to the new generation,” asserted Shri Modi.

Recalling that Indian prayers at the conclusion of rituals seek goodwill among all beings and welfare for the entire world rooted in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, treating the whole world as one family, the Prime Minister linked individual and national wellbeing to global harmony. “We consider mutual goodwill itself as the base of global wellbeing,” affirmed PM Modi.

Observing that mutual goodwill depends on mutual trust built around shared commonalities, the Prime Minister drew on India's experience of embracing and celebrating diversity across varied languages, lifestyles, and traditions,inspired by the Vedic recitation heard at the start of the forum, to turn plurality into unity. “When we adopt this generous perspective, then our diversity itself becomes the basis of our unity,” asserted Shri Modi.

Concluding his address by invoking the Vedic call ‘Sangachchhadhwam Samvadadhwam Sam Vo Manansi Janatam’ to walk together, converse together, and achieve harmony of thoughts, the Prime Minister extended congratulations on the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum and best wishes for productive deliberations.

Speaking at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. https://t.co/RzZCS5bjnd

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 20, 2026

साम्राज्यों ने दुनिया के नक्शे जरूर बदले हैं, लेकिन civilisational dialogues ने दुनिया के विचार बदले हैं, उन्हें समृद्ध किया है। इसीलिए, SCO civilisational summit केवल एक ceremonial platform नहीं है। ये विश्व को दिशा देने का एक मंच बन सकता है: PM @narendramodi

— PMO India (@PMOIndia) November 20, 2026

21वीं सदी की Technology ने दुनिया में Cultural Connectivity की नई संभावनाएं पैदा की हैं। जिन रास्तों पर कभी हमारे पूर्वजों को महीनों यात्रा करनी पड़ती थी, आज उन्हीं देशों के लोग कुछ ही सेकंड में एक-दूसरे से जुड़ सकते हैं। Digital Platforms ने Knowledge Sharing, Cultural Exchange और International Collaboration को पहले से आसान बना दिया है। SCO के देशों को इन नई संभावनाओं का पूरा लाभ उठाना चाहिए: PM @narendramodi

— PMO India (@PMOIndia) November 20, 2026

हमारे देशों के Museums, Libraries और Archives में हजारों वर्षों की अनमोल विरासत सुरक्षित है। प्राचीन Manuscripts, दुर्लभ ग्रंथ, ऐतिहासिक दस्तावेज और कलाकृतियां हमारे जुड़ाव के अनेक पहलुओं को सामने लाती हैं। आज Technology की मदद से इस विरासत को नई पीढ़ी तक पहुंचाने के बहुत अच्छे अवसर बने हैं। हम प्राचीन ग्रंथों के Digitisation और Translation में सहयोग कर सकते हैं। Joint Research Projects के माध्यम से हम अपने साझा इतिहास के नए पहलुओं को सामने ला सकते हैं। इससे दुनिया के किसी भी हिस्से में बैठा एक युवा, दूसरे देश की Cultural Heritage को कहीं बेहतर तरीके से समझ सकेगा: PM @narendramodi at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum

— PMO India (@PMOIndia) November 20, 2026

हमारी संस्कृति ने हमें ‘वसुधैव कुटुंबकम्’ की सीख दी है। यानी, ये पूरा विश्व ही हमारा परिवार है। इसलिए, हमारे यहाँ अपने कल्याण की इच्छा विश्व कल्याण के भाव में ही रची बसी है। हम आपसी सद्भाव को ही global wellbeing का base मानते हैं: PM @narendramodi

— PMO India (@PMOIndia) November 20, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Mines
India's Critical Mineral Push is Securing Mineral Supplies through both Domestic and Overseas Sources: Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 9:32PM by PIB Delhi

Speaking at the Ministry of Mines-FICCI closed-door industry interaction Shri Keshav Chandra, Secretary, Ministry of Mines, Government of India, highlighted the Ministry's reform agenda to enhance the sector's global competitiveness through geological exploration, responsible mining, advanced processing, research, recycling and technology-enabled governance. He also outlined recent auction reforms, including relaxation of minimum bidder requirements for certain minerals and automatic issuance of Letters of Intent.

Responding comprehensively to the concerns raised by the industry, Shri Chandra apprised participants of the various initiatives and measures already undertaken or under consideration by the Ministry. He addressed operational challenges relating to mineral block development. He urged the industry to actively consider extraction of critical minerals from resources such as redmud.

The interaction also witnessed the launch of concept paper, Enabling Overseas Investment in Critical Minerals: Policy, Financial and Institutional Framework for Securing India's Critical Mineral Supply Chains. Shri Chandra emphasised that to secure mineral supplies, opportunities are being explored both at domestic as well as overseas level. He observed that the paper's emphasis on moving from MoUs to project delivery aligns with the Ministry's efforts, including KABIL's overseas engagements, and expressed interest in examining its recommendations.

On overseas critical mineral investments, he discussed the importance of enabling mechanisms to improve project viability. He emphasised the Ministry's continued efforts to address industry concerns through policy and regulatory reforms, institutional coordination and targeted interventions, while encouraging industry to actively participate in strengthening India's domestic and overseas mineral supply chains.

Opening the interaction, Dr. Pankaj Satija, Co-Chair, FICCI Mining Committee and Executive VP, JSW, appreciated the Ministry's reforms in exploration, mineral auctions and mine operationalisation. He highlighted growing global supply chain vulnerabilities arising from export controls, domestic value-addition requirements and processing technology restrictions, underscoring the importance of diversified and resilient mineral supply chains for India's industrial and economic security.

FICCI noted that the concept paper, prepared pursuant to the mandate received from the Ministry of Mines, draws on extensive research and stakeholder consultations to identify barriers to overseas mineral investments and propose actionable solutions.

The paper also presents a Country-Priority Mineral Matrix to guide strategic overseas investments and proposes a tiered framework for prioritising projects for government facilitation. It emphasises stronger institutional coordination, streamlined approvals and integration of overseas mineral investments with domestic processing and manufacturing capabilities to translate international partnerships into assured mineral supplies for India.

Under the guidance of Shri Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Head, National Critical Mineral Mission, Ministry of Mines, the paper has been authored by Mr. Arpan Gupta, Director, FICCI and Mr. Siddhant Chandra, Assistant Director, FICCI.

The interaction brought together senior industry representatives to discuss policy and regulatory priorities, overseas investments and financing mechanisms for strengthening India's mineral security.

President's Secretariat
MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF BULGARIA CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 9:27PM by PIB Delhi

H.E. Mrs Velislava Petrova-Chamova, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Bulgaria, called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 20, 2026).

Welcoming Foreign Minister Petrova-Chamova and her delegation to Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President expressed confidence that this visit, the first by a Bulgarian Foreign Minister in 17 years, will provide fresh momentum to the India-Bulgaria partnership.

The President was happy to note that cooperation between India and Bulgaria continues to grow across sectors such as trade and investment, defense, education, science and technology, AI, space, mobility, and cultural and people-to-people ties. She added that with the implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement there are significant new opportunities to further deepen our trade, investment, and technological ties.

The President also appreciated Bulgaria’s consistent support to India and close cooperation on multilateral platforms, including on the need for reform of the UN Security Council.
