item.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Home Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Home Affairs Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy towards terrorism, and this policy is yielding positive results Following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Latif Bhat, Kashmir is now free of locally recruited terrorists born in India, this marks a major milestone in the fight against terrorism We are building a system in which all police stations across the country will…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy towards terrorism, and this policy is yielding positive results
Following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Latif Bhat, Kashmir is now free of locally recruited terrorists born in India, this marks a major milestone in the fight against terrorism
We are building a system in which all police stations across the country will work on a unified strategy to combat terrorism
Hallmark of a successful agency is its ability to apprehend terrorists and put them behind bars before they can carry out a terrorist attack, all state police forces should study this model and implement it
To completely eliminate terrorism, organized crime, and drug-related problems, it is essential to bring offenders hiding abroad back to India, since 2019, 303 fugitives have been brought back to India from 36 countries
It is essential to dismantle entire terror financing network, to achieve this, better coordination with agencies responsible for financial investigations is necessary
Success cannot be achieved without launching a simultaneous assault on the entire terror network
We will not succeed in fight against terrorism unless we have a shared objective and clearly defined accountability at every stage of process to achieve that objective
We need to strengthen the concept of a proactive offensive approach in our counter-terrorism policy, with a greater emphasis on enhancing structural and operational capabilities
Once a case comes to light, investigation must continue until the entire network is dismantled, ATS has a crucial role to play in this process
Every state's ATS should strengthen its cyber expert unit
By expanding the scope of MAC to include cyber security, narco-terrorism, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, and by establishing a National Memory Bank, we have laid a new foundation for strengthening our preparedness
Not only have legal powers of NIA been enhanced, but its national presence has also been expanded, approval has been granted for 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices simultaneously
NIA has been empowered to conduct investigations to protect the interests of Indians residing abroad
Dismantling of PFI network is a significant example of how effective coordinated operations by police forces across India can be
In a single night, police forces from 11 states, along with central agencies, jointly dealt a major blow to PFI network, this operation is now a case study for the entire world
Shahzad Bhatti network has been designated a terrorist organisation under UAPA, more than 40 of its modules have been dismantled across the country, over 100 cases have been registered, and more than 271 arrests have been made
Union Home Minister released NIA publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’, laid the foundation stone for NIA office complex in Chandigarh, and inaugurated residential complex at Maidan Garhi i
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference organised in New Delhi. On the occasion, Union Home Minister released the publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’ brought out by National Investigation Agency (NIA). He also laid the foundation stone of NIA office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated NIA residential complex built at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on seven officers and personnel of the National Investigation Agency.

On this occasion, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan, Director Intelligence Bureau (IB) Dr. Mahesh Dikshit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Anand Swarup, and Director General National Investigation Agency (NIA) Shri Rakesh Aggarwal, along with several other senior officers, were present. Senior police officers from the states and Union Territories, officers from counter-terrorism agencies, and experts from related fields including law, forensics and technology are participating in this conference.

Addressing the conference, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that India has been a victim of terrorism and we have been confronting terrorism for a long time. He noted that police forces of different states had made various kinds of efforts, but a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings. Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station.

Shri Amit Shah said that some successful operations have recently been carried out against terrorism, which has strengthened the confidence of our country. He stated that just yesterday we achieved a significant milestone in the fight against terrorism. With the elimination of Lashkar terrorist Latif Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists. Shri Shah noted that this situation has come about after 35 years.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Shahzad Bhatti network has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). More than 40 of its modules have been neutralised across the country. In the action taken against this network, over 100 cases have been registered and more than 271 arrests have been made. Shri Shah stated that the hallmark of a successful agency is to apprehend terrorists and put them behind bars even before they can execute a terrorist incident. He said that the police of every state should analyse this model, accept it, and implement it in their respective areas.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that since 2019 we have launched a special drive to bring fugitives back to India, and so far 303 fugitives have been brought back from 36 countries, thereby strengthening the security of our nation. He noted that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Ministry of Home Affairs have made special efforts in this regard. Our intelligence agencies have made outstanding efforts in bringing back fugitives living abroad through scientific methods. Shri Shah stated that if we are to completely eliminate the three menaces— terrorism, organised crime and drugs, it is essential to bring the culprits and masterminds who have taken shelter abroad before Indian courts.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy against terrorism, and positive results of this are being achieved. He stated that, as part of continuous efforts in this direction, NIA Act was first amended on 2nd August 2019. New offences were brought under the jurisdiction of NIA and additional jurisdictions were granted to it. Shri Shah added  that UAPA was amended on 14th August 2019, under which NIA was empowered to seize the properties of terrorists and a process was initiated to declare individuals as terrorists. Union Home Minister noted that in September 2019 a unified action plan was prepared to counter radicalisation, which was finalised in December 2019 after discussions with various ministries. In September 2022, PFI network was dismantled. He said that the destruction of PFI network is a striking example of how effective a joint operation by the Indian police can be. In a single night, coordinated action was carried out simultaneously in 11 states, completely dismantling the entire PFI network and breaking its backbone. By destroying the PFI network, we have preemptively eliminated several serious problems that the country could have faced in the future. He added that the dismantling of PFI network is the key to preventing many potential incidents that could have occurred in the times to come.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the functioning of the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) has been reorganised. Cyber security, narcotics, organised crime networks and emerging radicalisation hotspots have been brought under the purview of the MAC. In 2023, the methodology of the MAC was restructured using state-of-the-art technology. A National Memory Bank was established and efforts were made to create a centralised database. He further stated that during this period, not only were the legal powers of NIA enhanced, but its national character was also expanded. Almost simultaneously, 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices were approved. NIA was empowered to conduct investigations for the protection of the interests of Indians residing abroad. A ban was imposed on the glorification of terrorism. A 25-point integrated action plan was formulated to control the funding of terrorists, and this is being effectively monitored.

Shri Amit Shah said, NIA officers have been trained to gain international exposure, and 70 new NIA Special Courts have been established across the country. He stated that peace had been established in three major hotspots, networks such as PFI and Shahzad Bhatti had been dismantled, and a scientific mechanism had been developed to bring back fugitives from abroad. He also highlighted the implementation of a new comprehensive approach to border security, the complete removal of illegal religious structures along the borders, and improved coordination among various agencies to strengthen economic security. Shri Shah stated that the government had worked simultaneously and effectively on all these fronts.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that we are moving forward with an ecosystem-based approach to combating terrorism through cooperation between the Centre and the States, and that this cooperation needs to be further strengthened. He said that we have strengthened the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) on the legal front, and that the flow of information needs to be made smoother and more robust at the institutional level. He emphasised that we must also change our work culture to achieve victory in this fight. On the operational front, agencies must enhance their capabilities while also undertaking modernisation. We must target the entire chain of terror financing, which requires better coordination with financial investigation agencies. Shri Shah stated that we will not achieve success unless we strike at the entire terrorist network in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.

Shri Amit Shah stated that in the fight against terrorism, our approach must be based on shared and collective goals, along with clearly defined accountability. He emphasised that unless our goals are shared and accountability for achieving them is clearly established, success cannot be achieved. He further said that this conference must be made outcome-oriented, which will be possible only when all participants make concerted efforts in this direction.

Union Home Minister said that India needs to strengthen the concept of proactive action in its counter-terrorism policy, with greater emphasis on structural and operational capabilities. Shri Amit Shah stated that the entire terrorist network must be investigated and its capabilities dismantled. He said that by investigating the entire network, many incidents could be prevented before they occur. Shri Shah emphasised the need to develop a mechanism through which police station-level intelligence is transmitted through multiple levels to the Director General of Police (DGP), enabling the extraction of actionable intelligence. He also said that the Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS) of every state need to strengthen their cyber expert units, as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. Union Home Minister further stated that establishing a Quadrangular Regional Security Grid in Border States should be a key priority. He also stressed the need to enhance the capabilities of the ATS units across all states.

****

The two Ministers welcomed the steady materialisation of India-Japan defence cooperation through close communication between them, including…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri and Japan’s Minister of Defense hold bilateral talks in Tokyo
India & Japan agree to deepen defence cooperation across key domains and reaffirm commitment to peace & stability in Indo-Pacific
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of Defense of Japan Mr Shinjiro Koizumi in Tokyo on November 19, 2026. The two Ministers welcomed the steady materialisation of India-Japan defence cooperation through close communication between them, including the holding of their third Defence Ministers’ Meeting within a short period of time, following their interactions in August and October this year.

Both the leaders welcomed the signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) toward the utilisation of firing ranges in India, whereby Japan Self-Defense Forces would, for the first time, conduct live-fire training etc., including those involving surface-to-ship missiles, at firing ranges in India. They concurred on accelerating coordination between the defence authorities of the two countries toward its early realisation.

The two Ministers welcomed the steady progress in materialising maritime security cooperation under the ‘Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation’ signed in August this year. In particular, they confirmed that the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level, would follow up on working level talks on areas including enhancing mine counter-measures capabilities and exploring the possibility of joint development in naval shipbuilding and design.

The two Ministers agreed to further deepen cooperation towards creating an environment that would facilitate information sharing between the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force and the Indian Navy.

The two Ministers welcomed the deepening of cooperation through joint exercises between the respective Services, including the multilateral naval exercise ‘Malabar 2026’ involving Japan, the United States, India and Australia, and the Japan-India Maritime Exercise ‘JAIMEX26’, both conducted in Japan this month. They also concurred on further advancing exchanges between their respective Special Operations Forces.

Regarding defence equipment and technology cooperation, the two Ministers shared their expectation for an early conclusion of the UNICORN related arrangements, and the Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) by India by February 2027. They also affirmed that they would materialise defence R&D cooperation between DRDO and ATLA in the field of state-of-the-art missile and defence technologies.

 

The two Ministers concurred on promoting cooperation between the two air services in the field of Air Domain Awareness and confirmed that the working level talks would also be followed through the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level.

Amid an increasingly complex and uncertain security environment in the Indo-Pacific region, the two Ministers concurred on further promoting multilateral defence cooperation, including trilateral cooperation, in addition to bilateral defence cooperation between Japan and India, and on advancing practical cooperation for peace and stability in the region.

The two Ministers shared their determination to steadily implement these concrete areas of cooperation and elevate Japan-India defence cooperation to greater heights, thereby contributing together to the peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Rehabilitation and Livelihood Opportunities through NAPDDR
Mr. Sudesh Kumar Of Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh Treated And Rehabilitated Under Ministry-Supported De-Addiction Treatment, Counselling And Rehabilitation Assistance
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

Access to comprehensive de-addiction treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services plays a significant role in promoting individual well-being, strengthening family relationships, economic self-reliance and social reintegration among individuals affected by substance dependence.

Mr. Sudesh Kumar (name changed), a 42-year-old resident of Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh, belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, has successfully overcome alcohol addiction with rehabilitation support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

Having studied up to high school, Rajesh worked as a driver and also undertook daily wage labour to support his wife and two children. However, alcohol addiction gradually affected his personal, professional and financial well-being, resulting in irregular employment, financial instability and strained family relationships.

With a determination to lead a healthier life and secure a better future for his children, and with encouragement from his family members, Sudesh Kumar approached the Sarvodaya Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) in Annamayya district of Andhra Pradesh.

On February 5, 2026, Sudesh received comprehensive de-addiction treatment and rehabilitation assistance under the NAPDDR Scheme, which included individual counselling, family counselling, group counselling, yoga, meditation, motivational sessions and psychosocial support.

For individuals undergoing recovery from substance dependence, access to structured rehabilitation and sustained counselling is an important enabler of personal and social transformation. These interventions helped Sudesh understand the harmful effects of alcohol addiction, rebuild his self-confidence and develop a positive outlook towards life. Family counselling further strengthened his relationships with family members.

As per the follow-up conducted on April 27, 2026, Sudesh had completely abstained from alcohol consumption and was leading a sober and responsible life. He had also established a small tea shop in Kadapa, enabling him to earn a stable income, support his family and work towards economic self-reliance.

Beyond providing de-addiction treatment, the NAPDDR Scheme seeks to promote behavioural transformation, emotional well-being, social reintegration and sustainable rehabilitation, thereby enabling individuals to lead healthy, productive and dignified lives.

Sudesh’s  journey from alcohol dependence to recovery and entrepreneurship highlights the significance of targeted rehabilitation interventions in restoring self-confidence, strengthening livelihood opportunities and bringing positive changes in the lives of individuals and their families.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s sustained commitment towards holistic rehabilitation, social empowerment, economic self-reliance and inclusive socio-economic development, contributing to the larger vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.title: Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
item.description: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation MoSPI’s transformative Initiatives on SDGs and Statistical Database Stewardship for fortifying the architecture of India’s National Statistical System showcased Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi Reaffirming India’s abiding commitment to partnership and shared progress in the field of official statistics, the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA)- Ministry of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation
MoSPI’s transformative Initiatives on SDGs and Statistical Database Stewardship for fortifying the architecture of India’s National Statistical System showcased
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

Reaffirming India’s abiding commitment to partnership and shared progress in the field of official statistics, the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA)- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD), organised an interaction of international participants from twenty-six partner countries of the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme on 17 November 2026. The engagement offered the visiting delegates a meaningful vantage point on the manner in which India builds, governs and sustains its statistical institutions.

The occasion was graced by the eminent presence of Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics) and Dr. Purnendu Kishore Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance)-In-Charge, MoSPI, along with senior officers of the Ministry, including Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division and Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division. Dr. P. C. Parida, Director, NILERD and faculty of NILERD also participated.

Setting the tone for the day’s deliberations, Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division recalled India’s timeless message that the world is one family and that all people are one’s own kin. Anchored in this civilisational outlook, he stressed that the country has consistently striven to extend its support to other nations in improving and strengthening their statistical systems. Ms. Reena Singh, Deputy Director General, NSSTA, while moderating the interaction, emphasized the crucial role of MoSPI in strengthening the country’s official statistical system ensuring the availability of reliable, credible and timely statistical information, and supporting evidence based policymaking across sectors. She also emphasized the pivotal role of NSSTA for strengthening the capacity of the statistical system in India.

The keynote address, delivered by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), furnished the delegates with a comprehensive panorama of the National Statistical System of India. In the course of his address, he elaborated on the institutional framework, the organisational structure and the functioning of the Statistical System, thereby giving an overview of the various statistical products and varied surveys undertaken by MoSPI.

The substantive core of the interaction consisted of two technical sessions. The first session on “Overview of SDG Monitoring in India” was led by Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, SSD, Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, SSD, and Shri Indradeep Roy Chaudhary, Director, SSD. The session provided an overview of more than 270 national indicators identified by MoSPI for monitoring SDGs and its continuous process of alignment with the Global Indicator Framework. The session on “Developing and Managing Statistical Database” was presented by Shri Vishnu Mishra, Director, Data Innovation and Information Division (DIID), MoSPI which provided insights into the e-Sankhyiki portal, microdata portal, semantic search, Model Context Protocol (MCP) micro and macro datasets etc.

Bringing the proceedings to a close, Shri P. K. Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance)-In-Charge, engaged with the international participants and shared valuable perspectives on India’s statistical ecosystem in his concluding remarks. He urged the delegates to carry the learnings of the interaction back with them and apply them towards strengthening the statistical systems of their respective countries.

India reaffirms its unwavering commitment to all participating nations through sustained technical cooperation, knowledge-sharing and institutional partnership to translate shared learning  into actionable outcomes.

***

item.title: ​​​​​​​Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari Calls for Greater Focus on Road Safety, Construction Quality and Sustainable Technologies
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
item.description: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways ​​​​​​​Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari Calls for Greater Focus on Road Safety, Construction Quality and Sustainable Technologies At the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, Minister emphasises innovation, use of alternative materials, scientific planning and accountability in road infrastructure development Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today addressed the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
​​​​​​​Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari Calls for Greater Focus on Road Safety, Construction Quality and Sustainable Technologies
At the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, Minister emphasises innovation, use of alternative materials, scientific planning and accountability in road infrastructure development
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today addressed the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress (IRC) in Hyderabad, Telangana, and called upon engineers, contractors, consultants and policymakers to work collectively towards improving the quality, safety, durability and sustainability of India's road infrastructure.

The event was attended by Telangana Chief Minister Shri A. Revanth Reddy, Minister for Roads and Buildings, Telangana, Shri Komatireddy Venkat Reddy, President IRC Shri L K Padhi, Director General (Road Development) & Special Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri Sudip Chaudhary, and Secretary General, Indian Roads Congress, Shri Rahul Gupta, among other dignitaries, senior government officials, engineers and industry representatives.

Congratulating the engineers, contractors and officials for their contribution to the development of the country's National Highway network, Shri Gadkari acknowledged their dedicated efforts and technical expertise. He emphasised that continuous upgradation of knowledge, research, innovation and adoption of global best practices are essential for developing future-ready infrastructure.

Highlighting the role of the Indian Roads Congress in setting technical standards for the road sector, the Minister noted that IRC has developed several technical codes, guidelines, manuals and publications that guide road infrastructure development in the country. He urged the organisation to strengthen international cooperation and facilitate greater exchange of knowledge, technology and successful practices to keep Indian standards aligned with evolving global developments.

Focus on Construction Quality and Road Safety

The Minister stressed that quality, safety and durability must remain the foremost priorities in road construction. He called for greater accountability among contractors, consultants and engineers and stated that any compromise in construction quality must invite appropriate action. He also emphasised transparent, time-bound and result-oriented implementation of highway projects.

Shri Gadkari underlined the need to improve the quality of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), strengthen technical supervision and ensure effective implementation of road safety audits. He urged engineers to identify and rectify accident-prone locations through proper planning, improved junction design, and provision of flyovers and underpasses wherever required. Emphasising the importance of protecting human lives, he called for a collective commitment towards reducing road accidents and eliminating black spots through better engineering and design.

Innovation and Sustainable Construction Practices

Emphasising the need to reduce construction costs while improving quality, the Minister called for greater use of innovative and alternative construction materials. He highlighted the potential of plastic waste, used tyres, steel slag, municipal solid waste and agricultural residue in road construction, wherever technically suitable.

He also referred to the use of bio-bitumen developed from rice straw and highlighted the potential of research and field applications of alternative materials in promoting sustainable highway construction and reducing dependence on conventional resources.

The Minister encouraged wider adoption of alternative fuels and biofuels in construction equipment, including electric, ethanol, biodiesel, CNG, LNG and hydrogen-based technologies. He highlighted their potential to reduce pollution, lower dependence on imported fossil fuels and create additional opportunities for farmers through the diversification of agricultural produce towards the energy sector.

Shri Gadkari also called for greater use of treated wastewater in construction activities, particularly in view of increasing water stress. He highlighted the importance of recycling municipal waste and reusing available resources in infrastructure development. He further encouraged research into tree transplantation and plantation along highways to strengthen environmental protection.

Road Infrastructure as an Enabler of Economic Growth

The Minister highlighted the role of quality road infrastructure in improving connectivity, reducing travel time and logistics costs, and supporting trade, industry, agriculture and tourism. Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, he underlined the importance of connecting rural areas through all-weather road networks to improve access to markets and economic opportunities.

He also stressed the need to explore innovative financing mechanisms, including public-private partnerships and monetisation of existing highway assets, to mobilise resources for infrastructure development.

Shri Gadkari urged the Indian Roads Congress to focus not only on developing technical standards and guidelines but also on their effective implementation across the country. He called for greater collaboration among the Central and State Governments, research institutions, industry stakeholders and engineering professionals to address emerging challenges in the road sector.

The Minister expressed confidence that the deliberations at the 85th Annual Session would contribute to the development of safer, more durable, sustainable and technologically advanced road infrastructure in the country.

***

Across the festival precincts and the capital city, artisans and event teams have put the finishing touches on thematic installations,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Through the Lens: Venues and Avenues in Panaji Gear Up to Host the 57th International Film Festival of India
Canopies of Light and Golden Peacocks Herald the 57th IFFI in Panaji
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 19 November 2026

 

With final preparations wrapping up across Panaji, Goa is all set to host the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Across the festival precincts and the capital city, artisans and event teams have put the finishing touches on thematic installations, walk-through film-reel tunnels, delegate kiosks, and ceremonial arches celebrating the festival's theme, 'Stories Without Borders'.

The capital city of Goa has been transformed into a dazzling hub of cinema and culture ahead of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Major festival venues—including the ESG complex, Kala Academy, and the surrounding avenues of Panaji; feature elaborate thematic installations celebrating India's rich cinematic heritage.

A vibrant daytime installation featuring the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) emblem set against colourful geometric accents welcomes visitors in Panaji, Goa.

 

Film posters displayed under the official 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) and NFDC archway celebrate diverse cinema at the festival venue in Panaji, Goa.

 

A wide view of the decorated traffic island adorned with 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI 2026) installations and colourful motifs in Panaji, Goa, ahead of the festival's inauguration.

 

Newly erected delegate registration and information kiosks bearing the official 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) branding line the tree-lined promenade at the festival venue in Panaji, Goa.

 

Event crew members install film posters inside a giant cinema-reel-themed walk-through tunnel at the festival premises as final preparations conclude for the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI)

 

A 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI 2026) installation stands at a decorated traffic island in Panaji, Goa, ahead of the festival's opening

 

A grand illuminated entrance arch adorned with vibrant peacock-feather motifs and cascading overhead drapery welcomes delegates and cinephiles.

 

A glowing '57' installation featuring the iconic IFFI Golden Peacock emblem stands amidst illuminated heritage architecture and cascading fairy lights at the festival premises in Panaji, Goa, ahead of the 57th International Film Festival of India.

 

Canopies of warm fairy lights and official 57th IFFI banners transform the tree-lined avenues of Panaji into a festive corridor in preparation for the International Film Festival of India in Goa.

 

Vibrant LED lighting and decorative peacock-themed signage illuminate the streets along the Mandovi riverfront in Panaji, Goa, as the city gears up to host the 57th International Film Festival of India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya chairs 240th meeting of Central Board of Trustees (CBT), EPF
CBT approves Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF members, enabling periodic payouts of retirement savings
The Board approves major relaxation in EPF withdrawal: Minimum PF balance requirement reduced from 25% to 10% and waiting period for final withdrawal from 12 months to 2 months
EDLI exemption reforms: Relief and transitional support for establishments under the Scheme
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, chaired the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) in New Delhi today. Co-Vice-Chairperson Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar (Secretary, Labour & Employment), and Member Secretary Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi (CPFC), alongside representatives of Central/State Governments, employers and employees, also attended the meeting.

The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), in recent years, has introduced several key reforms and innovations to strengthen social security delivery through wider coverage, simplified claim settlement and digitalisation. These include enhancement in wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000, introduction of simplified partial withdrawal rules and liberalised withdrawal limits, and rolling out of CITES 2.01, among others. With a view to taking this spirit of reform further, several key proposals were put forth by EPFO in today’s meeting, chaired by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.

The following agenda items were placed before the Board, relating to pension reforms, provident fund flexibility, investment management, governance, exemption policy and digital transformation of EPFO:-

  • Introduction of Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for EPF Members: The Board approved a proposal to introduce Systematic Withdrawal Plan, which will enable retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire amount in one go.

This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference. This facility would provide members with a structured source of periodic income while allowing the remaining corpus to continue generating returns, thereby helping augment their retirement income and supplement their pension benefits. The facility would be entirely voluntary, with no compulsion on members to opt for withdrawals. The option may also be extended to eligible family members/beneficiaries, ensuring greater flexibility and financial security for the family. This aims to ensure stable post-retirement income, reduce reinvestment risks, strengthen fund sustainability and facilitate the extension of social security coverage to gig and platform workers.

SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving ownership of the underlying corpus. Approximately 6.32 lakh EPF members aged above 55 years possess provident fund accumulations exceeding ₹5 lakh are expected to be the primary beneficiaries of the proposed SWP framework during the initial phase. In case of the member's death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments. The initiative will enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream, while safeguarding their families' interests. Apart from the immediate potential beneficiaries indicated above, the SWP scheme is likely to attract many other PF members retiring in the future who seek an additional post-retirement stream of withdrawals from their accumulated PF corpus.

Additionally, to further boost flexibility and move towards the goal of universal social security, the proposal also introduces UAN-linked mechanisms for direct voluntary contributions and third-party micro-contributions (such as customer tips), completely independent of traditional employer payroll systems. The necessary amendments to the EPF scheme will be notified accordingly after approval from the Ministry. The proposal for a corresponding amendment in the Income Tax Act is being taken up with the Ministry of Finance.

  • Review of minimum balance and waiting period for final PF withdrawal: Board approved the provisions relating to the minimum balance requirement and waiting period for withdrawal, with a view to safeguarding the long-term social security interests of EPF members. A provision had earlier been made for earmarking 25% of the contributions in the Members’ account as Minimum Balance to be maintained by the member at all times. Now, the minimum balance requirement  for EPF  has been reduced from existing 25% to 10% and waiting period has been reduced from 12 months to 2 months. The changes aim to provide greater financial flexibility to EPF members while safeguarding their long-term social security interests.
  • Relief in EDLI exemption cases: The Board approved amendments to EDLI Scheme, 2026, to facilitate resolution of pending legacy exemption cases and provide a six-month window to eligible establishments for renewal of expired exemptions, along with relief from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period. This will provide relief to eligible establishments by facilitating the settlement of pending and expired exemption cases, with a six-month window for renewal and relaxation from contributions, interest and penal damages for the verified transitional period.

The proposed amendments aim to resolve long-pending exemption cases under the earlier EDLI Scheme, 1976, and address difficulties faced by establishments during the transition to the new Scheme. This will help establishments that had been maintaining group insurance policies for their employees but could not complete formal exemption or renewal procedures due to administrative and procedural difficulties.

Establishments that maintained continuous group insurance coverage with benefits equal to or better than the statutory EDLI Scheme and duly settled eligible insurance claims may receive relief from contribution liability for the intervening period, along with protection from penal damages and interest, subject to verification. This initiative reflects the Government's commitment to reducing compliance difficulties, ensuring a fair transition to the new legal framework and providing relief to establishments while safeguarding employees' insurance benefits.

  • Investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs): The Board in-principle approved to permit investment of up to 3% of fresh accretion in eligible Alternative Investment Funds, within the existing overall investment ceiling, initially through government-backed entities. The decision aims to diversify EPFO's investment portfolio while ensuring prescribed safeguards and investment oversight.
  • Surrender/cancellation of EPF exemptions: Proposals concerning surrender of exemption by 27 establishments and cancellation of exemption in four establishments were reviewed. These cases involve transfer of accumulated provident fund savings amounting to approximately ₹5,996 crore to EPFO, covering 1,44,437 members, bringing their accounts under EPFO's direct administration.
  • Implementation of CITES 2.0: The Board was apprised of the progress of Centralised IT Enabled System (CITES) 2.0, a centralised, UAN-based digital platform developed by C-DAC to modernise EPFO services. Post implementation of CITIES 2.0 auto-processing of claims increased from 39% to 71% of the total claim processed. The introduction of pre-validation greater automation and simplified withdrawal limits reduced overall rejection ratio from 23% to 7.82%. The overall processing and the average claims settlement time has declined from 11.15 days to 2.57 days.
  • Budget Estimates 2026-27 and 2027-28 of EPFO: The Board approved Revised Estimates for 2026-27 and Budget Estimates for 2027-28 of EPFO under EPF, EPS and EDLI Schemes, covering projected receipts, income and expenditure, to ensure effective financial planning and management of EPFO funds.

The proposals placed before the CBT meeting, underline EPFO's commitment to strengthening the country's social security framework, providing greater flexibility in accessing retirement savings, ensuring sustainable pension administration, safeguarding members' investments and delivering technology-driven, transparent and efficient services to EPF members and pensioners.

The deliberations focused on developing Bastar as a model tribal region through…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
High-Level Meeting in Raipur Reviews Comprehensive Development Plan for Bastar Region
Focus on tribal livelihoods, health, education, infrastructure, forest rights and cultural heritage
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level meeting to deliberate upon the Comprehensive Development Plan for Bastar Region was held in Raipur today under the chairpersonship of Shri Vikas Sheel, Chief Secretary, Government of Chhattisgarh. The deliberations focused on developing Bastar as a model tribal region through coordinated, locally responsive and outcome-oriented interventions.

The delegation from the Ministry of Tribal Affairs was led by Shri Manish Thakur, Additional Secretary, MoTA along with Ms. Samidha Singh, Director, MoTA, Mr. Akhila Biharia Ota and Ms. Sweta Mishra, Senior Advisors MoTA and Shri Subhash Kumar, DAJGUA Division MoTA.

Attendees from Govt. of Chhattisgarh included Shri Vikas Sheel, Chief Secretary; Shri Manoj Kumar Pingua, Forest and Climate Change Department; Smt. Shahla Nigar, Women and Child Development Department; Dr. Kamal Preet Singh, School Education Department; Shri Siddharth Komal Pardeshi, Agriculture Development, Farmers Welfare and Biotechnology Department; Shri Amit Kataria, Health and Family Welfare Department; Shri Solid Bharati Dasan, Tourism and Culture Department; Shri Basavaraju S., Technical Education, Employment and Skill Development Department; Shri Rajesh Singh Rana, Rural Industries Department; Dr. Saransh Mittar, Energy Department; and Shri D. Rahul Venkat, Commissioner, Tribal and Scheduled Caste Development.

The Development Plan covers the seven districts of Bastar Division—Bastar, Kanker, Kondagaon, Narayanpur, Dantewada, Bijapur and Sukma. Building upon the Ministry’s engagement with the State and district administration, the meeting provided a platform to examine developmental gaps, identify implementation priorities and strengthen convergence among Central schemes, State departments and district-level institutions, including ITDAs/ITDPs.

Key interventions discussed included community-managed crèches in vulnerable tribal areas; a proposed Sickle Cell Disease Centre of Competence at Jagdalpur; targeted malaria and tuberculosis elimination; mother-tongue-based multilingual education; and adult, digital and financial literacy. Livelihood priorities encompassed tamarind and mahua value-addition clusters, agriculture and horticulture, livestock and fisheries, tribal entrepreneurship, traditional craft clusters, the proposed TRIFOOD Park at Jagdalpur and community-led eco-tourism.

The Plan also envisages conservation of sacred groves and indigenous medicinal plants, promotion of tribal music and crafts, strengthening of the BADAL Academy, recognition of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group habitat rights and community forest resource management. Proposals for village electrification and other basic amenities were also highlighted. The Ministry’s presentation outlined interventions at different stages of approval, proposal development and implementation.

The meeting underscored the importance of community participation, district-specific planning, time-bound follow-up and effective institutional coordination to translate proposed interventions into measurable improvements in the quality of life and livelihood opportunities of tribal communities across Bastar.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Academic and Research Opportunities through National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students
Rajesh Kumar from Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand, Pursue Ph.D. under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:21PM by PIB Delhi

Access to higher education and research opportunities plays a significant role in promoting academic excellence, professional advancement and socio-economic empowerment, particularly among students belonging to Scheduled Caste communities.

Mr. Rajesh Kumar (name changed), a 30-year-old research scholar from Udham Singh Nagar district of Uttarakhand, is pursuing his Ph.D. with financial assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

With a keen interest in academics and research, Rajesh aspires to become an Assistant Professor and contribute to the higher education sector. His academic aspirations reflect his commitment towards educational advancement and professional growth.

In 2020, Rajesh began receiving financial assistance under the NFSC Scheme, which includes fellowship assistance, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency support. The assistance has helped him address the financial requirements associated with doctoral studies and research activities.

For scholars pursuing doctoral studies, access to sustained financial assistance is an important enabler of academic advancement. The fellowship provides financial stability, while the House Rent Allowance supports accommodation-related expenses and contingency assistance facilitates research-related expenditure.

Since receiving support under the Scheme, Rajesh has reported an improvement in his financial position and positive changes in his life. The assistance has enabled him to focus on his academic pursuits while continuing to work towards his professional aspiration of becoming an Assistant Professor.

Beyond providing financial assistance, the NFSC Scheme seeks to encourage academic excellence, research capabilities and professional development among students belonging to Scheduled Caste communities, thereby strengthening their participation in higher education.

Rajesh’s academic journey highlights the significance of targeted educational interventions in nurturing talent, strengthening research opportunities and enabling scholars to realise their academic and professional aspirations.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s sustained commitment towards educational empowerment, inclusive socio-economic development and equitable access to higher education and research opportunities, contributing to the larger vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry Of Social Justice And Empowerment Opens Online Registration For National Entrance Test For SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 To Expand Access To Quality Residential Education
SHRESHTA Scheme Aims to Provide Quality Education to Meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) and Eligible De-notified Tribe (DNT) Students in Reputed Private Residential Schools
Online Registration to Remain Open Until November 30, 2026
Official National Testing Agency (NTA) Portal is  https://Exams.Nta.Nic.In/Shreshta Official NTA Website is www.nta.ac.in
National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) Scheduled to be Held on January 10, 2027
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:39PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening access to quality education and promoting inclusive educational opportunities, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, under Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, in collaboration with the National Testing Agency (NTA), has opened online registration for National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027.

The Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA) aims to provide quality education to meritorious students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and De-notified Tribes (DNTs) not covered under the SC, ST and OBC categories, by facilitating access to reputed private residential schools.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the initiative seeks to strengthen educational empowerment by enabling students from targeted communities to access conducive learning environments, pursue academic excellence and realise their full potential. He said access to quality school education plays a pivotal role in advancing social mobility, strengthening academic capabilities and creating opportunities for holistic development.

He said through SHRESHTA Scheme, the Ministry seeks to bridge educational disparities and enable meritorious students from targeted communities to pursue their academic aspirations. The Scheme reflects the Ministry’s sustained emphasis on education as an instrument of social transformation, empowerment and inclusive socio-economic development, Official said.

The Official informed the online registration process for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 commenced on November 14, 2026, and will remain open until November 30, 2026 (up to 11:50 PM), he said.

He added to facilitate candidates in making necessary corrections to their submitted application forms, a correction window will remain operational from December 2 to December 4, 2026.

The National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 is scheduled to be conducted on January 10, 2027, he further said.

The Official said the eligible candidates may submit their online applications through the official National Testing Agency (NTA) portal at https://exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta

The Ministry encourages all eligible candidates to complete their online registration within the prescribed timeline and take advantage of the opportunity to access quality residential education under the SHRESHTA Scheme, the Official said.

Through targeted educational interventions such as SHRESHTA, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reaffirm its commitment to promoting equal educational opportunities, empowering future generations and building an inclusive and equitable society in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, the Official added.

For any queries or assistance relating to the examination and application process, the candidates may contact the National Testing Agency through its official email address, shreshta@nta.ac.in, or helpline numbers 011-40759000 / 1800-180-4747. Candidates may also visit the official NTA website at www.nta.ac.in

item.title: Apollo MedSkills, Neuland Foundation, ZEN Technologies and Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services Sign SHAs with Government Under PM-SETU for ₹1,011 Crore ITI Transformation Projects in Telangana
item.category: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
item.description: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Apollo MedSkills, Neuland Foundation, ZEN Technologies and Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services Sign SHAs with Government Under PM-SETU for ₹1,011 Crore ITI Transformation Projects in Telangana Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:34PM by PIB Delhi In a significant milestone in the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme, Shareholders' Agreements (SHAs) have been signed for four Industrial Training Institute (ITI) clusters in Telangana…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Apollo MedSkills, Neuland Foundation, ZEN Technologies and Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services Sign SHAs with Government Under PM-SETU for ₹1,011 Crore ITI Transformation Projects in Telangana
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:34PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant milestone in the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme, Shareholders' Agreements (SHAs) have been signed for four Industrial Training Institute (ITI) clusters in Telangana with Apollo MedSkills Ltd., Neuland Foundation, ZEN Technologies Ltd. and Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services as Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs). The agreements mark the commencement of the implementation phase of approved Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs) for the Old City, Sangareddy, Medchal and Patancheru clusters, paving the way for industry-led transformation of Government ITIs in the State.

The SHAs have been signed between the Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, Government of Telangana, and the respective industry partners, establishing the institutional framework for implementation of these projects under PM-SETU.

The four clusters represent an approved investment of approximately ₹1,011 crore, including:

  • Old City Cluster with Apollo MedSkills Ltd. as Anchor Industry Partner in the Healthcare & Life Sciences sector, with an approved investment of ₹241 crore;
  • Sangareddy Cluster with Neuland Foundation as Anchor Industry Partner in the Pharmaceuticals & Chemicals sector, with an approved investment of ₹241 crore;
  • Medchal Cluster with ZEN Technologies Ltd. as Anchor Industry Partner in the Defence & Electronics sector, with an approved investment of ₹254 crore; and
  • Patancheru Cluster with Sri Siddhartha Infratech & Services as Anchor Industry Partner in the Diversified Manufacturing sector, with an approved investment of ₹275 crore.

The signing of the SHAs formalises collaboration among the Government of India, the Government of Telangana and the industry partners for execution of the approved projects. Dedicated Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) will now be established for each cluster to oversee implementation and long-term operations. Under the PM-SETU framework, the industry partner will hold a 51 per cent stake in the SPV, while the Government of India and the State Government will each hold 24.5 per cent equity participation.

PM-SETU Moves from Planning to Implementation

With the signing of these agreements, the four Telangana projects move from the planning phase into active implementation. These partnerships are expected to deepen industry participation in vocational education and accelerate the transformation of participating ITIs into modern, future-ready centres of technical excellence. With this milestone, the total number of Shareholders' Agreements signed under PM-SETU has now reached seven, reflecting the growing momentum of industry-led institutional transformation across the country.

The approved investment plans envisage a comprehensive package of interventions, including:

  • Modernisation of training infrastructure, workshops and laboratories;
  • Introduction of industry-relevant technologies and equipment;
  • Alignment of curricula with evolving sectoral requirements;
  • Capacity building and training of instructors;
  • Enhanced industry exposure and apprenticeship opportunities; and
  • Strengthening of placement and employability outcomes for trainees.

By bringing industry expertise directly into the governance and development of ITIs, the initiative aims to create institutions that are responsive to the needs of key sectors of the economy while equipping youth with skills required for emerging job opportunities.

Smt Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, welcomed all industry partners and commended their commitment to transforming ITIs across the country. She noted that PM-SETU is establishing a new paradigm in skill development by placing industry at the heart of institutional transformation.

Representatives from the four industry partners reaffirmed their commitment to supporting the Government's vision of a world-class vocational education ecosystem and contributing sector-specific expertise across healthcare, pharmaceuticals, defence electronics and manufacturing to enhance the quality and relevance of training delivered through the participating ITIs.

Scindia Initiative to strengthen India's domestic telecom manufacturing ecosystem, attract investment and generate employment opportunities Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior Gains Momentum with Distribution of Letters of Intent to 25 Companies
Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Leadership, India Moves from Telecom Services to Telecom Manufacturing: Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia
Initiative to strengthen India's domestic telecom manufacturing ecosystem, attract investment and generate employment opportunities
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh, organised a Letter of Intent (LoI) Distribution Ceremony for 25 companies investing in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior, in Bhopal today. The event marked an important milestone in advancing India's vision of becoming a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technology development.

The ceremony was graced by Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav and Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. Senior officials of the Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, along with representatives from the telecom and electronics industries, participated in the programme. The programme also marked the announcement of Phase-II of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone, signalling a significant step towards expanding the zone's manufacturing ecosystem and strengthening investment opportunities in the telecom and electronics sectors.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said “India has established itself as a global leader in telecom services. However, the time has now come for the next paradigm shift in the telecom industry. We must move from being a services nation to becoming a product nation. It is the responsibility of the Government of India to create an ecosystem that enables industry to establish manufacturing facilities and grow.

The Minister further emphasized, “Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision has always been that there was a time when India depended on the world, but today India is self-reliant. The day is not far when the world will depend on India. We must work towards making this vision a reality in the coming decade. This is India's time, and this is the time for Madhya Pradesh."

The Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav, highlighted “This is the first time in the history of India that we have been able to build a zone dedicated to telecom sector. It is the best example of how the Central and State Government work in tandem for rapid development of industry. For this zone, we have given approval to 170 acres of land through the Cabinet.”

The programme featured a presentation on the Telecom Manufacturing Zone project and its development roadmap by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Industry representatives also shared their perspectives on investment opportunities and industry participation.

 

The Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior is envisaged as an integrated industrial cluster dedicated to telecom manufacturing, research and development, and innovation. Spread across approximately 170 acres, the zone will facilitate manufacturing activities in areas such as telecom equipment, components, optical fibre, software and passive infrastructure.

The latest engagement builds on the Department's continued efforts to attract investment through investor outreach programmes in New Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru. Earlier investor engagements in New Delhi and Mumbai had resulted in investment commitments of ₹5,500 crore, with a potential to generate nearly 20,000 employment opportunities.

The Telecom Manufacturing Zone is aligned with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and “Make in India, Make for the World”. It aims to strengthen domestic supply chains, reduce import dependence, encourage indigenous research and product development, enhance exports and position India as a trusted global destination for telecom manufacturing.

The distribution of Letters of Intent marks another significant step towards translating investor interest into manufacturing opportunities on the ground. The initiative reflects the strong partnership between the Central Government and the Government of Madhya Pradesh towards building a robust, globally competitive and self-reliant telecom manufacturing ecosystem.

The Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior, is poised to contribute to India's emergence as a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technological advancement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C R Paatil reviews Progress of Maharashtra under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain 2026 in Pune
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Paatil, and Chief Minister of Maharashtra, Shri Devendra Fadnavis, participated in a high-level review meeting at Pune, Maharashtra on Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain- 2026, organised by the National Water Mission (NWM), Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, in collaboration with the Government of Maharashtra.

More than 300 officials participated in the meeting from different Departments of the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the State of Maharashtra. The review meeting witnessed participation from  State Government Departments, including Revenue and Forest, Water Resources, Rural Development, Agriculture, Public Works, Urban Development, Employment Guarantee Scheme, Water Supply and Sanitation, and Soil and Water Conservation, along with the Groundwater Surveys and Development Agency (GSDA), Divisional Commissioners, District Collectors, Municipal Commissioners, Chief Executive Officers of Zilla Parishads and other senior district-level officials from across Maharashtra.

The meeting focused on reviewing the progress of JSJB: CTR-2026 and strengthening coordinated efforts towards water conservation, rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge across the State. The programme commenced with opening remarks and a context-setting presentation on JSJB by the National Water Mission, highlighting the objectives and significance of the initiative, as well as the need for sustained efforts to foster community participation in water conservation.

A detailed discussion was held with District Magistrates, Municipal Commissioners and Divisional Forest Officers on issues related to JSJB: CTR-2026, the Jal Jeevan Mission, and the Swachh Bharat Mission. The interaction provided an opportunity to review district-level implementation, discuss challenges and strengthen coordination among the concerned departments and field-level authorities.

During the meeting, the Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) made presentations on the progress of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM). The presentations provided an overview of the initiatives and progress under these flagship programmes, emphasising the importance of coordinated implementation at the State and district levels.

In his special address, Chief Minister, Maharashtra, Shri Devendra Fadnavis highlighted the State Government's commitment to strengthening water conservation efforts and ensuring effective implementation of JSJB: CTR-2026 across Maharashtra. He emphasised the importance of collective participation and coordinated action in addressing water-related challenges and assured that the target would be completed within the timeline.

In his concluding remarks, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Paatil emphasised the importance of sustained efforts towards water conservation, groundwater recharge and people's participation. He underscored the need for effective implementation of JSJB: CTR-2026 and convergence with other flagship programmes to strengthen water security and promote sustainable water management.

The meeting reaffirmed the importance of a coordinated approach involving the Central Government, State Government, district administrations, local bodies, and other stakeholders to advance the objectives and strengthen water conservation efforts across Maharashtra.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Rajasthan Unit, seizes 16.43 kg illicit opium concealed in car at Kota; two suspects arrested
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Rajasthan Unit, has seized 16.43 kg illegal opium concealed in the spare wheel (stepney) of a Maruti Suzuki Brezza car at the Hanging Bridge Toll Plaza, Kota, Rajasthan, on 18 November 2026. Two persons involved in the transportation of the contraband were arrested, and the vehicle used for its transportation was also seized.

 

Car used for trafficking of illicit opium

Acting on specific intelligence regarding the transportation of a huge consignment of opium from Jhalawar to Jaipur in a Rajasthan-registered Brezza car, the CBN, Rajasthan Unit, swiftly constituted a dedicated team of officers on the morning of 18 November 2026. The team strategically deployed surveillance along the suspected route and maintained close watch over the movement of the vehicle. Upon identifying the suspected car, the officers successfully intercepted it at the National Highway 27 near Kota Bypass, along with its two occupants.

Nine packets containing 16.43 kilograms illicit opium seized

A meticulous search of the vehicle led to the recovery of nine packets containing 16.43 kilogram illicit opium, ingeniously concealed inside the spare wheel (stepney) of the car. Following completion of the requisite legal formalities, the recovered contraband and the vehicle were seized, and both occupants were arrested under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

Modus Operandi used for trafficking of illicit Opium           

Further investigation is underway to establish the source of the seized contraband and identify the individuals and organised networks involved in its procurement, transportation and distribution. Efforts are also being made to trace the wider linkages of the drug trafficking network.

This successful operation reflects the sustained efforts, vigilance and commitment of CBN officers towards curbing the menace of drug trafficking.  In line with its zero-tolerance approach towards illicit narcotics, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) remains committed not only to seizing illegal drugs but also to identifying and dismantling the trafficking networks and cartels involved in the narcotics trade. Such intelligence-based enforcement actions will continue as part of the endeavor to achieve a Drug-Free India.

In calendar year 2026, all units of Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) have seized approximately 432 kg opium in 62 cases and arrested 74 suspects till Oct. 2026.

As part of the national endeavor towards a Drug-Free India, the CBN will continue to intensify intelligence-led enforcement operations and take stringent action against those involved in narcotics trafficking.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Himalayan marmot droppings could reveal clues about climate change
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

A new study has probed pollen grains, fungal spores and elemental signatures in the faeces of the Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) to trace valuable information on the environmental conditions of the higher Himalaya and how climate change has affected them.

The Himalaya is highly sensitive to changes in temperature, precipitation and snow cover, which can have a significant impact on alpine vegetation and wildlife habitats. Most conventional palaeoenvironmental studies are based on lake sediments, peat and soil. Scientists from Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an Autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), explored the potential of faeces of Himalayan marmot as an alternative biological archive for environmental changes with climate footprints. This could be especially valuable in remote, arid mountain environments where conventional sedimentary archives are rare.

The Himalayan marmot, a type of herbivorous mammal living at high altitudes in the cold and dry alpine environment of the Himalayan region, relies on local vegetation for food and shelter.

Pollen preserved in the faeces of marmots has left the footprints of the composition of plants consumed by the animal and provides information about the surrounding alpine-steppe vegetation.

The important plant groups in the diet of the marmot were Artemisia, Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae, Poaceae, Cyperaceae and Chenopodiaceae.

Fig 1. Field photographs- a and b.  Alpine steppe vegetation at Pensila Pass in the Himalayan marmot habitat area. c. A Himalayan marmot in their natural habitat in Pensila Pass area. d. Alpine steppe vegetation in Rimkhim area. e. A Himalayan marmot in natural habitat in Rimkhim area. f. Midden faeces of Marmota himalayana, g. Shape and size of the marmot’s faeces pellet.

Photograph credits by Hukam Singh, Manish Mehta, and Vinit Kumar.

Researchers Sadhan K Basumatary, Hukam Singh, Manish Mehta, Swati Tripathi, Mahesh G. Thakkar, H. Gregory McDonald, Eline N. van Asperen & Vinit Kumar identified pollen grains and fungal spores preserved in faeces through palynological analysis, statistical methods for comparing samples from two Himalayan regions and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (FESEM–EDS) to identify elemental composition.

They first evaluated ratios of three types of pollens: Artemisia/Chenopodiaceae, Artemisia/Cyperaceae and Artemisia/Ephedra, for vegetation and climate interpretation based on faecal samples of marmots.

The results indicated that the mixed plant-based diet was dominated by groups like Artemisia, Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae and Chenopodiaceae, pointing toward alpine vegetation and related environmental conditions. Based on the generated data, it was found that the Himalayan marmot could be a strong indicator species for understanding vegetation and climate changes in the higher Himalaya.

Fig 2. Palynomorphs assemblage recovered from the Marmota himalayana faeces samples.

  1. Ephedra, b. Cluster of Poaceae pollen, c. Cyperaceae, d. Cluster of Asteroideae pollen, e. Asteroideae, f. Artemisia, g. Chenopodiaceae, h. Amaranthaceae, i. and j. Convolvulaceae, k. Pinus sp., l. Abies, m. Sporormiella, n. Podospora, o. Cluster of Saccobolus, p. Pleospora, q. Cluster of Thecaphora, r. Meliola, s. Bipolaris, t. Alternaria, u. Arcella, v. Botryococcus.

This study also confirms that changes in the habitat of marmots can indicate shifts in altitude in relation to changing environmental conditions. This combination of pollen, fungal spores and elemental analysis provides a valuable modern reference for future palaeoecological and coprolite studies.

The study published in PLOS ONE would serve as a modern reference for reconstructing past ecological change and assessing potential impacts of climate change. The findings may also help with biodiversity conservation by improving our understanding of marmot habitat requirements, monitoring changes in the ecosystem and informing conservation strategies for associated wildlife, including the snow leopard, for which marmots are an important prey species.

It can contribute to biodiversity conservation, environmental monitoring, climate research and sustainable management of fragile Himalayan ecosystems.

Publication link:

https://doi. org/10.1371/journal.pone.0358642
