item.description: Ministry of Defence Raksha Mantri visits Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Naval Base in Yokosuka Growing India-Japan maritime cooperation is a reflection of deep trust & shared commitment towards a free, open & rules-based Indo-Pacific: Shri Rajnath Singh “India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies despite global challenges, defence sector is witnessing unprecedented growth” Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi “The growing maritime cooperation between India and Japan is a reflection of the deep trust and shared commitment…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri visits Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Naval Base in Yokosuka
Growing India-Japan maritime cooperation is a reflection of deep trust & shared commitment towards a free, open & rules-based Indo-Pacific: Shri Rajnath Singh
“India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies despite global challenges, defence sector is witnessing unprecedented growth”
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

“The growing maritime cooperation between India and Japan is a reflection of the deep trust and shared commitment of the two nations towards a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh in a post on X following his visit to the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) Naval Base in Yokosuka on November 18, 2026, along with Japan’s Minister of Defense Mr Shinjiro Koizumi. Upon his arrival in Japan, Raksha Mantri commenced his engagements with a visit to the Ministry of Defense, where he was received by his Japanese counterpart.

Shri Rajnath Singh was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour, following which the two Ministers interacted briefly at the Ministry. They, later, travelled to the JMSDF Naval Base in a Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) helicopter. At the Naval Base, the two Ministers toured the Mogami-class multi-mission frigate JS Natori.

本日小泉進次郎防衛大臣(@shinjirokoiz)とともに 横須賀の海上自衛隊基地を訪問し、もがみ型多機能護衛艦「なとり」を視察しました。 インドと日本の海洋分野における協力関係の進展は自由で開かれた法の支配に基づくインド太平洋の実現に向けた、両国間の深い信頼と共通の決意を反映するものです。

— Rajnath Singh (@rajnathsingh) November 18, 2026

Raksha Mantri also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Tokyo at an event organised by the Embassy of India. Addressing the gathering, he highlighted India's remarkable economic transformation, asserting that the country has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, despite challenges arising from the situation in West Asia.

Highlighting the unprecedented growth in India’s defence sector, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that domestic defence production has crossed a record Rs 1.80 lakh crore, up from Rs 48,000 crore a decade ago. He added that defence exports have registered a remarkable increase from Rs 600 crore to an all-time high of Rs 38,000 crore, reflecting India's growing indigenous capabilities and expanding footprint in the global defence market.

Emphasising the Government's zero-tolerance policy towards corruption, Raksha Mantri stated that corruption has been significantly curbed over the last 12 years, with benefits of welfare schemes reaching their intended beneficiaries. “No one can question the integrity of our Government,” he added. He also highlighted the Government's efforts towards poverty alleviation and the significant improvements in sanitation and cleanliness across the country.

Raksha Mantri is on a two-day visit to Japan. On November 19, 2026, he will participate in the 4th India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with Japan's Minister of Defense. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Raksha Mantri and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, along with Mr Shinjiro Koizumi and Japan's Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Toshimitsu Motegi. The bilateral meeting between Shri Rajnath Singh and Mr Shinjiro Koizumi will be their third meeting this year.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NAMASTE Scheme Promotes Safer Working Conditions And Dignity For A Sanitation Worker Mr Sinu In Palakkad, Kerala
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

For 47-year-old Sinu (name changed), the PPE kit represents more than protective equipment. It reflects recognition of the occupational risks faced by sanitation workers and reinforces the importance of safety, dignity and respect for those who play an essential role in maintaining clean and healthy communities.

For years, Mr Sinu, sanitation worker from Palakkad, Kerala, had carried out his duties while facing daily exposure to waste, dust and potentially harmful gases. The absence of adequate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) exposed him to occupational health risks, including respiratory conditions, skin infections and other work-related illnesses.

As the primary earning member and sole financial support for his family, any health setback could have affected the well-being and financial stability of his household. Despite these challenges, he remained committed to his work and aspired to perform his duties in safer conditions, with dignity and confidence.

Mr Sinu got opportunity on 7 October 2025, when he received a complete PPE kit under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. This proved a significant step towards improving his working conditions. The kit included a safety helmet, safety goggles, a gas mask with filter, nitrile gloves, gum boots and full-body protective clothing.

The protective equipment has helped reduce his direct exposure to hazardous substances while carrying out sanitation-related activities. With access to essential safety gear, he is now able to perform his duties with greater confidence and an improved sense of workplace security.

The intervention has brought a meaningful improvement to his working conditions by addressing a longstanding concern about occupational safety. Although the assistance did not result in a direct change in income, it has helped lower potential health risks and strengthened his confidence in continuing his livelihood while taking better precautions for his well-being.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote the safety, dignity and well-being of sanitation workers by facilitating access to protective equipment and safer working practices. The initiative reflects the Government’s commitment to ensuring that sanitation workers can carry out their essential duties with greater protection and dignity.

item.title: MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
item.category: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
item.description: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities Dialogue focuses on accessible training, meaningful employment and pathways to economic independence Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) held an interaction with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on strengthening disability inclusion in skill…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
Dialogue focuses on accessible training, meaningful employment and pathways to economic independence
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) held an interaction with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on strengthening disability inclusion in skill development and expanding pathways to employment and entrepreneurship. The engagement formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India.

The interaction provided an opportunity to examine how skill development systems can support the dignity, autonomy and economic participation of persons with disabilities. The dialogue centred on addressing barriers across the journey from access to training and certification to employment, retention and career progression, in keeping with the principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).

Speaking on the engagement, Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, MSDE said, “An inclusive skill ecosystem must recognise both the diversity of learners and the equal worth of their aspirations. For persons with disabilities, access to training must translate into the freedom to choose a vocation, demonstrate competence and progress in the world of work. Our endeavour is to embed accessibility across the skilling journey and strengthen the connection between learning and livelihoods. The measure of our progress must be the opportunities people are able to exercise and the economic independence they are able to achieve.”

The engagement brought into focus the importance of accessible training infrastructure, digital learning platforms, learning materials and assessment processes. Reasonable accommodation, assistive technologies and the capacity of trainers and assessors were identified as important considerations in enabling learners with different disabilities to participate on an equal basis. The discussions also underscored the importance of embedding accessibility and appropriate support within mainstream training programmes, alongside disability-specific interventions, to enable greater participation and inclusion.

The dialogue also addressed the relationship between skilling and labour market inclusion. Industry engagement, accessible workplaces and support during the transition from training to employment are critical to ensuring that acquired skills lead to sustained livelihoods. The discussions also emphasised upon the enabling measures to enhance the participation of persons with disabilities in skill training and government employment, while encouraging greater inclusion and employment opportunities in the private sector.

Entrepreneurship and self-employment were also discussed as important pathways to economic independence, including the role of access to finance, mentoring, technology and markets in supporting entrepreneurs with disabilities.

Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities said, “The right to work begins with having a real opportunity to learn, choose and participate. Inclusive vocational training must equip persons with disabilities for the full range of opportunities in a changing economy, with accessibility and reasonable accommodation built into its design. Meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and their representative organisations is essential to this process. Their experience and expertise can help institutions translate commitments into practical changes that advance equality and independence.”

The dialogue also highlighted the role of evidence in strengthening disability inclusion, including through better understanding of participation, training outcomes and pathways to employment. Particular attention was drawn to addressing barriers faced by women with disabilities and persons in rural and underserved areas.

The engagement situated inclusive skilling within the wider objective of enabling persons with disabilities to participate as equal contributors to economic and social development. It provided a platform for exchanging perspectives on how policy, institutional practice, technology and employer participation can work together to expand opportunity.

The United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities is an independent expert appointed by the Human Rights Council. The mandate promotes the rights of persons with disabilities through dialogue, country visits, recommendations and the exchange of good practices.

item.title: National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society Focuses on Preventive Education, Awareness, Identification, Counselling, Treatment, Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration Article 47 of the Constitution Mandates the State to Endeavour to Prohibit Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Drugs Injurious to Health Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been implementing a scheme for the prevention of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society
Focuses on Preventive Education, Awareness, Identification, Counselling, Treatment, Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration
Article 47 of the Constitution Mandates the State to Endeavour to Prohibit Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Drugs Injurious to Health
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been implementing a scheme for the prevention of alcoholism and substance abuse since 1985-86, reflecting its sustained commitment towards addressing substance dependence through preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative interventions. This is in accordance with its Constitutional mandate and commitment to address alcoholism and substance abuse while building a healthy, inclusive and socially empowered society.

The Article 47 of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption, except for medicinal purposes, of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the magnitude of the challenge was highlighted by the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India, conducted in 2018 by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, New Delhi, and released in February 2019. The survey provided important insights into the extent and pattern of substance use across the country and underscored the need for comprehensive interventions, he said.

According to the survey, approximately 16 crore people consumed alcohol in India, of whom more than 5.7 crore required assistance for harmful or dependent use. Around 3.1 crore people used cannabis products, while 2.26 crore used opioids. Of these, approximately 25 lakh individuals were dependent on cannabis, while nearly 77 lakh required assistance for opioid use, the Official informed.

The Official added the survey further revealed that more than 7 crore individuals were affected by substance use disorders, including nearly 1.2 crore children and 58 lakh women, highlighting the importance of sustained awareness, early intervention, accessible treatment and rehabilitation services.

The Official said the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) has been designed to address the multifaceted challenges associated with substance use through a comprehensive and coordinated approach.

 

The Ministry continues to strengthen preventive and rehabilitative efforts while promoting a compassionate, supportive and inclusive approach towards individuals affected by substance use disorders, he added.

He said that NAPDDR is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with Central Sector components and focuses on two key objectives.

The Official said the first objective is to reduce drug demand through preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation. The second objective is to reduce the stigma and discrimination associated with drug dependence, which often create barriers to the social acceptance and reintegration of affected individuals, he said.

He said the Plan recognises that addressing substance dependence requires not only treatment and rehabilitation but also an enabling social environment in which individuals can seek assistance without fear of discrimination or exclusion.

The Official said the awareness generation and preventive education play a significant role in informing individuals, families and communities about the harmful consequences of substance use. Early identification and timely counselling, along with access to appropriate treatment and rehabilitation facilities, are essential components of the national response, the Official said.

He further said that reducing stigma and discrimination is equally important to ensure that individuals recovering from substance dependence can return to their families and communities and participate meaningfully in society.

The Official said with its focus on prevention, awareness, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Ministry is working towards building a healthier and drug-free society, in alignment with the constitutional vision and the broader goal of inclusive socio-economic development.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27
PSBs’ profitability soars to highest ever with aggregate net profit of Rs. 1,09,540 crore, growing by 16.9% y-o-y
Total PSBs business crosses Rs. 300 lakh crore; with y-o-y growth at 15.5%
Gross advances of PSBs grew to ₹127 lakh crore, registering a robust growth of 18.8% evenly panned across retail, agriculture and MSME segments
PSBs record historic low stressed assets, with gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and net NPA ratio to 0.33% as on 30.09.2026
Systemic reforms, improved governance and Government’s commitment of healthy PSBs manifest through improved financial performance of PSBs in profitability, business growth, asset quality and capital position
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

The sustained improvement in financial health across different financial parameters, including, inter alia, capital adequacy, business growth, low slippages, healthy asset quality and outstandingly improved profitability, establishes the complete turnaround in overall functioning of Public Sector Banks (PSBs). It shows that PSBs are not only making profit but also meeting the requirements of credit supply need with improved underwriting capabilities, aided by technology and higher governance standards.

PSBs’ aggregate net profit reached ₹1.10 lakh crore with 16.9% y-o-y growth and aggregate operating profit reached ₹1.81 lakh crore with 13.9% y-o-y growth. Return on assets of PSBs continue to improve, reaching 1.11% with y-o-y improvement of 3bps. The continued improvement in profitability in both net and operating profit for the fifth consecutive year shows fruitful outcome of enablement of deeply engaged reforms drive and establishment of better governance standards by the Government.

Aggregate business of PSBs grew by 15.5% y-o-y to ₹301.6 lakh crore as on 30.9.2026, crossing the ₹300 lakh crore business mark for the first time. While aggregate deposits grew by 13.1% y-o-y to reach ₹275 lakh crore, the aggregate advances grew at 18.8% y-o-y to reach ₹136.4 lakh crore. The robust credit growth having evenly panned out across different segments, i.e. Retail, Agriculture, MSME, shows PSBs’ continued support to grassroot economic development, inculcation of entrepreneurship and deepening financial inclusion. Credit growth for retail, agriculture and MSME loans was recorded at 17%, 19.5%, 20.4%, respectively.

PSBs’ asset quality remains in continual improvement, recording another long-time low, with Gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and Net NPA ratio declining to 0.33%. Low levels of NPAs are aided by better underwriting standards visible through low slippages of 0.62% and continually focused collections efforts visible through improved recoveries and upgradations of 21.1%. All PSBs are now having provisioning coverage ratio of above 90%, reflecting prudent banking practices and resilient financial performance.

Capital buffers of PSBs remain well above regulatory minimum benchmark through higher retained earnings and strong capital raising, showing availability of adequate cushion to support credit growth while also having capability to absorb systemic shocks. CRAR of PSBs was at 16.89% as on 30.9.2026, improved by 93bps y-o-y. The improvement was also aided by decline in RWA density by 94bps y-o-y to 47.9%.

Cost to income ratio of PSBs also improved by 191 bps y-o-y to 47.38% for H1FY2026-27, aided by decline in cost per asset to 1.60% by 14bps y-o-y. The improved operational efficiency shows gains of investment in technologies and digital transformation, a reflection of efficient cost management.

Performance of PSBs is true reflection of outcomes of institutionalisation of reforms by the Government in PSBs, primarily aimed at better governance standards, improved operational efficiency, prudency in banking practices, enhanced risk management and continual adaptability of technology. The steps taken by the Government in improving operational standards of PSBs is now being reflected in the financial performance, aimed supporting India’s growth aspirations of Viksit Bharat 2047.

item.title: One-day capacity building workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” organised in Kolkata, West Bengal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
item.description: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation One-day capacity building workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” organised in Kolkata, West Bengal MoSPI is accelerating India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 through robust Sustainable Development Goal monitoring framework at the State and UT levels The workshop focuses on strengthening State/UT Indicator Frameworks by supporting States/UTs currently developing their indicator frameworks and featuring sub-national monitoring best practices Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
One-day capacity building workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” organised in Kolkata, West Bengal
MoSPI is accelerating India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 through robust Sustainable Development Goal monitoring framework at the State and UT levels
The workshop focuses on strengthening State/UT Indicator Frameworks by supporting States/UTs currently developing their indicator frameworks and featuring sub-national monitoring best practices
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the Department of Planning, Statistics and Programme Monitoring, Government of West Bengal and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a one-day Capacity Building Workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” in Kolkata, West Bengal on 18th November, 2026. The workshop brought together government officials from States and Union Territories that are in process of development of their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks (SIFs/UTIFs) and the three (3) States/UT sharing best practices, with the aim of strengthening institutional capacities and providing targeted technical support to advance the process. Around 50 participants attended the workshop, comprising officers from MoSPI, UNDP, and States/UTs-West Bengal, Maharashtra, Delhi, Odisha, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

 

With around four years remaining to achieve the 2030 Agenda, strengthening sub-national monitoring systems is critical to advancing SDG localisation and translating national commitments into measurable outcomes at the State/UT levels. State/UT-level monitoring enables governments to track progress against SDG targets, identify development gaps and align policies and interventions with local priorities.

As per SDGs-National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2026, 33 States and Union Territories have developed their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Strengthening the remaining frameworks and improving existing monitoring systems is important to ensure comprehensive SDG monitoring across the country.

In the inaugural session, Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, emphasised the importance of strengthening monitoring systems at the State and local levels. She highlighted that national-level data alone cannot capture the diversity of development challenges across India. State and District Indicator Frameworks are essential to translate national SDG commitments into locally relevant priorities and measurable outcomes. She also underlined the need to strengthen statistical capacities and improve the quality and timeliness of data.

Shri Pawan Kadyan, Senior Special Secretary, Department of Finance, Government of West Bengal, highlighted the need for State Indicator Frameworks to reflect ground realities and local development priorities. He emphasised that monitoring should extend to districts, blocks and Gram Sabhas. He also stressed the need to move beyond tracking scheme implementation and fund utilisation towards measuring actual development outcomes, enabling a shift towards outcome-oriented governance. Representative of UNDP, Mr. Jaimon Uthup, Policy Specialist emphasized the commitment to supporting the Government of India and States/UTs in building robust data systems, technical capacities, and inclusive monitoring mechanisms.

Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, highlighted the ongoing statistical reforms undertaken by MoSPI to address emerging data needs and strengthen the evidence base for development planning. He emphasised the importance of linking Indicator Frameworks not only with the SDGs but also with India's longer-term development goals under Viksit Bharat. He noted that updated base years and new statistical surveys to capture the unorganised sector and services economy are strengthening the country's statistical system.

The technical sessions commenced with a presentation by Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, on strengthening the SDG monitoring architecture at national and sub-national levels. The session covered the National Indicator Framework (NIF), its alignment with State/UT Indicator Frameworks, principles for indicator selection, data sources, reporting periodicity and institutional responsibilities.

A key component of the workshop was the sharing of good practices and experiences from States that have made progress in strengthening SDG monitoring and localisation. Representatives from Maharashtra, Delhi and Odisha presented their approaches, highlighting institutional arrangements, data systems and lessons that could inform the development and strengthening of State/UT Indicator Frameworks.

Officials from the participating State and UT administrations presented their progress, institutional preparedness, data readiness and challenges in developing their respective frameworks. The discussions helped identify State/UT-specific priorities, institutional requirements and data-related gaps.

The workshop also included a facilitated group exercise led by MoSPI and UNDP, focusing on the development and refinement of draft State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Participants reviewed potential indicators for each SDG, identified State/UT-specific indicators reflecting local development priorities, mapped responsible departments and data sources, and assessed data availability and gaps. The exercise also emphasised the integration of gender-responsive and disaggregated indicators, wherever relevant, and the prioritisation of indicators based on relevance and monitoring requirements.

The workshop concluded with discussions on key recommendations and next steps for finalising and strengthening the respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. MoSPI and UNDP reaffirmed their commitment to providing continued technical support to the all States/UTs.

The workshop reiterated the importance of robust sub-national statistical systems in advancing SDG localisation and evidence-based policymaking. State and UT Indicator Frameworks provide a common basis for tracking progress against the SDGs while reflecting local development priorities and longer-term Vision 2047 agendas. These frameworks can also strengthen planning, monitoring and decision-making at State and sub-State levels

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat initiates stakeholder consultations
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

The High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat constituted by the Government of India, in its first two sittings discussed the key areas for examination under its Terms of Reference. It also identified stakeholder groups for consultation, including banks, non-banking financial companies, development financial institutions, regulators, industry associations, fintech organisations and others.

To ensure a structured consultative process, the Committee has circulated questionnaires to stakeholder groups, inviting their views and suggestions on key areas of banking sector reforms.

Going forward, the Committee will hold consultation meetings with key stakeholders to gather further inputs for its recommendations on Banking for Viksit Bharat 2047.

These consultations will help the Committee frame recommendations to strengthen the Indian banking sector and make it competitive, resilient, inclusive and future-ready.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
In line with PM Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on 19th November 2026
Organised by National Investigation Agency (NIA), this year’s Conference will hold discussions on 'Cross-Border Terrorism' theme
Conference to serve as a platform for collective deliberation among security agencies, investigators and experts on emerging terror threats
The conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders with the 'Whole of Government approach'
Subjects like, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations and effective management of trials, will be discussed
Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, espionage, and emerging hybrid threats to national security
The deliberations will enable LEAs to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate the two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on Thursday, 19th November 2026. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference will deliberate on the theme 'Cross-Border Terrorism'.

Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies / forces, an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism.

In keeping with the 'Whole of Government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy.

The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, and emerging hybrid threats to national security. Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges.

This year, the conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for State police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the Government to improve prosecution.

Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations.

The conference will be attended by senior police officers of States and Union Territories, officers of Central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India positions CDRI as a key Global Platform for Climate-resilient Infrastructure; Calls for translating Commitments into Action at COP31, in Antalya (Türkiye)
CDRI provides a Global Platform for Strengthening Disaster-resilient Infrastructure through International Cooperation: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi

Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted India's leadership in advancing global cooperation on disaster-resilient infrastructure at the CDRI Ministerial Dialogue on ‘Disaster Resilient Infrastructure for Climate Adaptation’ at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. He emphasised that climate action must go hand in hand with climate negotiations, with the success of international commitments ultimately measured by their translation into concrete action on the ground.

Shri Yadav stressed the need for practical outcomes in adaptation, mitigation and resilience, backed by stronger international cooperation and collective efforts. He highlighted the importance of knowledge sharing, technical expertise and capacity building, particularly for developing countries, to strengthen institutional capabilities and facilitate access to proven technologies. The Minister underscored that affordable and sustainable finance, complemented by strong institutional frameworks and technical capacities, is essential for developing resilient infrastructure.

Describing the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) as a unique global initiative, Shri Yadav highlighted its role in bringing together governments, international institutions, development partners and technical experts to promote collaboration, exchange best practices and strengthen infrastructure resilience. He noted that discussions at COP31 had reinforced resilience as a key priority and called for translating shared commitments into collaborative initiatives and tangible outcomes.

Representatives from participating countries highlighted their respective priorities and challenges. Trinidad and Tobago stressed the importance of grant and affordable finance, risk assessment tools and cooperation with the Government of India in agro-processing. Namibia highlighted the severe impact of drought on rural livelihoods and called for adequate funding to strengthen infrastructure resilience. Japan emphasised accelerating the deployment of Early Warning Systems, sharing disaster risk reduction expertise and strengthening regional networks in vulnerable countries. Guatemala underscored the need for affordable finance, while Jordan called for greater cooperation in facilitating access to finance and strengthening infrastructure planning.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Challenges to Academic Aspirations
NFSC Fellowship Supports a First-Generation Learner From Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh
Fellowship and HRA Assistance Since November 2020 Helped a Scholar Pursue Ph.D. Studies and Build a Career in Education
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

The experience of Mr. Rajesh Kumar (name changed) highlights how targeted fellowship assistance can help expand access to higher education and promote social empowerment.

It reflects the role of educational support in enabling individuals to pursue their potential and contribute to a more inclusive and equitable society.

Access to higher education can be particularly challenging for students from financially constrained backgrounds, especially those who are the first in their families to pursue advanced studies.

For Mr. Rajesh Kumar, a resident of Jaunpur district in Uttar Pradesh, financial difficulties and limited awareness of higher educational opportunities presented significant hurdles in pursuing his academic aspirations.

As a first-generation learner, he had limited information about avenues for higher education and available scholarship schemes. Alongside financial constraints, family responsibilities and social pressure to seek immediate employment or settle down made it difficult to continue on the path of advanced education. Despite these challenges, he remained determined to pursue higher studies and aspired to become an Assistant Professor.

A significant support came in November 2020, when he began receiving assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The fellowship, along with House Rent Allowance (HRA), provided financial assistance to support his pursuit of Ph.D. studies.

The assistance helped ease the financial burden associated with higher education and enabled him to continue working towards his academic goals despite the ups and downs along the way. It also provided an opportunity to focus on education at a time when financial and social circumstances could otherwise have restricted his choices.

Beyond financial assistance, the fellowship support contributed to widening his access to educational opportunities. In his account, the support helped him move beyond barriers and work towards becoming an educated and socially conscious individual.

Today, Mr. Kumar is working as a teacher at a self-financed college and is engaged in the field of education. His present role reflects his progress in translating his educational journey into a professional contribution. His aspiration to become an Assistant Professor continues to represent the academic goal that has guided his pursuit of higher studies.

His journey underscores the importance of sustained financial support in enabling first-generation learners to pursue higher education. By helping address economic barriers, the NFSC Scheme supports students in continuing their studies and working towards their professional aspirations.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to inaugurate FICCI Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention on 19 November
FICCI’s Centenary Year Convention to focus on the theme “Bharat 2047”
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) on 19 November 2026 at around 11 AM at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

The convention, themed “Bharat 2047”, will bring together over 2,500 delegates, including industry leaders, CEOs, ambassadors, diplomats and policymakers. The year 2026-27 marks FICCI's centenary year, as the organisation completes 100 years of its establishment on 7 April 2027.

Established in 1927, FICCI was founded at a time when Indian enterprises had limited representation in economic policymaking. Since Independence, FICCI has been associated with India's economic transformation and its growing integration with the global economy.

Today, FICCI represents over 2.5 lakh companies across the public, private and multinational sectors, directly and through more than 300 affiliated regional and state-level industry associations. It has partnership agreements with 250 national business associations in over 100 countries.

item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
From ASEAN to Europe: India's Exports Gain Momentum Across FTA Partners and Beyond
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

India's exports to key FTA partners and major trading markets recorded broad-based growth during April–September FY 2026–27. Exports to ASEAN surged 58% to US$ 28.06 billion, while shipments to SAFTA partners rose 22% to US$ 15.29 billion. Exports to the European Union increased 5% to US$ 38.79 billion. Strong growth in Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Japan, South Korea and Oman, alongside gains in other European markets, reflected India's widening export footprint and strengthening trade linkages across global markets.

 

Introduction

India's exports to key Free Trade Agreement (FTA) partners and major trade-partner markets recorded broad-based growth during April-September FY 2026-27. Strong export performance across ASEAN, South Asia, East Asia and several European markets reflected the growing geographical diversification of India's trade.

Among the major export destinations, Singapore, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Oman, Italy and Spain registered particularly strong growth. ASEAN emerged as a significant contributor to the overall expansion, while neighbouring South Asian markets recorded sustained growth.

Exports to developed markets, including the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Australia and the United Kingdom, also increased during the period. The performance across these markets highlights the widening geographical spread of India's exports and its expanding trade linkages.

 

ASEAN Emerges as a Major Growth Engine

India's exports to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) recorded significant growth during the first half of FY 2026-27. Under the CECA framework, exports to ASEAN increased 58%, from US$ 17.75 billion in April-September FY 2025-26 to US$ 28.06 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2026-27.

  • Singapore emerged as one of the strongest-performing markets in the region. India's exports to Singapore more than doubled, increasing 103% from US$ 5.45 billion to US$ 11.07 billion.
  • Malaysia also registered a substantial increase, with exports rising 83% from US$ 3.05 billion to US$ 5.58 billion during the period
  • Exports to Vietnam increased 36% to US$ 3.83 billion, while shipments to Indonesia rose 36% to US$ 2.98 billion.
  • Thailand remained another important export destination, with shipments valued at US$ 2.65 billion.

 

 

Exports to SAFTA Partners Rise 22%

Exports to South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) partners also recorded growth during April-September FY 2026-27. Total exports to SAFTA markets increased 22%, from US$ 12.55 billion to US$ 15.29 billion during the corresponding period.

  • Sri Lanka emerged as a major growth market, with exports rising 73% from US$ 2.28 billion to US$ 3.94 billion.
  • Exports to Nepal increased 19%, from US$ 3.66 billion to US$ 4.37 billion.
  • Bhutan also recorded growth of 16%, with exports reaching US$ 711.4 million.
  • Among smaller South Asian markets, Maldives registered strong growth of 52%, with exports increasing from US$ 222.2 million to US$ 337.4 million.
  • Bangladesh remained India's largest export destination within SAFTA, with shipments valued at US$ 5.66 billion, registering growth of 2%.

 

 

Japan and South Korea Strengthen East Asian Export Momentum

India's exports to Japan and South Korea recorded notable increases during April-September FY 2026-27, contributing to the broader expansion of trade across Asian markets.

  • Exports to Japan increased 40%, from US$ 2.92 billion to US$ 4.10 billion during the period.
  • Similarly, exports to South Korea increased 24%, from US$ 3.15 billion to US$ 3.91 billion.

The strong growth in both markets adds to the broader momentum across India's Asian trade partners, alongside the sizable increases recorded in Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam and Indonesia.

 

EFTA Markets Maintain Positive Export Growth

India's exports to European Free Trade Association (EFTA) partners increased by approximately 5%, from US$ 980.2 million to US$ 1.03 billion during April-September FY 2026-27.

  • Switzerland remained India's largest export destination among EFTA partners. Exports to the country increased 11%, reaching US$ 758.4 million.
  • Norway also recorded positive growth, with exports increasing 14% to US$ 264.0 million.
  • Liechtenstein registered 30% export growth, although from a relatively smaller base.

 

 

European Union Markets Record Steady Growth

Total exports to the European Union (EU) increased 5%, from US$ 36.97 billion to US$ 38.79 billion, supported by growth across several major European destinations.

  • Spain emerged as one of the strongest-performing markets, with exports increasing 45% from US$ 3.23 billion to US$ 4.68 billion.
  • Italy also recorded substantial growth, with Indian exports rising 25%, from US$ 3.63 billion to US$ 4.55 billion.
  • Germany remained a major European export destination, recording growth of 12%, with exports reaching US$ 6.34 billion.
  • Exports to France increased 9% to US$ 3.73 billion.

Several smaller European markets, including Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Estonia and the Czech Republic, also registered particularly strong growth during the period.

 

 

New-Generation Trade Partners Add to Export Momentum

Beyond ASEAN, South Asia and major East Asian and European markets, India's exports to several other trading partners also recorded positive growth during April-September FY 2026-27.

  • Oman registered particularly strong growth, with exports increasing 47%, from US$ 2.23 billion to US$ 3.29 billion.
  • Exports to Australia increased 11%, from US$ 3.69 billion to US$ 4.10 billion.
  • The United Kingdom also recorded positive growth, with Indian exports rising 7%, from US$ 6.83 billion to US$ 7.32 billion.
  • Mauritius witnessed a notable increase of 45%, with exports reaching US$ 346.2 million during the period.

 

New-Generation Trade Partners Add to Export Momentum

India's export performance during April-September FY 2026-27 reflects sustained growth across several FTA partner markets and major trading destinations. ASEAN emerged as a particularly dynamic region, driven by the doubling of exports to Singapore and substantial increases in shipments to Malaysia, Vietnam and Indonesia.

South Asian markets also contributed to the expansion, with Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives registering positive growth. At the same time, increased exports to Japan, South Korea, Oman, Australia and several European markets demonstrated the widening geographical spread of India's export destinations.

The broad-based growth across traditional and emerging markets highlights the increasing diversification of India's export footprint and strengthening trade linkages across Asia, Europe and other major global markets.

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
9th Naturopathy Day Celebrated Across the Country under the Theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’
National-level celebration at CRIYN, Nagamangala, Karnataka, highlights the role of Yoga and Naturopathy in preventive and promotive healthcare
“Naturopathy and healthy lifestyles are essential for preventive healthcare and building a Swasth Bharat”: Shri Prataprao Jadhav
“Scientific research, health awareness and community participation are key to advancing naturopathy”: Secretary, Ministry of Ayush
ReGEN-Beta Diabetes Lifestyle Trial, Nature Cure 360 and key research publications released
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

The 9th Naturopathy Day was celebrated across the country today under the theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’, underscoring the importance of naturopathy and nature-based healthcare in promoting preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and holistic well-being. The national-level celebration was organised by the Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN), Ministry of Ayush, in collaboration with the National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, conveyed their greetings and best wishes through video messages played during the programme.

In his message, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the importance of naturopathy in strengthening preventive healthcare and promoting healthy lifestyles.

Shri Jadhav called upon citizens to adopt healthy habits and contribute towards building a Swasth Bharat. He also appreciated the efforts of practitioners, researchers, institutions and other stakeholders in promoting naturopathy and creating greater public awareness about the system.

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, in his message, emphasised the role of naturopathy in preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle promotion and fostering harmony with nature. He underlined the importance of scientific research, health awareness and community participation in advancing naturopathy and encouraged citizens to adopt informed and sustainable health practices.

Shri N. Cheluvarayaswamy, Minister for Water Resources (Major and Medium Irrigation), Government of Karnataka and MLA from Nagamangala, attended the programme as the Chief Guest, while Ms. Alarmelmangai D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, was the Guest of Honour.

Addressing the gathering, Shri N. Cheluvarayaswamy appreciated the establishment and development of CRIYN, Nagamangala, and highlighted its potential to address the healthcare needs of the region. He emphasised the need to make the institute's facilities accessible to the general public, enabling people in the surrounding areas to benefit from naturopathy-based healthcare services.

He assured his full support and cooperation for the further development of the institute and expressed his willingness to coordinate with the State Government to facilitate the implementation of Ministry of Ayush projects and other Government of India initiatives in Karnataka.

Ms. Alarmelmangai D. highlighted the growing recognition of Yoga and Naturopathy and their relevance in addressing lifestyle-related disorders through preventive and promotive healthcare. She also highlighted the expansion of CCRYN's research infrastructure, including the Central Research Institutes of Yoga and Naturopathy at Nagamangala, Karnataka, and Jhajjar, Haryana, along with its facilities at Rohini, Delhi. She acknowledged the contribution of NIN, Pune, to education, research, training, clinical services and public awareness.

Prof. (Dr.) Jyoti Keswani, Director, CCRYN, in her welcome address, highlighted the significance of Naturopathy Day and the Council's role in advancing research, institutional development and the promotion of Yoga and Naturopathy.

The programme featured the release of several research publications, educational resources and initiatives by CCRYN and NIN, Pune. These included documentary films on CRIYN Nagamangala and Jhajjar, the Indian Journal of Yoga & Naturopathy (Volume 1, Issue 3), a Yoga and Naturopathy book, an Intern Booklet and ReGEN-Beta, a clinical trial on lifestyle interventions for Type 2 Diabetes. NIN, Pune, released Nature Cure 360: A Community Health Initiative towards a Sustainable Healthy Future and The Family Doctor.

A Naturopathy Food Fair and a medicinal plant plantation drive were also organised, highlighting the role of natural resources, healthy lifestyles and nature-based healthcare practices.

Prof. (Dr.) Jyoti Keswani, Director, CCRYN; Prof. (Dr.) Geetha B. Shetty, Director, NIN, Pune; and Dr. Vadiraja H.S., Assistant Director, Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy, Nagamangala, Ministry of Ayush, were among those present at the programme.

The celebration of the 9th Naturopathy Day reaffirmed the importance of research-backed Yoga and Naturopathy in strengthening preventive and promotive healthcare. Through sustained efforts in research, institutional development, public awareness and community participation, the Ministry of Ayush continues to promote holistic well-being and advance the vision of a healthy India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to dedicate India's First Indigenous H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Chicken Vaccine to the Nation on 20 November
ICAR-NIHSAD Develops Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine to Strengthen Poultry Disease Control  
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 9:38AM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, will dedicate India’s first indigenous Inactivated H5N1 (Clade 2.3.2.1a) Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) Vaccine for Chickens to the Nation on 20th November, 2026 at ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal. Developed indigenously by ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, the vaccine is the first of its kind in India against the H5N1 HPAI virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a.

Background

Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting poultry. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses for poultry farmers due to the large-scale culling of birds and restrictions on trade. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also affect global trade, prices of poultry products and the livelihoods of farmers. Since the first detection of the disease in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported in the country.

A major outbreak of bird flu could reduce India's GDP growth by up to 1.5 per cent, while more than 20 per cent of the country's poultry population could be at risk if the disease spreads without control. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs. 2,200–3,000 crore. An outbreak in Manipur also resulted in losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the state's GDP. The disease is also a public health concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003.

Studies of the virus have shown that the H5N1 strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. In recent times, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, along with three human cases. This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans.

At present, no specific commercial vaccine is available against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. Therefore, developing an indigenous vaccine is important for India. The vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD aims to address this need by providing protection against Clade 2.3.2.1a H5N1 virus strains circulating in the country.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan visits Samrala, Punjab, under ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’; says “farmers’ plans will be made in the fields, not sitting in offices in Delhi”
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan gives a strong message to those who blame farmers for stubble burning: “Farmers are food providers; stubble is food for the soil and a means of increasing organic carbon”
Integrated farming can transform farmers’ livelihoods: “Punjab Agricultural University’s three-crop model can generate savings of up to ₹1.5 lakh per acre,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, praising the initiative
Government takes strict action against black marketing of fertilisers and fake pesticides: “Farmer IDs will prevent the diversion of urea and DAP; stringent legislation to be introduced against counterfeit pesticides,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Major relief for potato, onion and tomato growers: “Central government to bear the entire transportation cost when farmers sell their produce in other states,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Government to intervene directly when prices of fruits and vegetables fall: “Under the Market Intervention Scheme, compensation for losses will be transferred directly to farmers’ bank accounts,” says Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Focus on mechanisation and natural farming to make small landholdings profitable: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan assures farmers that machinery for stubble management will be made more affordable
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today interacted directly with farmers and agricultural scientists at a programme organised at Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Samrala, in Ludhiana, Punjab, under the nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’, being conducted from 22 October to 30 November 2026 with the resolve of ‘Healthy Soil, Prosperous Farmers’. Paying tribute to the land of Punjab and acknowledging the innovations developed by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), the Union Minister discussed several important aspects of agricultural development, including integrated farming, crop diversification, soil health and stubble management. He also outlined key initiatives and forthcoming measures by the central government to help farmers obtain fair prices for their produce. Emphasising the need to make agriculture more sustainable and profitable, he said that policies and programmes must be shaped by understanding the actual needs of farmers and the challenges they face in their fields. The interaction focused on practical ways to improve farm incomes, make better use of available resources and protect the long-term health of agricultural land.

At the beginning of the programme, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan paid his respects to Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji and said that the path shown by Guru Sahib through the teachings of ‘Kirat Karo, Naam Japo and Vand Chhako’ – “work honestly, remember the divine and share with others” – had the power to make the entire world a better place. He said that he had not come to the programme with the arrogance of a ministerial position, but as a farmer and as ‘Mama’, to serve the farming community. Shri Chouhan emphasised that agricultural policies and schemes should not be formulated by sitting in closed rooms in Delhi. Instead, those responsible for making decisions must go to the fields, sit with farmers and understand their experiences, requirements and difficulties first-hand. He said that farmers should be at the centre of agricultural policymaking, and that their voices and practical knowledge must guide decisions that affect their livelihoods. According to him, meaningful agricultural planning can only emerge through direct engagement with those who work on the land.

Saluting the hard work and contribution of Punjab’s farmers, Shri Chouhan recalled that there was a time when India was compelled to import red wheat from other countries to meet its food requirements. However, following the Green Revolution, which began in Punjab, the country’s foodgrain reserves had grown substantially, and India was now in a position to meet its food requirements with its own production. He said that India had overtaken China to become the world’s largest producer of rice and was the second-largest producer of wheat. He credited the farmers of Punjab for playing a major role in this transformation and for helping strengthen the country’s food security through their dedication and hard work. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s visit to Manila, he also mentioned that the Prime Minister had paid obeisance at the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara there and laid the foundation stone for its reconstruction along with members of the sangat. Shri Chouhan said that such gestures reflected the importance of the Sikh community's traditions and its contribution to society.

Expressing concern over the declining size of agricultural landholdings, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that India did not have the kind of large farms, extending over thousands of hectares, that were common in some other countries. It was therefore essential to develop farming models that could generate higher returns from smaller areas of land. He praised the three-crop model developed by Punjab Agricultural University, under which farmers could cultivate three crops on just one acre and earn a net annual income of up to ₹1.5 lakh. He described the model as an important example of how small landholdings could be used more productively and profitably. He also instructed KVK Samrala to take steps to popularise the model across the region so that more farmers could learn about it and adopt it according to their own requirements. He said that such practical models could help address the challenges arising from shrinking landholdings while improving the economic prospects of small farmers.

Shri Chouhan said that continued dependence on the wheat-paddy cropping cycle was gradually reducing the fertility of agricultural land. He urged farmers to diversify their crops and move towards integrated farming by combining foodgrain cultivation with activities such as growing fruits, flowers and vegetables, cultivating medicinal plants, animal husbandry, goat rearing and fish farming. He explained that farmers should not rely exclusively on wheat and paddy, but should explore other suitable agricultural and allied activities based on their land, resources and local conditions. By combining different crops and activities, farmers could make better use of their land, create additional sources of income and reduce their dependence on a single cropping pattern. He stressed that crop diversification and integrated farming were important not only for improving farmers’ earnings but also for maintaining the long-term productivity and health of the soil.

Addressing the deteriorating condition of soil and the indiscriminate use of fertilisers, Shri Chouhan said that applying excessive quantities of fertilisers and pesticides without first testing the soil was harming the natural ecosystem of agricultural land. Such practices were destroying beneficial insects and earthworms, which play an important role in maintaining soil fertility. He appealed to farmers to experiment with natural farming on at least half of their land rather than attempting to shift their entire holdings to the practice immediately. He said that adopting natural farming on a portion of their land would help improve soil health and that farmers would be able to maintain their production levels as well. He encouraged them to assess the results and gradually expand the practice. He emphasised that farmers needed to pay greater attention to the actual nutritional requirements of their soil and avoid unnecessary use of chemical inputs. Protecting soil health, he said, was essential for sustaining agricultural productivity and ensuring that farmland remained fertile for future generations.

Taking a clear stand in support of farmers on the issue of stubble burning, Shri Chouhan said that farmers should not be unfairly blamed or portrayed negatively every time the issue of pollution was discussed. He said that farmers were becoming increasingly aware of the importance of managing crop residue and were making efforts to handle stubble rather than burn it. Stubble, he emphasised, was food for the soil, and incorporating it into the field helped increase organic carbon content. It therefore had an important role to play in maintaining soil health and improving the quality of agricultural land. He assured farmers that the government would work towards making machinery such as seeders, used for stubble management, more affordable and ensuring that mechanisation schemes were better suited to their needs. He said that farmers needed access to practical and cost-effective equipment to manage crop residue without resorting to burning. The government, he added, would focus on making such machinery more accessible and helping farmers adopt suitable mechanised solutions.

Tak marketing, Shri Chouhan said that the central government was making DAP available to farmers at ₹1,350 per bag, even though its cost was approximately ₹5,000. Similarly, a bag of urea costing around ₹3,000 was being supplied to farmers at just ₹266. He explained that the government was bearing the substantial subsidy burden to ensure that farmers could obtain these essential inputs at affordable prices. To prevent subsidised fertilisers from being diverted for industrial purposes or other unauthorised uses, the government was rapidly issuing ‘Farmer IDs’. He informed farmers that six lakh Farmer IDs had already been created in Punjab. These IDs would help ensure that fertilisers reached the farmers who needed them, in a timely manner and in quantities based on the actual requirements of their land and crops, including crops such as potatoes. He said that the system would help prevent the diversion and misuse of subsidised urea and DAP. He also announced that the central government was preparing to introduce a new and stringent Pesticide Act, along with a new seed law, to protect farmers from fake pesticides and poor-quality seeds being sold in the market. The proposed legal measures would strengthen safeguards against fraudulent and substandard agricultural inputs.

Referring to fluctuations in crop prices and the need to eliminate the role of middlemen, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan outlined two major measures to provide relief to farmers. He said that if prices of potatoes, onions or tomatoes fell in Punjab, while better prices were available in major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai, the central government would bear the entire transportation cost of moving the produce to those markets for sale through state government agencies. This would allow farmers to access better-paying markets in other states without having to bear the additional burden of transportation expenses. He also explained that under the ‘Market Intervention Scheme’, if farmers were compelled to sell their produce at very low prices, the central and state governments would intervene jointly, sharing the cost equally, with each contributing 50 per cent. The amount representing the difference in prices would then be transferred directly to the farmers’ bank accounts. These measures, he said, were intended to protect farmers against sharp price declines, reduce the impact of market fluctuations and ensure that they received better returns for their produce.

During the programme, Shri Chouhan also appreciated the use of a modern, driverless, mapping-based tractor, recognising the potential of such technology in agricultural operations. He said that agriculture was a state subject, but there should be no politics between the central and state governments when it came to serving farmers and addressing their concerns. He informed the gathering that the central government had approved all the proposals submitted by Punjab’s Agriculture Minister under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). He reiterated that the Centre was ready to work with the state government to support agricultural development and improve the welfare of farmers. Shri Chouhan also said that any farmer wishing to share suggestions or raise concerns could meet him directly in Delhi by arranging an appointment. He stressed that farmers should feel free to bring their problems and ideas to his attention so that their concerns could be considered and addressed. Union Agriculture Commissioner P.K. Singh, PAU Vice-Chancellor Dr Harvinder Singh Dhaliwal, and a large number of agricultural scientists and progressive farmers were present on the occasion.

Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, today launched the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform at the valedictory session of the National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”, organised by NITI Aayog at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
Cabinet Secretary launches Karmayogi Sankalpa at NITI Aayog’s National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”
Civil servants across the country to record commitments to specific changes in their leadership practice on the iGOT Karmayogi platform
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 9:25PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, today launched the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform at the valedictory session of the National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”, organised by NITI Aayog at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops being organised by NITI Aayog on the completion of twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government.

Under the Karmayogi Sankalpa, each civil servant records one commitment to a specific change in their own leadership practice. The commitment sets out where the officer will act, the leadership attributes the officer will build, the change that citizens will see, and the action the officer will take. Participants at Bharat Mandapam and officers joining through the iGOT Karmayogi platform recorded their commitments at the time of the launch. The commitments of government officers will be followed up by Karmayogi Bharat. The Sankalpa will be taken forward through Ministries, State Governments and training institutions, with a target of 25,000 commitments to be recorded on the platform by 25 December 2026, which is observed as Good Governance Day.

The day opened with the inaugural keynote address by Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, followed by first-hand accounts on the reconstruction of Kutch after the 2001 earthquake, the response to Covid-19, Lakhpati Didi and the opening up of the space economy. In the Case Clinic, each group examined one decision from its assigned episode, considering what public purpose required in the decision, what stood against it, and how the decision was held to its purpose through implementation.

A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” was moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog. The panelists were Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, former President, NASSCOM and Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh.

The panelists shared their thoughts on Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership principles and their relevance to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma highlighted the paradigm shift in governance during the Prime Minister’s tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat, emphasizing his ability to create new processes, build institution and human resource capacity and placing local communities at the centre of development.

Prof. Vishal Gupta underscored the Prime Minister’s ability to inspire belief in ambitious goals. He stressed that political will must go hand in hand with administrative reforms and highlighted Seva Bhav as a defining principle of leadership.

Ms. Debjani Ghosh emphasized that technology must ultimately be measured by its impact on people and society. She called for placing human-centricity at the heart of AI and technological advancement, ensuring that innovation translates into meaningful societal change.

Ms. Narayani Bhatia highlighted the Prime Minister’s lateral thinking, ability to identify interconnected opportunities. She particularly emphasised his practice of deep listening and empathy, noting that giving people, including young bureaucrats, the space to share their perspectives is one of the most valuable qualities of his leadership.

In the Application Clinic, government officers applied the learnings from the Case Clinic to live leadership challenges from the current postings of participating officers.

At the valedictory session, Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, presented a recap of the day’s proceedings. Additionally, various groups presented their application for challenges related to ASR SAATHI – Safe Antenatal Assistance aimed at tracking and sustaining maternal care across remote tribal habitations; operationalizing closed-loop referral pathways to deliver universal health coverage for non-communicable diseases; making every Saras Mela deliver year-round buyer commitments so SHG enterprises can sustain Lakhpati Didi incomes; and ensuring the initial and long-term functionality of grey water management assets under SBM-G.

In his closing remarks, Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, said that “Leadership lessons can be studied through academic courses and research, but the most valuable lessons come from observing and working with accomplished leaders. Drawing upon his experience of working with leaders like the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he highlighted key administrative leadership practices that civil servants can adopt. Karmayogi Sankalpa will carry the learning of the workshop into the field. Dr. Somanathan emphasised that effective leadership is best understood through the experience of accomplished leaders and highlighted the importance of learning from their administrative skills.

He added that effective administrative leadership is about translating vision into measurable outcomes through purposeful questioning, active listening, decisive decision-making, accountability and adherence to due process.

The analysis of the groups will be developed by case writers into case studies, which will be published on the iGOT Karmayogi platform for use by civil servants and training institutions. The application plans prepared by every group and the commitments recorded under the Karmayogi Sankalpa will carry the learning of the workshop into the field. The next National Workshop in the series, on “Governance as Delivery” will be held in January 2027. The workshop concluded with a vote of thanks by Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog.
