item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
WOMEN’S REPRESENTATION MUST EXTEND FROM PANCHAYATS TO PARLIAMENT; HOPEFUL OF IMPLEMENTATION OF NARI SHAKTI VANDAN ADHINIYAM: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
WOMEN’S GREATER PARTICIPATION IN POLICYMAKING AND LEGISLATION WILL MAKE DEMOCRACY MORE RESPONSIVE AND ACCOUNTABLE: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
AI AND TECHNOLOGY CAN STRENGTHEN TRANSPARENCY, ACCOUNTABILITY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF DEMOCRATIC INSTITUTIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK TO BE DEVELOPED FOR DIGITAL EMPOWERMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING OF WOMEN REPRESENTATIVES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER INAUGURATES THE FIRST COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS (CWP) INDIA REGION CONFERENCE IN BENGALURU; CM, KARNATAKA AND OTHER DIGNITARIES GRACE THE OCCASION
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasized the need for greater representation of women across all democratic institutions. Shri Birla noted that women must have an effective role not merely as participants but also in leadership, policymaking and law-making. Referring to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam enacted in 2023, he expressed hope that the provision for 33 per cent representation of women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies would move towards implementation, enabling women's leadership to extend from Panchayats to Parliament. He noted that several States have already provided for 50 per cent representation of women in Panchayats and Municipalities. Greater participation of women in legislative institutions and decision-making processes would contribute to building a stronger, more sensitive and accountable democracy. Women bring sensitivity, commitment and a strong sense of responsibility to public life, qualities that are particularly important in addressing the aspirations and challenges of society. Highlighting the pivotal role of women in strengthening democratic institutions, Shri Birla mentioned that greater participation of women in policymaking, legislation and decision-making would make democracy more responsive, inclusive and accountable. Shri Birla made these observations while inaugurating the First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region Conference at Bengaluru.

Noting that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and technology are transforming every sphere of social life and, when used responsibly and accountably, he observed that AI can bring significant improvements in governance. He emphasised that public representatives must leverage technology and e-governance to strengthen their engagement with citizens, understand their problems and ensure timely and effective solutions. Technology can play a vital role in establishing transparent, accountable and efficient systems of governance. Observing that Parliamentary Committees function as ‘Mini Parliaments’, the Speaker said that these committees have made valuable contributions towards addressing the socio-economic challenges faced by women and have made important recommendations to the Government. AI and technology can further strengthen their monitoring and oversight functions and make their work more effective. He indicated that a dedicated session on AI and technology would be organised to enhance the understanding and capacities of women Members of Parliament and legislators in this regard.

The Speaker called for the need to develop an institutional framework to strengthen the capacities of elected women representatives across Panchayats, Municipalities, State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament. The initiative should focus on enabling women representatives, including Panchayat Sarpanches and Municipal Chairpersons, to effectively use AI, technology and digital platforms for public engagement, monitoring and ensuring transparency in governance, he noted. Shri Birla stressed that the ability of public representatives to use technology effectively would directly influence the quality of outcomes delivered to citizens, particularly women and people at the grassroots level. He also underscored the importance of mentorship by experienced women legislators to guide emerging leaders and strengthen their legislative and leadership capabilities.

Shri Birla opined that women have made significant contributions to India's journey from the freedom struggle to nation-building and are today providing leadership in virtually every sphere, including education, science, technology, research, entrepreneurship, sports, defence, space and politics. He said that technology and digital platforms are creating new opportunities for women's economic self-reliance and expanding their participation in social and political life. At the same time, empowering women digitally and ensuring a safe digital environment remain important priorities. Highlighting Karnataka's rich democratic heritage, the Speaker referred to the twelfth-century Anubhava Mantapa of Lord Basaveshwara as an important symbol of the region's democratic traditions. He also recalled the courage and valour of Kittur Rani Chennamma, whose legacy continues to inspire generations.

Shri Birla hoped that the two-day conference would provide an important platform for women parliamentarians and legislators from Commonwealth countries to exchange experiences, innovations and best practices. He observed that dialogue, discussion and the exchange of diverse perspectives, including agreement and disagreement, constitute the strength of democracy. Sharing successful practices from different legislatures would help strengthen democratic institutions and promote innovation from Panchayats to Parliament. Expressing confidence in the outcomes of the conference, the Speaker said that women's leadership would help take the nation towards a more inclusive, balanced and just society, with democratic institutions becoming stronger, more accountable and result-oriented, ensuring that the voice of the last person in society is heard and addressed.

Earlier, the Speaker welcomed the participants and thanked Dr. D. Purandeswari, Chairperson of the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference in India, the Chief Minister of Karnataka and the Presiding Officers of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council for their initiative and efforts in organising the conference.

AS INDIA MOVES TOWARDS THE VISION OF VIKSIT BHARAT BY 2047, THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN SHAPING THE NATION'S FUTURE: SMT. D. PURANDESWARI

Addressing the gathering, Chairperson, CWP India Region, Dr. Daggubati Purandeswari noted that women's empowerment in a democracy cannot be measured only by the number of women occupying public offices. It must also be reflected in their ability to participate meaningfully in legislative debates, influence policy decisions, exercise leadership and contribute to the governance and development of the nation. She stressed that we must move beyond ensuring representation towards creating an enabling environment in which women can exercise their leadership with much aplomb and effectiveness. Appreciating Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, she said that the legislation represents a historic step towards strengthening women's political representation. Greater participation of women in legislatures will bring wider perspectives, experiences and concerns into public policy and democratic deliberations, she added.

Speaking on the Theme of the Conference, the Chairperson of the CWP India Region observed that the outcome of the discussions in the Conference should not remain confined to resolutions and recommendations. We must strive to develop an actionable framework for strengthening gender-sensitive parliamentary institutions and enhancing the leadership capabilities of women public representatives, she suggested. She further noted that as India moves towards the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the role of women in shaping the nation's future will be decisive and a developed India cannot be realised without the equal participation, leadership and contribution of its women.

Chief Minister, Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar delivered the Keynote Address. Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Deputy Chief Minister, Karnataka, Dr. G. Parameshwara; and Speaker, Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Shri G. S. Patil also addressed the gathering on this occasion. Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Shri Saleem Ahmed delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Chairman, Karnataka legislative Council, Dr. Umashree delivered the Vote of Thanks.

135 women law makers from Parliament of India and State Legislatures are participating in the two - day Conference. Theme of the Conference is ‘Strong Foundations, Stronger Voices: Inclusive Cyberspace and Mentorship Pathways for New Women Legislators’. Two Plenary Sessions will be held during the Conference: (i) ‘Empowering Women Digitally: Safe Cyberspace, Smart Choices’, and (ii)  ‘Capacity Building and Mentorship for Women Legislators’, In a special initiative complementing the broader deliberations, UN Women India will organise a side event on Menopause on 17 November 2026. The Conference will conclude on 18 November 2026 with the Valedictory Address of Governor, Karnataka, Dr. Sudha Yadav.

The Conference is expected to achieve the following outcomes:

  1. Facilitate the exchange of experiences, perspectives and good practices on creating safe and inclusive cyber space and digital empowerment for women legislators.
  2. Identify effective frameworks to mentorship, capacity building and leadership development, particularly for newly elected women legislators.
  3. Explore the ways to strengthen institutional safeguards and mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of women in parliamentary processes.
  4. Promote cooperation and collaboration among legislatures in advancing women's parliamentary leadership.

 

बेंगलुरु के विधान सौध में आयोजित First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians Conference के उद्घाटन सत्र को संबोधित किया। इस अवसर पर Commonwealth Countries की महिला सांसदों एवं विभिन्न राज्यों एवं केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से आए विधायकों और जनप्रतिनिधियों के साथ महिला नेतृत्व और लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं में उनकी प्रभावी भागीदारी पर विचार साझा किए। भगवान बसवेश्वर के ‘अनुभव मंडपम’ की गौरवशाली लोकतांत्रिक परंपरा और कित्तूर की रानी चेन्नम्मा के अदम्य शौर्य की साक्षी कर्नाटक की यह धरती ज्ञान, नवाचार और प्रगतिशील चेतना की विशिष्ट पहचान रखती है। भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, संविधान निर्माण और राष्ट्र के नवनिर्माण में महिलाओं का योगदान अविस्मरणीय रहा है। आज वे शिक्षा, विज्ञान, प्रौद्योगिकी, खेल, अंतरिक्ष, रक्षा और राजनीति सहित प्रत्येक क्षेत्र में अपनी प्रतिभा एवं नेतृत्व से नए प्रतिमान स्थापित कर रही हैं। वर्तमान समय में AI और डिजिटल माध्यमों का उत्तरदायी एवं नैतिक उपयोग नीति निर्माण, विधायी कार्यवाही, जनसंवाद और सुशासन को अधिक प्रभावी बना सकता है। ऐसे में, technology और AI के इस युग में महिलाओं का Digital Empowerment तथा उनके लिए सुरक्षित Cyber Space सुनिश्चित करना हमारी सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी है। महिला सांसद केवल जनप्रतिनिधि ही नहीं हैं बल्कि स्वयं में institution हैं। अनुभवी महिला जनप्रतिनिधियों की Mentorship, निरंतर संवाद और Capacity Building के माध्यम से नई पीढ़ी के नेतृत्व को दिशा एवं सामर्थ्य प्रदान किया जाना चाहिए। मेरा दृढ़ विश्वास है कि जब महिलाओं को पंचायत से पार्लियामेंट तक समान अवसर, सुरक्षित वातावरण और निर्णय प्रक्रिया में प्रभावी भागीदारी मिलेगी, तब लोकतंत्र की जड़ें और अधिक गहरी होंगी। महिला नेतृत्व की शक्ति, संवेदनशीलता और उत्तरदायित्व से भारत का लोकतंत्र अधिक समावेशी, पारदर्शी, जवाबदेह और सशक्त बनेगा। यही सामर्थ्य विकसित भारत 2047 की संकल्पना को साकार करने का आधार बनेगा। #CWPIndia #WomenInParliament

Purandeswari एवं अन्य गणमान्यों द्वारा किए गए आत्मीय स्वागत से अभिभूत हूँ। #CWPIndia #WomenInParliament

आज बेंगलुरु के विधान सौध में आयोजित प्रथम First Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference के उद्घाटन सत्र में सम्मिलित होकर संबोधित करूँगा। इस अवसर पर सम्मेलन में सम्मिलित हो रहे महिला सांसदों एवं विभिन्न राज्यों एवं केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों से आए विधायकों और जनप्रतिनिधियों के साथ संवाद करूँगा। महिला नेतृत्व, विधायी संस्थाओं में उनकी प्रभावी भागीदारी, डिजिटल सशक्तीकरण एवं सुरक्षित साइबरस्पेस तथा महिला जनप्रतिनिधियों के क्षमता निर्माण और मेंटरशिप को समर्पित यह सम्मेलन अनुभवों के आदान-प्रदान और सार्थक विमर्श का महत्वपूर्ण मंच है। विश्वास है कि यह पहल महिला नेतृत्व को नई दिशा देने के साथ लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं को अधिक समावेशी एवं सशक्त बनाने और विकसित भारत 2047 के संकल्प को गति प्रदान करेगी। Live Link: https://t.co/63VtHEAu00

item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27 Smartphone Exports Grow 35.8% to USD 18.17 Billion Non-Smartphone Electronics Exports Rise 56.5% to USD 13.79 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27 Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44.0% during April–September FY 2026-27, increasing from USD 22.20 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26 to USD 31.97 billion. While smartphones continued to account…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India’s Electronic Goods Exports Grow 44% to USD 31.97 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
Smartphone Exports Grow 35.8% to USD 18.17 Billion
Non-Smartphone Electronics Exports Rise 56.5% to USD 13.79 Billion in April–September FY 2026-27
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi

India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44.0% during April–September FY 2026-27, increasing from USD 22.20 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2025-26 to USD 31.97 billion. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.

Exports of smartphones (HS 85171300) increased by 35.8%, from USD 13.38 billion in April–September FY 2025-26 to USD 18.17 billion during April–September FY 2026-27. Smartphones continued to be the largest component of India’s electronic goods exports. However, their share in total electronic goods exports moderated from 60.3% to 56.8%, amid faster growth in other electronics segments.

Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of 56.5%, increasing from USD 8.81 billion to USD 13.79 billion during the period. Consequently, the share of non-smartphone electronics in total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7% to 43.2%, indicating a broadening of India’s electronics export basket.

Exports of parts and accessories comprising mounted printed circuit boards (HS 84733030) increased from USD 63.3 million to USD 2.10 billion, registering growth of 3,219%. Singapore was the leading destination, with exports reaching USD 1.87 billion, followed by China at USD 111.5 million.

Exports of populated, loaded or stuffed printed circuit boards (HS 85177910) also registered significant growth of 304%, increasing from USD 213.7 million to USD 864.1 million. China was the leading destination at USD 789.2 million, while exports to Hong Kong increased from USD 5.9 million to USD 25.3 million.

Exports of network transmission and routing equipment (HS 85176290) nearly doubled, rising by 98% from USD 732.9 million to USD 1.45 billion. Hong Kong led the growth, with exports increasing from USD 264.7 million to USD 857.7 million. The United States and the Netherlands were also important destinations, with exports of USD 130.9 million and USD 124.4 million, respectively.

Exports of memory integrated circuits (HS 85423200) recorded growth of 2,333%, increasing from USD 23.1 million to USD 562.4 million. Malaysia emerged as the largest destination at USD 390.8 million, followed by Singapore at USD 102.4 million and Hong Kong at USD 25.2 million.

Similarly, exports of solid-state non-volatile storage devices (HS 85235100) increased by 1,680%, from USD 14.6 million to USD 260.5 million. China was the leading destination at USD 108.6 million, followed by Singapore at USD 76.8 million, Hong Kong at USD 22.3 million and the United States at USD 20.7 million.

The growth in India’s electronics exports reflects an increasingly diversified export basket, with non-smartphone electronics registering faster growth and gaining a larger share in overall exports. While smartphones continued to remain the largest component, with exports reaching USD 18.17 billion, the non-smartphone segment recorded stronger growth, increasing its contribution to total electronic goods exports.

The expansion across printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory integrated circuits and solid-state storage devices, along with rising exports to markets such as Singapore, China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, underscores the growing contribution of these segments to India’s electronics export growth.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Shabbir Azad/ Ishita Biswas

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA INAUGURATES THE YEAR-LONG GOLDEN JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS OF INDIAN COUNCIL OF MEDICAL RESEARCH-NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MALARIA RESEARCH
PREMIER INSTITUTIONS LIKE THE ICMR CAN TAKE THE LEAD IN ACHIEVING THE HEALTH-RELATED GOALS OF VIKSIT BHARAT THROUGH RESEARCH, COLLABORATION AND INNOVATION: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:58PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu inaugurated the year-long Golden Jubilee Celebrations of the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Malaria Research in New Delhi today (November 17, 2026). 

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that malaria has long been a serious public health challenge in many countries around the world, including India. At the time of independence, it was one of the most critical public health challenges in our country. It is a matter of satisfaction that India has made remarkable progress in malaria control over the last few years. Improved healthcare services, modern diagnostic techniques, effective medicines, mosquito-control campaigns, and community participation have played a significant role in curbing the spread of this disease. India’s progress toward malaria elimination has received global recognition. In 2024, India moved out of the World Health Organization’s ‘High Burden to High Impact’ category. This achievement has been made possible through the collective efforts of our public health programs, scientists, healthcare workers, and citizens. The National Institute of Malaria Research has played a pivotal role in this long battle against malaria. Over the past five decades, it has conducted pioneering research in areas such as malaria parasites, mosquitoes, vector control, insecticide resistance, and community-based surveillance.

The President said that new challenges, such as climate change, unplanned urbanization, and the growing resistance of mosquitoes to insecticides, could pose fresh obstacles to the eradication of malaria. In such a scenario, the efforts of healthcare workers alone cannot prevent the spread of malaria. It is also necessary to focus on preventing water stagnation, eliminating mosquito breeding sources, and managing the environment. She expressed confidence that policymakers and the scientific community are making concerted efforts in this direction.

The President said that in recent years, dengue has also emerged as a major challenge in the country. This challenge is likely to become even more formidable due to global warming and shifts in monsoon patterns. Research and studies conducted by the ICMR have provided direction to our fight against diseases such as tuberculosis, leprosy, and kala-azar. The ICMR has also played a significant role in shaping our national health programs. During the COVID-19 pandemic, it established a nationwide testing network in record time and partnered in the development of India’s first indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. She expressed confidence that the ICMR is also taking effective measures toward the diagnosis of diseases like dengue.

President said that the occasion of a golden jubilee is not only a time to reflect upon and take pride in past achievements, but also an opportunity to set decisive goals for the future. We are moving forward with the objective of building Viksit Bharat by 2047. Strong collaboration among research institutions, centres of technical and higher education, and the industrial sector is crucial for building a healthy and empowered India. Premier institutions like the ICMR can take the lead in fostering such collaboration. She expressed confidence that the ICMR and its affiliated institutions will contribute to achieving the health-related goals of Viksit Bharat through research, collaboration and innovation.

Click here to see President's speech in Hindi

item.title: NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
item.dc:creator: NITI Aayog
item.description: NITI Aayog NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government.…
item.content:encoded:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:46PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government. The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001 and as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and has led the Government at the State and the Union levels without a break since then. Throughout this period, he has held public office as a mission of service. His description of himself as the Pradhan Sevak places the citizen at the centre of every office of government, and the principles of Antyodaya, Jan Bhagidari and Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas have guided the direction of governance at both levels.

The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops. The deliberations and first-hand experiences shared during the series will be developed into case studies and learning material for civil services training institutes, educational institutions and universities. Over the course of the series, the learning from these twenty-five years will also be taken forward through research and teaching material that sets out directions for policy and administration in the years leading up to Viksit Bharat @2047.

More than 900 participants attended the workshop, of whom 250 took part directly in the deliberations. The participants included Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments, District Collectors of Aspirational Districts, students of educational institutions and universities, and community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The proceedings are also streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and at Central and State Administrative Training Institutes, enabling officers from across the country to participate in the programme.

The workshop commenced with the National Song and the National Anthem followed by welcome address by Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog. He highlighted that the objective of this workshop is to document the learnings from 25 years of leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister and translate them into institutional knowledge for the future.

He outlined four key lessons from the leadership journey. First, purpose must take precedence over hierarchical position, shifting the focus from individual leadership to a shared collective mission. Second, service must replace command, with governance centred on reaching the last person in the queue. Third, intrinsic conviction builds resilience, enabling adversity to become an opportunity for societal transformation. And fourth, true empowerment must outlive individual leadership through strong institutions, capable teams and sustainable systems.

Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, delivered the opening remarks. He said, “The role of strong political and administrative leadership is crucial in driving India's development journey. The transformational vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister, marks a significant shift in India's national aspiration to become Viksit by 2047, reflecting the country’s transition towards a developed, prosperous and globally competitive nation.”

He highlighted NITI Aayog's integrated roadmap for realising this ambition of building a USD 30-40 trillion economy by 2047, with a per capita income of USD 15,000-18,000, supported by sustained annual real GDP growth of 7-10%.

Delivering the inaugural keynote address, Dr. P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, said that “India’s governance journey has been marked by defining milestones that demonstrate the power of decisive leadership and the ability to translate vision into action. From swift response to the 2001 Kutch earthquake to the country’s coordinated response to the COVID-19 pandemic, from expanding India’s footprint in the global space economy to the transformative impact of Lakhpati Didi initiative, these actions reflect how strong political will, responsive administration and mission-driven governance can bring about meaningful change in people’s lives.”

Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank, said that “The leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, both as Chief Minister of Gujarat and subsequently as Prime Minister of India, has consistently recognised entrepreneurship as a key driver of economic growth and nation-building. The institutionalisation of support systems, strengthening of financial and entrepreneurial ecosystems, and the emergence of a vibrant start-up landscape reflect this commitment.”

Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, explained the design and structure of the workshop. He stated that the workshop approaches leadership through the decisions and actions in which it becomes visible, with the day’s proceedings structured to move from experience to analysis and from analysis to practice. The proceedings followed five stages: Learn, Analyse, Reflect, Apply and Commit under which participants learnt from first-hand accounts of significant decisions, analysed them through deliberations involving government, academia and citizens, reflected on enduring practices of public leadership, applied the learning to challenges in their own work and committed to specific changes in their leadership practices. He added that the workshop seeks to build an Indian body of knowledge on public leadership, drawing on Indian decisions and institutions, which will shape the way civil servants are trained and the way they lead in the years towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

During the Leadership Moments session, four speakers shared first-hand accounts of key moments and the leadership lessons emerging from them.

Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary and Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Gujarat, spoke on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake. He highlighted that, Kutch 2001 was not merely a story of restoring normalcy, it was a story of creating a new normal through Jan Bhagidari, institutional strength and collective resolve. The experience highlighted four key pillars of effective governance, clarity and decisiveness in vision, solidarity and commitment, people’s participation with State support, and strong institution building.

Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC and former Member, Independent Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response, emphasised that under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s COVID-19 response evolved from a whole-of-government approach into a whole-of-society movement. With the safety of doctors, nurses and frontline warriors prioritised, technology as its backbone, and Jan Andolan driving public participation, India mounted a coordinated response. Through Vaccine Maitri, the country further extended its commitment to global solidarity, supplying approximately 300 million vaccine doses to over 100 countries.

Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India said that “The Lakhpati Didi initiative is an example of how a vision can be translated into action at an unprecedented scale. The Hon’ble Prime Minister recognised rural women as entrepreneurs, producers and service providers, giving the initiative a clear and ambitious goal. Lakhpati Didi initiative goes beyond income generation, it is about fostering economic independence, dignity and recognition for women within their families and society. That, to me, is its larger purpose.”

Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO and former Secretary, Department of Space, Government of India, highlighted how liberalised FDI norms have opened new avenues for private sector participation, enabling space to emerge as a significant contributor to the economy. He emphasized that ISRO is playing a crucial role in facilitating this transition by extending its expertise, infrastructure and facilities to private players. Looking ahead, India’s Space Vision 2047, will further advance our scientific capabilities and strengthen India's position as a global space power.

Following the session, participants took part in the Case Clinic, where each group examined a specific decision from its assigned episode. Each group comprised of government officers, community partners and students, and was guided by a case writer trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission. The group deliberations, together with the first-hand accounts shared by the speakers, will be developed into case studies by the Capacity Building Commission and made available on the iGOT Karmayogi platform for use by civil servants, training institutions and universities.

Later in the day, a panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be held and government officers will take part in the Application Clinic. Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa and deliver the closing remarks.

***

MJPS/PRK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
IFFI 2026 Celebrates Kannada and Tulu Cinema
Spotlights Girish Kasaravalli's 50-Year Cinematic Journey
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:45PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 17 November 2026

 

From the socially conscious parallel cinema of Girish Kasaravalli to contemporary family dramas, folklore-rooted epics and documentary storytelling, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is bringing the richness and diversity of Kannada and Tulu cinema into focus in Goa.

Kannada Films:

Kantara: A Legend - Chapter 1, directed by and starring Rishab Shetty, is set during the Kadamba era. Berme, a young forest dweller, enters the neighbouring kingdom of Bangra and witnesses the harsh treatment of forest communities by its rulers. When Prince Kulashekara attacks the tribes and kills many of their people, Berme joins them in their fight for justice and dharma. The story brings together folklore, faith and a struggle to protect the forest communities. The film is featured in both Indian Panorama’s Mainstream Cinema section and the International Competition.

Ruby-Cube, directed by P. Sheshadri, follows three generations of a family during a short holiday at a hill station. Rohini, a psychologist, reunites with her estranged husband Moorthy through their daughter Chitra, who is facing difficulties in her marriage. As the family spends time together, old tensions and unresolved emotions come to the surface. A Rubik’s Cube becomes a symbol of the complexities of relationships, showing how patience and understanding can help people find a way forward.

The Hug of Emptiness, directed by Dr. Pradeep Kenchanuru (Dr. Pradeep Kumar Shetty K), tells the story of Chandrashekhar, whose property was taken over by the Sullia Cooperative Bank in 2003 after he failed to repay a loan. Believing the action to be unjust, he begins a legal battle that continues for more than two decades. Without a permanent home, he lives in his car while pursuing justice. The documentary portrays his long struggle, loneliness and determination in the face of an uncertain future.

Ulididdu Sampige Maatra (Only the Flower Remained), directed by Abhishek, follows Manjanna, who lives alone with memories of a woman he loved and lost. When a photograph of her is damaged, he approaches an artist and asks him to recreate her portrait from memory. After receiving the painting, Manjanna meets a mysterious stranger. The unexpected encounter changes the way he looks at his past and leads him towards an ending he had not imagined. The short film explores loss, remembrance and emotional change.

 

Tulu Films:

Pili Channe, directed by Anupama Sharadhi, follows a tribal woman who learns traditional herbal healing from her grandmother. Before her death, the grandmother gives her a sacred stone believed to carry the healing knowledge of the forest. Pili Channe uses her skills to help her community, earning their trust. When a greedy village doctor and the village chief try to take the stone for themselves, she refuses to give it up. The film explores traditional wisdom, courage and the protection of ancestral knowledge. It will have its World Premiere at IFFI 2026.

Special Session on Girish Kasaravalli:

IFFI 2026 will also host an in-conversation session titled “The Moral Universe of Parallel Cinema: 50 Years of Girish Kasaravalli” on 21 November. Moderated by Naman Ramachandran, the session will look back at five decades of filmmaking by the acclaimed Kannada director. From his debut film Ghatashraddha to works such as Tabarana Kathe, Thaayi Saheba and Dweepa, Kasaravalli’s films have explored social injustice, moral choices and the lives of marginalised people. The conversation will examine his approach to storytelling and the relationship between cinema and social conscience.

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rajith Chandran/ Lekshmi Priya/ Praveen/ Darshana Rane

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SAHYADRI PARTICIPATES IN BILATERAL NAVAL EXERCISE JAIMEX 2026 WITH JAPAN MARITIME SELF-DEFENCE FORCE
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship Sahyadri participated in the bilateral naval exercise JAIMEX 2026 with the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) on 13–14 Nov 2026. The exercise provided an opportunity for both navies to undertake coordinated maritime engagements and strengthen operational cooperation.

During the exercise, INS Sahyadri operated alongside JMSDF Ship JS Ise, undertaking a series of maritime operational engagements. These included tactical manoeuvres, communication drills and cross-deck landings, providing valuable opportunities for both navies to practise coordinated operations and enhance their understanding of each other's procedures and capabilities.

The engagements focused on strengthening interoperability, improving operational coordination and fostering mutual understanding between the participating units. The exercise also provided an opportunity to exchange professional experiences and reinforce established Navy-to-Navy cooperation.

The participation of INS Sahyadri in JAIMEX 2026 reflects the growing depth of the India–Japan maritime partnership and the continued engagement between the two navies. Such exercises contribute to strengthening mutual trust, enhancing operational familiarity and advancing cooperation in the maritime domain.

The exercise reaffirms the enduring India–Japan maritime partnership and the shared commitment of both navies to strengthening maritime cooperation, operational coordination and mutual understanding, contributing to a safe and stable Indo-Pacific.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister participates in the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit in Manila
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit in Manila ​at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., President of the Republic of the Philippines. He congratulated President Marcos for the successful chairship of ASEAN under the theme ‘Navigating Our Future, Together’ and its support as a Country Coordinator for India.

Addressing the Summit, Prime Minister underlined the importance India attaches to its Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with the ASEAN. Prime Minister affirmed that ASEAN and India should work for peace, stability and predictability in the region and beyond. Noting that India believes in a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, he stated that the future of the region depends on cooperation, and not competition.

Emphasizing that India remains firmly committed to ASEAN’s unity and centrality, he stated that ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and VIKSIT BHARAT 2047 will help meet the shared aspirations of people of India and ASEAN.

He further added that at a time of global uncertainties, shared values, common global outlook and deep cultural ties between India and ASEAN have given a new dimension to the partnership. He stated that India’s ACT EAST policy has given a new momentum to India-ASEAN ties.

Alluding to the importance of technology for future of the world, he emphasized that India and ASEAN should not just be consumers of technologies, but should co-create them and work together to skill our people.

Prime Minister noted that 2027 will be a special year for India-ASEAN relationship, when the two sides will be celebrating 35 years of their ties and 5 years of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

Prime Minister suggested several proposals to strengthen India-ASEAN engagements including:

● Long-term ASEAN-India Maritime Cooperation Plan on enhancing connectivity, scientific research, disaster management, Coast Guard cooperation, maritime domain awareness and Seafarers’ security;

● Joint Cyber Forensics Training Program for capacity building in the region;

● ASEAN-India Nuclear Energy Technical Exchanges;

● ASEAN-India Space Hackathon;

● ASEAN-India cooperation on mining and critical minerals;

● ASEAN-India Youth Connect through Youth Summit, Young Parliamentarian Exchanges and Start-up Hackathons;

● Enhancing scholarships for ASEAN countries at Nalanda University;

● ASEAN-India Creative Partnership Pavilion at the WAVES 2027; and

● Free e-visa for tourists from the ASEAN countries.

Prime Minister thanked the President of Philippines for hosting the Summit and conveyed good wishes to the Prime Minister of Singapore as the incoming chair of ASEAN.

The leaders adopted ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management [link]. The Opening Remarks of Prime Minister may be seen here [link].

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India and Sweden launch LeadIT 3.0 at COP31 to accelerate Low-carbon Industrial Transition; Brazil joins LeadIT as its newest Country Member
LeadIT 3.0 to focus on Scaling Industrial Projects, Mobilising Capital and Delivering Tangible Outcomes from 2027 to 2030
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 12:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today announced the launch of the third phase of the Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT 3.0) at the Industry Leaders’ Roundtable during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. The roundtable was co-chaired by Shri Yadav and H.E. Helena Dyrssen, State Secretary, Ministry of Climate and Enterprise, Sweden. Also present on the occasion was Mr. Selwin Hart, Special Advisor and Assistant Secretary-General, UN Climate Action.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav highlighted that geopolitical conflicts, volatile energy markets and competing development priorities make international cooperation even more important, particularly in hard-to-abate industrial sectors. He emphasised that India’s priorities of poverty alleviation, energy access, job creation and infrastructure development must advance alongside its pursuit of a sustainable, low-carbon future.

Highlighting India's climate achievements, the Minister noted that the country has achieved a 37.38% reduction in emissions intensity between 2005 and 2022 and reached 50% non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity capacity, five years ahead of its target. India's additional forest carbon sink has also reached approximately 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. India's achievements under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi were given a round of applause and the country's commitment was termed as a guiding light for other Nations in the fight against climate change. India's efforts in decarbonising hard to abate sectors was appreciated by Mr. Hart and the European Union.

Recalling LeadIT's progress since its launch by India and Sweden in 2019, Shri Yadav highlighted that its second phase facilitated eleven pre-pilot projects in steel and cement under the India-Sweden Industry Transition Partnership, besides expanding cooperation into low-carbon heavy-duty transport. The projects cover hydrogen-based ironmaking, electrification of industrial heat, carbon capture and utilisation, clinker substitution, industrial circularity and artificial intelligence to reduce cement demand. LeadIT has also supported South Africa's investment plan under the Climate Investment Funds and Ethiopia's engagement on low-carbon cement, he informed.

The Minister highlighted that LeadIT's membership has grown to 20 countries and 33 companies, and welcomed Brazil as its newest country member, strengthening the Global South's voice and opportunities for South-South cooperation. LeadIT 3.0, covering 2027–2030, would shift the focus from establishing partnerships to scaling industrial projects, mobilising capital and delivering tangible results. Its three priorities will be technology development and diffusion through industrial projects; capital mobilisation and de-risking to connect projects with finance; and capacity building and policy support, including carbon markets and workforce transition. Steel, cement and transport will remain core sectors, while the platform will remain open to new sectors and technologies.

Emphasising the need to move from feasibility studies to pilots, demonstration and replication, Shri Yadav called upon countries and companies to join the initiative and translate industrial transition commitments into action, highlighting that LeadIT 3.0 is being launched at COP31, which the Presidency has called the ‘COP of Implementation’. He stated that the transition must also create opportunities for workers, communities and developing economies. Concluding his remarks, the Minister underscored the importance of collective action in advancing the global industrial transition.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English Translation of Prime Minister’s Opening Remarks during the 23rd India - ASEAN Summit
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 12:16PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, President Marcos,
Your Majesty,
Excellencies,

Namaskar!

It is a great pleasure to reconnect once again with our ASEAN family. I warmly congratulate and thank President Marcos for his successful ASEAN Chairmanship and his valuable contribution as India’s Country Coordinator.

This is my thirteenth interaction with ASEAN leaders in this format. Over the past few years, our Act East Policy has given new momentum and greater depth to India-ASEAN relations. Our partnership has now expanded beyond our shared culture and heritage, acquiring new dimensions in areas such as digital technology, defence, and space.

Since 2014, we have undertaken more than 100 initiatives to strengthen people-to-people ties, launched nearly 250 Quick Impact Projects, and provided over 10,000 skill-building scholarships.

Today, direct flights between India and nine ASEAN countries, along with growing tourism, are further evidence of our close ties.

Friends,

Over the past few years, the world has faced one crisis after another. Today, what the world needs most is peace, stability, and predictability. In this context, this year’s theme, “Navigating Our Future, Together,” holds special significance.

Together, India and ASEAN represent nearly one-fourth of the world’s population. That is why it is essential to ensure that our future is shaped not by competition, but by cooperation. We have both the capabilities and the shared resolve to achieve this. Together, we can make this region a symbol of peace and stability.

Friends,

This is my third visit to an ASEAN country this year, reflecting the special importance ASEAN holds for India. We firmly believe that India's growth and ASEAN's prosperity are deeply interconnected.

In the coming years, both the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and Viksit Bharat 2047 can help us turn our shared aspirations into reality.

Over the past twelve years, we have given fresh momentum to our partnership. Now, together, we must give a new direction to the future of our region. India’s commitment to ASEAN unity and centrality in this partnership has been, and will remain, unwavering.

I am confident that today’s meeting will take our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive, and prosperous Indo-Pacific.

I look forward to hearing your views and suggestions.
 

Thank you very much.

***

DISCLAIMER -This is the approximate translation of Prime Minister's remarks. Original remarks were delivered in Hindi.

 

MJPS/SS/VJ/SS

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister visits Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila, Philippines
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 12:01PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila today and led the foundation-stone laying ceremony for the redevelopment of the Gurudwara in the presence of Panj Pyare. On the occasion, several dignitaries including Senator H.E. Francis Joseph Escudero and Hon’ble Mayor of Manila City, Mr. Francisco Isko Moreno were present.

Originally established in 1901 and formally organised in 1903, the institution was registered as Khalsa Diwan in 1924. The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara holds a unique distinction of being the oldest Gurudwara in the Philippines. It continues to play an important role through its spiritual, cultural and philanthropic activities for the Sikh and other communities in Manila.

The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara continues to stand as a vital bridge between the Indian-Sikh community and Philippine society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri to attend 4th India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue and hold bilateral talks with his Japanese counterpart in Tokyo
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 11:38AM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will participate in the 4th edition of India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with his Japanese counterpart during his official visit to Japan from November 18 to 19, 2026. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Raksha Mantri and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, along with Japan’s Minister of Defense Mr Shinjiro Koizumi and Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Toshimitsu Motegi. The dialogue will review the full spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, exchange views on regional & global developments, and reaffirm the shared commitment of the two nations to a free, open, inclusive, and rule-based Indo-Pacific.

The bilateral talks between Raksha Mantri and the Japanese Minister of Defense will be their third meeting this year. Building on the momentum from their interactions in New Delhi in August 2026 and on the margins of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October 2026, the two Ministers will deliberate on advancing defence equipment and technology collaboration, maritime security, enhancing the scale & complexity of joint exercises across all three services, and deepening industrial partnerships.

India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership rooted in shared democratic values, mutual trust & converging strategic interests. The upcoming visit aims to further deepen bilateral defence ties and chart the roadmap for enhanced operational & industrial synergy between the two countries.

*****

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives Shri Amit Shah interacts with officials and reviews activities related to registration, regulation, monitoring and good governance of Multi-State Cooperative Societies Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation emphasises transparent, accountable and systematic development of cooperative societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region in accordance…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives
Shri Amit Shah interacts with officials and reviews activities related to registration, regulation, monitoring and good governance of Multi-State Cooperative Societies
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation emphasises transparent, accountable and systematic development of cooperative societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy
Shri Amit Shah stresses the need for effective monitoring of cooperative societies and strict compliance with regulatory provisions to prevent potential irregularities
CRCS Regional Office in Pune oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Of the 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across the country, 420 have been registered since the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation
Regional Offices in Pune, Lucknow, Chennai and Kolkata will strengthen monitoring, grievance redressal and regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:59PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi', transparency, accountability, good governance and institutional strengthening in the cooperative sector are being continuously promoted under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. As part of these efforts, Shri Amit Shah today visited the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune, Maharashtra. During the visit, he interacted with officials and reviewed the progress of various initiatives relating to the registration, regulation, monitoring and reform of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. Shri Amit Shah particularly sought information regarding the functioning of cooperative societies in Maharashtra, their registration status and measures being taken to further strengthen the regulatory framework. The establishment of Regional Offices of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies is a significant initiative towards ensuring effective regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and decentralisation of cooperative administration across the country.

During the review, Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the development of Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region must be aligned with the objectives and guidelines of the National Cooperation Policy. He stated that the role of the Regional Office should not remain confined merely to registration-related activities but should extend to ensuring effective supervision, regulatory compliance, transparency and accountability in the functioning of cooperative societies.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also reviewed ongoing activities with the officials and emphasised that registration, inspection, auditing, grievance redressal and other statutory processes relating to cooperative societies must be carried out in a transparent and time-bound manner. He underscored the importance of an effective regulatory framework to promote good governance in cooperative institutions and safeguard the interests of all stakeholders, including members and depositors.

The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) is a statutory authority under the Ministry of Cooperation, appointed under Article 243ZH(f) of the Constitution and Section 4(1) of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002. It regulates cooperative societies whose objectives and areas of operation extend beyond the boundaries of a single State. The CRCS is entrusted with important statutory powers and responsibilities, including registration and regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, amendments to their registered bye-laws, supersession of Boards in accordance with statutory provisions, inquiries, inspections, audits, settlement of disputes, and liquidation and winding up of defunct societies.

At present, a total of 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are registered across the country. Of these, 420 societies have been registered since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation on 6 July 2021. In view of the increasing number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and their expanding geographical presence, Regional Offices are being established to ensure effective monitoring, regulatory compliance and good governance.

The first Regional Office of the CRCS, established in Pune for the Western Region, oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These include 756 societies in Maharashtra, 59 in Gujarat, two in Goa and one in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Thus, a substantial proportion of the country's registered Multi-State Cooperative Societies falls within the jurisdiction of the Pune Regional Office.

The Pune Regional Office commenced its operations on 15 April 2026. The Department of Expenditure has sanctioned 10 posts for the office. Arrangements are being made for the deployment of officers and essential support personnel to ensure effective and timely execution of regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies.

To further strengthen the monitoring and administrative framework for Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Ministry of Cooperation has initiated steps to establish additional Regional Offices in Lucknow for the Northern Region, Chennai for the Southern Region and Kolkata for the Eastern and North-Eastern Regions, in addition to the Pune office. These offices will facilitate decentralisation of regulatory administration, faster approval processes, improved monitoring and compliance, greater financial inclusion, effective grievance redressal and expansion of digital services.

The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies has also undertaken several important initiatives for the digitisation, reform and strengthening of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. These include the development of an online system for processes such as registration of societies, amendments to bye-laws, filing of annual returns and opening of branches. Other significant measures include amendments to the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, computerisation of the offices of the Cooperative Election Authority and the Cooperative Ombudsman, and the establishment of the Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund (CRRDF).

In a significant step towards strengthening financial discipline, transparency and accountability in Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026) has also been issued. These reforms aim to ensure better financial management, effective regulatory oversight and protection of the interests of members of cooperative institutions.

The visit of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to the Pune Regional Office marks an important step towards strengthening the regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, enhancing the effectiveness of regional monitoring mechanisms and promoting transparency, accountability and good governance in the cooperative sector in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy.

***

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh
Only a few individuals, like Ramoji Rao, transform themselves into institutions during their lifetime; their contributions continue to inspire the nation forever
Ramoji Rao was well-informed about developments from every corner of country, and his views on resolving every problem were clear, forthright and fearless
Born into a poor farming family, Ramoji Rao launched 'Eenadu' without any backing and ensured that first voice of morning reaching every Telugu household was voice of truth
Ramoji Rao kept pace with technological advancements in every era, built the ETV network in Telugu and several other Indian languages, and took television channels to mobile platforms as well
Many people struggle to build their careers, but it is those who struggle to uphold values who truly become great, Shri Ramoji Rao not only fought for values but also established them
Padma Vibhushan was not merely an honour for Ramoji Rao; it was a recognition of journalism, literature and Telugu identity, through his enterprise, he built an institution that continues to uphold his values even in his absence
He did not run newspapers and news channels merely for profit, despite financial losses and immense pressure, he upheld journalism as fourth pillar of democracy
He also made immense contributions to film industry, it is difficult to imagine a film studio for any regional-language film industry without Ramoji Film City
Under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi, country has witnessed decisive leadership after a long time, with era of policy paralysis giving way to the politics of performance
World's longest and most powerful hydrogen-powered train has been developed in India using entirely indigenous technology and has also begun running on tracks
Under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi, 98% of Gram Panchayats have been connected through 4G connectivity, and 50 crore Indians have come out of poverty over the past 12 years—a fact also acknowledged by the World Bank
Andhra Pradesh will emerge as most developed state in the country over next 10 years
USD 15 billion AI hub being developed by Google in Visakhapatnam will be its largest hub outside the United States, which is a matter of pride for the entire country
Shri Chandrababu Naidu has successfully translated investments worth ₹30 lakh crore into reality on the ground in just two and a half years, which is a matter of great pride
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. On the occasion, Governor of Andhra Pradesh Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu, Union Ministers Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Shri K. Ram Mohan Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri K. Pawan Kalyan, and several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the award ceremony, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today marks the 90th birth anniversary of Ramoji Rao, who is no longer among us. He said that there are individuals who, through their dedicated work during their lifetime, evolve into institutions, and the institutions they establish continue to inspire the nation forever. Shri Shah said that he had met Ramoji Rao on four occasions and he remained well-informed about developments from every corner of the country. He had a clear understanding of every problem facing the nation and its possible solutions. He held firm convictions of his own and had the courage to express them fearlessly and candidly. He said that Ramoji Rao had an excellent understanding of ground realities. He said that Ramoji Rao continues to serve as a role model for young people in several fields, including agriculture, education, filmmaking and media.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao had an in-depth understanding of the geographical situation, population, challenges and root causes of insurgency in the Northeast. Shri Amit Shah said more he came to know about Ramoji Rao, the greater his respect for him became.

Shri Amit Shah said that when one looks back at the 90-year life of Ramoji Rao, it becomes evident that hardly anyone else could have made such an extensive contribution to the nation across so many fields. He said that Ramoji Rao was born into a poor family in Krishna district and had no inheritance, resources or formal degree in journalism. However, he possessed vision in his eyes and mind, along with unwavering determination. Shri Shah said that by launching the newspaper Eenadu, Ramoji Rao sought to make the voice of truth resonate among readers. He said that if Ramoji Rao's contribution were to be assessed today, it could be said that in the world of journalism, the only media group chairman with whom he could be compared was Ram Nath Goenka.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao always kept pace with changing times and evolving technology. He said that when private news channels were first introduced, no one other than Ramoji Rao could have envisioned the possibility of running 24-hour news channels in regional languages. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao launched ETV not only in Telugu but also in almost all the regional languages of the country. He added that Ramoji Rao not only enriched the country's regional languages but also took the innovative initiative of making the voice of truth resonate among people across the country through the ETV network.

Shri Amit Shah said that on one occasion, when he asked Ramoji Rao what he wished to accomplish with the time he had left, the latter had replied that he wanted to launch a TV channel on mobile phones. He said that today, his mobile channels are available in all languages. It is this passion to keep contributing and the zeal to constantly strive and overcome challenges that make Ramoji Rao truly great.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that when we look at the owners of today's newspapers and news channels, their business objectives and their focus on profits, we realise what a towering personality Ramoji Rao was. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao must have firmly believed that journalism, in its true sense, constitutes the fourth pillar of democracy. He made numerous sacrifices and faced many struggles throughout his life to uphold this conviction.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao spent two major phases of his life in struggle. Despite significant financial losses and numerous challenges, he maintained the impartiality of his news channel and upheld its role as a true fourth pillar of democracy. Shri Shah said that those who struggle to build their careers are also great individuals. Struggle is a unique quality that makes a person great. However, those who struggle to uphold values are even greater. Ramoji Rao always fought for values and worked to establish them.

Shri Amit Shah said that when Ramoji Rao was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2016, a renowned Gujarati newspaper from Gujarat had written that the honour was not merely a recognition of Ramoji Rao, but also an honour for journalism, literature, education and Telugu pride. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao had not merely built a news industry; he had created institutions rather than businesses. Institutions are those that continue to function and uphold the same values even after their founders are no longer present.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao also made significant contributions to the film industry. He said that it is difficult to imagine the film industry of any language without Ramoji Film City. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao assured filmmakers that if they came with the funds and their creative vision, everything else would be available at his studio, and they would not need to go anywhere else.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that several individuals have been selected for the Excellence Awards this year. People who have made significant contributions to the nation in fields such as science and technology, young icons, service to humanity, art and culture, education, medicine and healthcare, rural development, journalism and women's achievements are being honoured on this occasion. He said that he would like to tell all nine award recipients, who are being recognised for their contributions in these nine fields crucial to the country's development, that they may receive many more awards in their lives, but an award associated with the name of Ramoji Rao holds a special significance of its own.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the able leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is moving forward on the path of progress. He said that over the past 13 years, the country has witnessed stability, continuity and decisive leadership after a long period. The era when policy paralysis was widely discussed has now given way to performance-driven politics and development based on sound policies. Union Home Minister said that significant progress has been made in several areas, including the abrogation of Article 370, ending the five-decade-old problem of Naxalism, driving the country's economic growth and ensuring national security. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's economy is advancing rapidly, while opportunities are expanding at an equally fast pace across all sectors.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that despite the prolonged wars between Russia and Ukraine, and between the United States and other countries, positive projections have emerged regarding India's economic growth.  Moody’s has recently raised its growth forecast for India for 2026–27 from 6.5% to 7%. In 2025–26, India recorded exports worth a record USD 863 billion, and our next target is USD 1 trillion. He expressed confidence that we would achieve this target.

Shri Shah said that India has become the world's second-largest producer in the manufacturing sector. India now produces more steel than the United States and Japan combined. This achievement has been accomplished over the past 12 years. He further said that earlier, only 58 Gram Panchayats had internet connectivity, whereas today, 2 lakh 15 thousands Gram Panchayats have been connected through 4G services, accounting for approximately 98 per cent of the total Gram Panchayats.

Shri Amit Shah said that India has made significant progress in the economic sector as well. The world's longest and highest-capacity hydrogen train has been built in India using completely indigenous technology, and its operations have also commenced.

He said that in 2014, the country had only 76 airports, whereas today, India has made significant strides, with the number of airports reaching 150. Shri Shah further said that, according to a World Bank report, during the 12 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's tenure, 50 crore Indians have come out of poverty, which is a matter of great satisfaction for everyone.

Union Home Minister said that for nearly 40 years, the country witnessed more than 2,000 Naxal attacks every year. However, today, it is a matter of satisfaction that not a single Naxal attack is taking place. He said that this is a collective achievement of all of us.

He said that Andhra Pradesh, too, is progressing rapidly under the leadership of Shri Chandrababu Naidu. He added that he has been consistently studying the data from Shri Chandrababu Naidu's second term in office and can confidently say that Andhra Pradesh will become the most developed state in the country over the next 10 years.

Shri Shah said that Google's USD 15 billion AI hub is a matter of pride not only for Andhra Pradesh but also for the entire country. The establishment of a USD 15 billion AI hub by Google in Visakhapatnam is a matter of pride for the people of India as well as Andhra Pradesh. Both the one-gigawatt data centre and Google's largest AI hub outside the United States are significant achievements for the country. A new gateway for undersea cables will also be established in Andhra Pradesh.

He said that the foundation stone of the state's first semiconductor unit has been laid, and major steel plants have been established. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has recently inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, and on the same day, foundation stones were laid for projects worth ₹18,000 crore.

Shri Shah said that a closer examination of all these initiatives reveals that Shri Chandrababu Naidu has facilitated the grounding of investments worth ₹30 lakh crore in Andhra Pradesh in just two-and-a-half years.

Shri Amit Shah said that once the Polavaram Dam is completed and water reaches every part of Andhra Pradesh, it will create an unparalleled opportunity for the farmers of the state. He said that taking the project forward with firm determination and a time-bound approach is a significant achievement.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for Country-Driven Just Transition Mechanism at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye); Emphasizes Adequate Finance, Technology Transfer and Capacity Building for Developing Countries
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for a Two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism that respects National Sovereignty and diverse National Circumstances
India stresses that Just Transition must address Employment, Social Protection, Adaptation, Poverty Eradication and Energy Access
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye), the Minister reiterated India's commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.

Presented India's views at the 4th Annual High-level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye today. Underlined the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning. India supports the operationalisation of a two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism, responsive to developing-country needs and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) November 16, 2026

Shri Yadav emphasised that just transition must follow a whole-of-economy and whole-of-society approach, addressing employment, social protection, adaptation, poverty eradication, energy access and sustainable development. He highlighted that adequate financial support, technology transfer and capacity-building are essential to enable developing countries to implement their national priorities. 

Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India's sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country's renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added.

The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism. While the Work Programme should continue to provide a platform for dialogue and exchange of experiences, the Mechanism should facilitate practical support through technical assistance, capacity-building and cooperation, translating the learnings from ongoing discussions into action, he stated.

Reaffirming India's support for operationalising a two-tier, Party-guided Just Transition Mechanism, Shri Yadav stressed that it must be responsive to the needs of developing countries and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances. The Mechanism should build on existing efforts, avoid duplication and facilitate access to adequate means of implementation. It must neither prescribe uniform sectoral pathways nor create new obligations, but enable countries to pursue their own just transition pathways in accordance with national priorities, while ensuring that workers, communities and vulnerable groups are not left behind, the Minister stressed.

Shri Yadav observed that COP31 presents an important opportunity to move from exchanging experiences to practical, country-driven implementation. India stands ready to work constructively with all Parties towards an inclusive outcome that advances just transition while safeguarding the developmental priorities of developing countries, the Minister concluded.

Ministry of Women and Child Development
NCPCR takes suo motu cognizance of alleged sexual assault of a 14-year-old tribal girl in Ranchi; Commission's team to visit Ranchi on 17 November
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 16 November 2026: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has taken suo motu cognizance, under Section 13(1)(j) of the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, of media reports that an FIR has been registered against MLA Bhushan Bara for the alleged sexual assault of a 14-year-old tribal girl in Ranchi, Jharkhand.

On 14 November 2026, the Commission issued a notice to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Ranchi, seeking immediate action in the matter.

A Commission team led by Dr. Sudha Chaudhary, Registrar, NCPCR, will visit Ranchi on 17 November 2026 to inquire into the matter.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) Renew Scientific Partnership to Promote Joint Research, Innovation and Technology Development
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

India and Belarus took an important step towards strengthening their bilateral scientific and technological partnership with the signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation (PoC) for the period 2027–2029 between the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) of India, and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) at New Delhi on 16th November 2026.

The Programme of Cooperation was signed during a meeting between Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, and Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, who is visiting India from 15–18 November 2026 in connection with the 12th Meeting of the Belarusian-Indian Intergovernmental Commission on Cooperation in Economy, Trade, Industry, Science, Technology and Culture and the India-Belarus Business Forum.

The signing of the Second PoC builds upon the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Scientific and Technical Cooperation signed between CSIR and NASB on 22 May 2023. Under the first Programme of Cooperation (2024–2026), the two institutions launched a Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) proposals in October 2024, resulting in the approval seven joint projects.These projects are currently progressing through their second year of implementation.

The Second Programme of Cooperation (2027–2031) provides a renewed framework for expanding bilateral scientific collaboration, facilitating joint research and development initiatives and strengthening linkages between research institutions and scientists of both countries. It is expected to provide an impetus to collaborative research, technology development, knowledge exchange and innovation-driven partnerships through focused cooperation in mutually identified areas of science and technology.

As a key initiative under the Second Programme of Cooperation, CSIR and NASB propose to launch the Second Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Proposals from 27 November 2026 inviting proposals from researchers and scientists of both countries for undertaking collaborative research projects in mutually identified priority areas. The call is expected to provide fresh impetus to bilateral research partnerships, encourage scientific exchanges and facilitate the development of innovative solutions through joint research and technological collaboration.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, highlighted the importance of sustained scientific partnerships in addressing emerging global challenges and advancing innovation-led development. The DG, CSIR emphasised the significant potential for Indian and Belarusian researchers to work together by leveraging their respective scientific strengths and institutional capabilities.

Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, highlighted the importance of continued scientific engagement between India and Belarus and expressed interest in further strengthening institutional cooperation and expanding opportunities for joint research and technological collaboration, specifically through organizing Joint Laboratories between NASB and CSIR and exploring mechanisms to support cooperation activities targeting upscaling and translational research activities.

The signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation marks an important milestone in India–Belarus scientific relations. The renewed partnership is expected to further strengthen research collaboration, promote institutional linkages and create new opportunities for scientific exchange and innovation, contributing to the broader objectives of bilateral cooperation between the two countries.
