item.title: NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam CEO & MD, NICDC, Briefs Dignitaries on Progress of Three Industrial Nodes in Andhra Pradesh Summit Focuses on Strengthening Global Partnerships, Attracting Investments and Positioning India as a Global Manufacturing Hub NICDC Pavilion Showcases Andhra Pradesh’s Industrial Potential, Investment Opportunities and Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 11:33AM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam
CEO & MD, NICDC, Briefs Dignitaries on Progress of Three Industrial Nodes in Andhra Pradesh
Summit Focuses on Strengthening Global Partnerships, Attracting Investments and Positioning India as a Global Manufacturing Hub
NICDC Pavilion Showcases Andhra Pradesh’s Industrial Potential, Investment Opportunities and Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi

The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) organised the 31st edition of the CII Partnership Summit 2026 on 12–13 November 2026 in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, under the theme “Navigating the New World Order: Trade | Technology | Trust | Thought Leadership.” Organised in association with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, and hosted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Summit brought together policymakers, international delegates, global business leaders and investors to deliberate on emerging opportunities in trade, technology and economic cooperation.

The inaugural session was attended by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal; Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu; Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan; and Union Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu. Shri Nara Lokesh, Minister for Human Resources Development, IT, Electronics & Communication and RTG, Government of Andhra Pradesh, also delivered a special address.

The inaugural session also witnessed the participation of several senior leaders, Union and State Ministers, overseas trade ministers, senior government officials, policymakers and prominent industry representatives from India and abroad, reflecting the strong participation in efforts to strengthen international trade, investment, industrial cooperation and strategic partnerships.

The Summit provided a platform for deliberations on international trade, global value chains, resilient supply chains, advanced manufacturing, defence technology, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, smart manufacturing, green energy, future mobility and emerging technologies. Discussions focused on strengthening international partnerships, attracting investments and positioning India as a competitive destination for global manufacturing and innovation.

During the Summit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu visited the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) pavilion. Shri Rajat Kumar Saini, CEO & MD, NICDC, briefed the dignitaries on the development and progress of NICDC's three Greenfield Industrial Smart City nodes in Andhra Pradesh: Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy.

The NICDC pavilion showcased India's evolving industrial infrastructure landscape and investment opportunities through various initiatives and digital platforms. Key highlights included the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities, BHAVYA (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana), the Industrial Corridor Land Platform (ICLP), which enables investors to discover and compare verified industrial land opportunities across India, and Koyla Shakti, a Smart Coal Analytics Dashboard. The pavilion also featured a 360-degree Virtual Reality (VR) Tour, offering visitors an immersive overview of NICDC's industrial corridor projects.

Shri Rajat Kumar Saini apprised the dignitaries of the development progress of the three industrial nodes. The updates highlighted the progress of infrastructure development across the projects and NICDC's continued efforts towards creating investment-ready industrial destinations in the State.

The pavilion also showcased Andhra Pradesh's industrial potential, highlighting the three nodes' combined project area of 7,223 acres, investment potential of ₹31,360 crore and employment potential of 2 lakh. The three nodes are being developed under different industrial corridors and are envisaged as integrated industrial ecosystems supported by world-class infrastructure and connectivity. Their development is aimed at facilitating large-scale investments, strengthening manufacturing capabilities, generating employment and accelerating industrial growth in Andhra Pradesh.

Through these displays and interactions, NICDC highlighted investment opportunities across manufacturing and emerging sectors, positioning Andhra Pradesh as an attractive destination for domestic and international investors.

During the Japan Country Session, H.E. Mr Keiichi Ono, Ambassador of Japan to India, highlighted the growing India–Japan economic partnership, noting that 31 Japanese companies across three cities in Andhra Pradesh have generated over 8,000 local jobs. He also highlighted opportunities for collaboration in steel, pharmaceuticals, clean energy and semiconductors.

Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries & Commerce and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh, highlighted the State's industrial infrastructure, strategic ports, sectoral opportunities and focus on translating investment commitments into project implementation.

Shri Rajat Kumar Saini delivered the opening remarks, outlining five key areas for deeper cooperation: manufacturing and industrial corridor development, resilient supply chains, advanced technologies, sustainable industrial development, and MSME partnerships and skill development. He emphasised the need to translate investment opportunities into actionable partnerships, highlighting Japan's commitment to facilitate investments of JPY 10 trillion in India over the next decade.

Mr Kiyotaka Doho, Director General, JETRO Chennai, highlighted the growing interest among Japanese companies in India and Andhra Pradesh, with over 80 per cent of surveyed companies planning to expand their operations. Mr Rajesh Mittal, President & MD, Isuzu Motors India, underscored the importance of Japanese manufacturing practices, quality standards, skill development and local supplier ecosystems.

Through the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across various industrial corridors, NICDC is working towards strengthening India's manufacturing ecosystem, enhancing logistics efficiency and creating investment-ready industrial destinations. Its initiatives aim to attract domestic and international investments, generate employment and facilitate the integration of Indian industries with global value chains.

Other distinguished dignitaries present at the event included Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri B. C. Janardhan Reddy, Minister for Roads and Buildings, Infrastructure and Investments, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri G. Sai Prasad, Chief Secretary to the Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri R. Mukundan, President, CII and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Limited; and Shri Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII.

NICDC's participation in the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 provided an opportunity to showcase the progress of its industrial corridor projects, engage with global stakeholders and highlight investment opportunities in Andhra Pradesh. These efforts contribute to the Government of India's vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and achieving Viksit Bharat @2047.

National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC), under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, is mandated to develop world-class Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across the country. Through integrated industrial infrastructure and digital initiatives, NICDC aims to enhance manufacturing competitiveness, attract investments and promote sustainable economic development.

item.title: India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties Both sides agree to set up a Joint Working Group to explore Terms of Reference for a Preferential or Free Trade Agreement India–Egypt bilateral trade grows 35% to USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26; trade during April–September 2026 rises 65% to USD 5.04 billion More than 300 Indian and Egyptian companies participate in India–Egypt Business Forum to explore trade, investment and manufacturing partnerships Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
Both sides agree to set up a Joint Working Group to explore Terms of Reference for a Preferential or Free Trade Agreement
India–Egypt bilateral trade grows 35% to USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26; trade during April–September 2026 rises 65% to USD 5.04 billion
More than 300 Indian and Egyptian companies participate in India–Egypt Business Forum to explore trade, investment and manufacturing partnerships
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:37AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, co-chaired the 7th session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital today. The meeting marked the first occasion on which this important bilateral institutional mechanism was convened at the ministerial level, underscoring the priority both governments attach to strengthening the economic dimension of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of USD 12 billion. They emphasised the need to diversify trade, promote value-added exports and address trade-related challenges. As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries.

The meeting was preceded by bilateral discussions between the two Ministers on expanding trade, facilitating investments and developing long-term industrial and commercial linkages. The JTC provided an opportunity to review existing trade ties, assess challenges faced by businesses and identify new areas for closer collaboration.

The Committee reviewed the growth in India–Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to reach USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26 (April 2025–March 2026). Trade during April–September 2026 also grew by 65% to reach USD 5.04 billion, compared to USD 3.08 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. The increase reflects the growing momentum in commercial exchanges and the potential for further diversification of the trade basket. Significant complementarities exist for enhanced trade in industrial goods, energy and fertilisers, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles and agricultural products.

The discussions primarily focused on expanding trade, developing supply chains and establishing predictable trade pathways. Both sides considered measures to address non-tariff barriers, facilitate customs processes, strengthen standards and conformity assessment, and improve market access. They also discussed practical issues affecting business operations, including product registrations and trade-related regulatory procedures.

Discussions also focused on strengthening business exchanges and encouraging joint manufacturing and investment. Priority sectors included pharmaceuticals and medical devices, engineering and electrical equipment, fertilisers, textiles, renewable energy and emerging technologies. Opportunities for Indian investment in Egyptian industrial zones, as well as Egyptian investment in India's expanding manufacturing and services sectors, also formed an important part of the agenda.

Both sides expressed interest in strengthening the framework agreement between Invest India and Egypt’s General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, including a proposed digital platform for sharing investment information and facilitating business linkages.

Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains. India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships.

Speaking at the Joint Trade Committee meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted five areas of strong complementarity between India and Egypt: pharmaceuticals and healthcare, leveraging India’s strengths in affordable medicines, vaccines and medical technology; engineering and automobiles, covering machinery, auto components and industrial manufacturing; agriculture and food processing, including food security, fertilisers, irrigation and cold-chain infrastructure; digital and fintech, through UPI linkages, local currency trade and India’s Digital Public Infrastructure; and culture and museums, through proposed collaboration between the Grand Egyptian Museum and India’s upcoming Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum in conservation, curation and digitisation.

The ministerial-level JTC is an important step towards advancing the economic priorities of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. It was held against the backdrop of the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the BRICS Summit in India in September 2026. The JTC seeks to translate this political momentum into stronger trade flows, new investments, joint manufacturing, greater market access and more resilient supply chains connecting India, Egypt and wider regional markets.

The next JTC meeting was agreed to be held in New Delhi in 2028, or earlier at a mutually convenient date.

The India–Egypt Business Forum brought together more than 300 companies from India and Egypt today, providing a platform to strengthen business engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, addressed the Forum, which was attended by industry leaders and senior business representatives from a wide range of sectors.

The Forum was organised on the sidelines of Shri Piyush Goyal’s official visit to Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The opening session was addressed by Dr. Mohamed Awad, Chief Executive Officer of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and Chairman of Sanmar Group; and Mr. Ahmed ElWakil, President of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce.

Addressing the session, Shri Goyal proposed a four-point action agenda ahead of the 80th anniversary of India–Egypt diplomatic relations in 2027. The agenda included resolving identified trade barriers within a time-bound framework; encouraging Egyptian investments in Indian states and industrial clusters, with Invest India facilitating opportunities; bringing suppliers of large companies into the partnership to create opportunities for smaller businesses; and institutionalising annual reviews to track progress and translate business discussions into concrete contracts.

Underscoring the ambition of the partnership, Shri Goyal said, "Years from now, when someone studies this decade, let them find factories with labels that say: Made in Egypt, with India. Made in India, with Egypt."

A dedicated session on investment opportunities in Egypt brought together senior representatives of GAFI and the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), who presented the country’s industrial and investment opportunities. Egypt’s strategic location linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas, its expanding ports and logistics infrastructure, and its access to African, Arab and European markets offer opportunities for Indian businesses seeking to establish manufacturing and export-oriented operations.

The Forum also featured a session on the experiences of Indian companies operating in Egypt, including TCI Sanmar, Galaxy Chemical and Abdos. Their presence illustrated the potential for Indian investments to contribute to Egyptian industrial production, employment, technology development, exports and integration into regional supply chains. Representatives of the two business communities explored areas of cooperation in engineering and electrical equipment, chemicals and fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, textiles, food processing, automotive components, renewable energy and logistics.

A special panel on the digital economy brought together stakeholders from Egypt’s digital technology and transformation ecosystem and leading Indian startups and technology companies. Moderated by Eng. Ayman El Gohary, Chairman of Global for Smart Solutions, the panel included experts and industry leaders from both countries. The Egyptian participants included Eng. Mahmoud Sofrata of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), Mr. Fady Ismaeel of AGX, Dr. Kareem Hamza of National System and Dr. Sideek Ahmed of Eram Holding. Indian industry representatives included Mr. Rajesh Ranganathan of Zoho and Mr. Pradeep Gilbile of Datamorphosis. The discussions focused on opportunities in enterprise technology, digital solutions, innovation and industry partnerships.

Earlier in the day, the 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) meeting was held at the New Administrative Capital. Shri Goyal and Minister Saleh addressed the Council. The Council was co-chaired by Mr. Ganesh Kumar, Executive Vice Chairman, TCI Sanmar Chemicals SAE, on the Indian side, and Mr. Khaled Aboul Makarem of Makarem Tex on the Egyptian side. Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of FICCI, also addressed the Council.

The Joint Business Council provided a platform for focused discussions on priority sectors, including chemicals and petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, food processing and agri-business, renewable energy and green hydrogen, infrastructure, ports and logistics, information technology and digital services, textiles and automotive manufacturing. The Council also examined ways to strengthen institutional links between business organisations, including the possibility of establishing sectoral working groups, customs and trade facilitation, business visas and a calendar of reciprocal trade missions for 2026-27.

The two engagements highlighted the complementarities between the Indian and Egyptian economies. India offers a large and growing market, competitive manufacturing, engineering and digital capabilities, while Egypt offers an established industrial base, strategic connectivity, skilled human resources and access to markets in Africa and the wider region. Bilateral trade exceeds USD 6.5 billion, while Indian investments in Egypt already exceed USD 5.5 billion. Both sides see significant potential for deeper two-way investment, joint manufacturing, technology partnerships and the development of supply chains serving domestic and international markets.

Shri Goyal’s visit follows the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the September 2026 BRICS Summit in India. The high-level visit, the India–Egypt Business Forum involving more than 300 companies and the India–Egypt Joint Business Council engagements reflect the shared ambition to further strengthen economic engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.

Shri Piyush Goyal held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, to review bilateral trade and investment relations and explore avenues for further economic cooperation. Discussions covered trade expansion, market access, investment opportunities, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers and challenges faced by Indian businesses in Egypt, including visa-related issues. Shri Goyal emphasised the importance of facilitating Indian investments and strengthening bilateral supply chains and business-to-business linkages.Shri Piyush Goyal also held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Eng. Khaled Hashem, Minister of Industry of Egypt, to discuss opportunities for strengthening industrial cooperation, promoting manufacturing partnerships and enhancing investment linkages. Both sides discussed potential cooperation in industrial development, technology partnerships, MSME development, industrial automation and advanced manufacturing.

India and Egypt have exciting opportunities to work together in transforming transport, logistics and supply chain infrastructure. Had an excellent meeting with Lt. Gen. Eng. Kamel Al-Wazir, Egypt’s Minister of Transport, to explore greater collaboration in railways, highways, ports and multimodal connectivity. Looking forward to seeing Indian and Egyptian companies collaborating more in Egypt’s infrastructure development. 🇮🇳🇪🇬

— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) November 15, 2026

Had a great conversation with Egypt's Minister of Industry, Mr. Khaled Hasham Ali Maher, on strengthening India-Egypt industrial ties. Indian businesses in Egypt are contributing to investment, jobs, exports, and innovation, and we discussed how to support their further growth. Egypt's location makes it a gateway to Africa, Europe, and the Arab world, and a natural partner for joint manufacturing, technology tie-ups, and resilient supply chains. We also explored how their industrial policy can complement Make in India, and how to strengthen MSMEs through joint training in automation and advanced manufacturing, and technology sharing. Excited about the future of this partnership! 🇮🇳🇪🇬

— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) November 15, 2026

Hello from Egypt! 🇪🇬 An eventful first day, with much to look forward to as India-Egypt explore new possibilities of partnership. https://t.co/rPgV4uu4ua

— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) November 15, 2026

Addressed the India-Egypt Joint Business Council Meeting alongside Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt. Highlighted the strong complementarities between our two economies and the significant potential for greater private-sector participation. The presence of over 700 registered Indian companies in Egypt reflects the growing depth of our business ties. Called upon businesses from both countries to strengthen existing partnerships and explore new avenues of collaboration in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles and other key sectors.

— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) November 15, 2026

Over 300 companies from India and Egypt across sectors met under one roof at the India-Egypt Business Forum. This reflects the enthusiasm for the possibilities and the potential that our partnership can unlock. I spoke about India's scale and robust consumer market can complement Egypt's strategic location, which can generate great outcomes across fields like trade & investment, education, healthcare, engineering, manufacturing, technology solutions, and much more. 📹 https://t.co/iIb0jACxGz

— Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) November 15, 2026

Two ancient civilisations. A future full of possibilities. 🇮🇳🇪🇬 Had a good meeting with Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Egypt's Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade. We talked about expanding bilateral trade, boosting investments and finding new avenues of cooperation. The India-Egypt partnership is set for greater heights!

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings on the conclusion of the four-day Chhath Mahaparv
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 8:55AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today noted that the four-day ritual of Chhath Mahaparv concluded with the offering of Arghya to the rising Sun God. Observing that a wonderful confluence of firm determination and spiritual practice was witnessed during this divine festival dedicated to nature, he prayed to Chhathi Maiya to bestow her auspicious blessings upon all the devotees observing the fast as well as his family members across the country.

The Prime Minister shared on X:

"उदीयमान सूर्यदेव को अर्घ्य अर्पित करने के साथ आज महापर्व छठ का चार दिवसीय अनुष्ठान संपन्न हुआ। प्रकृति को समर्पित इस दिव्य उत्सव में दृढ़ संकल्प और आध्यात्मिक साधना का अद्भुत संगम देखने को मिला। छठी मइया से विनती है कि वे सभी व्रतियों के साथ-साथ देशभर के मेरे परिवारजनों को अपना शुभाशीष प्रदान करें।"

Honble Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla, will participate in the ongoing 10-day Vishwa Shanti Mahayagya at the historic Shri Hatkeshwar Mahadev Mandir in Vadnagar, Gujarat, on 18 November 2026.

​The grand Mahayagya, which commenced on 11 November 2026, and will conclude on 20 November 2026, is being held under the divine guidance and presence of Kanchi Kamakoti Peethadhipati Jagadguru Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswati Swamigal. Organized with the sacred purpose of promoting global peace, social harmony, and public welfare, the event features daily rituals, alongside 144 participating Vedic scholars and devotees from across India.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister’s Departure Statement Ahead of His Visit to the Philippines
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:53AM by PIB Delhi

Today, I am embarking on a visit to Manila to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on 17 November 2026, at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India's Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision. Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.

At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity.

The East Asia Summit provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges. I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

I also look forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines, whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries.

I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India's partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific.

****

MJPS/SS/PRK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Akashvani Launches ‘AIR Rising Stars’ to Provide National Platform to Young Musical Talent
26 Musical Concerts to Be Organised Across the Country from 17th to 30th November 2026
AIR Rising Stars to Promote Young Musical Artists Below 30 Years of Age as Part of Akashvani’s 90-Year Celebrations
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:56PM by PIB Delhi

In a major initiative to encourage young musical talent and carry forward India’s rich and diverse musical heritage, Akashvani is launching the inaugural season of the “AIR Rising Stars”, a nationwide series of special musical concerts exclusively by the young artists below 30 years of age. The first season of the concert series will be organised at 26 locations across the country from 17th November to 30th November 2026. These concerts will provide distinguished national platform to young and emerging musical artists to showcase their talent and connect with wider audiences.

The initiative is being undertaken as part of the celebrations marking 90 years of Akashvani and reflects its continued commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting musical talent across generations. AIR Rising Stars seeks to carry this legacy forward by placing the spotlight on the next generation of performers.

Focus on Young Graded and Emerging Artists

The concerts will primarily feature young graded artists of Akashvani below 30 years of age, representing different genres and musical traditions. In cases where suitable graded young artists are not available in a particular category, deserving ungraded young artists may also be provided an opportunity, subject to the prescribed guidelines and selection by the concerned Akashvani Station.

The concerts will showcase the diversity of India’s musical heritage through Hindustani Classical Music (Vocal and Instrumental), Carnatic Classical Music (Vocal and Instrumental), Light and Folk Music, Western Music and other regional musical forms, as appropriate to the participating stations.

Nationwide Celebration at 26 Locations

The concerts will be organised by 26 participating Akashvani Stations at Shimla, Dehradun, Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi, Jaipur, Jalandhar, Suratgarh, Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Dharwad, Bengaluru, Mysuru, Madurai, Thiruvananthapuram, Tiruchirappalli, Kolkata, Imphal, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Sangli, Nagpur, Puducherry, Jammu, Guwahati and Rampur.

Each participating station will organise a musical concert at a suitable venue, featuring promising young artists from the respective region. Eminent personalities, music connoisseurs, youth icons, students and members of the public will also be invited to encourage the participating artists and make the initiative a nationwide celebration of young musical talent.

Multi-Platform Broadcast and Digital Outreach

A key feature of AIR Rising Stars: Season-1 will be its extensive multi-platform broadcast and digital outreach, taking the performances of young artists beyond the concert venues to audiences across the country.

The concerts will be broadcast through the network of Akashvani Stations and will also receive coverage on Doordarshan, on “Raagam” Youtube channel of Akashvani, youtube channels of 26 Akashvani Stations, “NewsOnAir” mobile app and Prasar Bharati’s “WAVES OTT” platform. This integrated broadcast strategy will provide participating artists wider visibility through radio, television and digital platforms.

Cash Prizes for Top Three Performances

To encourage young artists and promote wider digital engagement, cash prizes and certificates will be awarded to the three participating artists whose performances secure the highest number of views on YouTube by 15th January 2027.

First Prize: ₹20,000

Second Prize: ₹15,000

Third Prize: ₹10,000

This initiative will provide additional recognition to young performers and encourage them to reach out to wider audiences through digital platforms.

It may be noted that Akashvani has a long tradition of organising the Akashvani Sangeet Sammelan , which has successfully completed 67 editions. Akashvani Sangeet Sammelan provides an esteemed platform for renowned Top Grade and A Grade artists to showcase their musical excellence, whereas AIR Rising Stars is an exclusive initiative aimed at providing a dedicated platform to young graded artists, who otherwise have limited opportunities to perform in such prestigious concert platforms organised by Akashvani.

Through “AIR Rising Stars:”, Akashvani aims to create a distinctive national platform for the next generation of musicians while strengthening the connection between India’s enduring musical traditions and its youth. The initiative will further reinforce Akashvani’s longstanding role as a promoter of India’s rich cultural and musical heritage and a nurturing ground for emerging musical talent.

*****

Mahesh Kumar/ Utkarsh Upadhyay

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Inaugurates EPFO Lounge and ESIC Pavilion at IITF 2026
Kiosks showcase citizen-centric initiatives for accessible social security and healthcare
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, today inaugurated the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) Lounge and the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Central Provident Fund Commissioner (CPFC) Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi, Director General, ESIC, Shri Ashok Kumar Singh, and other senior officers from both EPFO and ESIC were present on the occasion.

Following the inauguration, Dr. Mandaviya witnessed the initiatives and facilities being offered at the respective kiosks, and also interacted with visitors.  The Union Minister expressed his appreciation for the citizen-centric, technology-driven initiatives aimed at making social security services more accessible, efficient, and engaging for workers, pensioners, employers and the general public.

EPFO Lounge

The EPFO Lounge features an engaging puppet show (Raja Rancho) highlighting EPFO’s benefits. It also showcases dedicated kiosks offering a wide range of support, including the Nidhi Aapke Nikat / Grievances kiosk for grievance resolution; an E-services Desk for online guidance, claim filing, and KYC correction; a Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana / Face Authentication Technology kiosk; an information kiosk on New Schemes of EPFO; a Pension Help Desk for pension queries and Digital Life Certificates; and a National Career Services (NCS) / e-Shram kiosk for employment and social security services.

ESIC Pavilion

At the ESIC Pavilion, visitors have access to public-friendly facilities such as free health check-ups (including blood pressure monitoring and blood glucose tests), on-the-spot Aadhaar seeding, and across-the-counter grievance resolution, alongside face-to-face interactions with senior ESIC officers from Delhi and Haryana. To make awareness interactive and engaging, the pavilion features digital screens, audio-visual presentations, a Know ESIC quiz, an interactive Take a Selfie and Become a Doctor activity, as well as daily goody bags and merchandise for lucky participants. Additionally, a unique QR-code-based direct feedback mechanism has been introduced, with responses monitored daily by the Insurance Commissioner to ensure citizens' suggestions directly reach senior management.

Both spaces will remain open to visitors throughout IITF 2026 from 14th to 27th November 2026 at Hall No. 4, Bharat Mandapam, with the EPFO Lounge located on the Ground Floor (Stall No. 8A) and the ESIC Pavilion on the First Floor (Stall No. 4F-05-A). Workers, pensioners, employers, their families, and the general public are cordially invited to visit both stalls to avail of on-the-spot services, participate in interactive activities, and learn more about the government's social security initiatives.

***

Rini Choudhury / Aishwarya Asthana

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Agriculture Pavilion in IITF 2026 Witnesses Massive Footfall
Pavilion to remain open every day till November 27, 2026, to showcase its unique display of modern agriculture
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Agriculture Pavilion set-up by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA&FW) in the 'India International Trade Fair (IITF)' 2026 has emerged as a major crowd-puller at Pragati Maidan. Commencing from November 13 and to be  continued till November 27th 2026, the pavilion today witnessed  extraordinary public participation. The momentum received a major boost with the visit of the Joint Secretary (Extension), who interacted extensively with exhibitors, farmers, and tech innovators, praising their efforts towards awareness creation about sustainable and modern agriculture.

The theme of the pavilion beautifully reflects the progress of MoA&FW in empowering farmers through farmer-centric  interventions of flagship schemes, technology transfer and direct market linkages from 'Seed to Market'.

Strategic Display of Key initiatives and Achievement of MoA&FW Schemes in Agriculture Pavilion include :

• Digital Agriculture & Public Infrastructure: A cornerstone of the pavilion depicts the live demonstration of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, featuring AgriStack, Decision Support System (DSS) for geospatial intelligence, and AR/VR-based Digital Crop Surveys.

• National Mission on Natural Farming & Core Missions: The pavilion spotlights the shift toward eco-friendly farming with full-scale models on Natural Farming, alongside interactive displays from the Pulses Mission and Oilseeds Development ("Save Oil" campaign), stepping towards self-reliance.

• Millets for Nutrition: Backed by the Directorate of Millets Development, this zone attracts massive crowds to  visualise live seed samples, nutritional education, and counters for processed and value-added millet products, as a super food.

• Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY): A dedicated area showcases the success milestones, and the security net provided by the government's premier Crop Insurance Scheme to millions of Indian farmers.

• Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): Underlining the conservation of water through Micro Irrigation automation set-ups display, high-efficiency water conservation techniques and smart irrigation systems.

• Empowering FPOs & Agri-Marketing: Giving regional agriculture a global platform, several Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and the e-NAM (electronic-National Agriculture Market) network are showcasing their high-quality produce.

The Major highlights include:

            • Kashmiri Saffron & Spices: Saffron, Kahwa, and pure essential oils directly from FPO Pampore.

            • Organic & Native Grains: Multi-flavored Jaggery from Hargaon FPO, and unique Black and Basmati rice varieties showcased by FPO, Dasuya.

            • North-East Organic Bounty: Exotic fruit wines, Lakadong turmeric, and bamboo shoot pickles brought by Tangsim Agro FPO from Meghalaya.

• Advanced Horticulture & Allied Sectors: Live hydroponic farming display by  'National Horticulture Board (NHB)', cocoa processing techniques, and high-interest live Beehive & Honey Extraction demonstrations by 'National Bee Board' are keeping families and children highly engaged.

• Plant Protection & Modern Agriculture Machinery: Interactive zones on safe pesticide use, the Pest Surveillance System (NPSS), Mobile App, and actual display of advanced mechanical farm tools emphasize smart farming.

The Agriculture Pavilion remains open every day till November 27, 2026, to showcase its unique display of modern agriculture to the urban visitors, industry professionals, and visiting farmers with a profound, technology driven to depict the resilient and sustainable future of Indian agriculture.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Zoological Park organises 21st Sunday Bird Walk to Promote Citizen Science and Biodiversity Documentation
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, organised the 21st edition of ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’ on 15 November 2026, from 7:30 AM to 10:30 AM promoting public participation in biodiversity monitoring and wildlife conservation. The walk was conducted under the expert guidance of Shri Vineet Kumar, Bird Expert, with the support of dedicated volunteers.

A total of eight participants, comprising bird enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens with an interest in biodiversity, took part in the programme. The walk was also attended by the zoo officials and the resource expert, who interacted with participants and shared their knowledge and insights throughout the activity.

During the walk, participants recorded 42 bird species, with more than 600 individual birds observed in the designated area. A significant highlight of this edition of Sunday Bird Walk was the addition of a new species to the bird checklist of the National Zoological Park —Northern Shoveler (Spatula clypeata). This addition represents a valuable contribution to the ongoing documentation of the Zoo's avian diversity and underscores the importance of systematic bird monitoring and citizen science in understanding and conserving biodiversity.

The walk also provided participants with a hands-on learning experience in bird identification and field-based biodiversity documentation. Shri Vineet Kumar shared valuable insights into bird ecology, behaviour and conservation, highlighting the ecological significance of birds, particularly their role in natural pest control and their importance as indicators of ecosystem health.

Through initiatives such as Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP, the National Zoological Park continues to foster environmental awareness, encourage citizen participation in biodiversity conservation and strengthen public engagement in documenting the rich avian diversity of the Zoo.

To ensure meaningful learning and effective participation, each Sunday Bird Walk is limited to 20–25 participants. Prior registration is mandatory, and places are allotted on a first-come, first-served basis. The registration form remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park and through the NZP Saathi mobile application.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah performs Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society, virtually inaugurates Western Regional Office of Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launches Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Maharashtra
Pioneers like Vitthalrao Vikhe Patil and Vaikunthbhai Mehta laid the foundation of the cooperative movement in Maharashtra, establishing a system to ensure that the benefits of agricultural trade reach farmers
The sugar mill and machinery manufacturing facility established by our cooperative pioneers in Pune as National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited (NHEC) is being revived today
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, several significant initiatives have been undertaken to strengthen PACS, dairy cooperatives and cooperative sugar mills following the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi attended a programme in Gadchiroli, a region that has recently witnessed significant progress towards freedom from Naxalism, on the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda
Western Regional Office for regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies inaugurated in Pune; Shri Amit Shah congratulates cooperative leaders of Maharashtra
Bharat Taxi, envisioned as a nationwide cooperative-based transport service, launched in Pune; Sarathis to receive their entire earnings without any commission deductions through a fully transparent system
The idea of cooperative-based Bharat Taxi emerged from the need to address the exploitation faced by drivers over the years; Sarathis are now becoming owners of their own transport enterprise
Bhoomi Pujan performed for the revival of National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited (NHEC), a pioneering manufacturer of sugar mills and centrifugal machinery, with the support of cooperative institutions
The revived NHEC facility will manufacture sugar mills, power generation plants, ethanol and CBG plants, dairy processing equipment and containers, with every rupee of earnings accruing to cooperative institutions
Circular economy in the dairy and sugar sectors will generate additional income for farmers from cattle dung and other by-products while helping reduce t
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' and further strengthening, modernising and making the cooperative movement in the country more inclusive, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today performed the Bhoomi Pujan for the revival of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative) Multi-State Cooperative Society at Talegaon Dabhade in Pune district, Maharashtra. On the occasion, he also virtually inaugurated the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) and launched Bharat Taxi services in Pune. Deputy Chief Ministers of Maharashtra Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Maharashtra Minister for Higher and Technical Education and Parliamentary Affairs Shri Chandrakant Patil, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani, and several other dignitaries were present at the event.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah paid tribute to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and said that the land of Maharashtra has not only played a significant role in establishing and strengthening the spirit of Swaraj but has also given a new direction to the cooperative movement in the country. He said that Maharashtra, particularly Pune, can rightly be described as the fountainhead of the cooperative movement in western India. Pioneers of the cooperative movement, including Padma Shri Vitthalrao Patil and Vaikunthbhai Mehta, had endeavoured even before Independence to develop a system in which the maximum benefits arising from agriculture and trade would reach farmers.

Shri Amit Shah said that farmers, rural women, milk producers and those associated with the cooperative movement had long been demanding the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation at the Centre. He said that this demand remained unfulfilled during the tenure of previous governments, while the Central Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi established a dedicated Ministry of Cooperation, giving a new direction to the cooperative sector. He said that Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), district-level cooperative institutions and the dairy sector are steadily becoming stronger. The Central Government has undertaken several significant measures, including providing relief of approximately Rs. 15,000 crore to cooperative sugar mills and extending income tax relief of approximately Rs. 3,000 crore annually.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a major manufacturing facility producing machinery and equipment for sugar mills once operated on the very land where today's programme was being held. The factory had ceased operations during the tenure of a previous government. He said that the reconstruction of the same industrial complex is now being initiated, marking an occasion of pride and satisfaction for the cooperative sector.

Shri Amit Shah extended his greetings to the people of the country, particularly mothers and sisters, on the occasion of Chhath Mahaparv. Paying tribute to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his 151st birth anniversary, he said that Bhagwan Birsa Munda had ignited the spirit of resistance against colonial rule from the land of Jharkhand even before the wider freedom movement gathered momentum. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi decided to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. Shri Shah also referred to the progress made towards eliminating Naxalism in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, and the programme held there. Paying homage to Acharya Vinoba Bhave, he said that Vinoba Ji dedicated his life to cow welfare, Sarvodaya, the Bhoodan Movement and strengthening Indian languages through the Devanagari script. He recalled that Vinoba Bhave, a devoted follower of Mahatma Gandhi, spent a significant part of his life in Wardha, Maharashtra.

Referring to the inauguration of the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a large number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies operate across the western region, including Maharashtra and Gujarat. He said that there had been demands from different regions for the establishment of this office, which has now been set up in Pune. Shri Shah informed that the office would undertake regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu.

Referring to the launch of Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Shri Amit Shah said that cooperative-based Bharat Taxi services would be expanded across the country. He said that for many years, drivers associated with several taxi companies had to surrender a portion of their earnings as commission and, in many instances, faced exploitation. The concept of Bharat Taxi, based on the cooperative model, was developed to address this situation. He said that through Bharat Taxi, the Sarathi brothers and sisters, who were earlier recognised merely as drivers, are now becoming owners of their own company. The system ensures complete transparency, with the entire earnings of Sarathis being credited directly to their bank accounts without any commission deductions. He said that Bharat Taxi services should also be introduced in Nagpur, Nashik, Kolhapur and Solapur after Pune.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, referring to the Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative), said that the institution had previously operated from the same location and supplied sugar mills and centrifugal machinery across the world. He said that over time, the industrial unit ceased operations, and its approximately 110 acres of land increasingly faced the threat of illegal encroachment. The Ministry of Cooperation initiated efforts to revive this important cooperative industrial asset and began the process of its restoration with the support of institutions such as the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), Amul, IPL, IFFCO and the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).

Shri Amit Shah said that the manufacturing facility to be established at NHEC would not be limited to producing sugar mills. It would also manufacture power generation plants for sugar mills, Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants and various types of industrial equipment and plants related to the dairy sector. In addition, the facility would undertake container manufacturing for export to overseas markets. He said that the earnings generated from these industrial activities would accrue to cooperative institutions, thereby further strengthening the cooperative-based economic ecosystem.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that there was a time when sugar mills manufactured by NHEC were exported to 11 countries, including Zambia, Ethiopia and Vietnam. The manufacturing facility had such a strong order book and demand that the delivery of new orders could take approximately four years. He said that these industrial operations subsequently came to a halt, but the Central Government has now decided to revive this important cooperative institution.

Shri Amit Shah informed that, as part of the revival process of NHEC, the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) initially took over the management of the institution as its administrator. Subsequently, all audits that had remained pending for the previous two years were completed. Institutions including Amul, NDDB, NCDC, IFFCO, NABARD and IPL contributed towards mobilising the investment required for the revival of the institution. Its Board of Directors was reconstituted, and at its first meeting held on 9 October 2026, a resolution was taken to rebuild the institution. The Bhoomi Pujan of the project was performed today as part of this process.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a plan has been prepared to reschedule all liabilities and loans of NHEC and settle them in a transparent manner. He expressed confidence that production would commence at the facility before December 2027 and manufacturing of sugar mills would resume. He said that a circular economy would also be developed in the sugar and dairy sectors, creating additional income opportunities for farmers through the productive utilisation of resources such as cattle dung. Similarly, efforts would be made to reduce dependence on imports by increasing the utilisation of various by-products generated by sugar mills. He further informed that the second phase of the project envisages manufacturing containers for the railways, defence sector and exports.

Shri Amit Shah expressed confidence that, like successful cooperative institutions such as Amul, IFFCO and KRIBHCO, NHEC would also emerge as an important example for the cooperative movement in the country in the coming years. He congratulated all the institutions associated with the revival of NHEC and the farmers of Maharashtra on this initiative.

In his address, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also referred to the country's democratic system and the role of political parties, observing that the principal opposition party has faced successive electoral defeats in recent years. Referring to 'Bharat Summit 2026' held in Hyderabad, he said that the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition at the international conference concerning India's development journey, democratic system and national leadership were inappropriate. Shri Shah said that the electoral success or failure of political parties depends on their leadership, performance and the confidence reposed in them by the people.

Shri Amit Shah referred to the tenure of the previous government and said that several allegations and controversies relating to corruption had emerged during that period, whereas development across various sectors has gained momentum over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He highlighted achievements in agriculture, industrial development, India's historic accomplishment of reaching the Moon's south polar region, expansion of the startup ecosystem, modernisation of the railways, increase in the number of airports to approximately 150, expansion of the metro network, introduction of the National Education Policy and establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation advised the Leader of the Opposition that engaging with people in India's villages and understanding their concerns was more important than criticising the country on international platforms. He said that, in a democracy, the path to political power lies in reaching out to the people and earning their trust. Shri Shah said that all political parties, whether in government or in opposition, have a responsibility to safeguard the country's reputation, democratic institutions and national interests on international platforms. He also urged workers of the opposition party to reflect on the approach and political direction of their leadership, adding that the people of the country express their verdict through the democratic process.

Concluding his address, Shri Amit Shah said that a new beginning has been made in the cooperative sector today. Industrial production activities will resume at the approximately 110-acre complex that had remained closed for years. He extended his best wishes to cooperative sector workers and farmers across the country and expressed confidence that the revival of NHEC would give a new direction to cooperative-led industrial development in India.

During the programme, a Letter of Intent (LoI) was exchanged between NHEC and IDMC Limited, and share certificates were presented to Bharat Taxi Sarathis.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Dr M L Jat, DG ICAR inaugurates Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing and Farmers’ Training Centre at ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 6:59PM by PIB Bengaluru

Dr. M. L. Jat, Hon’ble Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), visited ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru, on 15 November 2026. During his visit, he inaugurated the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre (ATC) and the Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, including a Biosafety Level-II (BSL-II) Laboratory.

Following the inauguration of the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre, Dr. Jat interacted with progressive farmers, incubatees, entrepreneurs, nursery owners and practitioners of natural farming who have adopted ICAR-IIHR varieties and technologies. The interaction focused on natural farming practices, innovations in horticulture and strategies to mitigate the impact of El Niño and Super El Niño on horticultural crops. Farmers shared their experiences in adopting climate-resilient practices such as mulching, sprinkler irrigation, border cropping, intercropping with short-duration flower and vegetable crops, and green manuring. These interventions have helped improve crop yield, produce quality and farmers’ income.

Addressing the farmers, Dr. Jat emphasized the importance of encouraging educated youth, engineers and agricultural graduates to actively participate and invest in agriculture and horticulture by adopting scientific innovations. He highlighted the need to integrate modern scientific technologies with traditional wisdom and stressed that farmers must remain at the centre of all agricultural research and development initiatives. He also appreciated the role of ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) in popularizing innovative technologies through Government of India programmes, particularly the Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA). He assured that successful farmer innovations and experiences would be documented and disseminated widely to benefit farming communities across the country.

Subsequently, Dr. Jat inaugurated the Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, equipped with a Biosafety Level-II Laboratory, marking an important step towards strengthening advanced biotechnology research and genome-editing capabilities in horticultural crops. He emphasized that scientists should prepare for the future by developing self-reliance in genome resources for genome-editing research. He also highlighted the need for prioritization, better targeting, development of a strong data ecosystem and identification of opportunities where Indian agricultural research can achieve global standards and first-of-its-kind innovations.

During his interaction with postgraduate students, he stressed the importance of nurturing young scientific talent and strengthening human capital. He encouraged scientists to move beyond conventional approaches, embrace new opportunities and work towards making agriculture a major contributor to India's vision of a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047, with a targeted contribution of USD 6 trillion from agriculture. He also highlighted the potential of microbial technologies, biofertilizer start-ups and innovations in health and nutrition.

The visit also included interaction with postgraduate students, visits to research laboratories and a field visit to the institute's research facilities. The visit provided an important platform to strengthen the institute's research, innovation, farmer outreach and human resource development initiatives, reaffirming ICAR-IIHR's commitment to sustainable, climate-resilient and technology-driven horticultural development.

On this occasion Dr V B Patel, ADG Fruits and  spices, Director IIHR Dr Tusar Kanti Behera, Directors and Heads of the ICAR institutes in Bengaluru, Scientists of the institute, Postgraduate students, research scholars, Innovative farmers and Agri entrepreneurs were present.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
At the Climate Summit, India Makes the Case for a Sunday Bike Ride
At COP31 in Antalya, Fit India presented Sundays on Cycle, a weekly ride that has not missed a Sunday since December 2024, and invited every country to host one community ride in the next year.
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi

Most of the talk at a United Nations climate summit is about energy, finance and technology. On Saturday afternoon, at the International Solar Alliance Pavilion at COP31, India’s Fit India Movement made a smaller argument: that the climate fight is also won on ordinary streets, one weekend ride at a time.

“A city can build a bicycle lane, but only if its citizens choose to ride on it,” Mayank Srivastava, deputy director general of the Sports Authority of India, told the audience. “Infrastructure alone does not change how people live.”

The hour-long session, “Sundays on Cycle: From a Weekly Ride to a Way of Life,” was held at the pavilion (D 610) on the summit’s Children, Youth, Education and Skills Day at COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 29 August 2019, the  Fit India Movement reflects his vision of building a healthy, active, and prosperous India. The movement aims to make fitness an integral part of every Indian’s daily life by encouraging people to adopt healthy lifestyles, engage in regular physical activities, practise yoga, and participate in sports.

The Fit India Movement of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports presented the ride as a working example of Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), India’s campaign for sustainable lifestyles, with a simple message: one pedal, one purpose, one healthier world.

Sundays on Cycle, a free community ride, has been held every Sunday since Dec. 22, 2024. “It has not missed a single Sunday,” Mr. Srivastava said. Participation has reached close to 3.7 million at more than 30,000 locations across India, he said, and on World Bicycle Day this year, held with cycling’s world governing body, the Union Cycliste Internationale, organisers planned for 100,000 riders and about 400,000 turned up.

“More than the numbers, people have begun to take cycling seriously,” he said. “They return Sunday after Sunday, and what began as a campaign is becoming a habit.”

He argued that timing matters for countries like India. Many cities in the Global South are still being built, he said, and most trips in them are short enough to cycle. “If cycling becomes a habit before car dependence takes hold, those emissions need never be produced,” he said. “Avoiding them now is far cheaper than removing them later.”

Lindita Xhaferi-Salihu, who leads sectors engagement for Global Climate Action at UN Climate Change, delivered the keynote. She described Fit India as “a great model that can be replicated everywhere,” and spoke about her husband, who arrived in a new country as an 18-year-old refugee and found a community through a local handball club. “A community is only a community if somebody brings it together,” she said. “We cannot talk about communities if we don’t have somebody like Fit India bringing together people who share the same purpose and can act collectively for the betterment of their societies.” Climate negotiations, she added, are so technical that it has been hard to bring people along, and sport can be the “connective tissue” that does it.

A short film on the ride’s journey followed. In it, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, India’s minister for youth affairs and sports, who launched Sundays on Cycle in December 2024, described cycling as “much more than exercise” and “a powerful medium to carry the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s message of Fit India.” “Through initiatives like Fit India Sundays on Cycle,” he said, “we must take this passion to every household and every community.”

A panel moderated by Dr. Bhairavi Joshi, an adviser to Fit India, asked whether a weekend ride can change how cities are built.

Jim Walker of the Walk21 Foundation, who joined a Sundays on Cycle ride in Delhi last month, pointed to Bogotá, Colombia, where a similar street opening began about 50 years ago and now draws about 1.6 million people every Sunday onto 125 kilometres of car-free streets. “We get stuck in the habits of our cities,” he said.

Felipe A. Ramírez Buitrago, director of urban mobility at the WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities, said such events “teach with example.” Once people enjoy the streets, he said, cities can make the case for protected lanes and links to mass transit.

Gashaw Aberra of ITDP Africa said car-free days in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, had helped produce the country’s first non-motorised transport strategy, which sets targets for walkways and cycle tracks. “Instead of what can we learn from Africa, I would say, what can Africa learn from India,” he said.

Sanjay Seth, executive director of The Energy and Resources Institute, said walking and cycling should be counted in India’s climate commitments and in state and city plans, not treated only as awareness campaigns. “We need to make sure that we build safely; then behaviour will follow,” he said.

Asked for one action every city should take in the next 12 months, the panellists answered in a word or two: Maud De Vries, chief executive of BYCS, said “just do it”; others named infrastructure, community engagement and obstruction-free pathways.

Closing the session, Ms. Amarjyoti, executive director of Fit India, invited every nation, city and partner present to host at least one community-led “active morning” over the next 12 months and to share the experience through the One Planet Network. The Turkish Cycling Federation, she said, was the first partner to join. “A cycling culture is not built in a day,” she said. “It is built week after week by people who keep showing up.”

The organisers also released an impact report on the first 97 editions of the ride.

Ashish Khanna, director general of the International Solar Alliance, delivered a special address. He said the session had drawn the largest attendance the pavilion had seen, and urged sports facilities, from stadiums to gyms, to adopt solar power. “We are so proud that we could fit something related to sports and cycling in our agenda,” he said.

The ride’s 100th edition will be held across India on Nov. 29. Fit India said it would share a Sundays on Cycle toolkit to help other cities start their own rides, and invited people around the world to ride that day in their own communities.

Fit India also invited COP31 delegates to a special Sundays on Cycle ride in Antalya on Sunday, Nov. 15, held with the Turkish Cycling Federation (Türkiye Bisiklet Federasyonu) from Konyaaltı to the old town of Kaleiçi, carrying the Sunday ride from India’s neighbourhoods to the summit’s host city. In India, the ride’s 98th edition on the same day marked Children’s Day with cycling and Zumba.

“Ride together, change together,” Ms. Amarjyoti said.

This special edition of Sundays on Cycle at COP31 was held under the banner “India Pedals & The World Joins In!”, and was organised in partnership with the Turkish Cycling Federation in Antalya, Türkiye, on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The route saw cyclists begin the rally at Konyaaltı Caddesi and conclude at Işıklar.

About Fit India – Sundays on Cycle

Launched by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, in December 2024, Fit India – Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Sports Authority of India under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India, Navavrati Foundation, Fitspire, the Centre for Integrative Health, MY Bharat and other partners. Rides are held every Sunday in all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence, SAI Training Centres, Khelo India State Centres of Excellence and Khelo India Centres.

The COP31 session was supported by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Sports Authority of India, Fit India, Mission LiFE, the International Solar Alliance and BYCS India Foundation.

Prime Minister shares an article by Vice President Thiru C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighting the role of Eklavya Model Residential Schools in empowering tribal students
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, has shared an article written by the Vice President, Thiru C. P. Radhakrishnan.

The article outlines the evolution of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) and their role in creating new opportunities for tribal children through quality education and holistic development. It highlights key initiatives such as bridge courses, bilingual teaching, technology-enabled classrooms, sports and vocational training, alongside the achievements of students entering IITs, AIIMS and other premier institutions.

The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X:

“Eklavya Model Residential Schools are creating new opportunities for tribal children through quality education.

On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, Hon'ble @VPIndia, Thiru @CPR_VP, writes about the evolution of EMRS and its role in providing quality education and holistic development to tribal students.

He highlights initiatives such as bridge courses, bilingual teaching, technology-enabled classrooms, sports and vocational training, along with the achievements of students who are now entering IITs, AIIMS and other premier institutions.

A must-read!”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
57th IFFI Celebrates Cinematic Ties with Partner Country Russia Through an Evocative Four-Film Showcase
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 5:52PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 15 November 2026

 

Under the theme of "Stories Without Borders," the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), proudly spotlights Russia as its esteemed Partner Country. Scheduled to take place in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026, the festival reinforces enduring Indo-Russian cultural diplomacy by presenting a specially curated four-film package that bridges contemporary Russian auteur sensibilities with a celebrated Soviet musical classic.

Bringing together emerging directorial voices alongside a masterwork of satirical operetta, the Partner Country Russia section reflects the emotional breadth, stylistic audacity, and thematic depth of Russian filmmaking. From intimate explorations of family fractures, societal alienation, and personal redemption to a buoyant, Shostakovich-scored satire on urban aspirations, the showcase will offer festival delegates and cinephiles an immersive journey into the human condition.

Anastasia Kuzina’s Bo Bo (98 min), making its India premiere at the 57th IFFI, is a poignant rural drama about identity, acceptance and prejudice. Through Nadia, a young girl facing mockery for her facial hemangioma, the film explores her search for self-expression through music, reminding us that true transformation lies not in changing appearances but in overcoming societal prejudice.

Sidney Lumet’s Birthday

Raul Geidarov’s Sidney Lumet’s Birthday (92 min), winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the Vyborg National Film Festival, makes its India Premiere at IFFI57. This heartfelt coming-of-age drama follows 17-year-old Dato as he navigates family tensions, abandonment and forgiveness, exploring the resilience needed to heal generational wounds.

New Home

Nikita Grushin’s New Home (101 min), set for its World Premiere at IFFI 2026, is a moving drama about second chances and redemption. Following seven years in prison, Anna struggles to rebuild her life with the help of social services and Roman’s support. Featuring powerful performances, the film explores the challenges of reintegration, healing and confronting the past to find a new beginning.

Cheryomushki

Herbert Rappaport’s Cheryomushki (91 min), making its India Premiere at IFFI, is a delightful musical satire set in post-war Moscow. Following four young couples dreaming of better homes, the film blends catchy melodies, lively choreography and humour to expose bureaucratic corruption while celebrating community spirit and solidarity.

Through this specially curated selection, IFFI 2026 reaffirms the enduring cultural ties between India and Russia, while offering audiences an opportunity to engage with the diversity and evolving expressions of Russian cinema. The four films, spanning different genres and generations of filmmaking, reflect cinema's ability to transcend geographical boundaries and foster mutual understanding through shared human experiences.

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026, will bring together filmmakers, industry professionals and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world under the theme “Stories Without Borders.” With a diverse line-up of Indian and international films, special country showcases, premieres, competitions and industry engagements, IFFI 2026 continues its tradition of celebrating cinematic excellence and promoting cross-cultural exchange through cinema.

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rajith Chandran/ Lekshmi Priya S S / Swadhin Shakti Prasad/ Darshana Rane

item.title: India to strengthen engagement with Italy based 'International Physics Centre', says Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology India to strengthen engagement with Italy based 'International Physics Centre', says Minister Dr Jitendra Singh India and 'International Centre for Theoretical Physics' (ICTP) initiate ‘India- ICTP Co-operation Fund’ to institutionalise scientific collaboration and researcher mobility: Dr. Jitendra Singh Letter of Intent signed between DST and ICTP to strengthen long-standing research partnership and create greater opportunities for Indian scientists, researchers and students Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:59PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India to strengthen engagement with Italy based 'International Physics Centre', says Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
India and 'International Centre for Theoretical Physics' (ICTP) initiate ‘India- ICTP Co-operation Fund’ to institutionalise scientific collaboration and researcher mobility: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Letter of Intent signed between DST and ICTP to strengthen long-standing research partnership and create greater opportunities for Indian scientists, researchers and students
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi

India and the "International Centre for Theoretical Physics" (ICTP) have taken a significant step towards institutionalising their longstanding scientific partnership with the initiation of the ‘India-ICTP Co-operation Fund’, aimed at strengthening the engagement and mobility of Indian researchers with the international research centre.

A Letter of Intent (LoI) was signed between the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and ICTP in this regard during the visit of Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, to ICTP in Trieste, Italy. The LoI was exchanged from the Indian side by Dr Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Head of the International Cooperation in DST.

Welcoming the initiative, Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed the hope that the India-ICTP Co-operation Fund would give greater impact to the existing engagement between the two sides and benefit Indian researchers. He noted the importance of institutionalising the ongoing association to provide further impetus to scientific collaboration and researcher mobility.

The initiative builds upon India's longstanding partnership with ICTP, which has seen active participation by Indian scientists, researchers and students across multiple programmes. Through the proposed Co-operation Fund, DST and ICTP seek to provide a more structured framework for this existing engagement, with particular emphasis on creating further opportunities for Indian researchers.

ICTP is a leading global hub for advanced research, higher education and capacity-building in physics, mathematics and related fields. Its association with India extends across research collaboration, academic exchange, workshops and capacity-building activities involving several Indian institutions.

Institutions including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), CSIR, leading universities and IITs have collaborated with ICTP through joint research, workshops and exchange programmes. Indian researchers regularly benefit from ICTP's visiting fellowships, diploma programmes and postdoctoral opportunities, while ICTP experts frequently engage with India's scientific communities working in high-energy physics, astrophysics, climate modelling and computational science.

The initiation of the India-ICTP Co-operation Fund and the signing of the LoI mark an important step towards strengthening these existing avenues of engagement and advancing the researcher mobility component of the partnership.

The collaboration has contributed to strengthening global networks of scientific excellence, bringing together researchers and institutions and supporting fundamental discoveries as well as innovations with societal impact. The proposed initiative is expected to further enhance the impact of this engagement and benefit India's scientific research community.

Dr. Jitendra Singh's visit to ICTP, which included a welcome lunch and the initiation of the researcher mobility programme, formed part of his official visit to Italy from November 11 to 15, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy Unveil Logo and Mascot for 8th Edition of Khelo India Youth Games 2026
Khelo India Youth Games to be held in Telangana from December 11 to 22 across six cities
Around 8,000 athletes and participants expected to take part
Edition to feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events
Softball to make its debut as a competitive sport, while Sailing and Karra Samu will feature as demonstration sports for the first time
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Chief Minister of Telangana A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), scheduled to be held in Telangana from December 11 to 22, 2026.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and integrating sports into the broader vision of the country’s development.
